text_mt: while others describe that all the worlds are to be purified. / The guru, illustrious Bhūtirājamiśra, however, taught that outside are a hundred Rudras, // 410

sanskrit_iast:
aṣṭāvantaḥ sākaṃ śarveṇetīdṛśī nivṛttiriyaṃ syāt /
rudrāḥ kālī vīro dharābdhilakṣmyaḥ sarasvatī guhyam // 411
meaning:
अष्टावन्तः साकं शर्वेणेतीदृशी निवृत्तिरियं स्यात् /
रुद्राः काली वीरो धराब्धिलक्ष्म्यः सरस्वती गुह्यम् // 411
text_mt: and inside eight together with Śarva; such would be this Nivṛtti. / The Rudras, Kālī, the hero, Dharā, Abdhi, Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, and Guhya: // 411

sanskrit_iast:
ityaṣṭakaṃ jale'nau vahnyatiguhyadvayaṃ maruti vāyoḥ /
svapuraṃ gayādi khe ca vyoma pavitrāṣṭakaṃ ca bhuvanayugam // 412
meaning:
इत्यष्टकं जलेऽनौ वह्न्यतिगुह्यद्वयं मरुति वायोः /
स्वपुरं गयादि खे च व्योम पवित्राष्टकं च भुवनयुगम् // 412
text_mt: this is the octad in water. In fire, there is the pair of Vahni and Atiguhya; in wind, the wind's / own city and Gayā, etc.; and in space, Vyoma and the pair of pure worlds (Pavitrāṣṭaka). // 412

sanskrit_iast:
abhimāne'haṅkāracchagalādyaṣṭakamathāntarā nabho'haṃkṛt /
tanmātrārkenduśratipurāṣṭakaṃ buddhikarmadevānām // 413
meaning:
अभिमानेऽहङ्कारच्छगलाद्यष्टकमथान्तरा नभोऽहंकृत् /
तन्मात्रार्केन्दुश्रतिपुराष्टकं बुद्धिकर्मदेवानाम् // 413
text_mt: In pride (egoity) is the octad beginning with Ahaṅkāra and Chagala; then between space and egoity / is the octad of worlds of the tanmātras, sun, moon, and Śruti; of the deities of the intellect and action [organs], // 413

sanskrit_iast:
daśa tanmātrasamūhe bhuvanaṃ punarakṣavargavinipatite /
manasaścetyabhimāne dvāviṃśatireva bhuvanānām // 414
meaning:
दश तन्मात्रसमूहे भुवनं पुनरक्षवर्गविनिपतिते /
मनसश्चेत्यभिमाने द्वाविंशतिरेव भुवनानाम् // 414
text_mt: ten; in the aggregate of the subtle elements, a world; again, in the category falling under the sense organs / and mind [there are worlds]; thus in pride (egoity) there are twenty-two worlds. // 414

sanskrit_iast:
dhiyi daivīnāmaṣṭau kruttejoyogasaṃjñakaṃ trayaṃ tadumā /
tatpatiratha mūrtyaṣṭakasuśivadvādaśakavīrabhadrāḥ syuḥ // 415
meaning:
धियि दैवीनामष्टौ क्रुत्तेजोयोगसंज्ञकं त्रयं तदुमा /
तत्पतिरथ मूर्त्यष्टकसुशिवद्वादशकवीरभद्राः स्युः // 415
text_mt: In the intellect are eight worlds of the goddesses, the triad called Krut, Tejas, and Yoga, their Umā / and their lord; then the octad of forms (Mūrtyaṣṭaka), the twelve Suśivas, and the Vīrabhadras; // 415

sanskrit_iast:
tadatha mahādevāṣṭakamiti buddhau saptadaśa saṃkhyā /
guṇatattve paṅktitrayamiti ṣaṭpañcāśataṃ purāṇi viduḥ // 416
meaning:
तदथ महादेवाष्टकमिति बुद्धौ सप्तदश संख्या /
गुणतत्त्वे पङ्क्तित्रयमिति षट्पञ्चाशतं पुराणि विदुः // 416
text_mt: then the octad of Mahādevas: thus in the intellect the number is seventeen. / In the Gunatattva are three rows; thus they know fifty-six cities. // 416

sanskrit_iast:
yadyapi guṇasāmyātmani mūle krodheśvarāṣṭakaṃ tathāpi dhiyi /
tacchodhitamiti gaṇanāṃ na punaḥ prāptaṃ pratiṣṭhāyām // 417
meaning:
यद्यपि गुणसाम्यात्मनि मूले क्रोधेश्वराष्टकं तथापि धियि /
तच्छोधितमिति गणनां न पुनः प्राप्तं प्रतिष्ठायाम् // 417
text_mt: Although the octad of Krodheśvaras is in the root [matter] characterized by equilibrium of the gunas, nevertheless / it is purified in the intellect; hence it is not counted again in Pratiṣṭhā. // 417

sanskrit_iast:
iti jalatattvānmūlaṃ tattvacaturviṃśatiḥ pratiṣṭhāyām /
ambādituṣṭivargastārādyāḥ siddhayo'ṇimādigaṇaḥ // 418
meaning:
इति जलतत्त्वान्मूलं तत्त्वचतुर्विंशतिः प्रतिष्ठायाम् /
अम्बादितुष्टिवर्गस्ताराद्याः सिद्धयोऽणिमादिगणः // 418
text_mt: Thus, from the water tattva to the root, twenty-four tattvas are in Pratiṣṭhā. / The group of satisfactions (tuṣṭis) beginning with Ambā, the accomplishments (siddhis) beginning with Tārā, the host of Aṇimā and the rest, // 418

sanskrit_iast:
guravo guruśiṣyā ṛṣivarga iḍādiśca vigrahāṣṭakayuk /
gandhādivikārapuraṃ buddhiguṇāṣṭakamahaṃkriyā viṣayaguṇāḥ // 419
meaning:
गुरवो गुरुशिष्या ऋषिवर्ग इडादिश्च विग्रहाष्टकयुक् /
गन्धादिविकारपुरं बुद्धिगुणाष्टकमहंक्रिया विषयगुणाः // 419
text_mt: the gurus, the guru-disciples, the group of sages, Iḍā and so forth endowed with an octad of bodies, / the city of the transformations of fragrance and so on, the octad of intellect-qualities, ego-making, the sense-qualities, // 419

sanskrit_iast:
kāmādisaptaviṃśakamāgantu tathā gaṇeśavidyeśamayau /
iti pāśeṣu puratrayamitthaṃ puruṣe'tra bhuvanaṣoḍaśakam // 420
meaning:
कामादिसप्तविंशकमागन्तु तथा गणेशविद्येशमयौ /
इति पाशेषु पुरत्रयमित्थं पुरुषेऽत्र भुवनषोडशकम् // 420
text_mt: the twenty-seven beginning with Kāma, the adventitious, as well as those consisting of Gaṇeśa and the Vidyeśvaras: / thus there is a triad of cities in the fetters; in this manner, there are sixteen worlds in Puruṣa. // 420

sanskrit_iast:
niyatau śaṅkaradaśakaṃ kāle śivadaśakamiti puradvitayam /
rāge suhṛṣṭabhuvanaṃ guruśiṣyapuraṃ ca vitkalāyugale // 421
meaning:
नियतौ शङ्करदशकं काले शिवदशकमिति पुरद्वितयम् /
रागे सुहृष्टभुवनं गुरुशिष्यपुरं च वित्कलायुगले // 421
text_mt: In Niyati there is the decad of Śaṅkaras, in Kāla the decad of Śivas: thus a pair of cities; / in Rāga is the world Suhṛṣṭa, and the city of Guru-śiṣyas in the pair of Vidyā and Kalā; // 421

sanskrit_iast:
bhuvanaṃ bhuvanaṃ niśi puṭapuratrayaṃ vākpuraṃ pramāṇapuram /
iti saptaviṃśatipurā vidyā puruṣāditattvasaptakayuk // 422
meaning:
भुवनं भुवनं निशि पुटपुरत्रयं वाक्पुरं प्रमाणपुरम् /
इति सप्तविंशतिपुरा विद्या पुरुषादितत्त्वसप्तकयुक् // 422
text_mt: one world [each]; in night (Māyā) the triad of Puṭa cities, the city of Vāc, and the city of Pramāṇa: / thus Vidyā comprises twenty-seven cities, joined with the heptad of tattvas beginning with Puruṣa. // 422

sanskrit_iast:
vāmeśarūpasūkṣmaṃ śuddhaṃ vidyātha śaktitejasvimitiḥ /
suviśuddhiśivau mokṣa dhuveṣisaṃbuddhasamayasauśivasaṃjñāḥ // 423
meaning:
वामेशरूपसूक्ष्मं शुद्धं विद्याथ शक्तितेजस्विमितिः /
सुविशुद्धिशिवौ मोक्ष धुवेषिसंबुद्धसमयसौशिवसंज्ञाः // 423
text_mt: Vāmeśa, Rūpa, Sūkṣma, Śuddha, Vidyā, Śaktitejas, Miti, / Suviśuddha, Śiva, Mokṣa, Dhuveśa, Saṃbuddha, Samaya, and Sauśiva: [these] are the names [of the worlds].

sanskrit_iast:
saptadaśapurā śāntā vidyeśasadāśivapuratritayayuktā /
bindvardhendunirodhyaḥ parasauśivamindhikādipurasauṣumne // 424
meaning:
सप्तदशपुरा शान्ता विद्येशसदाशिवपुरत्रितययुक्ता /
बिन्द्वर्धेन्दुनिरोध्यः परसौशिवमिन्धिकादिपुरसौषुम्ने // 424
text_mt: Śāntā has seventeen worlds, conjoined with the triad of the worlds of Vidyeśa and Sadāśiva; / Bindu, Ardhendu, Nirodhikā, Parasauśiva, and in the Suṣumnā the worlds Indhikā and the rest,

sanskrit_iast:
paranādo brahmabilaṃ sūkṣmādiyutordhvakuṇḍalī śaktiḥ /
vyāpivyomānantānāthānāśritapurāṇi pañca tataḥ // 425
meaning:
परनादो ब्रह्मबिलं सूक्ष्मादियुतोर्ध्वकुण्डली शक्तिः /
व्यापिव्योमानन्तानाथानाश्रितपुराणि पञ्च ततः // 425
text_mt: Paranāda, Brahmabila, the Śakti as Ūrdhvakuṇḍalī endowed with Sūkṣmā and the rest, / then the five worlds Vyāpin, Vyoman, Ananta, Anātha, and Anāśrita.

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaṣṭhaṃ ca paramamanāśritamatha samanābhuvanaṣoḍaśī yadi vā /
bindvāvaraṇaṃ parasauśivaṃ ca pañcendhikādibhuvanāni // 426
meaning:
षष्ठं च परममनाश्रितमथ समनाभुवनषोडशी यदि वा /
बिन्द्वावरणं परसौशिवं च पञ्चेन्धिकादिभुवनानि // 426
text_mt: And the sixth, supreme Anāśrita; or else there is a group of sixteen worlds of Samanā: / the envelopment of Bindu, Parasauśiva, the five worlds beginning with Indhikā,

sanskrit_iast:
sauṣumnaṃ brahmabilaṃ kuṇḍalinī vyāpipañcakaṃ samanā /
iti ṣoḍaśabhuvaneyaṃ tattvayugaṃ śāntyatītā syāt // 427
meaning:
सौषुम्नं ब्रह्मबिलं कुण्डलिनी व्यापिपञ्चकं समना /
इति षोडशभुवनेयं तत्त्वयुगं शान्त्यतीता स्यात् // 427
text_mt: the Suṣumnā, Brahmabila, Kuṇḍalinī, the group of five Vyāpins, and Samanā. / Thus, Śāntyatītā would comprise this set of sixteen worlds [and] two principles.

sanskrit_iast:
śrīmanmataṅgaśāstre ca kramo'yaṃ purapūgagaḥ /
kālāgnirnarakāḥ khābdhiyutaṃ mukhyatayā śatam // 428
meaning:
श्रीमन्मतङ्गशास्त्रे च क्रमोऽयं पुरपूगगः /
कालाग्निर्नरकाः खाब्धियुतं मुख्यतया शतम् // 428
text_mt: And in the venerable Mataṅga treatise, this sequence is followed regarding the collection of worlds: / Kālāgni, the hells, and principally one hundred and forty [worlds],

sanskrit_iast:
kūṣmāṇḍaḥ saptapātālī saptalokī maheśvaraḥ /
ityaṇḍamadhyaṃ tadbāhye śataṃ rudrā iti sthitāḥ // 429
meaning:
कूष्माण्डः सप्तपाताली सप्तलोकी महेश्वरः /
इत्यण्डमध्यं तद्बाह्ये शतं रुद्रा इति स्थिताः // 429
text_mt: Kūṣmāṇḍa, the seven netherworlds, the seven lokas, and Maheśvara; / thus is the interior of the egg, and outside it are established one hundred Rudras.

sanskrit_iast:
sthānānāṃ dviśatī bhūmiḥ saptapañcāśatā yutā /
pañcāṣṭakasya madhyāddvātriṃśadbhūtacatuṣṭaye // 430
meaning:
स्थानानां द्विशती भूमिः सप्तपञ्चाशता युता /
पञ्चाष्टकस्य मध्याद्द्वात्रिंशद्भूतचतुष्टये // 430
text_mt: The earth comprises two hundred and fifty-seven stations. / Out of the forty [stations], thirty-two are in the four elements;

sanskrit_iast:
tanmātreṣu ca pañca syurviśvedevāstato'ṣṭakam /
pañcamaṃ sendriye garve buddhau devāṣṭakaṃ guṇe // 431
meaning:
तन्मात्रेषु च पञ्च स्युर्विश्वेदेवास्ततोऽष्टकम् /
पञ्चमं सेन्द्रिये गर्वे बुद्धौ देवाष्टकं गुणे // 431
text_mt: and in the subtle elements there are five; next, the group of eight Viśvedevas / is fifth in the egoity endowed with sense faculties; in the intellect is the octad of gods; in the qualities,

sanskrit_iast:
yogāṣṭakaṃ krodhasaṃjñaṃ mūle kāle sanaiyate /
patadrugādyāścāṅguṣṭhamātrādyā rāgatattvagāḥ // 432
meaning:
योगाष्टकं क्रोधसंज्ञं मूले काले सनैयते /
पतद्रुगाद्याश्चाङ्गुष्ठमात्राद्या रागतत्त्वगाः // 432
text_mt: the octad of yoga called Krodha; in the root [matter] and in time, together with Niyati; / Patadruga and the rest, and Aṅguṣṭhamātra and the rest reside in the principle of attachment;

sanskrit_iast:
dvādaśaikaśivādyāḥ syurvidyāyāṃ kalane daśa /
vāmādyāstriśatī seyaṃ triparvaṇyabdhirasyayuk // 433
meaning:
द्वादशैकशिवाद्याः स्युर्विद्यायां कलने दश /
वामाद्यास्त्रिशती सेयं त्रिपर्वण्यब्धिरस्ययुक् // 433
text_mt: there are twelve, Ekāśiva and the rest; in Vidyā [there are] ten in Kalana, / Vāmā and the rest. This [group of] three hundred and sixty-four consists of three stages.

sanskrit_iast:
śaivāḥ kecidihānantāḥ śraikaṇṭhā iti saṃgrahaḥ /
yatra yadā parabhogān bubhukṣate tatra yojanaṃ kāryam // 434
meaning:
शैवाः केचिदिहानन्ताः श्रैकण्ठा इति संग्रहः /
यत्र यदा परभोगान् बुभुक्षते तत्र योजनं कार्यम् // 434
text_mt: Certain Śaivas here [reckon them] endless, while the followers of Śrīkaṇṭha make this summary. / Wherever [and] whenever one desires to experience higher enjoyments, unification is to be performed there,

sanskrit_iast:
śodhanamatha taddhānau śeṣaṃ tvantargataṃ kāryam /
ityāgamaṃ prathayituṃ darśitametadvikalpitaṃ tena // 435
meaning:
शोधनमथ तद्धानौ शेषं त्वन्तर्गतं कार्यम् /
इत्यागमं प्रथयितुं दर्शितमेतद्विकल्पितं तेन // 435
text_mt: or purification; upon abandoning that, however, the remainder is to be internalized. / Thus has this variation been shown by him in order to elucidate the scripture.

sanskrit_iast:
anye'pi bahuvikalpāḥ svadhiyācāryaiḥ samabhyūhyāḥ /
śrīpūrvaśāsane punaraṣṭādaśādhikaṃ śataṃ kathitam // 436
meaning:
अन्येऽपि बहुविकल्पाः स्वधियाचार्यैः समभ्यूह्याः /
श्रीपूर्वशासने पुनरष्टादशाधिकं शतं कथितम् // 436
text_mt: Other numerous variations also are to be deduced by the masters by their own intelligence. / In the venerable Pūrvaśāsana, however, one hundred and eighteen are stated.

sanskrit_iast:
tadiha pradhānamadhikaṃ saṃkṣepeṇocyate śodhyam /
kālāgniḥ kūṣmāṇḍo narakeśo hāṭako'tha bhūtalapaḥ // 437
meaning:
तदिह प्रधानमधिकं संक्षेपेणोच्यते शोध्यम् /
कालाग्निः कूष्माण्डो नरकेशो हाटकोऽथ भूतलपः // 437
text_mt: That which is primary and foremost to be purified is stated here in brief: / Kālāgni, Kūṣmāṇḍa, Narakeśa, Hāṭaka, then the protector of the earth-plane,

sanskrit_iast:
brahmā munilokeśo rudrāḥ pañcāntarālasthāḥ /
adhare'nantaḥ prācyāḥ kapālivahnyantanirṛtibalākhyāḥ // 438
meaning:
ब्रह्मा मुनिलोकेशो रुद्राः पञ्चान्तरालस्थाः /
अधरेऽनन्तः प्राच्याः कपालिवह्न्यन्तनिरृतिबलाख्याः // 438
text_mt: Brahmā, Munilokeśa, the five Rudras abiding in the intermediate space, / at the base Ananta, [then] the eastern [Rudras] named Kapālin, Vahnyanta, Nirṛti, and Bala,

sanskrit_iast:
laghunidhipatividyādhipaśambhūrdhvāntaṃ savīrabhadrapati /
ekādaśabhirbāhye brahmāṇḍaṃ pañcabhistathāntarikaiḥ // 439
meaning:
लघुनिधिपतिविद्याधिपशम्भूर्ध्वान्तं सवीरभद्रपति /
एकादशभिर्बाह्ये ब्रह्माण्डं पञ्चभिस्तथान्तरिकैः // 439
text_mt: Laghunidhipati, Vidyādhipa, Śambhu, and ending with the upward [regent], along with the lord Vīrabhadra; / by eleven [Rudras] on the outside, and likewise by five internal [Rudras], the egg of Brahmā [is filled].

sanskrit_iast:
iti ṣoḍaśapurametannivṛttikalayeha kalanīyam /
lakulīśabhārabhūtī diṇḍyāṣāḍhī ca puṣkaranimeṣau // 440
meaning:
इति षोडशपुरमेतन्निवृत्तिकलयेह कलनीयम् /
लकुलीशभारभूती दिण्ड्याषाढी च पुष्करनिमेषौ // 440
text_mt: Thus this sixteen-world [domain] is to be reckoned here in the Nivṛtti-kalā. / Lakulīśa, Bhārabhūti, Diṇḍin, Āṣāḍhin, Puṣkara, Nimeṣa,

sanskrit_iast:
prabhāsasureśāviti salile pratyātmakaṃ saparivāre /
bhairavakedāramahākālā madhyāmrajalpākhyāḥ // 441
meaning:
प्रभाससुरेशाविति सलिले प्रत्यात्मकं सपरिवारे /
भैरवकेदारमहाकाला मध्याम्रजल्पाख्याः // 441
text_mt: Prabhāsa, and Sureśa: thus [eight] in water, each individual along with their retinue; / Bhairava, Kedāra, Mahākāla, Madhyama, Jalpa,

sanskrit_iast:
śrīśailahariścandrāviti guhyāṣṭakamidaṃ mahasi /
bhīmendrāṭṭahāsavimalakanakhalanākhalakurusthitigayākhyāḥ // 442
meaning:
श्रीशैलहरिश्चन्द्राविति गुह्याष्टकमिदं महसि /
भीमेन्द्राट्टहासविमलकनखलनाखलकुरुस्थितिगयाख्याः // 442
text_mt: Śrīśaila, and Hariścandra: this secret octad is in fire; / Bhīma, Indra, Aṭṭahāsa, Vimala, Kanakhala, Nākala, Kurukṣetra, and Gayā:

sanskrit_iast:
atiguhyāṣṭakametanmaruti ca satanmātrake ca sākṣe ca /
sthāṇusuvarṇākhyau kila bhadro gokarṇako mahālayakaḥ // 443
meaning:
अतिगुह्याष्टकमेतन्मरुति च सतन्मात्रके च साक्षे च /
स्थाणुसुवर्णाख्यौ किल भद्रो गोकर्णको महालयकः // 443
text_mt: this most secret octad is in wind, in the subtle elements, and in the sense faculties; / Sthāṇu, Suvarṇa, Bhadra, Gokarṇa, Mahālaya,

sanskrit_iast:
avimuktarudrakoṭī vastrāpada ityadaḥ pavitraṃ khe /
sthūlasthūleśaśaṅkuśrutikālañjarāśca maṇḍalabhṛt // 444
meaning:
अविमुक्तरुद्रकोटी वस्त्रापद इत्यदः पवित्रं खे /
स्थूलस्थूलेशशङ्कुश्रुतिकालञ्जराश्च मण्डलभृत् // 444
text_mt: Avimukta, Rudrakoṭi, and Vastrāpada: this sacred [octad] is in space; / Sthūla, Sthūleśa, Śaṅkuśruti, Kālañjara, Maṇḍalabhṛt,

sanskrit_iast:
mākoṭāṇḍadvitayacchagalāṇḍā aṣṭakaṃ hyahaṅkāre /
anye'haṅkārāntastanmātrāṇīndriyāṇi cāpyāhuḥ // 445
meaning:
माकोटाण्डद्वितयच्छगलाण्डा अष्टकं ह्यहङ्कारे /
अन्येऽहङ्कारान्तस्तन्मात्राणीन्द्रियाणि चाप्याहुः // 445
text_mt: Mākoṭa, the pair of Aṇḍas, and Chagalaṇḍa: this octad is in egoity; / others say that up to egoity are the subtle elements and the sense faculties as well.

sanskrit_iast:
dhiyi yonyaṣṭakamuktaṃ prakṛtau yogāṣṭakaṃ kilākṛtaprabhṛti /
iti saptāṣṭakabhuvanā pratiṣṭhitiḥ salilato hi mūlāntā // 446
meaning:
धियि योन्यष्टकमुक्तं प्रकृतौ योगाष्टकं किलाकृतप्रभृति /
इति सप्ताष्टकभुवना प्रतिष्ठितिः सलिलतो हि मूलान्ता // 446
text_mt: In the intellect the octad of wombs is taught, and in Prakṛti the octad of yoga beginning with Akṛta; / thus Pratiṣṭhā consists of fifty-six worlds, from water up to the root [matter].

sanskrit_iast:
nari vāmo bhīmograu bhaveśavīrāḥ pracaṇḍagaurīśau /
ajasānantaikaśivau vidyāyāṃ krodhacaṇḍayugmaṃ syāt // 447
meaning:
नरि वामो भीमोग्रौ भवेशवीराः प्रचण्डगौरीशौ /
अजसानन्तैकशिवौ विद्यायां क्रोधचण्डयुग्मं स्यात् // 447
text_mt: In the Puruṣa: Vāma, Bhīma, Ugra, Bhaveśa, Vīra, Pracaṇḍa, Gaurīśa, / Aja, Sānanta, and Ekaśiva; in Vidyā there is the pair Krodha and Caṇḍa,

sanskrit_iast:
saṃvarto jyotiratho kalāniyatyāṃ ca sūrapañcāntau /
vīraśikhīśaśrīkaṇṭhasaṃjñametattrayaṃ ca kāle syāt // 448
meaning:
संवर्तो ज्योतिरथो कलानियत्यां च सूरपञ्चान्तौ /
वीरशिखीशश्रीकण्ठसंज्ञमेतत्त्रयं च काले स्यात् // 448
text_mt: Saṃvarta, and Jyotis; then in Kalā and Niyati, Sūrapañcānta; / Vīra, Śikhīśa, and Śrīkaṇṭha: this triad is in Kāla;

sanskrit_iast:
samahātejā vāmo bhavodbhavaścaikapiṅgaleśānau /
bhuvaneśapuraḥsarakāvaṅguṣṭha ime niśi sthitā hyaṣṭau // 449
meaning:
समहातेजा वामो भवोद्भवश्चैकपिङ्गलेशानौ /
भुवनेशपुरःसरकावङ्गुष्ठ इमे निशि स्थिता ह्यष्टौ // 449
text_mt: along with Mahātejas: Vāma, Bhavodbhava, Ekapiṅgala, Īśāna, / preceded by Bhuvaneśa, and Aṅguṣṭha: these eight reside in night (Māyā).

sanskrit_iast:
aṣṭāviṃśatibhuvanā vidyā puruṣānniśāntamiyam /
hālāhalarudrakrudambikāghorikāḥ savāmāḥ syuḥ // 450
meaning:
अष्टाविंशतिभुवना विद्या पुरुषान्निशान्तमियम् /
हालाहलरुद्रक्रुदम्बिकाघोरिकाः सवामाः स्युः // 450
text_mt: This Vidyā[-kalā] consists of twenty-eight worlds, extending from Puruṣa to the end of night (Māyā); / Hālāhala, Rudrakrud, Ambikā, and Aghorikā, along with Vāmā,

sanskrit_iast:
vidyāyāṃ vidyeśāstvaṣṭāvīśe sadāśive pañca /
vāmā jyeṣṭhā raudrī śaktiḥ sakalā ca śontayam // 451
meaning:
विद्यायां विद्येशास्त्वष्टावीशे सदाशिवे पञ्च /
वामा ज्येष्ठा रौद्री शक्तिः सकला च शोन्तयम् // 451
text_mt: are in Vidyā; the eight Vidyeśas are in Īśa; in Sadāśiva are five: / Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, Raudrī, Śakti, and Sakalā; [this] is the Śāntā-kalā.

sanskrit_iast:
aṣṭādaśa bhuvanā syāt śāntyatītā tvabhuvanaiva /
iti deśādhvavibhāgaḥ kathitaḥ śrīśambhunā samādiṣṭaḥ // 452
meaning:
अष्टादश भुवना स्यात् शान्त्यतीता त्वभुवनैव /
इति देशाध्वविभागः कथितः श्रीशम्भुना समादिष्टः // 452
text_mt: It has eighteen worlds, whereas Śāntyatītā is indeed without worlds. / Thus has been explained the division of the spatial path as commanded by the venerable Śambhu.

sanskrit_iast: atha tattvapravibhāgo vistarataḥ kathyate kramaprāptaḥ // 1
meaning: अथ तत्त्वप्रविभागो विस्तरतः कथ्यते क्रमप्राप्तः // 1
text_mt: Now the classification of principles, arriving in due order, is explained in detail. // 1b
title: Tattvaprakāśana

sanskrit_iast:
yānyuktāni purāṇyamūni vividhaibhadairyadeṣvanvitaṃ rūpaṃ bhāti paraṃ prakāśaniviḍaṃ devaḥ sa ekaḥ śivaḥ /
tatsvātantryarasātpunaḥ śivapadādbhede vibhāte paraṃ yadrūpaṃ bahudhānugāmi tadidaṃ tattvaṃ vibhoḥ śāsane // 2
meaning:
यान्युक्तानि पुराण्यमूनि विविधैभदैर्यदेष्वन्वितं रूपं भाति परं प्रकाशनिविडं देवः स एकः शिवः /
तत्स्वातन्त्र्यरसात्पुनः शिवपदाद्भेदे विभाते परं यद्रूपं बहुधानुगामि तदिदं तत्त्वं विभोः शासने // 2
text_mt: Whatever these aforesaid worlds may be, that inherent, supreme form full of compact luminosity which shines within them is the one God, Śiva. / Furthermore, due to the aesthetic relish of His absolute autonomy, when difference from the state of Śiva shines forth, whatever supreme form runs through the many is a principle in the teaching of the All-pervading Lord. // 2

sanskrit_iast:
tathāhi kālasadanādvīrabhadrapurāntagam /
dhṛtikāṭhinyagarimādyavabhāsāddharātmatā // 3
meaning:
तथाहि कालसदनाद्वीरभद्रपुरान्तगम् /
धृतिकाठिन्यगरिमाद्यवभासाद्धरात्मता // 3
text_mt: To explain: from the abode of Kāla up to the world of Vīrabhadra, / the nature of the earth [principle] exists due to the appearance of support, hardness, heaviness, and the like. // 3

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ jalāditattveṣu vācyaṃ yāvatsadāśive /
svasminkārye'tha dharmaughe yadvāpi svasadṛgguṇe // 4
meaning:
एवं जलादितत्त्वेषु वाच्यं यावत्सदाशिवे /
स्वस्मिन्कार्येऽथ धर्मौघे यद्वापि स्वसदृग्गुणे // 4
text_mt: In the same manner, [the common nature] is to be declared in the principles beginning with water up to Sadāśiva. / Whatever exists in its own effect, or in a collection of properties, or in an attribute similar to itself, // 4

sanskrit_iast:
āste sāmānyakalpena tananādvyāptṛbhāvataḥ /
tattattvaṃ kramaśaḥ pṛthvīpradhānaṃ puṃśivādayaḥ // 5
meaning:
आस्ते सामान्यकल्पेन तननाद्व्याप्तृभावतः /
तत्तत्त्वं क्रमशः पृथ्वीप्रधानं पुंशिवादयः // 5
text_mt: by way of a general universal, by virtue of extending and pervading, / that is a principle: in order, earth, Pradhāna, Puruṣa, Śiva, and so on. // 5

sanskrit_iast:
dehānāṃ bhuvanānāṃ ca na prasaṅgastato bhavet /
śrīmanmataṅgaśāstrādau taduktaṃ parameśinā // 6
meaning:
देहानां भुवनानां च न प्रसङ्गस्ततो भवेत् /
श्रीमन्मतङ्गशास्त्रादौ तदुक्तं परमेशिना // 6
text_mt: Consequently, an endless proliferation of bodies and worlds does not occur; / that has been stated by the Supreme Lord in the venerable Mataṅga treatise and elsewhere. // 6

sanskrit_iast:
tatraiṣāṃ darśyate dṛṣṭaḥ siddhayogīśvarīmate /
kāryakāraṇabhāvo yaḥ śivecchāparikalpitaḥ // 7
meaning:
तत्रैषां दर्श्यते दृष्टः सिद्धयोगीश्वरीमते /
कार्यकारणभावो यः शिवेच्छापरिकल्पितः // 7
text_mt: There, the relation of cause and effect observed among these in the doctrine of the Siddhayogīśvarī, / which is fashioned by Śiva's will, is shown: // 7

sanskrit_iast:
vastutaḥ sarvabhāvānāṃ karteśānaḥ paraḥ śivaḥ /
asvatantrasya kartṛtvaṃ nahi jātūpapadyate // 8
meaning:
वस्तुतः सर्वभावानां कर्तेशानः परः शिवः /
अस्वतन्त्रस्य कर्तृत्वं नहि जातूपपद्यते // 8
text_mt: In reality, the supreme Śiva, Īśāna, is the agent of all entities; / for agency never belongs to what lacks autonomy. // 8

sanskrit_iast:
svatantratā ca cinmātravapuṣaḥ parameśituḥ /
svatantraṃ ca jaḍaṃ ceti tadanyonyaṃ virudhyate // 9
meaning:
स्वतन्त्रता च चिन्मात्रवपुषः परमेशितुः /
स्वतन्त्रं च जडं चेति तदन्योन्यं विरुध्यते // 9
text_mt: And autonomy belongs [only] to the Supreme Lord whose form is pure consciousness; / for 'autonomous' and 'insentient' are mutually contradictory. // 9

sanskrit_iast:
jāḍyaṃ pramātṛtantratvaṃ svātmasiddhimapi prati /
na kartṛtvādṛte cānyat kāraṇatvaṃ hi labhyate // 10
meaning:
जाड्यं प्रमातृतन्त्रत्वं स्वात्मसिद्धिमपि प्रति /
न कर्तृत्वादृते चान्यत् कारणत्वं हि लभ्यते // 10
text_mt: Insentience is dependence on a conscious subject even for the establishment of its own existence; / and causality is indeed never found apart from agency. // 10

sanskrit_iast:
tasminsati hi tadbhāva ityapekṣaikajīvitam /
nirapekṣeṣu bhāveṣu svātmaniṣṭhatayā katham // 11
meaning:
तस्मिन्सति हि तद्भाव इत्यपेक्षैकजीवितम् /
निरपेक्षेषु भावेषु स्वात्मनिष्ठतया कथम् // 11
text_mt: The notion 'when that exists, this arises' has its very life solely in mutual dependence; / how could it apply to independent entities that rest in themselves? // 11

sanskrit_iast:
sa pūrvamatha paścātsa iti cetpūrvapaścimau /
svabhāve'natiriktau cetsama ityavaśiṣyate // 12
meaning:
स पूर्वमथ पश्चात्स इति चेत्पूर्वपश्चिमौ /
स्वभावेऽनतिरिक्तौ चेत्सम इत्यवशिष्यते // 12
text_mt: If it is said, 'that is prior and then this is posterior,' / if the prior and posterior are not distinct from intrinsic nature, only identity remains. // 12

sanskrit_iast:
bījamaṅkura ityasmin satattve hetutadvatoḥ /
ghaṭaḥ paṭaśceti bhavet kāryakāraṇatā na kim // 13
meaning:
बीजमङ्कुर इत्यस्मिन् सतत्त्वे हेतुतद्वतोः /
घटः पटश्चेति भवेत् कार्यकारणता न किम् // 13
text_mt:
If the nature of cause and effect were [nothing more than] ‘seed’ and ‘sprout’,
why would there not be a relation of cause and effect [just as well] between ‘pot’ and ‘cloth’? // 13

sanskrit_iast:
bījamaṅkurapatrāditayā pariṇameta cet /
atatsvabhāvavapuṣaḥ sa svabhāvo na yujyate // 14
meaning:
बीजमङ्कुरपत्रादितया परिणमेत चेत् /
अतत्स्वभाववपुषः स स्वभावो न युज्यते // 14
text_mt:
If it is argued that the seed transforms as the sprout, leaf, and so on,
such a nature is not appropriate for that whose form is not of that nature. // 14

sanskrit_iast:
sa tatsvabhāva iti cet tarhi bījāṅkurā nije /
tāvatyeva na viśrāntau tadanyātyantasaṃbhavāt // 15
meaning:
स तत्स्वभाव इति चेत् तर्हि बीजाङ्कुरा निजे /
तावत्येव न विश्रान्तौ तदन्यात्यन्तसंभवात् // 15
text_mt:
If [it is replied that] it has that nature, then seed and sprout do not
rest entirely in themselves, since what is other than them completely exists [there]. // 15

sanskrit_iast:
tataśca citrākāro'sau tāvānkaścitprasajyate /
astu cet na jaḍe'nyonyaviruddhākārasaṃbhavaḥ // 16
meaning:
ततश्च चित्राकारोऽसौ तावान्कश्चित्प्रसज्यते /
अस्तु चेत् न जडेऽन्योन्यविरुद्धाकारसंभवः // 16
text_mt:
Consequently, this entity would absurdly have to possess such a manifold form.
If [they say], ‘Let it be so,’ no: mutually contradictory forms cannot exist in an insentient entity. // 16

sanskrit_iast:
krameṇa citrākāro'stu jaḍaḥ kiṃ nu viruddhyate /
kramo'kramo vā bhāvasya na svarūpādhiko bhavet // 17
meaning:
क्रमेण चित्राकारोऽस्तु जडः किं नु विरुद्ध्यते /
क्रमोऽक्रमो वा भावस्य न स्वरूपाधिको भवेत् // 17
text_mt:
If [they say], ‘Let the insentient [seed] have a manifold form in succession; what contradiction is there?’—
succession or non-succession cannot be something additional to the entity's own nature. // 17

sanskrit_iast:
tathopalambhamātraṃ tau upalambhaśca kiṃ tathā /
upalabdhāpi vijñānasvabhāvo yo'sya so'pi hi // 18
meaning:
तथोपलम्भमात्रं तौ उपलम्भश्च किं तथा /
उपलब्धापि विज्ञानस्वभावो योऽस्य सोऽपि हि // 18
text_mt:
Those two are merely perception appearing thus; and why should perception be thus?
Indeed, the perceiver whose nature is consciousness—he too [would be manifold], // 18

sanskrit_iast:
kramopalambharūpatvāt krameṇopalabheta cet /
tasya tarhi kramaḥ ko'sau tadanyānupalambhataḥ // 19
meaning:
क्रमोपलम्भरूपत्वात् क्रमेणोपलभेत चेत् /
तस्य तर्हि क्रमः कोऽसौ तदन्यानुपलम्भतः // 19
text_mt:
if he perceives in succession because his nature is the perception of succession.
Then what is that succession of his, since nothing other than that is perceived? // 19

sanskrit_iast:
svabhāva iti cennāsau svarūpādadhiko bhavet /
svarūpānadhikasyāpi kramasya svasvabhāvataḥ // 20
meaning:
स्वभाव इति चेन्नासौ स्वरूपादधिको भवेत् /
स्वरूपानधिकस्यापि क्रमस्य स्वस्वभावतः // 20
text_mt:
If [they say], ‘It is [its] intrinsic nature,’ no; it cannot be additional to its own nature.
If [it is replied that] succession, though not additional to its own nature, arises from its own nature, // 20

sanskrit_iast:
svātantryādbhāsanaṃ syāccet kimanyadbrūmahe vayam /
itthaṃ śrīśiva evaikaḥ karteti paribhāṣyate // 21
meaning:
स्वातन्त्र्याद्भासनं स्याच्चेत् किमन्यद्ब्रूमहे वयम् /
इत्थं श्रीशिव एवैकः कर्तेति परिभाष्यते // 21
text_mt:
and that it shines forth through absolute autonomy, then what else are we saying?
Thus, glorious Śiva alone is designated as the [sole] agent. // 21

sanskrit_iast:
kartṛtvaṃ caitadetasya tathāmātrāvabhāsanam /
tathāvabhāsanaṃ cāsti kāryakāraṇabhāvagam // 22
meaning:
कर्तृत्वं चैतदेतस्य तथामात्रावभासनम् /
तथावभासनं चास्ति कार्यकारणभावगम् // 22
text_mt:
And this agency of his is nothing other than shining forth in such a manner;
and such a shining forth occurs as the relation of cause and effect. // 22

sanskrit_iast:
yathā hi ghaṭasāhityaṃ paṭasyāpyavabhāsate /
tathā ghaṭānantaratā kiṃ tu sā niyamojjhitā // 23
meaning:
यथा हि घटसाहित्यं पटस्याप्यवभासते /
तथा घटानन्तरता किं तु सा नियमोज्झिता // 23
text_mt:
For just as the cloth's being together with the pot shines forth,
so does its succeeding the pot; but that [succession] is devoid of regular invariable rule. // 23

sanskrit_iast:
ato yanniyamenaiva yasmādābhātyanantaram /
tattasya kāraṇaṃ brūmaḥ sati rūpānvaye'dhike // 24
meaning:
अतो यन्नियमेनैव यस्मादाभात्यनन्तरम् /
तत्तस्य कारणं ब्रूमः सति रूपान्वयेऽधिके // 24
text_mt:
Therefore, when a thing invariably shines forth immediately after another,
we call that [first] thing its cause, when there is additionally an experiential continuity of form. // 24

sanskrit_iast:
niyamaśca tathārūpabhāsanāmātrasārakaḥ /
bījādaṅkura ityevaṃ bhāsanaṃ nahi sarvadā // 25
meaning:
नियमश्च तथारूपभासनामात्रसारकः /
बीजादङ्कुर इत्येवं भासनं नहि सर्वदा // 25
text_mt:
And the regular invariable rule has as its sole essence the mere shining forth of such a form;
for the shining forth as ‘the sprout is from the seed’ does not occur always, // 25

sanskrit_iast:
yogīcchānantarodbhūtatathābhūtāṅkuro yataḥ /
iṣṭe tathāvidhākāre niyamo bhāsate yataḥ // 26
meaning:
योगीच्छानन्तरोद्भूततथाभूताङ्कुरो यतः /
इष्टे तथाविधाकारे नियमो भासते यतः // 26
text_mt:
since such a sprout arises immediately after the will of a yogin;
for a regular invariable rule shines forth only when such a specific form is desired. // 26

sanskrit_iast:
svapne ghaṭapaṭādīnāṃ hetutadvatsvabhāvatā /
bhāsate niyamenaiva bādhāśūnyena tāvati // 27
meaning:
स्वप्ने घटपटादीनां हेतुतद्वत्स्वभावता /
भासते नियमेनैव बाधाशून्येन तावति // 27
text_mt:
In a dream, the causal nature of pot, cloth, and so forth
shines forth with regular invariable rule, free from contradiction in that realm. // 27

sanskrit_iast:
tato yāvati yādrūpyānniyamo bādhavarjitaḥ /
bhāti tāvati tādrūpyāddṛḍhahetuphalātmatā // 28
meaning:
ततो यावति याद्रूप्यान्नियमो बाधवर्जितः /
भाति तावति ताद्रूप्याद्दृढहेतुफलात्मता // 28
text_mt:
Therefore, to whatever extent and in whatever form a regular invariable rule devoid of sublation
shines forth, to that extent and in that form an unwavering relation of cause and effect exists. // 28

sanskrit_iast:
tathābhūte ca niyame hetutadvattvakāriṇi /
vastutaścinmayasyaiva hetutā taddhi sarvagam // 29
meaning:
तथाभूते च नियमे हेतुतद्वत्त्वकारिणि /
वस्तुतश्चिन्मयस्यैव हेतुता तद्धि सर्वगम् // 29
text_mt:
And when such an invariable rule establishes the status of cause and effect,
in reality the causal nature belongs only to that which consists of consciousness, for that pervades all. // 29

sanskrit_iast:
ata eva ghaṭodbhūtau sāmagrī heturucyate /
sāmagrī ca samagrāṇāṃ yadyekaṃ neṣyate vapuḥ // 30
meaning:
अत एव घटोद्भूतौ सामग्री हेतुरुच्यते /
सामग्री च समग्राणां यद्येकं नेष्यते वपुः // 30
text_mt:
Precisely for this reason, the totality of causal factors is called the cause in the production of a pot;
and if one does not accept that the totality of factors has a single form, // 30

sanskrit_iast:
hetubhedānna bhedaḥ syāt phale taccāsamañjasam /
yadyasyānuvidhatte tāmanvayavyatirekitām // 31
meaning:
हेतुभेदान्न भेदः स्यात् फले तच्चासमञ्जसम् /
यद्यस्यानुविधत्ते तामन्वयव्यतिरेकिताम् // 31
text_mt:
then diversity in the cause would not produce diversity in the effect, and that is absurd.
If [it is said that] whatever conforms to positive and negative concomitance with respect to a thing // 31

sanskrit_iast:
tattasya hetu cetso'yaṃ kuṇṭhatarko na naḥ priyaḥ /
samagrāśca yathā daṇḍasūtracakrakarādayaḥ // 32
meaning:
तत्तस्य हेतु चेत्सोऽयं कुण्ठतर्को न नः प्रियः /
समग्राश्च यथा दण्डसूत्रचक्रकरादयः // 32
text_mt:
is its cause, we do not favor this blunt reasoning.
And just as the complete collection—the stick, string, wheel, hands, and so on—[is the cause], // 32

sanskrit_iast:
dūrāśca bhāvinaścetthaṃ hetutveneti manmahe /
yadi tatra bhavenmerurbhaviṣyanvāpi kaścana // 33
meaning:
दूराश्च भाविनश्चेत्थं हेतुत्वेनेति मन्महे /
यदि तत्र भवेन्मेरुर्भविष्यन्वापि कश्चन // 33
text_mt:
we consider that distant and future things are causes in this manner as well.
If Mount Meru, or something that will exist in the future, were present there, // 33

sanskrit_iast:
na jāyeta ghaṭo nūnaṃ tatpratyūhavyapohitaḥ /
yathā ca cakraṃ niyate deśe kāle ca hetutām // 34
meaning:
न जायेत घटो नूनं तत्प्रत्यूहव्यपोहितः /
यथा च चक्रं नियते देशे काले च हेतुताम् // 34
text_mt:
the pot certainly would not be produced, being obstructed by that impediment.
And just as the wheel attains the status of cause in a determined space and time, // 34

sanskrit_iast:
yāti karkisumervādyāstadvatsvasthāvadhi sthitāḥ /
tathā ca teṣāṃ hetunāṃ saṃyojanaviyojane // 35
meaning:
याति कर्किसुमेर्वाद्यास्तद्वत्स्वस्थावधि स्थिताः /
तथा च तेषां हेतुनां संयोजनवियोजने // 35
text_mt:
so do Cancer, Mount Sumeru, and the like, situated within their own limits;
and likewise in the bringing together and separating of these causes // 24

sanskrit_iast:
niyate śiva evaikaḥ svatantraḥ kartṛtāmiyāt /
kumbhakārasya yā saṃvit cakradaṇḍādiyojane // 36
meaning:
नियते शिव एवैकः स्वतन्त्रः कर्तृतामियात् /
कुम्भकारस्य या संवित् चक्रदण्डादियोजने // 36
text_mt:
in a determined manner, autonomous Śiva alone attains agency.
The consciousness of the potter in bringing together the wheel, stick, and so forth // 36

sanskrit_iast:
śiva eva hi sā yasmāt saṃvidaḥ kā viśiṣṭatā /
kaumbhakārī tu saṃvittiravacchedāvabhāsanāt // 37
meaning:
शिव एव हि सा यस्मात् संविदः का विशिष्टता /
कौम्भकारी तु संवित्तिरवच्छेदावभासनात् // 37
text_mt:
is indeed Śiva alone, because what distinction is there in consciousness?
But the potter's consciousness, because it appears delimited, // 37

sanskrit_iast:
bhinnakalpā yadi kṣepyā daṇḍacakrādimadhyataḥ /
tasmādekaikanirmāṇe śivo viśvaikavigrahaḥ // 38
meaning:
भिन्नकल्पा यदि क्षेप्या दण्डचक्रादिमध्यतः /
तस्मादेकैकनिर्माणे शिवो विश्वैकविग्रहः // 38
text_mt:
is considered distinct, if it must be counted along with the stick, wheel, and so on.
Therefore, in the fashioning of each individual thing, Śiva, whose sole body is the universe, // 38

sanskrit_iast:
karteti puṃsaḥ kartṛtvābhimāno'pi vibhoḥ kṛtiḥ /
ata eva tathābhānaparamārthatayā sthiteḥ // 39
meaning:
कर्तेति पुंसः कर्तृत्वाभिमानोऽपि विभोः कृतिः /
अत एव तथाभानपरमार्थतया स्थितेः // 39
text_mt:
is the agent; even the bound soul's conceit of agency is the work of the all-pervading Lord.
For this very reason, since reality consists in shining forth in that manner, // 39

sanskrit_iast:
kāryakāraṇabhāvasya loke śāstre ca citratā /
māyāto'vyaktakalayoriti rauravasaṃgrahe // 40
meaning:
कार्यकारणभावस्य लोके शास्त्रे च चित्रता /
मायातोऽव्यक्तकलयोरिति रौरवसंग्रहे // 40
text_mt:
there is variety in the relation of cause and effect both in worldly experience and in scripture.
In the Rauravasaṃgraha [it is taught] that the unmanifest and Kalā [arise] from Māyā; // 40

sanskrit_iast:
śrīpūrve tu kalātattvādavyaktamiti kathyate /
tata eva niśākhyānātkalībhūtādaliṅgakam // 41
meaning:
श्रीपूर्वे तु कलातत्त्वादव्यक्तमिति कथ्यते /
तत एव निशाख्यानात्कलीभूतादलिङ्गकम् // 41
text_mt:
in the Śrīpūrva, however, it is stated that the unmanifest [arises] from the principle of Kalā.
Therefore, the explanation that ‘the markless [unmanifest] arises from the night [Māyā] that has become fractional’ // 41

sanskrit_iast:
iti vyākhyāsmadukte'sminsati nyāye'tiniṣphalā /
loke ca gomayātkīṭāt saṃkalpātsvapnataḥ smṛteḥ // 42
meaning:
इति व्याख्यास्मदुक्तेऽस्मिन्सति न्यायेऽतिनिष्फला /
लोके च गोमयात्कीटात् संकल्पात्स्वप्नतः स्मृतेः // 42
text_mt:
is completely pointless once this principle stated by us is accepted.
And in worldly experience, a scorpion [is born] from cow dung, from an insect, from conceptual imagination, from a dream, from memory, // 42

sanskrit_iast:
yogīcchāto dravyamantraprabhāvādeśca vṛścikaḥ /
anya eva sa cet kāmaṃ kutaścitsvaviśeṣataḥ // 43
meaning:
योगीच्छातो द्रव्यमन्त्रप्रभावादेश्च वृश्चिकः /
अन्य एव स चेत् कामं कुतश्चित्स्वविशेषतः // 43
text_mt:
from the will of a yogin, from the power of substances and mantras, and so forth.
If it is argued that it is entirely different due to some specific difference of its own, so be it, // 43

sanskrit_iast:
sa tu sarvatra tulyastatparāmarśaikyamasti tu /
tata eva svarūpe'pi krame'pyanyādṛśī sthitiḥ // 44
meaning:
स तु सर्वत्र तुल्यस्तत्परामर्शैक्यमस्ति तु /
तत एव स्वरूपेऽपि क्रमेऽप्यन्यादृशी स्थितिः // 44
text_mt:
yet it is equal everywhere, for there is unity in the reflective awareness of it.
Therefore, even with regard to essence and succession, a diverse condition // 44

sanskrit_iast:
śāstreṣu yujyate citrāt tathābhāvasvabhāvataḥ /
puṃrāgavitkalākālamāyā jñānottare kramāt // 45
meaning:
शास्त्रेषु युज्यते चित्रात् तथाभावस्वभावतः /
पुंरागवित्कलाकालमाया ज्ञानोत्तरे क्रमात् // 45
text_mt:
is appropriate in the scriptures, because of the manifold nature of reality shining thus.
In the Jñānottara, the order is Puruṣa, Rāga, Vidyā, Kalā, Kāla, and Māyā; // 45

sanskrit_iast:
niyatirnāsti vairiñce kalordhve niyatiḥ śratā /
puṃrāgavittrayādūrdhvaṃ kalāniyatisaṃpuṭam // 46
meaning:
नियतिर्नास्ति वैरिञ्चे कलोर्ध्वे नियतिः श्रता /
पुंरागवित्त्रयादूर्ध्वं कलानियतिसंपुटम् // 46
text_mt:
in the Vairiñca, Niyati is absent, [or rather] Niyati is taught above Kalā;
above the triad of Puruṣa, Rāga, and Vidyā is the pair of Kalā and Niyati, // 46

sanskrit_iast:
kālo māyeti kathitaḥ kramaḥ kiraṇaśāstragaḥ /
pumānniyatyā kālaśca rāgavidyākalānvitaḥ // 47
meaning:
कालो मायेति कथितः क्रमः किरणशास्त्रगः /
पुमान्नियत्या कालश्च रागविद्याकलान्वितः // 47
text_mt:
then Kāla and Māyā—this order is declared in the Kiraṇaśāstra;
Puruṣa, accompanied by Niyati, and Kāla endowed with Rāga, Vidyā, and Kalā— // 47

sanskrit_iast:
ityeṣa krama uddiṣṭo mātaṅge pārameśvare /
kāryakāraṇabhāvīye tattve itthaṃ vyavasthite // 48
meaning:
इत्येष क्रम उद्दिष्टो मातङ्गे पारमेश्वरे /
कार्यकारणभावीये तत्त्वे इत्थं व्यवस्थिते // 48
text_mt:
this is the order taught in the supreme lord's Mātaṅga.
The principle governing the relation of cause and effect being thus established, // 48

sanskrit_iast:
śrīpūrvaśāstre kathitāṃ vacmaḥ kāraṇakalpanām /
śivaḥ svatantradṛgrūpaḥ pañcaśaktisunirbharaḥ // 49
meaning:
श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे कथितां वच्मः कारणकल्पनाम् /
शिवः स्वतन्त्रदृग्रूपः पञ्चशक्तिसुनिर्भरः // 49
text_mt:
we now explain the scheme of causes taught in the Śrīpūrva scripture.
Śiva, whose nature is autonomous perception, completely replete with the five powers, // 49

sanskrit_iast:
svātantryabhāsitabhidā pañcadhā pravibhajyate /
cidānandeṣaṇājñānakriyāṇāṃ susphuṭatvataḥ // 50
meaning:
स्वातन्त्र्यभासितभिदा पञ्चधा प्रविभज्यते /
चिदानन्देषणाज्ञानक्रियाणां सुस्फुटत्वतः // 50
text_mt:
is divided fivefold through the difference manifested by his absolute autonomy,
because consciousness, bliss, will, knowledge, and action are clearly evident. // 50

sanskrit_iast:
śivaśaktisadeśānavidyākhyaṃ tattvapañcakam /
ekaikatrāpi tattve'smin sarvaśaktisunirbhare // 51
meaning:
शिवशक्तिसदेशानविद्याख्यं तत्त्वपञ्चकम् /
एकैकत्रापि तत्त्वेऽस्मिन् सर्वशक्तिसुनिर्भरे // 51
text_mt:
These are the five principles named Śiva, Śakti, Sadāśiva, Īśvara, and Vidyā.
Even in each single one of these principles, though completely replete with all powers, // 51

sanskrit_iast:
tattatprādhānyayogena sa sa bhedo nirūpyate /
tathāhi svasvatantratvaparipūrṇatayā vibhuḥ // 52
meaning:
तत्तत्प्राधान्ययोगेन स स भेदो निरूप्यते /
तथाहि स्वस्वतन्त्रत्वपरिपूर्णतया विभुः // 52
text_mt:
this or that distinction is determined by the predominance of this or that [power].
For the all-pervading Lord, through the perfection of his own absolute autonomy, // 52

sanskrit_iast:
niḥsaṃkhyairbahubhī rūpairbhātyavacchedavarjanāt /
śāṃbhavāḥ śaktijā mantramaheśā mantranāyakāh // 53
meaning:
निःसंख्यैर्बहुभी रूपैर्भात्यवच्छेदवर्जनात् /
शांभवाः शक्तिजा मन्त्रमहेशा मन्त्रनायकाह् // 53
text_mt:
shines forth in countless, manifold forms because he is devoid of delimitation:
the Śāmbhavas, those born of Śakti, the Mantramaheśas, the Mantranāyakas, // 53

sanskrit_iast:
mantrā iti viśuddhāḥ syuramī pañca gaṇāḥ kramāt /
svasminsvasmin gaṇe bhāti yadyadrūpaṃ samanvayi // 54
meaning:
मन्त्रा इति विशुद्धाः स्युरमी पञ्च गणाः क्रमात् /
स्वस्मिन्स्वस्मिन् गणे भाति यद्यद्रूपं समन्वयि // 54
text_mt:
and the Mantras—these five groups are pure in succession.
Whatever conforming form shines forth within its respective group, // 54

sanskrit_iast:
tadeṣu tattvamityuktaṃ kālāgnyāderdharādivat /
tena yatprāhurākhyānasādṛśyena viḍambitāḥ // 55
meaning:
तदेषु तत्त्वमित्युक्तं कालाग्न्यादेर्धरादिवत् /
तेन यत्प्राहुराख्यानसादृश्येन विडम्बिताः // 55
text_mt:
that is called a principle among these, just as the earth and so forth [comprehend] Kālāgni and the rest.
Therefore, as for what those say who, deceived by a superficial similarity of names, // 55

sanskrit_iast:
gurūpāsāṃ vinaivāttapustakābhīṣṭadṛṣṭayaḥ /
brahmā nivṛttyadhipatiḥ pṛthaktattvaṃ na gaṇyate // 56
meaning:
गुरूपासां विनैवात्तपुस्तकाभीष्टदृष्टयः /
ब्रह्मा निवृत्त्यधिपतिः पृथक्तत्त्वं न गण्यते // 56
text_mt:
have formed their favorite views from books without serving a guru:
‘Brahmā, the ruler of Nivṛtti, is not counted as a separate principle; // 56

sanskrit_iast:
sadāśivādyāstu pṛthag gaṇyanta iti ko nayaḥ /
brahmaviṣṇuhareśānasuśivānāśritātmani // 57
meaning:
सदाशिवाद्यास्तु पृथग् गण्यन्त इति को नयः /
ब्रह्मविष्णुहरेशानसुशिवानाश्रितात्मनि // 57
text_mt:
what principle is it, then, that Sadāśiva and the others are counted separately?
In the hexad called "causes," consisting of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Hara, Īśāna, Suśiva, and the Unattached, // 57

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaṭke kāraṇasaṃjñe'rdhajaratīyamiyaṃ kutaḥ /
iti tanmūlato dhvastaṃ gaṇitaṃ nahi kāraṇam // 58
meaning:
षट्के कारणसंज्ञेऽर्धजरतीयमियं कुतः /
इति तन्मूलतो ध्वस्तं गणितं नहि कारणम् // 58
text_mt:
whence this half-an-old-woman fallacy?’—
that [objection] is refuted at its very root, for a cause is not [as such] counted [as a distinct principle]. // 58

sanskrit_iast:
yathā pṛthivyadhipatirnṛpastattvāntaraṃ nahi /
tathā tattatkaleśānaḥ pṛthak tattvāntaraṃ katham // 59
meaning:
यथा पृथिव्यधिपतिर्नृपस्तत्त्वान्तरं नहि /
तथा तत्तत्कलेशानः पृथक् तत्त्वान्तरं कथम् // 59
text_mt:
Just as a king, though the ruler of the earth, is not a separate principle,
how could the lord of a particular Kalā be a separate principle? // 59

sanskrit_iast:
tadevaṃ pañcakamidaṃ śuddho'dhvā paribhāṣyate /
tatra sākṣācchivecchaiva kartryābhāsitabhedikā // 60
meaning:
तदेवं पञ्चकमिदं शुद्धोऽध्वा परिभाष्यते /
तत्र साक्षाच्छिवेच्छैव कर्त्र्याभासितभेदिका // 60
text_mt: Thus, this pentad is defined as the pure path; / therein, it is directly the will of Śiva that acts, bringing about differentiation through manifestation.

sanskrit_iast:
īśvarecchāvaśakṣubdhabhogalolikacidgaṇān /
saṃvibhaktumaghoreśaḥ sṛjatīha sitetaram // 61
meaning:
ईश्वरेच्छावशक्षुब्धभोगलोलिकचिद्गणान् /
संविभक्तुमघोरेशः सृजतीह सितेतरम् // 61
text_mt: In order to divide the hosts of consciousness, agitated by the will of the Lord and greedy for enjoyment, / Aghoreśa creates here what is other than white (the impure path).

sanskrit_iast:
aṇūnāṃ lolikā nāma niṣkarmā yābhilāṣitā /
apūrṇaṃmanyatājñānaṃ malaṃ sāvacchidojjhitā // 62
meaning:
अणूनां लोलिका नाम निष्कर्मा याभिलाषिता /
अपूर्णंमन्यताज्ञानं मलं सावच्छिदोज्झिता // 62
text_mt: The greed of bound souls is that desire which is devoid of karma; / when devoid of particular delimitation, it is the ignorance of conceiving oneself incomplete, which is mala.

sanskrit_iast:
yogyatāmātramevaitadbhāvyavacchedasaṃgrahe /
malastenāsya na pṛthaktattvabhāvo'sti rāgavat // 63
meaning:
योग्यतामात्रमेवैतद्भाव्यवच्छेदसंग्रहे /
मलस्तेनास्य न पृथक्तत्त्वभावोऽस्ति रागवत् // 63
text_mt: This is mere capacity with respect to apprehending future delimitation; / hence, like attachment, mala has no existence as a separate reality from this.

sanskrit_iast:
niravacchedakarmāṃśamātrāvacchedatastu sā /
rāgaḥ puṃsi dhiyo dharmaḥ karmabhedavicitratā // 64
meaning:
निरवच्छेदकर्मांशमात्रावच्छेदतस्तु सा /
रागः पुंसि धियो धर्मः कर्मभेदविचित्रता // 64
text_mt: Through delimitation to mere portions of karma that lack delimitation, however, it becomes / attachment in the soul, an attribute of the intellect, manifesting the diversity of differentiated karmas.

sanskrit_iast:
apūrṇamanyatā ceyaṃ tathārūpāvabhāsanam /
svatantrasya śivasyecchā ghaṭarūpo yathā ghaṭaḥ // 65
meaning:
अपूर्णमन्यता चेयं तथारूपावभासनम् /
स्वतन्त्रस्य शिवस्येच्छा घटरूपो यथा घटः // 65
text_mt: And this conceiving oneself incomplete is the shining forth in such a form; / it is the will of autonomous Śiva, just as a pot has the form of a pot.

sanskrit_iast:
svātmapracchādanecchaiva vastubhūtastathā malaḥ /
yathaivāvyatiriktasya dharāderbhāvitātmatā // 66
meaning:
स्वात्मप्रच्छादनेच्छैव वस्तुभूतस्तथा मलः /
यथैवाव्यतिरिक्तस्य धरादेर्भावितात्मता // 66
text_mt: The will to conceal one's own nature is itself mala existing as an entity, / just as the external state of earth and other [elements] is non-different [from consciousness].

sanskrit_iast:
tathaivāsyeti śāstreṣu vyatiriktaḥ sthito malaḥ /
vyatiriktaḥ svatantrastu na ko'pi śakaṭādivat // 67
meaning:
तथैवास्येति शास्त्रेषु व्यतिरिक्तः स्थितो मलः /
व्यतिरिक्तः स्वतन्त्रस्तु न कोऽपि शकटादिवत् // 67
text_mt: Thus in the scriptures mala is established as distinct only in this sense; / but it is not distinct as something autonomous, like a cart or the like.

sanskrit_iast:
tatsadvitīyā sāśuddhiḥ śivamuktāṇugā na kim /
malasya roddhrī kāpyasti śaktiḥ sa cāpyamuktagā // 68
meaning:
तत्सद्वितीया साशुद्धिः शिवमुक्ताणुगा न किम् /
मलस्य रोद्ध्री काप्यस्ति शक्तिः स चाप्यमुक्तगा // 68
text_mt: [Opponent:] Why would that impurity not attach to the liberated souls and Śiva, since it has a counterpart? / [Or] there is some blocking power of mala, and that resides only in the unliberated.

sanskrit_iast:
iti nyāyojjhito vādaḥ śraddhāmātraikakalpitaḥ /
roddhrī śaktirjaḍasyāsau svayaṃ naiva pravartate // 69
meaning:
इति न्यायोज्झितो वादः श्रद्धामात्रैककल्पितः /
रोद्ध्री शक्तिर्जडस्यासौ स्वयं नैव प्रवर्तते // 69
text_mt: [Reply:] This doctrine is devoid of logic, imagined solely through mere faith: / for that blocking power, being insentient, certainly cannot operate of its own accord.

sanskrit_iast:
svayaṃ pravṛttau viśvaṃ syāttathā ceśanikā pramā /
malasya roddhrīṃ tāṃ śaktimīśaścetsaṃyunakti tat // 70
meaning:
स्वयं प्रवृत्तौ विश्वं स्यात्तथा चेशनिका प्रमा /
मलस्य रोद्ध्रीं तां शक्तिमीशश्चेत्संयुनक्ति तत् // 70
text_mt: If it operated of its own accord, the whole universe would do so, and valid knowledge would reside in an inert master. / If the Lord connects that power which blocks mala,

sanskrit_iast:
kīdṛśaṃ pratyaṇumiti praśne nāstyuttaraṃ vacaḥ /
malaścāvaraṇaṃ tacca nāvāryasya viśeṣakam // 71
meaning:
कीदृशं प्रत्यणुमिति प्रश्ने नास्त्युत्तरं वचः /
मलश्चावरणं तच्च नावार्यस्य विशेषकम् // 71
text_mt: then to the question, 'In what manner with respect to each bound soul?', there is no answering word. / Moreover, mala is a veil, and that does not differentiate the veiled entity.

sanskrit_iast:
upalambhaṃ vihantyetadghaṭasyeva paṭāvṛtiḥ /
malenāvṛtarūpāṇāmaṇūnāṃ yatsatattvakam // 72
meaning:
उपलम्भं विहन्त्येतद्घटस्येव पटावृतिः /
मलेनावृतरूपाणामणूनां यत्सतत्त्वकम् // 72
text_mt: It obstructs perception, like the covering of a pot with a cloth. / As for the real nature of bound souls whose form is veiled by mala,

sanskrit_iast:
śiva eva ca tatpaśyettasyaivāsau malo bhavet /
vibhorjñānakriyāmātrasārasyāṇugaṇasya ca // 73
meaning:
शिव एव च तत्पश्येत्तस्यैवासौ मलो भवेत् /
विभोर्ज्ञानक्रियामात्रसारस्याणुगणस्य च // 73
text_mt: Śiva alone would see that, and that mala would belong only to him! / Furthermore, for the host of bound souls, whose essence consists solely of the pervasive Lord's knowledge and action,

sanskrit_iast:
tadabhāvo malo rūpadhvaṃsāyaiva prakalpate /
dharmāddharmiṇi yo bhedaḥ samavāyena caikatā // 74
meaning:
तदभावो मलो रूपध्वंसायैव प्रकल्पते /
धर्माद्धर्मिणि यो भेदः समवायेन चैकता // 74
text_mt: the absence thereof [called] mala would effect the destruction of their very nature! / The difference between property and bearer of property, and their oneness through inherence,

sanskrit_iast:
na tadbhavadbhiruditaṃ kaṇabhojanaśiṣyavat /
nāmūrtena na mūrtena prāvarītuṃ ca śakyate // 75
meaning:
न तद्भवद्भिरुदितं कणभोजनशिष्यवत् /
नामूर्तेन न मूर्तेन प्रावरीतुं च शक्यते // 75
text_mt: was not asserted by you, unlike the disciples of Kaṇāda. / Nor can [consciousness] be veiled by something formless or by something with form;

sanskrit_iast:
jñānaṃ cākṣuṣaraśmīnāṃ tathābhāve saratyapi /
sa eva ca malo mūrtaḥ kiṃ jñānena na vedyate // 76
meaning:
ज्ञानं चाक्षुषरश्मीनां तथाभावे सरत्यपि /
स एव च मलो मूर्तः किं ज्ञानेन न वेद्यते // 76
text_mt: for knowledge extends even as the rays of the eyes undergo such a state. / And if that mala has form, why is it not perceived by knowledge?

sanskrit_iast:
sarvageṇa tataḥ sarvaḥ sarvajñatvaṃ na kiṃ bhajet /
yaśca dhvāntātprakāśasyāvṛtistatpratighātibhiḥ // 77
meaning:
सर्वगेण ततः सर्वः सर्वज्ञत्वं न किं भजेत् /
यश्च ध्वान्तात्प्रकाशस्यावृतिस्तत्प्रतिघातिभिः // 77
text_mt: Then, through the all-pervading [knowledge], why would everyone not attain omniscience? / And as for the veiling of light by darkness through its counteracting agents,

sanskrit_iast:
mūrtānāṃ pratighastejo'ṇūnāṃ nāmūrta īdṛśam /
na ca cetanamātmānamasvatantro malaḥ kṣamaḥ // 78
meaning:
मूर्तानां प्रतिघस्तेजोऽणूनां नामूर्त ईदृशम् /
न च चेतनमात्मानमस्वतन्त्रो मलः क्षमः // 78
text_mt: the resistance among entities with form belongs to light particles; there is no such [resistance] in what is formless. / Nor is a non-autonomous mala capable of veiling the conscious self.

sanskrit_iast:
āvarītuṃ na cācyaṃ ca madyāvṛtinidarśanam /
uktaṃ bhavadbhirevetthaṃ jaḍaḥ kartā nahi svayam // 79
meaning:
आवरीतुं न चाच्यं च मद्यावृतिनिदर्शनम् /
उक्तं भवद्भिरेवेत्थं जडः कर्ता नहि स्वयम् // 79
text_mt: Nor should the example of veiling by liquor be cited [to that effect]; / for you yourselves have stated thus: an inert entity is never an agent by itself.

sanskrit_iast:
svatantrasyeśvarasyaitāḥ śaktayaḥ prerikāḥ kila /
ataḥ karmavipākajñaprabhuśaktibaleritam // 80
meaning:
स्वतन्त्रस्येश्वरस्यैताः शक्तयः प्रेरिकाः किल /
अतः कर्मविपाकज्ञप्रभुशक्तिबलेरितम् // 80
text_mt: These powers of the autonomous Lord are indeed the impelling agents. / Therefore, impelled by the force of the powers of the Master who knows the fruition of karma,

sanskrit_iast:
madyaṃ sūte madaṃ duḥkhasukhamohaphalātmakam /
na ceśapreritaḥ puṃso mala āvṛṇuyādyataḥ // 81
meaning:
मद्यं सूते मदं दुःखसुखमोहफलात्मकम् /
न चेशप्रेरितः पुंसो मल आवृणुयाद्यतः // 81
text_mt: liquor produces intoxication consisting of the fruits of pain, pleasure, and delusion. / Nor could mala veil the soul when impelled by the Lord, because,

sanskrit_iast:
nirmale puṃsi neśasya prerakatvaṃ tathocitam /
tulye nirmalabhāve ca prerayeyurna te katham // 82
meaning:
निर्मले पुंसि नेशस्य प्रेरकत्वं तथोचितम् /
तुल्ये निर्मलभावे च प्रेरयेयुर्न ते कथम् // 82
text_mt: in a spotless soul, the Lord's impelling is not appropriate in that manner. / And when souls are equal in their spotless state, why would [his powers] not impel [all of them]?

sanskrit_iast:
tamīśaṃ prati yuktaṃ yad bhūyasāṃ syātsadharmatā /
tena svarūpasvātantryamātraṃ malavijṛmbhitam // 83
meaning:
तमीशं प्रति युक्तं यद् भूयसां स्यात्सधर्मता /
तेन स्वरूपस्वातन्त्र्यमात्रं मलविजृम्भितम् // 83
text_mt: Toward that Lord, it is proper that the majority would share the same nature. / Therefore, [mala] is simply the flourishing of the autonomous nature of the Self;

sanskrit_iast:
nirṇītaṃ vitataṃ caitanmayānyatretyalaṃ punaḥ /
malo'bhilāṣaścājñānamavidyā lolikāprathā // 84
meaning:
निर्णीतं विततं चैतन्मयान्यत्रेत्यलं पुनः /
मलोऽभिलाषश्चाज्ञानमविद्या लोलिकाप्रथा // 84
text_mt: this has been determined and expounded by me elsewhere, so enough of repetition! / Mala is desire, ignorance, nescience, the expansion of greed,

sanskrit_iast:
bhavadoṣo'nuplavaśca glāniḥ śoṣo vimūḍhatā /
ahaṃmamātmatātaṅko māyāśaktirathāvṛtiḥ // 85
meaning:
भवदोषोऽनुप्लवश्च ग्लानिः शोषो विमूढता /
अहंममात्मतातङ्को मायाशक्तिरथावृतिः // 85
text_mt: the defect of existence, the raft, languor, desiccation, utter bewilderment, / the anguish of 'I' and 'mine', the power of Māyā, and the veil;

sanskrit_iast:
doṣabījaṃ paśutvaṃ ca saṃsārāṅkurakāraṇam /
ityādyanvarthasaṃjñābhistatra tatraiṣa bhaṇyate // 86
meaning:
दोषबीजं पशुत्वं च संसाराङ्कुरकारणम् /
इत्याद्यन्वर्थसंज्ञाभिस्तत्र तत्रैष भण्यते // 86
text_mt: it is called the seed of defects, bondage, the cause of the sprout of transmigratory existence, / and so on, by various meaningful designations in various contexts.

sanskrit_iast:
asmin sati bhavati bhavo duṣṭo bhedātmaneti bhavadoṣaḥ /
mañcavadasmin duḥkhasroto'ṇūn vahati yatplavastena // 87
meaning:
अस्मिन् सति भवति भवो दुष्टो भेदात्मनेति भवदोषः /
मञ्चवदस्मिन् दुःखस्रोतोऽणून् वहति यत्प्लवस्तेन // 87
text_mt: When this exists, existence becomes corrupted through duality; hence it is 'the defect of existence'. / Because like a raft it carries bound souls across the stream of suffering in this [world], it is a 'raft'.

sanskrit_iast:
śeṣāstu sugamarūpāḥ śabdāstatrārthamūhayeducitam /
saṃsārakāraṇaṃ karma saṃsārāṅkura ucyate // 88
meaning:
शेषास्तु सुगमरूपाः शब्दास्तत्रार्थमूहयेदुचितम् /
संसारकारणं कर्म संसाराङ्कुर उच्यते // 88
text_mt: The remaining words are easy to understand; one should infer the appropriate meaning there. / Karma, the cause of transmigratory existence, is called 'the sprout of transmigratory existence',

sanskrit_iast:
caturdaśavidhaṃ bhūtavaiciatryaṃ karmajaṃ yataḥ /
ata eva sāṃkhyayogapāñcarātrādiśāsane // 89
meaning:
चतुर्दशविधं भूतवैचिअत्र्यं कर्मजं यतः /
अत एव सांख्ययोगपाञ्चरात्रादिशासने // 89
text_mt: since the fourteen-fold diversity of beings arises from karma. / For this very reason, in the teachings of Sāṃkhya, Yoga, Pāñcarātra, and others,

sanskrit_iast:
ahaṃmameti saṃtyāgo naiṣkarmyāyopadiśyate /
niṣkarmā hi sthite mūlamale'pyajñānanāmani // 90
meaning:
अहंममेति संत्यागो नैष्कर्म्यायोपदिश्यते /
निष्कर्मा हि स्थिते मूलमलेऽप्यज्ञाननामनि // 90
text_mt: renunciation of 'I' and 'mine' is taught for the attainment of state free from karma. / For when one is devoid of karma, even though the root mala named ignorance remains,

sanskrit_iast:
vaicitryakāraṇābhāvānnordhva sarati nāpyadhaḥ /
kevalaṃ pārimityena śivābhedamasaṃspṛśan // 91
meaning:
वैचित्र्यकारणाभावान्नोर्ध्व सरति नाप्यधः /
केवलं पारिमित्येन शिवाभेदमसंस्पृशन् // 91
text_mt: due to the absence of the cause of diversity, one moves neither upward nor downward; / solely through limitation, without touching non-duality with Śiva,

sanskrit_iast:
vijñānakevalī proktaḥ śuddhacinmātrasaṃsthitaḥ /
sa punaḥ śāṃbhavecchātaḥ śivābhedaṃ parāmṛśan // 92
meaning:
विज्ञानकेवली प्रोक्तः शुद्धचिन्मात्रसंस्थितः /
स पुनः शांभवेच्छातः शिवाभेदं परामृशन् // 92
text_mt: one established in pure consciousness alone is called a vijñānakevalī. / He again, through the will of Śambhu, contemplating non-duality with Śiva,

sanskrit_iast:
kramānmantreśatannetṛrūpo yāti śivātmatām /
nanu kāraṇametasya karmaṇaścenmalaḥ katham // 93
meaning:
क्रमान्मन्त्रेशतन्नेतृरूपो याति शिवात्मताम् /
ननु कारणमेतस्य कर्मणश्चेन्मलः कथम् // 93
text_mt: gradually attains the nature of Śiva in the form of the lords of mantras and their masters. / [Objection:] If mala is the cause of this karma, how is it

sanskrit_iast:
sa vijñānākalasyāpi na sūte karmasaṃtatim /
maivaṃ sa hi malo jñānākale didhvaṃsiṣuḥ katham // 94
meaning:
स विज्ञानाकलस्यापि न सूते कर्मसंततिम् /
मैवं स हि मलो ज्ञानाकले दिध्वंसिषुः कथम् // 94
text_mt: that it does not generate a continuum of karma even for the vijñānākala? / [Reply:] Not so; for how could that mala, about to perish in a vijñānākala,

sanskrit_iast:
hetuḥ syāddhvaṃsamānatvaṃ svātantryādeva codbhavet /
didhvaṃsiṣudhvaṃsamānadhvastākhyāsu tisṛṣvatha // 95
meaning:
हेतुः स्याद्ध्वंसमानत्वं स्वातन्त्र्यादेव चोद्भवेत् /
दिध्वंसिषुध्वंसमानध्वस्ताख्यासु तिसृष्वथ // 95
text_mt: be a cause? The state of perishing arises from absolute autonomy alone. / Then, in the three states called 'desiring to perish', 'perishing', and 'perished',

sanskrit_iast:
daśāsvantaḥ kṛtāvasthāntarāsu svakramasthiteḥ /
vijñānākalamantreśatadīśāditvakalpanā // 96
meaning:
दशास्वन्तः कृतावस्थान्तरासु स्वक्रमस्थितेः /
विज्ञानाकलमन्त्रेशतदीशादित्वकल्पना // 96
text_mt: which contain intermediary states within them, in the order of their respective progression, / the designation of vijñānākala, lord of mantras, master thereof, etc., is posited.

sanskrit_iast:
tataśca supte turye ca vakṣyate bahubhedatā /
ataḥ pradhvaṃsanaunmukhyakhilībhūtasvaśaktikaḥ // 97
meaning:
ततश्च सुप्ते तुर्ये च वक्ष्यते बहुभेदता /
अतः प्रध्वंसनौन्मुख्यखिलीभूतस्वशक्तिकः // 97
text_mt: And hence, in deep sleep and the fourth state, manifold varieties will be described. / Therefore, how can mala, whose inherent power is incapacitated by readiness for destruction,

sanskrit_iast:
karmaṇo hetutāmetu malaḥ kathamivocyatām /
kiṃ ca karmāpi na malādyataḥ karma kriyātmakam // 98
meaning:
कर्मणो हेतुतामेतु मलः कथमिवोच्यताम् /
किं च कर्मापि न मलाद्यतः कर्म क्रियात्मकम् // 98
text_mt: be the cause of karma? Tell us! / Moreover, karma does not arise from mala, because karma is of the nature of action,

sanskrit_iast:
kriyā ca kartṛtārūpāt svātantryānna punarmalāt /
yā tvasya karmaṇaścitraphaladatvena karmatā // 99
meaning:
क्रिया च कर्तृतारूपात् स्वातन्त्र्यान्न पुनर्मलात् /
या त्वस्य कर्मणश्चित्रफलदत्वेन कर्मता // 99
text_mt: and action arises from absolute autonomy which is the nature of agency, not from mala. / But as for that character of karma, as granting manifold fruits,

sanskrit_iast:
prasiddhā sā na saṃkocaṃ vinātmani malaśca saḥ /
vicitraṃ hi phalaṃ bhinnaṃ bhogyatvenābhimanyate // 100
meaning:
प्रसिद्धा सा न संकोचं विनात्मनि मलश्च सः /
विचित्रं हि फलं भिन्नं भोग्यत्वेनाभिमन्यते // 100
text_mt: which is well known—that does not occur without contraction in the self, and that is mala. / For a manifold and differentiated fruit is conceived as an object of enjoyment

sanskrit_iast:
bhoktaryātmani teneyaṃ bhedarūpā vyavasthitiḥ /
iti svakāryaprasave sahakāritvamāśrayan // 101
meaning:
भोक्तर्यात्मनि तेनेयं भेदरूपा व्यवस्थितिः /
इति स्वकार्यप्रसवे सहकारित्वमाश्रयन् // 101
text_mt: by the enjoying self; hence this arrangement consisting of difference [ensues]. / Thus, resorting to co-operation in bringing forth its own effect,

sanskrit_iast:
sāmarthyavyañjakatvena karmaṇaḥ kāraṇaṃ malaḥ /
nanvevaṃ karmasadbhāvānmalasyāpi sthiteḥ katham // 102
meaning:
सामर्थ्यव्यञ्जकत्वेन कर्मणः कारणं मलः /
नन्वेवं कर्मसद्भावान्मलस्यापि स्थितेः कथम् // 102
text_mt: mala is the cause of karma by manifesting its capability. / [Objection:] Surely, in this way, since karma exists, and because mala also remains,

sanskrit_iast:
vijñānākalatā tasya saṃkoco hyasti tādṛśaḥ /
maivamadhvastasaṃkoco'pyasau bhāvanayā dṛḍham // 103
meaning:
विज्ञानाकलता तस्य संकोचो ह्यस्ति तादृशः /
मैवमध्वस्तसंकोचोऽप्यसौ भावनया दृढम् // 103
text_mt: how can there be the state of being a vijñānākala for him? For there is such contraction. / [Reply:] Not so; although his contraction is not destroyed, firmly through contemplation

sanskrit_iast:
nāhaṃ karteti manvānaḥ karmasaṃskāramujjhati /
phaliṣyatīdaṃ karmeti yā dṛḍhā vṛttirātmani // 104
meaning:
नाहं कर्तेति मन्वानः कर्मसंस्कारमुज्झति /
फलिष्यतीदं कर्मेति या दृढा वृत्तिरात्मनि // 104
text_mt: thinking 'I am not the agent', he casts off the latent impression of karma. / That firm conviction within the self that 'this karma will bear fruit'

sanskrit_iast:
sa saṃskāraḥ phalāyeha na tu smaraṇakāraṇam /
apradhvaste'pi saṃkoce nāhaṃ karteti bhāvanāt // 105
meaning:
स संस्कारः फलायेह न तु स्मरणकारणम् /
अप्रध्वस्तेऽपि संकोचे नाहं कर्तेति भावनात् // 105
text_mt: is the latent impression leading to fruit here, not the cause of memory; / [and it ceases] because of the contemplation 'I am not the agent', even though contraction is not yet destroyed.

sanskrit_iast:
na phalaṃ kṣīvamūḍhādeḥ prāyaścitte'tha vā kṛte /
yanmayādya tapastaptaṃ tadasmai syāditi sphuṭam // 106
meaning:
न फलं क्षीवमूढादेः प्रायश्चित्तेऽथ वा कृते /
यन्मयाद्य तपस्तप्तं तदस्मै स्यादिति स्फुटम् // 106
text_mt: There is no fruit for one intoxicated, bewildered, and the like, or when an expiation has been performed, / [or when one thinks:] 'Whatever austerity I have practiced today, clearly let it belong to him.'

sanskrit_iast:
abhisaṃdhimataḥ karma na phaledabhisandhitaḥ /
tathābhisaṃdhānākhyāṃ tu mānase karma saṃskriyām // 107
meaning:
अभिसंधिमतः कर्म न फलेदभिसन्धितः /
तथाभिसंधानाख्यां तु मानसे कर्म संस्क्रियाम् // 107
text_mt: The action of one who has an intention would not bear fruit according to that intention; / but producing in the mind a mental trace called 'intention'

sanskrit_iast:
phaloparaktāṃ vidadhatkalpate phalasampade /
yastu tatrāpi dārḍhyena phalasaṃskāramujjhati // 108
meaning:
फलोपरक्तां विदधत्कल्पते फलसम्पदे /
यस्तु तत्रापि दार्ढ्येन फलसंस्कारमुज्झति // 108
text_mt: colored by the fruit, an action becomes capable of yielding the fruit. / But whoever, even in that state, firmly casts off the trace of the fruit,

sanskrit_iast:
sa tatphalatyāgakṛtaṃ viśiṣṭaṃ phalamaśnute /
anayā paripāṭyā yaḥ samastāṃ karmasaṃtatim // 109
meaning:
स तत्फलत्यागकृतं विशिष्टं फलमश्नुते /
अनया परिपाट्या यः समस्तां कर्मसंततिम् // 109
text_mt: attains an exceptional fruit produced by the abandonment of that fruit. / Whoever, by this succession, completely abandons the entire continuum of karma

sanskrit_iast:
anahaṃyutayā projjhet sasaṃkoco'pi so'kalaḥ /
nanvitthaṃ duṣkṛtaṃ kiṃcidātmīyamabhisaṃdhitaḥ // 110
meaning:
अनहंयुतया प्रोज्झेत् ससंकोचोऽपि सोऽकलः /
नन्वित्थं दुष्कृतं किंचिदात्मीयमभिसंधितः // 110
text_mt: through the state of non-egoity, is free of parts (akala) even while contraction remains. / Now, [someone might object:] 'In this way, some misdeed of one's own might belong to another through intention.'

sanskrit_iast:
parasmai syānna vijñātaṃ bhavatā tāttvikaṃ vacaḥ /
tasya bhoktustathā cetsyādabhisaṃdhiryathātmani // 111
meaning:
परस्मै स्यान्न विज्ञातं भवता तात्त्विकं वचः /
तस्य भोक्तुस्तथा चेत्स्यादभिसंधिर्यथात्मनि // 111
text_mt: [We reply:] You have not understood the genuine teaching. / If there should be an intention in that experiencer [directing it] to another just as towards oneself,

sanskrit_iast:
tadavaśyaṃ parasyāpi satastadduṣkṛtaṃ bhavet /
parābhisaṃdhisaṃvittau svābhisaṃdhirdṛḍhībhavet // 112
meaning:
तदवश्यं परस्यापि सतस्तद्दुष्कृतं भवेत् /
पराभिसंधिसंवित्तौ स्वाभिसंधिर्दृढीभवेत् // 112
text_mt: then inevitably that misdeed would belong to the other as well, since [the intention] is actual. / When the intention regarding the other is conscious, one's own intention would become firm.

sanskrit_iast:
abhisaṃdhānavirahe tvasya no phalayogitā /
na me duṣkṛtamityeṣā rūḍhistasyāphalāya sā // 113
meaning:
अभिसंधानविरहे त्वस्य नो फलयोगिता /
न मे दुष्कृतमित्येषा रूढिस्तस्याफलाय सा // 113
text_mt: However, in the absence of intention, there is no connection to the fruit for him. / The deeply rooted conviction 'This is not my misdeed' results in its fruitlessness.

sanskrit_iast:
parābhisandhivicchede svātmanānabhisaṃhitau /
dvayorapi phalaṃ na syānnāśahetuvyavasthiteḥ // 114
meaning:
पराभिसन्धिविच्छेदे स्वात्मनानभिसंहितौ /
द्वयोरपि फलं न स्यान्नाशहेतुव्यवस्थितेः // 114
text_mt: When the intention towards another is broken, and there is no intention regarding oneself, / there would be no fruit for either of the two, because the cause of destruction is established.

sanskrit_iast:
sukhahetau sukhe cāsya sāmānyādabhisaṃdhitaḥ /
nirviśeṣādapi nyāyyā dharmādiphalabhoktṛtā // 115
meaning:
सुखहेतौ सुखे चास्य सामान्यादभिसंधितः /
निर्विशेषादपि न्याय्या धर्मादिफलभोक्तृता // 115
text_mt: Regarding the cause of pleasure and pleasure itself, because of this [agent's] general intention, / it is appropriate that he is the experiencer of the fruits of righteousness (dharma) and the like, even without distinction.

sanskrit_iast:
duḥkhaṃ me duḥkhaheturvā stādityeṣa punarna tu /
sāmānyo'pyabhisaṃdhiḥ syāttadadharmasya nāgamaḥ // 116
meaning:
दुःखं मे दुःखहेतुर्वा स्तादित्येष पुनर्न तु /
सामान्योऽप्यभिसंधिः स्यात्तदधर्मस्य नागमः // 116
text_mt: However, the thought 'May suffering or the cause of suffering be mine' / would never be even a general intention; therefore, unrighteousness (adharma) does not accrue [to him].

sanskrit_iast:
prakṛtaṃ brūmahe jñānākalasyoktacarasya yat /
anahaṃyutayā sarvā vilīnāḥ karmasaṃskriyāḥ // 117
meaning:
प्रकृतं ब्रूमहे ज्ञानाकलस्योक्तचरस्य यत् /
अनहंयुतया सर्वा विलीनाः कर्मसंस्क्रियाः // 117
text_mt: We state the present topic: that for the knower free of instruments mentioned before, / all impressions of karma have dissolved through the state of non-egoity.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmādasya na karmāsti kasyāpi sahakāritām /
malaḥ karotu tenāyaṃ dhvaṃsamānatvamaśnute // 118
meaning:
तस्मादस्य न कर्मास्ति कस्यापि सहकारिताम् /
मलः करोतु तेनायं ध्वंसमानत्वमश्नुते // 118
text_mt: Therefore, he has no karma; towards what could impurity provide assistance? / Because of that, he attains the state of being dissolved.

sanskrit_iast:
apadhvastamalastvantaḥśivāveśavaśīkṛtaḥ /
ahaṃbhāvaparo'pyeti na karmādhīnavṛttitām // 119
meaning:
अपध्वस्तमलस्त्वन्तःशिवावेशवशीकृतः /
अहंभावपरोऽप्येति न कर्माधीनवृत्तिताम् // 119
text_mt: However, one whose impurity is destroyed, being subjugated by the internal absorption in Śiva, / does not enter into a state dependent on karma even though he is devoted to the sense of 'I'.

sanskrit_iast:
uktaṃ śrīpūrvaśāstre ca tadetatparameśinā /
malamajñānamicchanti saṃsārāṅkurakāraṇam // 120
meaning:
उक्तं श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे च तदेतत्परमेशिना /
मलमज्ञानमिच्छन्ति संसाराङ्कुरकारणम् // 120
text_mt: And this very thing has been taught by the Supreme Lord in the venerable Pūrvaśāstra (Mālinīvijayottara): / 'They consider impurity to be ignorance, the cause of the sprout of transmigratory existence (saṃsāra).'

sanskrit_iast:
dharmādharmātmakaṃ karma sukhaduḥkhādilakṣaṇam /
lakṣayetsukhaduḥkhādi svaṃ kārya hetubhāvataḥ // 121
meaning:
धर्माधर्मात्मकं कर्म सुखदुःखादिलक्षणम् /
लक्षयेत्सुखदुःखादि स्वं कार्य हेतुभावतः // 121
text_mt: Karma consists of righteousness and unrighteousness, characterized by pleasure, pain, and the like; / it indicates its own effect—pleasure, pain, and the like—by virtue of being their cause.

sanskrit_iast:
nahi hetuḥ kadāpyāste vinā kārya nijaṃ kvacit /
hetutā yogyataivāsau phalānantaryabhāvitā // 122
meaning:
नहि हेतुः कदाप्यास्ते विना कार्य निजं क्वचित् /
हेतुता योग्यतैवासौ फलानन्तर्यभाविता // 122
text_mt: For a cause never exists anywhere without its own effect; / causality is simply this capacity that becomes actualized immediately prior to the fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
pūrvakasya tu hetutvaṃ pāramparyeṇa kiṃ ca tat /
lakṣyate sukhaduḥkhādyaiḥ samāne dṛṣṭakāraṇe // 123
meaning:
पूर्वकस्य तु हेतुत्वं पारम्पर्येण किं च तत् /
लक्ष्यते सुखदुःखाद्यैः समाने दृष्टकारणे // 123
text_mt: Moreover, the causality of what is prior, operating indirectly, / is indicated by pleasure, pain, and the like, even when an observed cause is identical,

sanskrit_iast:
citrairhetvantaraṃ kiṃcittacca karmeha darśanāt /
svāṅge prasādaraukṣyādi jāyamānaṃ svakarmaṇā // 124
meaning:
चित्रैर्हेत्वन्तरं किंचित्तच्च कर्मेह दर्शनात् /
स्वाङ्गे प्रसादरौक्ष्यादि जायमानं स्वकर्मणा // 124
text_mt: through varied effects, as some other cause; and in this world, from observation, that is karma. / One sees tranquility, roughness, and the like arising in one's own body due to one's own karma;

sanskrit_iast:
dṛṣṭamityanyadehasthaṃ kāraṇaṃ karma kalpyāte /
ihāpyanyānyadehasthe sphuṭaṃ karmaphale yataḥ // 125
meaning:
दृष्टमित्यन्यदेहस्थं कारणं कर्म कल्प्याते /
इहाप्यन्यान्यदेहस्थे स्फुटं कर्मफले यतः // 125
text_mt: therefore, karma is postulated as a cause residing in another body, / because even in this life, karma and fruit manifestly reside in different bodies.

sanskrit_iast:
kṛṣikarma madhau bhogaḥ śaradyanyā ca sā tanuḥ /
anusaṃdhāturekasya saṃbhavastu yatastataḥ // 126
meaning:
कृषिकर्म मधौ भोगः शरद्यन्या च सा तनुः /
अनुसंधातुरेकस्य संभवस्तु यतस्ततः // 126
text_mt: The work of agriculture takes place in spring, the enjoyment in autumn, and that body is different; / but because the existence of a single synthesizer is possible, therefore,

sanskrit_iast:
tasyaiva tatphalaṃ citraṃ karma yasya purātanam /
kṣīvo'pi rājā sūdaṃ cedādiśetprātarīdṛśam // 127
meaning:
तस्यैव तत्फलं चित्रं कर्म यस्य पुरातनम् /
क्षीवोऽपि राजा सूदं चेदादिशेत्प्रातरीदृशम् // 127
text_mt: that variegated fruit belongs to him alone whose prior karma it is. / If even an intoxicated king should instruct the cook: 'Serve such food tomorrow morning,'

sanskrit_iast:
bhojayetyanusaṃdhānādvinā prāpnoti tatphalam /
itthaṃ janmāntaropāttakarmāpyadyānusaṃdhinā // 128
meaning:
भोजयेत्यनुसंधानाद्विना प्राप्नोति तत्फलम् /
इत्थं जन्मान्तरोपात्तकर्माप्यद्यानुसंधिना // 128
text_mt: he receives that fruit without [subsequent] mindful synthesis. / In this way, one experiences the fruit even of karma acquired in another birth, without any present mindful synthesis;

sanskrit_iast:
vinā bhuṅkte phalaṃ hetustatra prācyā hyakampatā /
ata eva kṛtaṃ karma karmaṇā tapasāpi vā // 129
meaning:
विना भुङ्क्ते फलं हेतुस्तत्र प्राच्या ह्यकम्पता /
अत एव कृतं कर्म कर्मणा तपसापि वा // 129
text_mt: for the cause in that case is indeed the firmness of the earlier [action]. / For this very reason, an action that has been done may be arrested by an action, by austerity,

sanskrit_iast:
jñānena vā nirudhyeta phalapākeṣvanunmukham /
ārabdhakāryaṃ dehe'smin yatpunaḥ karma tatkatham // 130
meaning:
ज्ञानेन वा निरुध्येत फलपाकेष्वनुन्मुखम् /
आरब्धकार्यं देहेऽस्मिन् यत्पुनः कर्म तत्कथम् // 130
text_mt: or by knowledge, so long as it is not yet oriented towards the ripening of fruits. / On the other hand, how could karma that has already commenced its effect in this body

sanskrit_iast:
ucchidyatāmantyadaśaṃ niroddhuṃ nahi śakyate /
tatraiva dehe yattvanyadadyagaṃ vā purātanam // 131
meaning:
उच्छिद्यतामन्त्यदशं निरोद्धुं नहि शक्यते /
तत्रैव देहे यत्त्वन्यदद्यगं वा पुरातनम् // 131
text_mt: be cut off? For that which has reached its final stage cannot be arrested. / But whatever other karma exists in that very body, whether belonging to the present or to the past,

sanskrit_iast:
karma tajjñānadīkṣādyaiḥ śaṇḍhīkartuṃ prasahyate /
tathā saṃskāradārḍhya hi phalāya dṛḍhatā punaḥ // 132
meaning:
कर्म तज्ज्ञानदीक्षाद्यैः शण्ढीकर्तुं प्रसह्यते /
तथा संस्कारदार्ढ्य हि फलाय दृढता पुनः // 132
text_mt: that can be rendered sterile through knowledge, initiation, and the like. / Likewise, the firmness of the impression is indeed for the sake of the fruit; but whenever that firmness

sanskrit_iast:
yadā yadā vinaśyeta karmadhvastaṃ tadā tadā /
ato mohaparādhīno yadyapyakṛta kiṃcana // 133
meaning:
यदा यदा विनश्येत कर्मध्वस्तं तदा तदा /
अतो मोहपराधीनो यद्यप्यकृत किंचन // 133
text_mt: should perish, at that very time the karma is destroyed. / Therefore, although one subject to delusion may have done anything,

sanskrit_iast:
tathāpi jñānakāle tatsarvameva pradahyate /
uktaṃ ca śrīpare'hānādānaḥ sarvadṛgulvaṇaḥ // 134
meaning:
तथापि ज्ञानकाले तत्सर्वमेव प्रदह्यते /
उक्तं च श्रीपरेऽहानादानः सर्वदृगुल्वणः // 134
text_mt: nevertheless, at the time of knowledge all of that is utterly burned away. / And it is stated in the venerable Param: 'One who does not take and does not cast off, who is all-seeing and intense,

sanskrit_iast:
muhūrtānnirdahetsarva dehasthamakṛtaṃ kṛtam /
dehasthamiti dehena saha tādātmyamāśritā // 135
meaning:
मुहूर्तान्निर्दहेत्सर्व देहस्थमकृतं कृतम् /
देहस्थमिति देहेन सह तादात्म्यमाश्रिता // 135
text_mt: would in an instant burn away everything residing in the body, whether undone or done.' / 'Residing in the body' means that consciousness, through its autonomy, has embraced identity with the body;

sanskrit_iast:
svācchandyātsaṃvidevoktā tatrasthaṃ karma dahyate /
dehaikyavāsanātyāgāt sa ca viśvātmatāsthiteḥ // 136
meaning:
स्वाच्छन्द्यात्संविदेवोक्ता तत्रस्थं कर्म दह्यते /
देहैक्यवासनात्यागात् स च विश्वात्मतास्थितेः // 136
text_mt: the karma residing therein is burned / by abandoning the latent impression of oneness with the body, and that [abandonment] comes from abiding in the nature of the universe.

sanskrit_iast:
akālakalite vyāpinyabhinne yā hi saṃskriyā /
saṃkoca eva sānena so'pi dehaikatāmayaḥ // 137
meaning:
अकालकलिते व्यापिन्यभिन्ने या हि संस्क्रिया /
संकोच एव सानेन सोऽपि देहैकतामयः // 137
text_mt: For any impression in what is unconditioned by time, pervasive, and undivided / is merely a contraction; by this [contraction] it also consists of oneness with the body.

sanskrit_iast:
etatkārmamalaṃ proktaṃ yena sākaṃ layākalāḥ /
syurguhāgahanāntaḥsthāḥ suptā iva sarīsṛpāḥ // 138
meaning:
एतत्कार्ममलं प्रोक्तं येन साकं लयाकलाः /
स्युर्गुहागहनान्तःस्थाः सुप्ता इव सरीसृपाः // 138
text_mt: This has been declared to be the impurity of action (kārma mala), together with which the souls free of instruments in dissolution (layākala) / abide like serpents asleep inside a dense cave.

sanskrit_iast:
tataḥ prabuddhasaṃskārāste yathocitabhāginaḥ /
brahmādisthāvarānte'smin saṃsranti punaḥ punaḥ // 139
meaning:
ततः प्रबुद्धसंस्कारास्ते यथोचितभागिनः /
ब्रह्मादिस्थावरान्तेऽस्मिन् संस्रन्ति पुनः पुनः // 139
text_mt: Then, their impressions awakened, receiving their appropriate share, / they transmigrate again and again in this world from Brahmā down to immobile things.

sanskrit_iast:
ye punaḥ karmasaṃskārahānyai prārabdhabhāvanāḥ /
bhāvanāpariniṣpattimaprāpya pralayaṃ gatāḥ // 140
meaning:
ये पुनः कर्मसंस्कारहान्यै प्रारब्धभावनाः /
भावनापरिनिष्पत्तिमप्राप्य प्रलयं गताः // 140
text_mt: On the other hand, those who commenced contemplation for the destruction of karmic impressions, / but underwent dissolution before reaching the perfection of contemplation,

sanskrit_iast:
mahāntaṃ te tathāntaḥsthabhāvanāpākasauṣṭhavāt /
mantratvaṃ pratipadyante citrāccitraṃ ca karmataḥ // 141
meaning:
महान्तं ते तथान्तःस्थभावनापाकसौष्ठवात् /
मन्त्रत्वं प्रतिपद्यन्ते चित्राच्चित्रं च कर्मतः // 141
text_mt: owing to the excellence of the ripening of their internal contemplation, / attain the status of Mantras and diverse states from diverse karma in the great [dissolution].

sanskrit_iast:
asya kārmamalasyeyanmāyāntādhvavisāriṇaḥ /
pradhānaṃ kāraṇaṃ proktamajñānātmāṇavo malaḥ // 142
meaning:
अस्य कार्ममलस्येयन्मायान्ताध्वविसारिणः /
प्रधानं कारणं प्रोक्तमज्ञानात्माणवो मलः // 142
text_mt: Of this impurity of action, which extends across the path ending in Māyā, / the primary cause is declared to be the innate impurity (āṇava mala), which consists of ignorance.

sanskrit_iast:
kṣobho'sya lolikākhyasya sahakāritayā sphuṭam /
tiṣṭhāsāyogyataunmukhyamīśvarecchāvaśācca tat // 143
meaning:
क्षोभोऽस्य लोलिकाख्यस्य सहकारितया स्फुटम् /
तिष्ठासायोग्यतौन्मुख्यमीश्वरेच्छावशाच्च तत् // 143
text_mt: The agitation of this [Māyā] is called lolikā, clearly acting as an auxiliary cause; / it is the readiness and orientation to abide, and that arises through the will of the Lord.

sanskrit_iast:
na jaḍaścidadhiṣṭhānaṃ vinā kvāpi kṣamo yataḥ /
aṇavo nāma naivānyatprakāśātmā maheśvaraḥ // 144
meaning:
न जडश्चिदधिष्ठानं विना क्वापि क्षमो यतः /
अणवो नाम नैवान्यत्प्रकाशात्मा महेश्वरः // 144
text_mt: For what is inert is never capable anywhere without the presiding of consciousness. / The individual souls (aṇu) are indeed nothing other than the Great Lord whose nature is luminosity.

sanskrit_iast:
cidacidrūpatābhāsī pudgalaḥ kṣetravitpaśuḥ /
cidrūpatvācca sa vyāpī nirguṇo niṣkriyastataḥ // 145
meaning:
चिदचिद्रूपताभासी पुद्गलः क्षेत्रवित्पशुः /
चिद्रूपत्वाच्च स व्यापी निर्गुणो निष्क्रियस्ततः // 145
text_mt: Appearing as both conscious and unconscious, he is the individual soul (pudgala), the knower of the field, the bound soul (paśu). / And because his nature is consciousness, he is pervasive, devoid of qualities, and therefore inactive.

sanskrit_iast:
yogopāyepsako nityo mūrtivandhyaḥ prabhāṣyate /
acittvādajñatā bhedo bhogyādbhoktrantarādatha // 146
meaning:
योगोपायेप्सको नित्यो मूर्तिवन्ध्यः प्रभाष्यते /
अचित्त्वादज्ञता भेदो भोग्याद्भोक्त्रन्तरादथ // 146
text_mt: He is described as seeking the means of yoga, eternal, and free of bodily form. / Because of the unconscious aspect, there is ignorance and difference from what is enjoyed and from another experiencer.

sanskrit_iast:
teṣāmaṇūnāṃ sa mala īśvarecchāvaśādbhṛśam /
prabudhyate tathā coktaṃ śāstre śrīpūrvanāmani // 147
meaning:
तेषामणूनां स मल ईश्वरेच्छावशाद्भृशम् /
प्रबुध्यते तथा चोक्तं शास्त्रे श्रीपूर्वनामनि // 147
text_mt: Through the will of the Lord, that impurity of those individual souls / is intensely awakened; and so it has been said in the scripture named the venerable Pūrva (Mālinīvijayottara):

sanskrit_iast:
īśvarecchāvaśādasya bhogecchā saṃprajāyate /
bhogecchorupakārārthamādyo mantramaheśvaraḥ // 148
meaning:
ईश्वरेच्छावशादस्य भोगेच्छा संप्रजायते /
भोगेच्छोरुपकारार्थमाद्यो मन्त्रमहेश्वरः // 148
text_mt: 'Under the influence of the will of the Lord, the desire for enjoyment arises in him.' / For the benefit of the one who desires enjoyment, the first Lord of Mantras (Mantramaheśvara),

sanskrit_iast:
māyāṃ vikṣobhya saṃsāraṃ nirmimīte vicitrakam /
māyā ca nāma devasya śaktiravyatirekiṇī // 149
meaning:
मायां विक्षोभ्य संसारं निर्मिमीते विचित्रकम् /
माया च नाम देवस्य शक्तिरव्यतिरेकिणी // 149
text_mt: having agitated Māyā, creates the manifold transmigratory world. / And Māyā is the inseparable power of the Lord,

sanskrit_iast:
bhedāvabhāsasvātantryaṃ tathāhi sa tayā kṛtaḥ /
ādyo bhedāvabhāso yo vibhāgamanupeyivān // 150
meaning:
भेदावभासस्वातन्त्र्यं तथाहि स तया कृतः /
आद्यो भेदावभासो यो विभागमनुपेयिवान् // 150
text_mt: the absolute autonomy of the manifestation of difference. For it is thus that he was made by Her. / The initial manifestation of difference, which has not yet attained distinction,

sanskrit_iast:
garbhīkṛtānantabhāvivibhāsā sā parā niśā /
sā jaḍā bhedarūpatvāt kāryaṃ cāsyā jaḍaṃ yataḥ // 151
meaning:
गर्भीकृतानन्तभाविविभासा सा परा निशा /
सा जडा भेदरूपत्वात् कार्यं चास्या जडं यतः // 151
text_mt: and which contains within itself the infinite future manifestations, is the supreme night. / That [night] is inert because its nature is difference, for its effect is inert.

sanskrit_iast:
vyāpinī viśvahetutvāt sūkṣmā kāryaikakalpanāt /
śivaśaktyavinābhāvānnityaikā mūlakāraṇam // 152
meaning:
व्यापिनी विश्वहेतुत्वात् सूक्ष्मा कार्यैककल्पनात् /
शिवशक्त्यविनाभावान्नित्यैका मूलकारणम् // 152
text_mt: It is all-pervading because it is the cause of all; it is subtle because it is inferred only from its effect; / because it is inseparable from the power of Śiva, it is eternal, single, and the root cause.

sanskrit_iast:
acetanamanekātma sarva kārya yathā ghaṭaḥ /
pradhānaṃ ca tathā tasmāt kārya nātmā tu cetanaḥ // 153
meaning:
अचेतनमनेकात्म सर्व कार्य यथा घटः /
प्रधानं च तथा तस्मात् कार्य नात्मा तु चेतनः // 153
text_mt: Every effect is insentient and plural, like a pot, / and pradhāna is like that. Therefore [pradhāna] is an effect; the conscious self, however, is not.

sanskrit_iast:
ata evādhvani proktā pūrvaṃ māyā dvidhā sthitā /
yathā ca māyā devasya śaktirabhyeti bhedinam // 154
meaning:
अत एवाध्वनि प्रोक्ता पूर्वं माया द्विधा स्थिता /
यथा च माया देवस्य शक्तिरभ्येति भेदिनम् // 154
text_mt: For this very reason, māyā was previously stated to exist in two ways in the path. / And just as māyā, the power of the Lord, takes on the state of an differentiated

sanskrit_iast:
tattvabhāvaṃ tathānyo'pi kalādistattvavistaraḥ /
niruddhaśakteryā kiṃcitkartṛtodvalanātmikā // 155
meaning:
तत्त्वभावं तथान्योऽपि कलादिस्तत्त्वविस्तरः /
निरुद्धशक्तेर्या किंचित्कर्तृतोद्वलनात्मिका // 155
text_mt: tattva, so too does the rest of the expansion of tattvas, beginning with kalā. / That power of the Lord which—for [the soul] whose capacity is obstructed—consists in stimulating limited agency,

sanskrit_iast:
nāthasya śaktiḥ sādhastātpuṃsaḥ kṣeptrī kalocyate /
evaṃ vidyādayo'pyete dharāntāḥ paramārthataḥ // 156
meaning:
नाथस्य शक्तिः साधस्तात्पुंसः क्षेप्त्री कलोच्यते /
एवं विद्यादयोऽप्येते धरान्ताः परमार्थतः // 156
text_mt: and which casts the puruṣa down, is called kalā. / In this way, even these [tattvas] beginning with vidyā down to the earth are in the ultimate sense

sanskrit_iast:
śivaśaktimayā eva proktanyāyānusārataḥ /
tathāpi yatpṛthagbhānaṃ kalāderīśvarecchayā // 157
meaning:
शिवशक्तिमया एव प्रोक्तन्यायानुसारतः /
तथापि यत्पृथग्भानं कलादेरीश्वरेच्छया // 157
text_mt: identical with the power of Śiva, in accordance with the previously stated reasoning. / Nevertheless, the separate appearance of kalā and the rest through the will of the Lord

sanskrit_iast:
tato jaḍatve kāryatve pṛthaktattvasthitau dhruvam /
upādānaṃ smṛtā māyā kvacittatkāryameva ca // 158
meaning:
ततो जडत्वे कार्यत्वे पृथक्तत्त्वस्थितौ ध्रुवम् /
उपादानं स्मृता माया क्वचित्तत्कार्यमेव च // 158
text_mt: is the reason why, in being insentient, being effects, and existing as distinct tattvas, / māyā is indeed remembered as the material cause, and sometimes its effect itself is so.

sanskrit_iast:
tathāvabhāsacitraṃ ca rūpamanyonyavarjitam /
yadbhāti kila saṃkalpe tadasti ghaṭavadvahiḥ // 159
meaning:
तथावभासचित्रं च रूपमन्योन्यवर्जितम् /
यद्भाति किल संकल्पे तदस्ति घटवद्वहिः // 159
text_mt: So too, a form that is variegated in its manifestation and mutually exclusive, / which appears within conception, truly exists externally like a pot.
