sanskrit_iast:
khapuṣpādyastitāṃ brūmastato na vyabhicāritā /
khapuṣpaṃ kāladiṅmātṛsāpekṣaṃ nāstiśabdataḥ // 160
meaning:
खपुष्पाद्यस्तितां ब्रूमस्ततो न व्यभिचारिता /
खपुष्पं कालदिङ्मातृसापेक्षं नास्तिशब्दतः // 160
text_mt: We assert that even an empty-flower and the like have existence; therefore there is no deviation. / An empty-flower is [said] not to exist through the word 'is not' relative to time, space, and a cognizer,

sanskrit_iast:
dharādivat tathātyantābhāvo'pyevaṃ vivicyatām /
yatsaṃkalpyaṃ tathā tasya bahirdeho'sti cetanaḥ // 161
meaning:
धरादिवत् तथात्यन्ताभावोऽप्येवं विविच्यताम् /
यत्संकल्प्यं तथा तस्य बहिर्देहोऽस्ति चेतनः // 161
text_mt: just like the earth and the like. Absolute non-existence should also be examined in this way. / That which is conceivable in this way has a conscious body outside,

sanskrit_iast:
caitravatsauśivāntaṃ tat sarva tādṛśadehavat /
yasya deho yathā tasya tajjātīyaṃ puraṃ bahiḥ // 162
meaning:
चैत्रवत्सौशिवान्तं तत् सर्व तादृशदेहवत् /
यस्य देहो यथा तस्य तज्जातीयं पुरं बहिः // 162
text_mt: like Caitra; all that up to Suśiva has such a body. / Whatever body one has, outside of it is an abode of that same class.

sanskrit_iast:
ataḥ suśivaparyantā siddhā bhuvanapaddhatiḥ /
ātmanām tatpuraṃ prāpyaṃ deśatvādanyadeśavat // 163
meaning:
अतः सुशिवपर्यन्ता सिद्धा भुवनपद्धतिः /
आत्मनाम् तत्पुरं प्राप्यं देशत्वादन्यदेशवत् // 163
text_mt: Therefore, the series of worlds extending up to Suśiva is established. / That city is to be reached by souls because it is a place, like any other place.

sanskrit_iast:
ātmanāmadhvabhoktṛtvaṃ tato'yatnena siddhyati /
sā māyā kṣobhamāpannā viśvaṃ sūte samantataḥ // 164
meaning:
आत्मनामध्वभोक्तृत्वं ततोऽयत्नेन सिद्ध्यति /
सा माया क्षोभमापन्ना विश्वं सूते समन्ततः // 164
text_mt: Hence, the souls' status as enjoyers of the path is established effortlessly. / That māyā, undergoing agitation, brings forth the universe on every side,

sanskrit_iast:
daṇḍāhatevāmalakī phalāni kila yadyapi /
tathāpi tu tathā citrapaurvāparyāvabhāsanāt // 165
meaning:
दण्डाहतेवामलकी फलानि किल यद्यपि /
तथापि तु तथा चित्रपौर्वापर्यावभासनात् // 165
text_mt: just as an āmalakī tree struck with a stick [brings forth] fruits, indeed, although / even so, by appearing in such variegated succession,

sanskrit_iast:
māyākārye'pi tattvaughe kāryakāraṇatā mithaḥ /
sā yadyapyanyaśāstreṣu bahudhā dṛśyate sphuṭam // 166
meaning:
मायाकार्येऽपि तत्त्वौघे कार्यकारणता मिथः /
सा यद्यप्यन्यशास्त्रेषु बहुधा दृश्यते स्फुटम् // 166
text_mt: even in the mass of tattvas that are the effects of māyā, there is mutual cause-and-effect relation. / Although this is clearly seen in many ways in other scriptures,

sanskrit_iast:
tathāpi mālinīśāstradṛśā tāṃ saṃpracakṣmahe /
kalādivasudhāntaṃ yanmāyāntaḥ saṃpracakṣate // 167
meaning:
तथापि मालिनीशास्त्रदृशा तां संप्रचक्ष्महे /
कलादिवसुधान्तं यन्मायान्तः संप्रचक्षते // 167
text_mt: nonetheless we explain it according to the perspective of the Mālinīvijayottara. / What they explain within māyā, beginning with kalā and ending with the earth,

sanskrit_iast:
pratyātmabhinnamevaitat sukhaduḥkhādibhedataḥ /
ekasyāmeva jagati bhogasādhanasaṃhatau // 168
meaning:
प्रत्यात्मभिन्नमेवैतत् सुखदुःखादिभेदतः /
एकस्यामेव जगति भोगसाधनसंहतौ // 168
text_mt: is distinct for each individual soul, on account of the distinction of pleasure, pain, and the like. / In the single world, amidst the collection of instruments of enjoyment,

sanskrit_iast:
sukhādīnāṃ samaṃ vyakterbhogabhedaḥ kuto bhavet /
na cāsau karmabhedena tasyaivānupapattitaḥ // 169
meaning:
सुखादीनां समं व्यक्तेर्भोगभेदः कुतो भवेत् /
न चासौ कर्मभेदेन तस्यैवानुपपत्तितः // 169
text_mt: since pleasure and the rest are manifest equally, whence would arise difference in enjoyment? / Nor is this [difference] due to difference in karma, for that itself would be inexplicable.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmāt kalādiko vargo bhinna eva kadācana /
aikyametīśvarecchāto nṛttagītādivādane // 170
meaning:
तस्मात् कलादिको वर्गो भिन्न एव कदाचन /
ऐक्यमेतीश्वरेच्छातो नृत्तगीतादिवादने // 170
text_mt: Therefore, the group beginning with kalā is indeed distinct; at times / it attains unity through the will of the Lord, as in the performance of dance, song, and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
eṣāṃ kalāditattvānāṃ sarveṣāmapi bhāvinām /
śuddhatvamasti teṣāṃ ye śaktipātapavitritāḥ // 171
meaning:
एषां कलादितत्त्वानां सर्वेषामपि भाविनाम् /
शुद्धत्वमस्ति तेषां ये शक्तिपातपवित्रिताः // 171
text_mt: For all these existing tattvas beginning with kalā, / there is purity for those who have been purified by the descent of power.

sanskrit_iast:
kalā hi śuddhā tattādṛk karmatvaṃ saṃprasūyate /
mitamapyāśu yenāsmāt saṃsārādeṣa mucyate // 172
meaning:
कला हि शुद्धा तत्तादृक् कर्मत्वं संप्रसूयते /
मितमप्याशु येनास्मात् संसारादेष मुच्यते // 172
text_mt: For when kalā is pure, it brings forth that kind of state of action, / though limited, by which one is swiftly liberated from this saṃsāra.

sanskrit_iast:
rāgavidyākālayatiprakṛtyakṣārthasaṃcayaḥ /
itthaṃ śuddha iti procya gururmānastutau vibhuḥ // 173
meaning:
रागविद्याकालयतिप्रकृत्यक्षार्थसंचयः /
इत्थं शुद्ध इति प्रोच्य गुरुर्मानस्तुतौ विभुः // 173
text_mt: The collection consisting of rāga, vidyā, kāla, niyati, prakṛti, the senses, and objects / is thus pure; having declared this, the omnipresent guru in the hymn of the instruments of knowledge [said]:

sanskrit_iast:
evameṣā kalādīnāmutpattiḥ pravivicyate /
māyātattvāt kalā jātā kiṃcitkartṛtvalakṣaṇā // 174
meaning:
एवमेषा कलादीनामुत्पत्तिः प्रविविच्यते /
मायातत्त्वात् कला जाता किंचित्कर्तृत्वलक्षणा // 174
text_mt: In this way, this emergence of kalā and the rest is clearly discerned. / From the māyā-tattva arose kalā, characterized by limited agency.

sanskrit_iast:
māyā hi cinmayādbhedaṃ śivādvidadhatī paśoḥ /
suṣuptatāmivādhatte tata eva hyadṛkkriyaḥ // 175
meaning:
माया हि चिन्मयाद्भेदं शिवाद्विदधती पशोः /
सुषुप्ततामिवाधत्ते तत एव ह्यदृक्क्रियः // 175
text_mt: For māyā, producing the bound soul's separation from Śiva who is composed of consciousness, / brings about as it were a state of deep sleep; for that very reason, he is devoid of perception and action.

sanskrit_iast:
kalā hi kiṃcitkartṛtvaṃ sūte svāliṅganādaṇoḥ /
tasyāścāpyaṇunānyonyaṃ hyañjane sā prasūyate // 176
meaning:
कला हि किंचित्कर्तृत्वं सूते स्वालिङ्गनादणोः /
तस्याश्चाप्यणुनान्योन्यं ह्यञ्जने सा प्रसूयते // 176
text_mt: Kalā indeed generates limited agency by embracing the atom; / and when it is mutually tainted by the atom, it brings [effects] forth.

sanskrit_iast:
sadyonirvāṇadīkṣotthapuṃviśleṣe hi sā satī /
śliṣyantyapi ca no sūte tathāpi svaphalaṃ kvacit // 177
meaning:
सद्योनिर्वाणदीक्षोत्थपुंविश्लेषे हि सा सती /
श्लिष्यन्त्यपि च नो सूते तथापि स्वफलं क्वचित् // 177
text_mt: Indeed, when there is detachment of the soul arising from immediate-liberation initiation, even if it persists, / and even if it embraces, it never produces its fruit.

sanskrit_iast:
ucchūnateva prathamā sūkṣmāṅkurakaleva ca /
bījasyāmbvagnimṛtkambutuṣayogāt prasūtikṛt // 178
meaning:
उच्छूनतेव प्रथमा सूक्ष्माङ्कुरकलेव च /
बीजस्याम्ब्वग्निमृत्कम्बुतुषयोगात् प्रसूतिकृत् // 178
text_mt: Just like the first swelling and like the subtle sprout-portion / of a seed brings about generation through contact with water, heat, soil, shell, and chaff,

sanskrit_iast:
kalā māyāṇusaṃyogajāpyeṣā nirvikārakam /
nāṇuṃ kuryādupādānaṃ kiṃtu māyāṃ vikāriṇīm // 179
meaning:
कला मायाणुसंयोगजाप्येषा निर्विकारकम् /
नाणुं कुर्यादुपादानं किंतु मायां विकारिणीम् // 179
text_mt: so kalā, even though arisen from the contact of māyā and the atom, / does not make the immutable atom its material cause, but rather mutable māyā.

sanskrit_iast:
malaścāvārako māyā bhāvopādānakāraṇam /
karma syāt sahakāryeva sukhaduḥkhodbhavaṃ prati // 180
meaning:
मलश्चावारको माया भावोपादानकारणम् /
कर्म स्यात् सहकार्येव सुखदुःखोद्भवं प्रति // 180
text_mt: Mala is the obscuring [factor], māyā is the material cause of entities, / and karma would be merely an auxiliary cause with respect to the arising of pleasure and pain.

sanskrit_iast:
ataḥ saṃcchannacaitanyasamudbalanakāryakṛt /
kalaivānantanāthasya śaktyā saṃpreritā jaḍā // 181
meaning:
अतः संच्छन्नचैतन्यसमुद्बलनकार्यकृत् /
कलैवानन्तनाथस्य शक्त्या संप्रेरिता जडा // 181
text_mt: Therefore, insentient kalā alone, impelled by the power of Anantanātha, / accomplishes the effect of stimulating veiled consciousness.

sanskrit_iast:
na ceśaśaktirevāsya caitanyaṃ balayiṣyati /
tadupodbalitaṃ taddhi na kiṃcitkartṛtāṃ vrajet // 182
meaning:
न चेशशक्तिरेवास्य चैतन्यं बलयिष्यति /
तदुपोद्बलितं तद्धि न किंचित्कर्तृतां व्रजेत् // 182
text_mt: It is not the power of the Lord itself that will strengthen his consciousness; / for that which is stimulated by that would not enter into the state of limited agency.

sanskrit_iast:
seyaṃ kalā na karaṇaṃ mukhyaṃ vidyādikaṃ yathā /
puṃsi kartari sā kartrī prayojakatayā yataḥ // 183
meaning:
सेयं कला न करणं मुख्यं विद्यादिकं यथा /
पुंसि कर्तरि सा कर्त्री प्रयोजकतया यतः // 183
text_mt: This kalā is not an instrument in the primary sense, like vidyā and the rest; / for while the soul is the agent, it is an agent by virtue of being an instigator.

sanskrit_iast:
alakṣyāntarayoritthaṃ yadā puṃskalayorbhavet /
māyāgarbheśaśaktyāderantarajñānamāntaram // 184
meaning:
अलक्ष्यान्तरयोरित्थं यदा पुंस्कलयोर्भवेत् /
मायागर्भेशशक्त्यादेरन्तरज्ञानमान्तरम् // 184
text_mt: When, between the puruṣa and kalā whose distinction is thus unnoticed, / there arises an internal knowledge of difference, through the power of the Lord within māyā,

sanskrit_iast:
tadā māyāpuṃvivekaḥ sarvakarmakṣayādbhavet /
vijñānākalatā māyādhastānno yātyadhaḥ pumān // 185
meaning:
तदा मायापुंविवेकः सर्वकर्मक्षयाद्भवेत् /
विज्ञानाकलता मायाधस्तान्नो यात्यधः पुमान् // 185
text_mt: then the discernment of māyā and the puruṣa takes place through the exhaustion of all karma. / The state of being a knower free of instruments [arises]; the puruṣa does not go down below māyā.

sanskrit_iast:
dhīpuṃviveke vijñāte pradhānapuruṣāntare /
api na kṣīṇakarmā syāt kalāyāṃ taddhi saṃbhavet // 186
meaning:
धीपुंविवेके विज्ञाते प्रधानपुरुषान्तरे /
अपि न क्षीणकर्मा स्यात् कलायां तद्धि संभवेत् // 186
text_mt: Even when the discernment of intellect and puruṣa is known, between pradhāna and the puruṣa, / one would not have one's karma destroyed; for that can occur [only] at [the level of] kalā.

sanskrit_iast:
ataḥ sāṃkhyadṛśā siddhaḥ pradhānādho na saṃsaret /
kalāpuṃsorviveke tu māyādho naiva gacchati // 187
meaning:
अतः सांख्यदृशा सिद्धः प्रधानाधो न संसरेत् /
कलापुंसोर्विवेके तु मायाधो नैव गच्छति // 187
text_mt: Therefore, one who is perfected according to the Sāṃkhya view does not transmigrate below pradhāna; / but when discernment between kalā and the puruṣa occurs, he never goes below māyā.

sanskrit_iast:
malādviviktamātmānaṃ paśyaṃstu śivatāṃ vrajet /
sarvatra caiśvaraḥ śaktipāto'tra sahakāraṇam // 188
meaning:
मलाद्विविक्तमात्मानं पश्यंस्तु शिवतां व्रजेत् /
सर्वत्र चैश्वरः शक्तिपातोऽत्र सहकारणम् // 188
text_mt: Seeing himself distinguished from mala, however, he attains the state of Śiva. / And in every case, the divine descent of power is the auxiliary cause here.

sanskrit_iast:
māyāgarbhādhikārīyo dvayorantye tu nirmalaḥ /
seyaṃ kalā kāryabhedādanyaiva hyanumīyate // 189
meaning:
मायागर्भाधिकारीयो द्वयोरन्त्ये तु निर्मलः /
सेयं कला कार्यभेदादन्यैव ह्यनुमीयते // 189
text_mt: In the case of the [first] two, [the soul] is qualified within the womb of māyā; in the last, however, he is free of impurity. / This kalā is inferred to be distinct precisely through the difference in effects;

sanskrit_iast:
anyathaikaṃ bhavedviśvaṃ kāryāyetyanyanihnavaḥ /
iti mataṅgaśāstrādau yā proktā sā kalā svayam // 190
meaning:
अन्यथैकं भवेद्विश्वं कार्यायेत्यन्यनिह्नवः /
इति मतङ्गशास्त्रादौ या प्रोक्ता सा कला स्वयम् // 190
text_mt: otherwise, the universe would be one for an effect, and thus there would be denial of others. / That which is stated in the Mataṅga and other scriptures is itself kalā.

sanskrit_iast:
kiṃcidrūpatayākṣipya kartṛtvamiti bhaṅgitaḥ /
kiṃcidrūpaviśiṣṭaṃ yat kartṛtvaṃ tatkathaṃ bhavet // 191
meaning:
किंचिद्रूपतयाक्षिप्य कर्तृत्वमिति भङ्गितः /
किंचिद्रूपविशिष्टं यत् कर्तृत्वं तत्कथं भवेत् // 191
text_mt: Impugning agency as having a limited nature, in this indirect way: / How could agency qualified by a limited nature exist

sanskrit_iast:
ajñasyeti tataḥ sūte kiṃcijjñatvātmikāṃ vidam /
buddhiṃ paśyati sā vidyā buddhidarpaṇacāriṇaḥ // 192
meaning:
अज्ञस्येति ततः सूते किंचिज्ज्ञत्वात्मिकां विदम् /
बुद्धिं पश्यति सा विद्या बुद्धिदर्पणचारिणः // 192
text_mt: for an ignorant one? Hence, it produces vidyā, which consists in limited knowing. / That vidyā perceives the intellect; moving in the mirror of the intellect,

sanskrit_iast:
sukhādīn pratyayān mohaprabhṛtīn kāryakāraṇe /
karmajālaṃ ca tatrasthaṃ vivinakti nijātmanā // 193
meaning:
सुखादीन् प्रत्ययान् मोहप्रभृतीन् कार्यकारणे /
कर्मजालं च तत्रस्थं विविनक्ति निजात्मना // 193
text_mt: it distinguishes through itself the mental states of pleasure and the like, delusion and so forth, in effect and cause, / as well as the web of karma situated there.

sanskrit_iast:
buddhistu guṇasaṃkīrṇā vivekena kathaṃ sukham /
duḥkhaṃ mohātmakaṃ vāpi viṣayaṃ darśayedapi // 194
meaning:
बुद्धिस्तु गुणसंकीर्णा विवेकेन कथं सुखम् /
दुःखं मोहात्मकं वापि विषयं दर्शयेदपि // 194
text_mt: The intellect, however, is blended with the guṇas; how could it reveal, through discrimination, / an object consisting of pleasure, pain, or delusion?

sanskrit_iast:
svacchāyāṃ dhiyi saṃkrāmanbhāvaḥ saṃvedyatāṃ katham /
tayā vinaiti sāpyanyatkaraṇaṃ puṃsi kartari // 195
meaning:
स्वच्छायां धियि संक्रामन्भावः संवेद्यतां कथम् /
तया विनैति साप्यन्यत्करणं पुंसि कर्तरि // 195
text_mt: How could an entity entering the transparent intellect attain the state of being cognized / without that [vidyā]? It too is another instrument for the puruṣa as agent.

sanskrit_iast:
nanu cobhayataḥ śubhrādarśadaśīyadhīgatāt /
puṃsprakāśādbhāti bhāvaḥ maivaṃ tatpratibimbanam // 196
meaning:
ननु चोभयतः शुभ्रादर्शदशीयधीगतात् /
पुंस्प्रकाशाद्भाति भावः मैवं तत्प्रतिबिम्बनम् // 196
text_mt: 'Surely, an entity shines from the puruṣa's light, which is situated in the intellect acting as a mirror pure on both sides?' / Not so; that reflection

sanskrit_iast:
jaḍameva hi mukhyo'tha puṃsprakāśo'sya bhāsanam /
bahiḥsthasyaiva tasyāstu buddheḥ kiṃkalpanā kṛtā // 197
meaning:
जडमेव हि मुख्योऽथ पुंस्प्रकाशोऽस्य भासनम् /
बहिःस्थस्यैव तस्यास्तु बुद्धेः किंकल्पना कृता // 197
text_mt: is indeed insentient. Or if the primary light of the puruṣa is its manifestation / while remaining strictly external, why was the conception of the intellect fabricated?

sanskrit_iast:
abhedabhūmireṣā ca bhedaśceha vicāryate /
tasmādbuddhigato bhāvo vidyākaraṇagocaraḥ // 198
meaning:
अभेदभूमिरेषा च भेदश्चेह विचार्यते /
तस्माद्बुद्धिगतो भावो विद्याकरणगोचरः // 198
text_mt: And this is the ground of non-difference, whereas here difference is being investigated. / Therefore, an object situated in the intellect is the province of the instrument of [limited] knowledge (vidyā).

sanskrit_iast:
bhāvānāṃ pratibimbaṃ ca vedyaṃ dhīkalpanā tataḥ /
kiṃcittu kurute tasmānnūnamastyaparaṃ tu tat // 199
meaning:
भावानां प्रतिबिम्बं च वेद्यं धीकल्पना ततः /
किंचित्तु कुरुते तस्मान्नूनमस्त्यपरं तु तत् // 199
text_mt: And the reflection of objects is the knowable; the construct of the intellect [arises] therefrom. / Yet [the soul] acts to some limited extent; therefore, that other [factor] certainly exists.

sanskrit_iast:
rāgatattvamiti proktaṃ yattatraivoparañjakam /
na cāvairāgyamātraṃ tattatrāpyāsaktivṛttitaḥ // 200
meaning:
रागतत्त्वमिति प्रोक्तं यत्तत्रैवोपरञ्जकम् /
न चावैराग्यमात्रं तत्तत्राप्यासक्तिवृत्तितः // 200
text_mt: The principle of attachment (rāga) is taught to be that which causes coloring precisely there. / Nor is it merely the absence of dispassion, because an orientation toward attachment exists even there,

sanskrit_iast:
viraktāvapi tṛptasya sūkṣmarāgavyavasthiteḥ /
kālastuṭyādibhiścaitat kartṛtvaṃ kalayatyataḥ // 201
meaning:
विरक्तावपि तृप्तस्य सूक्ष्मरागव्यवस्थितेः /
कालस्तुट्यादिभिश्चैतत् कर्तृत्वं कलयत्यतः // 201
text_mt: Since subtle attachment persists even in one who is dispassionate and satisfied. / But time (kāla) limits this agency through moments (tuṭi) and the like; therefore,

sanskrit_iast:
kāryāvacchedi kartṛtvaṃ kālo'vaśyaṃ kaliṣyati /
niyatiryojanāṃ dhatte viśiṣṭe kāryamaṇḍale // 202
meaning:
कार्यावच्छेदि कर्तृत्वं कालोऽवश्यं कलिष्यति /
नियतिर्योजनां धत्ते विशिष्टे कार्यमण्डले // 202
text_mt: Time must inevitably restrict agency by delimiting its effects. / Restriction (niyati) brings about connection with a specific sphere of effects.

sanskrit_iast:
vidyā rāgo'tha niyatiḥ kālaścaitaccatuṣṭayam /
kalākāryaṃ bhoktṛbhāve tiṣṭhadbhoktṛtvapūritam // 203
meaning:
विद्या रागोऽथ नियतिः कालश्चैतच्चतुष्टयम् /
कलाकार्यं भोक्तृभावे तिष्ठद्भोक्तृत्वपूरितम् // 203
text_mt: [Limited] knowledge (vidyā), attachment (rāga), restriction (niyati), and time (kāla)—this group of four / is the effect of limited agency (kalā); abiding in the state of the experiencer, it fulfills the nature of being an experiencer.

sanskrit_iast:
māyā kalā rāgavidye kālo niyatireva ca /
kañcukāni ṣaḍuktāni saṃvidastatsthitau paśuḥ // 204
meaning:
माया कला रागविद्ये कालो नियतिरेव च /
कञ्चुकानि षडुक्तानि संविदस्तत्स्थितौ पशुः // 204
text_mt: Māyā, limited agency (kalā), attachment, [limited] knowledge, time, and restriction— / these are taught to be the six cuirasses of consciousness; when abiding therein, [consciousness] is a bound soul.

sanskrit_iast:
dehapuryaṣṭakādyeṣu vedyeṣu kila vedanam /
etatṣaṭkasasaṃkocaṃ yadavedyamasāvaṇuḥ // 205
meaning:
देहपुर्यष्टकाद्येषु वेद्येषु किल वेदनम् /
एतत्षट्कससंकोचं यदवेद्यमसावणुः // 205
text_mt: Among the knowables such as the body, the subtle body (puryaṣṭaka), and so on, cognition indeed [arises]; / that which, having the contraction of this group of six, is unknowable—that is the individual soul (aṇu).

sanskrit_iast:
uktaṃ śivatanuśāstre tadidaṃ bhaṅgyantareṇa punaḥ /
āvaraṇaṃ sarvātmagamaśuddhiranyāpyananyarūpeva // 206
meaning:
उक्तं शिवतनुशास्त्रे तदिदं भङ्ग्यन्तरेण पुनः /
आवरणं सर्वात्मगमशुद्धिरन्याप्यनन्यरूपेव // 206
text_mt: This same point has been stated once more in another manner in the Śivatanuśāstra: / ‘The covering is all-pervading; the other impurity is as if non-different in form.’

sanskrit_iast:
śivadahanakiraṇajālairdāhyatvāt sā yato'nyarūpaiva /
anidaṃpūrvatayā yadrañjayati nijātmanā tato'nanyā // 207
meaning:
शिवदहनकिरणजालैर्दाह्यत्वात् सा यतोऽन्यरूपैव /
अनिदंपूर्वतया यद्रञ्जयति निजात्मना ततोऽनन्या // 207
text_mt: Because it can be burned by the cluster of rays of the fire of Śiva, it is indeed different in form; / because it colors by its own nature without being preceded by ‘thisness’, it is non-different.

sanskrit_iast:
sahajāśuddhimato'ṇorīśaguhābhyāṃ hi kañcukastrividhaḥ /
tasya dvitīyacitiriva svacchasya niyujyate kalā ślakṣṇā // 208
meaning:
सहजाशुद्धिमतोऽणोरीशगुहाभ्यां हि कञ्चुकस्त्रिविधः /
तस्य द्वितीयचितिरिव स्वच्छस्य नियुज्यते कला श्लक्ष्णा // 208
text_mt: For the individual soul possessed of innate impurity, a threefold cuirass is produced by the Lord and Guha; / for that clear [soul], subtle kalā is joined like a second consciousness.

sanskrit_iast:
anayā vidvasya paśorupabhogasamarthatā bhavati /
vidyā cāsya kalātaḥ śaraṇāntardīpakaprabhevābhūt // 209
meaning:
अनया विद्वस्य पशोरुपभोगसमर्थता भवति /
विद्या चास्य कलातः शरणान्तर्दीपकप्रभेवाभूत् // 209
text_mt: Being impelled by this, the bound soul’s capacity for enjoyment arises; / and from kalā his [limited] knowledge arose, like the light of a lamp inside a house,

sanskrit_iast:
sukhaduḥkhasaṃvidaṃ yā vivinakti paśorvibhāgena /
rāgaśca kalātattvācchucivastrakaṣāyavat samutpannaḥ // 210
meaning:
सुखदुःखसंविदं या विविनक्ति पशोर्विभागेन /
रागश्च कलातत्त्वाच्छुचिवस्त्रकषायवत् समुत्पन्नः // 210
text_mt: Which discerns the consciousness of pleasure and pain distinctly for the bound soul. / And attachment is produced from the principle of kalā, like an astringent dye on a clean cloth,

sanskrit_iast:
tyaktuṃ vāñchati na yataḥ saṃsṛtisukhasaṃvidānandam /
evamavidyāmalinaḥsamarthitastriguṇakañcukabalena // 211
meaning:
त्यक्तुं वाञ्छति न यतः संसृतिसुखसंविदानन्दम् /
एवमविद्यामलिनःसमर्थितस्त्रिगुणकञ्चुकबलेन // 211
text_mt: Since he does not wish to abandon the joy of experiencing pleasure in cyclic existence (saṃsāra). / In this way, soiled by ignorance and empowered by the force of the three-attribute cuirass,

sanskrit_iast:
gahanopabhogagarbhe paśuravaśamadhomukhaḥ patati /
etena malaḥ kathitaḥ kambukavadaṇoḥ kalādikaṃ tuṣavat // 212
meaning:
गहनोपभोगगर्भे पशुरवशमधोमुखः पतति /
एतेन मलः कथितः कम्बुकवदणोः कलादिकं तुषवत् // 212
text_mt: The bound soul falls helplessly headlong into the abyss of enjoyment. / By this, impurity is described as being like the husk of the grain for the individual soul, and kalā and the rest like the chaff.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ kalākhyatattvasya kiṃcitkartṛtvalakṣaṇe /
viśeṣabhāge kartṛtvaṃ carcitaṃ bhoktṛpūrvakam // 213
meaning:
एवं कलाख्यतत्त्वस्य किंचित्कर्तृत्वलक्षणे /
विशेषभागे कर्तृत्वं चर्चितं भोक्तृपूर्वकम् // 213
text_mt: Thus, in the specific aspect characterized as ‘limited agency’ belonging to the principle called kalā, / agency has been discussed, preceded by the experiencer.

sanskrit_iast:
viśeṣaṇatayā yo'tra kiñcidbhāgastadotthitam /
vedyamātraṃ sphuṭaṃ bhinnaṃ pradhānaṃ sūyate kalā // 214
meaning:
विशेषणतया योऽत्र किञ्चिद्भागस्तदोत्थितम् /
वेद्यमात्रं स्फुटं भिन्नं प्रधानं सूयते कला // 214
text_mt: The limited aspect which is present here as a qualification—from that arises / the mere knowable, distinct and differentiated: kalā gives birth to the primal matter (pradhāna).

sanskrit_iast:
samameva hi bhogyaṃ ca bhoktāraṃ ca prasūyate /
kalā bhedābhisaṃdhānādaviyuktaṃ parasparam // 215
meaning:
सममेव हि भोग्यं च भोक्तारं च प्रसूयते /
कला भेदाभिसंधानादवियुक्तं परस्परम् // 215
text_mt: For simultaneously kalā gives birth to both the enjoyable and the experiencer / without separation from one another, through the intent toward differentiation.

sanskrit_iast:
bhoktṛbhogyātmatā na syādviyogācca parasparam /
vilīnāyāṃ ca tasyāṃ syānmāyāsyāpi na kiṃcana // 216
meaning:
भोक्तृभोग्यात्मता न स्याद्वियोगाच्च परस्परम् /
विलीनायां च तस्यां स्यान्मायास्यापि न किंचन // 216
text_mt: Nor can there be the nature of experiencer and enjoyable if there is mutual separation; / and when that [kalā] is dissolved, there would be nothing at all even for māyā.

sanskrit_iast:
nanu śrīmadrauravādau rāgavidyātmakaṃ dvayam /
sūte kalā hi yugapattato'vyaktamiti sthitiḥ // 217
meaning:
ननु श्रीमद्रौरवादौ रागविद्यात्मकं द्वयम् /
सूते कला हि युगपत्ततोऽव्यक्तमिति स्थितिः // 217
text_mt: [Objection:] But in the venerable Raurava and other scriptures [it is said that] the dyad consisting of attachment and [limited] knowledge / is indeed produced by kalā simultaneously, and after that the unmanifest (avyakta)—such is the established view.

sanskrit_iast:
uktamatra vibhātyeṣa kramaḥ satyaṃ tathā hyalam /
rajyamāno veda sarva vidaṃścāpyatra rajyate // 218
meaning:
उक्तमत्र विभात्येष क्रमः सत्यं तथा ह्यलम् /
रज्यमानो वेद सर्व विदंश्चाप्यत्र रज्यते // 218
text_mt: [Response:] It has been stated in this regard that this sequence appears; it is true, for fully indeed / one who is attached knows all, and knowing, one is also attached in this regard.

sanskrit_iast:
tathāpi vastusatteyamihāsmābhirnirūpitā /
tasyāṃ ca na kramaḥ ko'pi syādvā so'pi viparyayāt // 219
meaning:
तथापि वस्तुसत्तेयमिहास्माभिर्निरूपिता /
तस्यां च न क्रमः कोऽपि स्याद्वा सोऽपि विपर्ययात् // 219
text_mt: Nevertheless, it is the true state of the entity that has been determined by us here; / and in that regard, there is no sequence whatever, or that [order] too may be from inverted view.

sanskrit_iast:
tasmādvipratipattiṃ no kuryācchāstrodite vidhau /
evaṃ saṃvedyamātraṃ yat sukhaduḥkhavimohataḥ // 220
meaning:
तस्माद्विप्रतिपत्तिं नो कुर्याच्छास्त्रोदिते विधौ /
एवं संवेद्यमात्रं यत् सुखदुःखविमोहतः // 220
text_mt: Therefore, one should not raise a contradiction against the rule stated in the scripture. / In this way, whatever is merely to be experienced through pleasure, pain, and delusion,

sanskrit_iast:
bhotsyate yattataḥ proktaṃ tatsāmyātmakamāditaḥ /
sukhaṃ sattvaṃ prakāśatvāt prakāśo hlāda ucyate // 221
meaning:
भोत्स्यते यत्ततः प्रोक्तं तत्साम्यात्मकमादितः /
सुखं सत्त्वं प्रकाशत्वात् प्रकाशो ह्लाद उच्यते // 221
text_mt: Is experienced; therefore it is taught from the beginning to consist of their equilibrium. / Pleasure is sattva because it is luminous; luminosity is said to be delight.

sanskrit_iast:
duḥkhaṃ rajaḥ kriyātmatvād kriyā hi tadatatkramaḥ /
mohastamo varaṇakaḥ prakāśābhāvayogataḥ // 222
meaning:
दुःखं रजः क्रियात्मत्वाद् क्रिया हि तदतत्क्रमः /
मोहस्तमो वरणकः प्रकाशाभावयोगतः // 222
text_mt: Pain is rajas because it consists of action, for action is indeed the sequence of this and not-this; / delusion is tamas, a veil, because of its association with the absence of light.

sanskrit_iast:
ta ete kṣobhamāpannā guṇāḥ kārya pratanvate /
akṣubdhasya vijātīyaṃ na syāt kāryamadaḥ purā // 223
meaning:
त एते क्षोभमापन्ना गुणाः कार्य प्रतन्वते /
अक्षुब्धस्य विजातीयं न स्यात् कार्यमदः पुरा // 223
text_mt: These very qualities (guṇa), having attained agitation, spread forth their effects. / For an unagitated [entity], there could not be a heterogeneous effect such as this; earlier

sanskrit_iast:
uktameveti śāstre'smin guṇāṃstattvāntaraṃ viduḥ /
bhuvanaṃ pṛthagevātra darśitaṃ guṇabhedataḥ // 224
meaning:
उक्तमेवेति शास्त्रेऽस्मिन् गुणांस्तत्त्वान्तरं विदुः /
भुवनं पृथगेवात्र दर्शितं गुणभेदतः // 224
text_mt: It has indeed been stated thus: in this scripture, they understand the qualities to be a distinct reality; / a distinct realm is shown here due to the differentiation of the qualities.

sanskrit_iast:
īśvarecchāvaśakṣubdhalolikaṃ puruṣaṃ prati /
bhoktṛtvāya svatantreśaḥ prakṛtiṃ kṣobhayed bhṛśam // 225
meaning:
ईश्वरेच्छावशक्षुब्धलोलिकं पुरुषं प्रति /
भोक्तृत्वाय स्वतन्त्रेशः प्रकृतिं क्षोभयेद् भृशम् // 225
text_mt: Toward the individual soul whose desire is stirred under the influence of the Lord’s will, / the autonomous Lord violently agitates prakṛti for the sake of [his] status as an experiencer.

sanskrit_iast:
tena yaccodyate sāṃkhyaṃ muktāṇuṃ prati kiṃ na sā /
sūte puṃso vikāritvāditi tannātra bādhakam // 226
meaning:
तेन यच्चोद्यते सांख्यं मुक्ताणुं प्रति किं न सा /
सूते पुंसो विकारित्वादिति तन्नात्र बाधकम् // 226
text_mt: Therefore, the objection raised against the Sāṅkhya—why does it not / produce for the liberated soul, since the soul is mutable?—does not subvert our position.

sanskrit_iast:
guṇebhyo buddhitattvaṃ tat sarvato nirmalaṃ tataḥ /
puṃsprakāśaḥ sa vedyo'tra pratibimbatvamārchati // 227
meaning:
गुणेभ्यो बुद्धितत्त्वं तत् सर्वतो निर्मलं ततः /
पुंस्प्रकाशः स वेद्योऽत्र प्रतिबिम्बत्वमार्छति // 227
text_mt: From the qualities [arises] the principle of intellect, which is completely pure; therefore / the luminosity of the soul, as an object of knowledge, attains reflection in it.

sanskrit_iast:
viṣayapratibimbaṃ ca tasyāmakṣakṛtaṃ bahiḥ /
ataddvāraṃ samutprekṣāpratibhādiṣu tādṛśī // 228
meaning:
विषयप्रतिबिम्बं च तस्यामक्षकृतं बहिः /
अतद्द्वारं समुत्प्रेक्षाप्रतिभादिषु तादृशी // 228
text_mt: And the reflection of external objects in it is produced by the senses; / in conjecture, intuition, and so on, such an operation of the intellect

sanskrit_iast:
vṛttirbodho bhavedbuddheḥ sā cāpyālambanaṃ dhruvam /
ātmasaṃvitprakāśasya bodho'sau tajjaḍo'pyalam // 229
meaning:
वृत्तिर्बोधो भवेद्बुद्धेः सा चाप्यालम्बनं ध्रुवम् /
आत्मसंवित्प्रकाशस्य बोधोऽसौ तज्जडोऽप्यलम् // 229
text_mt: Independent of those [external senses] is cognition; and that is certainly the support / for the luminosity of the consciousness of the Self; although insentient, that cognition is fully [adequate for this].

sanskrit_iast:
buddherahaṃkṛt tādṛkṣe pratibimbitapuṃskṛteḥ /
prakāśe vedyakaluṣe yadahaṃmananātmatā // 230
meaning:
बुद्धेरहंकृत् तादृक्षे प्रतिबिम्बितपुंस्कृतेः /
प्रकाशे वेद्यकलुषे यदहंमननात्मता // 230
text_mt: From the intellect [arises] the ego (ahaṃkāra) in such [a condition]: when in the light wherein the soul is reflected / and which is tainted by knowables, there is the state of conceiving an ‘I’.

sanskrit_iast:
tayā pañcavidhaścaiṣa vāyuḥ saṃrambharūpayā /
prerito jīvanāya syādanyathā maraṇaṃ punaḥ // 231
meaning:
तया पञ्चविधश्चैष वायुः संरम्भरूपया /
प्रेरितो जीवनाय स्यादन्यथा मरणं पुनः // 231
text_mt: By this [ego], which takes the form of zealous effort, this fivefold vital breath / is impelled for the sake of living; otherwise, death would ensue.

sanskrit_iast:
ata eva viśuddhātmasvātantryāhaṃsvabhāvataḥ /
akṛtrimādidaṃ tvanyadityuktaṃ kṛtiśabdataḥ // 232
meaning:
अत एव विशुद्धात्मस्वातन्त्र्याहंस्वभावतः /
अकृत्रिमादिदं त्वन्यदित्युक्तं कृतिशब्दतः // 232
text_mt: Precisely for this reason, this is [taught to be] different from the unartificial nature of ‘I’ which is the absolute autonomy of the pure Self; / this is indicated by the word ‘making’ (kṛti) [in ahaṃkāra].

sanskrit_iast:
ityayaṃ karaṇaskandho'haṃkārasya nirūpitaḥ /
tridhāsya prakṛtiskandhaḥ sāttvarājasatāmasaḥ // 233
meaning:
इत्ययं करणस्कन्धोऽहंकारस्य निरूपितः /
त्रिधास्य प्रकृतिस्कन्धः सात्त्वराजसतामसः // 233
text_mt: Thus this instrument-aggregate of the ego has been described. / Its aggregate of prakṛti is threefold: sāttvika, rājasika, and tāmasika.

sanskrit_iast:
sattvapradhānāhaṃkārādbhoktraṃśasparśinaḥ sphuṭam /
manobuddhyakṣaṣaṭkaṃ tu jātaṃ bhedastu kathyate // 234
meaning:
सत्त्वप्रधानाहंकाराद्भोक्त्रंशस्पर्शिनः स्फुटम् /
मनोबुद्ध्यक्षषट्कं तु जातं भेदस्तु कथ्यते // 234
text_mt: From the ego dominated by sattva, touching the aspect of the experiencer, clearly / the group of six consisting of the mind and the cognitive senses is born; but the division is explained:

sanskrit_iast:
mano yatsarvaviṣayaṃ tenātra pravivakṣitam /
sarvatanmātrakartṛtvaṃ viśeṣaṇamahaṃkṛteḥ // 235
meaning:
मनो यत्सर्वविषयं तेनात्र प्रविवक्षितम् /
सर्वतन्मात्रकर्तृत्वं विशेषणमहंकृतेः // 235
text_mt: Because the mind has all things as its object, what is intended to be expressed here / is agency over all subtle elements (tanmātra) as a qualification of the ego.

sanskrit_iast:
buddhyahaṃkṛnmanaḥ prāhurbodhasaṃrabhaṇaiṣaṇe /
karaṇaṃ bāhyadevairyannaivāpyantarmukhaiḥ kṛtam // 236
meaning:
बुद्ध्यहंकृन्मनः प्राहुर्बोधसंरभणैषणे /
करणं बाह्यदेवैर्यन्नैवाप्यन्तर्मुखैः कृतम् // 236
text_mt: They say that intellect, ego, and mind are the instruments in cognizing, making effort, and willing, / which are not accomplished by external deities, nor even by internal-facing ones.

sanskrit_iast:
prāṇaśca nāntaḥkaraṇaṃ jaḍatvāt preraṇātmanaḥ /
prayatnecchāvibodhāṃśahetutvāditi niścitam // 237
meaning:
प्राणश्च नान्तःकरणं जडत्वात् प्रेरणात्मनः /
प्रयत्नेच्छाविबोधांशहेतुत्वादिति निश्चितम् // 237
text_mt: And the vital breath is not an internal organ because it is insentient, being an impelling force, / whereas [the internal organ] is determined to be the cause of the aspects of exertion, will, and knowledge.

sanskrit_iast:
avasāyo'bhimānaśca kalpanā ceti na kriyā /
ekarūpā tatastritvaṃ yuktamantaḥkṛtau sphuṭam // 238
meaning:
अवसायोऽभिमानश्च कल्पना चेति न क्रिया /
एकरूपा ततस्त्रित्वं युक्तमन्तःकृतौ स्फुटम् // 238
text_mt: Ascertainment, conceit, and mental construction—the action is not / of a single form; therefore, the threefold division in the internal organ is clearly justified.

sanskrit_iast:
na ca buddhirasaṃvedyā karaṇatvānmano yathā /
pradhānavadasaṃvedyabuddhivādastadujjhitaḥ // 239
meaning:
न च बुद्धिरसंवेद्या करणत्वान्मनो यथा /
प्रधानवदसंवेद्यबुद्धिवादस्तदुज्झितः // 239
text_mt: Nor is the intellect unexperienced, because it is an instrument, like the mind; / therefore the doctrine that the intellect is unexperienced like pradhāna is discarded.

sanskrit_iast:
śabdatanmātrahetutvaviśiṣṭā yā tvahaṃkṛtiḥ /
sā śrotre karaṇaṃ yāvadghrāṇe gandhatvabhoditā // 240
meaning:
शब्दतन्मात्रहेतुत्वविशिष्टा या त्वहंकृतिः /
सा श्रोत्रे करणं यावद्घ्राणे गन्धत्वभोदिता // 240
text_mt: The ego qualified by being the cause of the subtle element of sound / is the instrument with respect to the ear, up to [that which is] awakened by the quality of odor in the nose.

sanskrit_iast:
bhautikatvamato'pyastu niyamādviṣayeṣvalam /
ahaṃ śṛṇomi paśyāmi jighrāmītyādisaṃvidi // 241
meaning:
भौतिकत्वमतोऽप्यस्तु नियमाद्विषयेष्वलम् /
अहं शृणोमि पश्यामि जिघ्रामीत्यादिसंविदि // 241
text_mt: Let it also be elemental on account of the restriction to specific objects; / in the experience ‘I hear, I see, I smell,’ and so on,

sanskrit_iast:
ahaṃtānugamādāhaṃkārikatvaṃ sphuṭaṃ sthitam /
karaṇatvamato yuktaṃ kartraśaspṛktvayogataḥ // 242
meaning:
अहंतानुगमादाहंकारिकत्वं स्फुटं स्थितम् /
करणत्वमतो युक्तं कर्त्रशस्पृक्त्वयोगतः // 242
text_mt: Because it follows the sense of ‘I’, origin from the ego is clearly established; / therefore, its nature as an instrument is appropriate, through its connection with touching the aspect of the agent.

sanskrit_iast:
karturvibhinnaṃ karaṇaṃ preryatvāt karaṇaṃ kutaḥ /
karaṇāntaravāñchāyāṃ bhavettatrānavasthitiḥ // 243
meaning:
कर्तुर्विभिन्नं करणं प्रेर्यत्वात् करणं कुतः /
करणान्तरवाञ्छायां भवेत्तत्रानवस्थितिः // 243
text_mt: How can an instrument distinct from the agent be an instrument, since it must be impelled [by him]? / If another instrument is required [to impel it], there would be an infinite regress. // 243

sanskrit_iast:
tasmāt svātantryayogena kartā svaṃ bhedayan vapuḥ /
karmāśasparśinaṃ svāṃśaṃ karaṇīkurute svayam // 244
meaning:
तस्मात् स्वातन्त्र्ययोगेन कर्ता स्वं भेदयन् वपुः /
कर्माशस्पर्शिनं स्वांशं करणीकुरुते स्वयम् // 244
text_mt: Therefore, by virtue of his absolute autonomy, the agent, differentiating his own body, / makes a part of himself that touches the object-portion into an instrument by himself. // 244

sanskrit_iast:
karaṇīkṛtatatsvāṃśatanmayībhāvanāvaśāt /
karaṇīkurute'tyantavyatiriktaṃ kuṭhāravat // 245
meaning:
करणीकृततत्स्वांशतन्मयीभावनावशात् /
करणीकुरुतेऽत्यन्तव्यतिरिक्तं कुठारवत् // 245
text_mt: Through the power of identifying with that part of himself made into an instrument, / he turns something entirely distinct into an instrument, just like an axe. // 245

sanskrit_iast:
tenāśuddhaiva vidyāsya sāmānyaṃ karaṇaṃ purā /
jñaptau kṛtau tu sāmānyaṃ kalā karaṇamucyate // 246
meaning:
तेनाशुद्धैव विद्यास्य सामान्यं करणं पुरा /
ज्ञप्तौ कृतौ तु सामान्यं कला करणमुच्यते // 246
text_mt: For this reason, impure vidyā alone is his general instrument beforehand / in knowing; but in action, kalā is said to be the general instrument. // 246

sanskrit_iast:
nanu śrīmanmataṅgādau kalāyāḥ kartṛtoditā /
tasyāṃ satyāṃ hi vidyādyāḥ karaṇatvārhatājuṣaḥ // 247
meaning:
ननु श्रीमन्मतङ्गादौ कलायाः कर्तृतोदिता /
तस्यां सत्यां हि विद्याद्याः करणत्वार्हताजुषः // 247
text_mt: [Objection:] But in the venerable Mataṅga and other texts, kalā is declared to possess agency; / indeed, when it exists, vidyā and the others partake of suitability to be instruments. // 247

sanskrit_iast:
ucyate kartṛtaivoktā karaṇatve prayojikā /
tayā vinā tu nānyeṣāṃ karaṇānāṃ sthitiryataḥ // 248
meaning:
उच्यते कर्तृतैवोक्ता करणत्वे प्रयोजिका /
तया विना तु नान्येषां करणानां स्थितिर्यतः // 248
text_mt: [Response:] It is said in reply: agency alone is taught as the instigator in instrumentness, / for without it there is no existence of the other instruments. // 248

sanskrit_iast:
ato'sāmānyakaraṇavargāt tatra pṛthak kṛtā /
vidyāṃ vinā hi nānyeṣāṃ karaṇānāṃ nijā sthitiḥ // 249
meaning:
अतोऽसामान्यकरणवर्गात् तत्र पृथक् कृता /
विद्यां विना हि नान्येषां करणानां निजा स्थितिः // 249
text_mt: Therefore, it is separated there from the class of general instruments, / for without vidyā the other instruments have no existence of their own. // 249

sanskrit_iast:
kalāṃ vinā na tasyāśca kartṛtve jñātṛtā yataḥ /
kalāvidye tataḥ puṃso mukhyaṃ tatkaraṇaṃ viduḥ // 250
meaning:
कलां विना न तस्याश्च कर्तृत्वे ज्ञातृता यतः /
कलाविद्ये ततः पुंसो मुख्यं तत्करणं विदुः // 250
text_mt: And without kalā, [vidyā] has no [existence], since knowership exists within agency; / therefore, they consider kalā and vidyā to be the primary instruments of the person. // 250

sanskrit_iast:
ata eva vihīne'pi buddhikarmendriyaiḥ kvacit /
andhe paṅgau rūpagatiprakāśo na na bhāsate // 251
meaning:
अत एव विहीनेऽपि बुद्धिकर्मेन्द्रियैः क्वचित् /
अन्धे पङ्गौ रूपगतिप्रकाशो न न भासते // 251
text_mt: Precisely for this reason, even when a person is deprived of the cognitive and active senses in some respects, / being blind or lame, the manifestation of forms and locomotion does not fail to appear. // 251

sanskrit_iast:
kiṃtu sāmānyakaraṇabalādvedye'pi tādṛśi /
rūpasāmānya evāndhaḥ pratipattiṃ prapadyate // 252
meaning:
किंतु सामान्यकरणबलाद्वेद्येऽपि तादृशि /
रूपसामान्य एवान्धः प्रतिपत्तिं प्रपद्यते // 252
text_mt: Rather, by the power of the general instrument, even when such an object of knowledge exists, / the blind person attains perception only in the universal of form. // 252

sanskrit_iast:
tata eva tvahaṃkārāt tanmātrasparśino'dhikam /
karmendriyāṇi vākpāṇipāyūpasthāṅghri jajñire // 253
meaning:
तत एव त्वहंकारात् तन्मात्रस्पर्शिनोऽधिकम् /
कर्मेन्द्रियाणि वाक्पाणिपायूपस्थाङ्घ्रि जज्ञिरे // 253
text_mt: From that very ahaṃkāra, however, surpassing that which touches the subtle elements, / the active senses arose: voice, hands, anus, genitals, and feet. // 253

sanskrit_iast:
vacmyādade tyajāmyāśu visṛjāmi vrajāmi ca /
iti yāhaṃkriyā kāryakṣamā karmendriyaṃ tu tat // 254
meaning:
वच्म्याददे त्यजाम्याशु विसृजामि व्रजामि च /
इति याहंक्रिया कार्यक्षमा कर्मेन्द्रियं तु तत् // 254
text_mt: "I speak, I grasp, I swiftly discard, I emit, and I go"— / the sense of ego capable of doing such tasks is indeed an active sense. // 254

sanskrit_iast:
tena cchinnakarasyāsti hastaḥ karmendriyātmakaḥ /
tasya pradhānādhiṣṭhānaṃ paraṃ pañcāṅguliḥ karaḥ // 255
meaning:
तेन च्छिन्नकरस्यास्ति हस्तः कर्मेन्द्रियात्मकः /
तस्य प्रधानाधिष्ठानं परं पञ्चाङ्गुलिः करः // 255
text_mt: Therefore, even a person whose physical hand has been severed possesses the hand as an active sense; / the five-fingered hand is merely its primary physical base. // 255

sanskrit_iast:
mukhenāpi yadādānaṃ tatra yat karaṇaṃ sthitam /
sa pāṇireva karaṇaṃ vinā kiṃ saṃbhavet kriyā // 256
meaning:
मुखेनापि यदादानं तत्र यत् करणं स्थितम् /
स पाणिरेव करणं विना किं संभवेत् क्रिया // 256
text_mt: Even when grasping is done with the mouth, the instrument operating there / is indeed the hand: how could action occur without an instrument? // 256

sanskrit_iast:
tathābhāve tu buddhyakṣairapi kiṃ syātprayojanam /
darśanaṃ karaṇāpekṣaṃ kriyātvāditi cocyate // 257
meaning:
तथाभावे तु बुद्ध्यक्षैरपि किं स्यात्प्रयोजनम् /
दर्शनं करणापेक्षं क्रियात्वादिति चोच्यते // 257
text_mt: If it were otherwise, what purpose would there be even for the sense organs? / And it is said that seeing depends upon an instrument because it is an action. // 257

sanskrit_iast:
parairgamau tu karaṇaṃ neṣyate ceti vismayaḥ /
gamanotkṣepaṇādīni mukhyaṃ karmopalambhanam // 258
meaning:
परैर्गमौ तु करणं नेष्यते चेति विस्मयः /
गमनोत्क्षेपणादीनि मुख्यं कर्मोपलम्भनम् // 258
text_mt: It is astonishing that others do not accept an instrument in locomotion; / locomotion, upward projection, and so forth are the primary perceptible forms of action. // 258

sanskrit_iast:
punarguṇaḥ kriyā tveṣā vaiyākaraṇadarśane /
kriyā karaṇapūrveti vyāptyā karaṇapūrvakam // 259
meaning:
पुनर्गुणः क्रिया त्वेषा वैयाकरणदर्शने /
क्रिया करणपूर्वेति व्याप्त्या करणपूर्वकम् // 259
text_mt: According to the Grammarian system, however, this action is a secondary attribute; / through the invariable concomitance that "action is preceded by an instrument," [to say that] / knowledge is preceded by an instrument, while grasping is not, is clearly the flourishing of blindness. // 259

sanskrit_iast:
jñānaṃ nādānamityetat sphuṭamāndhyavijṛmbhitam /
tasmāt karmendriyāṇyāhustvagvadvyāptṝṇi mukhyataḥ // 260
meaning:
ज्ञानं नादानमित्येतत् स्फुटमान्ध्यविजृम्भितम् /
तस्मात् कर्मेन्द्रियाण्याहुस्त्वग्वद्व्याप्तॄणि मुख्यतः // 260
text_mt: Therefore, my teachers have said in the Mataṅga that the active senses primarily / pervade [the body] like the sense of touch, functioning in their respective locations. // 260

sanskrit_iast:
tatsthāne vṛttimantīti mataṅge guravo mama /
nanvanyānyapi karmāṇi santi bhūyāṃsi tatkṛte // 261
meaning:
तत्स्थाने वृत्तिमन्तीति मतङ्गे गुरवो मम /
नन्वन्यान्यपि कर्माणि सन्ति भूयांसि तत्कृते // 261
text_mt: [Objection:] But there are many other actions; for their sake, / instruments would also have to be stated, and thus there would be no finality regarding the senses! // 261

sanskrit_iast:
karaṇānyapi vācyāni tathā cākṣeṣvaniṣṭhitiḥ /
nanvetat kheṭapālādyairnirākāri na karmaṇām // 262
meaning:
करणान्यपि वाच्यानि तथा चाक्षेष्वनिष्ठितिः /
नन्वेतत् खेटपालाद्यैर्निराकारि न कर्मणाम् // 262
text_mt: Is it not true that Kheṭapāla and others refuted this, saying: "That which is an instrument of actions / is not an organ of sense; but rather, [an organ exists] for specific actions"? // 262

sanskrit_iast:
yatsādhanaṃ tadakṣaṃ syāt kiṃtu kasyāpi karmaṇaḥ /
etannāsmatkṛtapraśnatṛṣṇāsaṃtāpaśāntaye // 263
meaning:
यत्साधनं तदक्षं स्यात् किंतु कस्यापि कर्मणः /
एतन्नास्मत्कृतप्रश्नतृष्णासंतापशान्तये // 263
text_mt: This does not pacify the burning thirst of the question we have posed; / for peacocks are never satisfied with turbid, meager waters! // 263

sanskrit_iast:
nahyasvacchamitaprāyairjalaistṛpyanti barhiṇaḥ /
ucyate śrīmatādiṣṭaṃ śaṃbhunātra mamottaram // 264
meaning:
नह्यस्वच्छमितप्रायैर्जलैस्तृप्यन्ति बर्हिणः /
उच्यते श्रीमतादिष्टं शंभुनात्र ममोत्तरम् // 264
text_mt: The answer taught to me here by the venerable Śambhunātha is stated: // 264

sanskrit_iast:
svacchasaṃvedanodāravikalāprabalīkṛtam /
iha karmānusaṃdhānabhedādekaṃ vibhidyate // 265
meaning:
स्वच्छसंवेदनोदारविकलाप्रबलीकृतम् /
इह कर्मानुसंधानभेदादेकं विभिद्यते // 265
text_mt: Strengthened by pure consciousness and noble determinative reflection, / here a single action becomes differentiated through the division of mental intention. // 265

sanskrit_iast:
tatrānusaṃdhiḥ pañcātmā pañca karmendriyāṇyataḥ /
tyāgāyādānasaṃpattyai dvayāya dvitayaṃ vinā // 266
meaning:
तत्रानुसंधिः पञ्चात्मा पञ्च कर्मेन्द्रियाण्यतः /
त्यागायादानसंपत्त्यै द्वयाय द्वितयं विना // 266
text_mt: In that regard, mental intention is fivefold; therefore, the active senses are five: / for discarding, for attaining grasping, for the pair [of urination and evacuation], and—aside from this pair— // 266

sanskrit_iast:
svarūpaviśrāntikṛte caturdhā karma yadbahiḥ /
pāyupāṇyaṅghrijananaṃ karaṇaṃ taccaturvidham // 267
meaning:
स्वरूपविश्रान्तिकृते चतुर्धा कर्म यद्बहिः /
पायुपाण्यङ्घ्रिजननं करणं तच्चतुर्विधम् // 267
text_mt: for resting in one's own nature. The action that is external is fourfold; / the fourfold instrument is the anus, hands, feet, and genitals. // 267

sanskrit_iast:
antaṃ prāṇāśrayaṃ yattu karmātra karaṇaṃ hi vāk /
uktāḥ samāsataścaiṣāṃ citrāḥ kāryeṣu vṛttayaḥ // 268
meaning:
अन्तं प्राणाश्रयं यत्तु कर्मात्र करणं हि वाक् /
उक्ताः समासतश्चैषां चित्राः कार्येषु वृत्तयः // 268
text_mt: The internal action resting upon the vital breath, however, has voice as its instrument. / Thus the varied functions of these [senses] in their operations have been stated in brief. // 268

sanskrit_iast:
tadetadvyatiriktaṃ hi na karma kvāpi dṛśyate /
tatkasyārthe prakalpyeyamindriyāṇāmaniṣṭhitiḥ // 269
meaning:
तदेतद्व्यतिरिक्तं हि न कर्म क्वापि दृश्यते /
तत्कस्यार्थे प्रकल्प्येयमिन्द्रियाणामनिष्ठितिः // 269
text_mt: Indeed, no action is seen anywhere distinct from these; / for what purpose, then, should this lack of finality regarding the senses be conjectured? // 269

sanskrit_iast:
etatkartavyacakraṃ tadasāṃkaryeṇa kurvate /
akṣāṇi sahavṛttyā tu buddhyante saṃkaraṃ jaḍāḥ // 270
meaning:
एतत्कर्तव्यचक्रं तदसांकर्येण कुर्वते /
अक्षाणि सहवृत्त्या तु बुद्ध्यन्ते संकरं जडाः // 270
text_mt: The senses execute this wheel of duties without confusion; / but unintelligent people, because the functions occur together, perceive confusion. // 270

sanskrit_iast:
ukta indriyavargo'yamahaṃkārāt tu rājasāt /
tamaḥpradhānāhaṃkārād bhoktraṃśacchādanātmanaḥ // 271
meaning:
उक्त इन्द्रियवर्गोऽयमहंकारात् तु राजसात् /
तमःप्रधानाहंकाराद् भोक्त्रंशच्छादनात्मनः // 271
text_mt: This group of senses has been declared to arise from rājasika ahaṃkāra. / From ahaṃkāra dominated by tamas, whose nature is the concealing of the experiencer's portion, // 271

sanskrit_iast:
bhūtādināmnastanmātrapañcakaṃ bhūtakāraṇam /
manobuddhyakṣakarmākṣavargastanmātravargakaḥ // 272
meaning:
भूतादिनाम्नस्तन्मात्रपञ्चकं भूतकारणम् /
मनोबुद्ध्यक्षकर्माक्षवर्गस्तन्मात्रवर्गकः // 272
text_mt: called bhūtādi, [arises] the group of five subtle elements, the cause of the gross elements. / The group of the mind, cognitive senses, and active senses, and the group of subtle elements— // 272

sanskrit_iast:
ityatra rājasāhaṃkṛdyogaḥ saṃśleṣako dvaye /
anye tvāhurmano jātaṃ rājasāhaṃkṛteryataḥ // 273
meaning:
इत्यत्र राजसाहंकृद्योगः संश्लेषको द्वये /
अन्ये त्वाहुर्मनो जातं राजसाहंकृतेर्यतः // 273
text_mt: here the connection with rājasika ahaṃkāra is the unifying factor in both. / Others, however, say that the mind arose from rājasika ahaṃkāra, because // 273

sanskrit_iast:
samastendriyasaṃcāracaturaṃ laghu vegavat /
anye tu sāttvikāt svāntaṃ buddhikarmendriyāṇi tu // 274
meaning:
समस्तेन्द्रियसंचारचतुरं लघु वेगवत् /
अन्ये तु सात्त्विकात् स्वान्तं बुद्धिकर्मेन्द्रियाणि तु // 274
text_mt: it is skillful, light, and swift in operating through all the senses. / Yet others believe that the mind arises from the sāttvika, while the cognitive and active senses // 274

sanskrit_iast:
rājasādgrāhakagrāhyabhāgasparśīni manvate /
kheṭapālāstu manyante karmendriyagaṇaḥ sphuṭam // 275
meaning:
राजसाद्ग्राहकग्राह्यभागस्पर्शीनि मन्वते /
खेटपालास्तु मन्यन्ते कर्मेन्द्रियगणः स्फुटम् // 275
text_mt: arise from the rājasika, touching the divisions of subject and object. / But Kheṭapāla and his followers consider that the group of active senses clearly // 275

sanskrit_iast:
rājasāhaṃkṛterjāto rajasaḥ karmatā yataḥ /
śrīpūrvaśāstre tu mano rājasāt sāttvikātpunaḥ // 276
meaning:
राजसाहंकृतेर्जातो रजसः कर्मता यतः /
श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे तु मनो राजसात् सात्त्विकात्पुनः // 276
text_mt: arose from rājasika ahaṃkāra, because activity belongs to rajas. / In the venerable Pūrvaśāstra, however, the mind is said to arise from the rājasika, and all the senses, // 276

sanskrit_iast:
indriyāṇi samastāni yuktaṃ caitadvibhāti naḥ /
tathāhi bāhyavṛttīnāmakṣāṇāṃ vṛttibhāsane // 277
meaning:
इन्द्रियाणि समस्तानि युक्तं चैतद्विभाति नः /
तथाहि बाह्यवृत्तीनामक्षाणां वृत्तिभासने // 277
text_mt: moreover, from the sāttvika; and this appears sound to us. / For, regarding the manifestation of the functioning of the senses whose operation is external, // 277

sanskrit_iast:
ālocane śaktirantaryojane manasaḥ punaḥ /
uktaṃ ca guruṇā kuryānmano'nuvyavasāyi sat // 278
meaning:
आलोचने शक्तिरन्तर्योजने मनसः पुनः /
उक्तं च गुरुणा कुर्यान्मनोऽनुव्यवसायि सत् // 278
text_mt: their power lies in indeterminate perception, whereas that of the mind lies in internal synthesising. / And it was said by the master: "The mind, being reflective, should execute // 278

sanskrit_iast:
taddvayālambanā mātṛvyāpārātmakriyā iti /
tānmātrastu gaṇo dhvāntapradhānāyā ahaṃkṛteḥ // 279
meaning:
तद्द्वयालम्बना मातृव्यापारात्मक्रिया इति /
तान्मात्रस्तु गणो ध्वान्तप्रधानाया अहंकृतेः // 279
text_mt: actions consisting of the operations of the knower resting on both of these." / The group of subtle elements, however, arises from ahaṃkāra dominated by darkness; // 279

sanskrit_iast:
atrāvivādaḥ sarvasya grāhyopakrama eva hi /
pṛthivyāṃ saurabhānyādivicitre gandhamaṇḍale // 280
meaning:
अत्राविवादः सर्वस्य ग्राह्योपक्रम एव हि /
पृथिव्यां सौरभान्यादिविचित्रे गन्धमण्डले // 280
text_mt: on this point there is no dispute, for it is indeed the beginning of the object of perception. / In earth, within the manifold sphere of odor such as fragrance and the rest, // 280

sanskrit_iast:
yatsāmānyaṃ hi gandhatvaṃ gandhatanmātranāma tat /
vyāpakaṃ tata evoktaṃ sahetutvāttu na dhruvam // 281
meaning:
यत्सामान्यं हि गन्धत्वं गन्धतन्मात्रनाम तत् /
व्यापकं तत एवोक्तं सहेतुत्वात्तु न ध्रुवम् // 281
text_mt: the universal which is odorness is called the subtle element of odor. / For that reason it is declared all-pervasive, but because it has a cause, it is not permanent. // 281

sanskrit_iast:
svakāraṇe tirobhūtirdhvaso yattena nādhruvam /
evaṃ rasādiśabdāntatanmātreṣvapi yojanā // 282
meaning:
स्वकारणे तिरोभूतिर्ध्वसो यत्तेन नाध्रुवम् /
एवं रसादिशब्दान्ततन्मात्रेष्वपि योजना // 282
text_mt: Because its destruction is its disappearance into its own cause, it is not permanent. / The same application holds for the subtle elements beginning with taste up to sound. // 282

sanskrit_iast:
viśeṣāṇāṃ yato'vaśyaṃ daśā prāgaviśeṣiṇī /
kṣubhitaṃ śabdatanmātraṃ citrākārāḥ śratīrdadhat // 283
meaning:
विशेषाणां यतोऽवश्यं दशा प्रागविशेषिणी /
क्षुभितं शब्दतन्मात्रं चित्राकाराः श्रतीर्दधत् // 283
text_mt: Because particulars necessarily have a preceding non-particularized state. / The agitated subtle element of sound, bearing audibles of varied forms, // 283

sanskrit_iast:
nabhaḥ śabdo'vakāśātmā vācyādhyāsasaho yataḥ /
tadetatsparśatanmātrayogāt prakṣobhamāgatam // 284
meaning:
नभः शब्दोऽवकाशात्मा वाच्याध्याससहो यतः /
तदेतत्स्पर्शतन्मात्रयोगात् प्रक्षोभमागतम् // 284
text_mt: is space, since sound is of the nature of accommodation, sustaining the superimposition of the expressible. / When this [space] becomes agitated through contact with the subtle element of touch, // 284

sanskrit_iast:
vāyutāmeti tenātra śabdasparśobhayātmatā /
anye tvāhurdhvaniḥ khaikaguṇastadapi yujyate // 285
meaning:
वायुतामेति तेनात्र शब्दस्पर्शोभयात्मता /
अन्ये त्वाहुर्ध्वनिः खैकगुणस्तदपि युज्यते // 285
text_mt: it becomes wind; therefore, here there is the dual nature of sound and touch. / Others say that sound is the exclusive quality of space, and that is also fitting, // 285

sanskrit_iast:
yato vāyurnijaṃ rūpaṃ labhate na vināmbarāt /
uttarottarabhūteṣu pūrvapūrvasthitiryataḥ // 286
meaning:
यतो वायुर्निजं रूपं लभते न विनाम्बरात् /
उत्तरोत्तरभूतेषु पूर्वपूर्वस्थितिर्यतः // 286
text_mt: because wind does not attain its own nature without space, / since the preceding elements exist within each successive element. // 286

sanskrit_iast:
tata eva marudvyomnoraviyogo mithaḥ smṛtaḥ /
śabdasparśau tu rūpeṇa samaṃ prakṣobhamāgatau // 287
meaning:
तत एव मरुद्व्योम्नोरवियोगो मिथः स्मृतः /
शब्दस्पर्शौ तु रूपेण समं प्रक्षोभमागतौ // 287
text_mt: Precisely for this reason, wind and space are remembered as inseparable from one another. / Sound and touch, however, having become agitated together with form, // 287

sanskrit_iast:
tejastattvaṃ tribhirdharmaiḥ prāhuḥ pūrvavadeva tat /
taistribhiḥ sarasairāpaḥ sagandhairbhūriti kramaḥ // 288
meaning:
तेजस्तत्त्वं त्रिभिर्धर्मैः प्राहुः पूर्ववदेव तत् /
तैस्त्रिभिः सरसैरापः सगन्धैर्भूरिति क्रमः // 288
text_mt: are called the element of fire, possessing three properties, just as before. / Water possesses those three along with taste, and earth along with odor: such is the order. // 288

sanskrit_iast:
tatra pratyakṣataḥ siddho dharādiguṇasaṃcayaḥ /
nahi gandhādidharmaughavyatiriktā vibhāti bhūḥ // 289
meaning:
तत्र प्रत्यक्षतः सिद्धो धरादिगुणसंचयः /
नहि गन्धादिधर्मौघव्यतिरिक्ता विभाति भूः // 289
text_mt: In that context, the collection of properties belonging to earth and the others is established through direct perception; / for earth does not appear as something separate from the multitude of properties such as fragrance. // 289

sanskrit_iast:
yathā guṇaguṇidvaitavādināmekamapyadaḥ /
citraṃ rūpaṃ paṭe bhāti kramāddharmāstathā bhuvi // 290
meaning:
यथा गुणगुणिद्वैतवादिनामेकमप्यदः /
चित्रं रूपं पटे भाति क्रमाद्धर्मास्तथा भुवि // 290
text_mt: Just as for those who assert a duality between quality and possessor of quality, this single / variegated colour appears on a cloth, so too properties appear successively in earth. // 290

sanskrit_iast:
yathā ca vistṛte vastre yugapadbhāti citratā /
tathaiva yogināṃ dharmasāmastyenāvabhāti bhūḥ // 291
meaning:
यथा च विस्तृते वस्त्रे युगपद्भाति चित्रता /
तथैव योगिनां धर्मसामस्त्येनावभाति भूः // 291
text_mt: And just as when a cloth is unfolded its variegated nature appears all at once, / in the very same way earth appears to yogins in the totality of its properties. // 291

sanskrit_iast:
gandhādiśabdaparyantacitrarūpā dharā tataḥ /
upāyabhedādbhātyeṣā kramākramavibhāgataḥ // 292
meaning:
गन्धादिशब्दपर्यन्तचित्ररूपा धरा ततः /
उपायभेदाद्भात्येषा क्रमाक्रमविभागतः // 292
text_mt: Therefore, earth, consisting of variegated forms beginning with fragrance and ending with sound, / appears in this way through the distinction of succession and non-succession according to differences of means. // 292

sanskrit_iast:
tata eva kramavyaktikṛto dhībheda ucyate /
ṣaṣṭhīprayogo dhībhedādbhedyabhedakatā tathā // 293
meaning:
तत एव क्रमव्यक्तिकृतो धीभेद उच्यते /
षष्ठीप्रयोगो धीभेदाद्भेद्यभेदकता तथा // 293
text_mt: For that very reason, a distinction in cognition brought about by the successive manifestation is spoken of; / the use of the genitive case arises from the distinction in cognition, as does the relation of qualificand and qualifier. // 293

sanskrit_iast:
tena dharmātirikto'tra dharmī nāma na kaścana /
tatrānekaprakārāḥ syurgandharūparasāḥ kṣitau // 294
meaning:
तेन धर्मातिरिक्तोऽत्र धर्मी नाम न कश्चन /
तत्रानेकप्रकाराः स्युर्गन्धरूपरसाः क्षितौ // 294
text_mt: Therefore, there is no substantive distinct from its properties here at all. / Among them, fragrance, colour, and taste in earth are of manifold kinds; // 294

sanskrit_iast:
saṃsparśaḥ pākajo'nuṣṇāśītaḥ śabdo vicitrakaḥ /
śauklyaṃ mādhuryaśītatve citrāḥ śabdāśca vāriṇi // 295
meaning:
संस्पर्शः पाकजोऽनुष्णाशीतः शब्दो विचित्रकः /
शौक्ल्यं माधुर्यशीतत्वे चित्राः शब्दाश्च वारिणि // 295
text_mt: its touch is produced by heat and is neither hot nor cold; its sound is varied. / Whiteness, sweetness, coolness, and varied sounds are in water. // 295

sanskrit_iast:
śuklabhāsvaratoṣṇatvaṃ citrāḥ śabdāśca pāvake /
apākajaścāśītoṣṇo dhvaniścitraśca mārute // 296
meaning:
शुक्लभास्वरतोष्णत्वं चित्राः शब्दाश्च पावके /
अपाकजश्चाशीतोष्णो ध्वनिश्चित्रश्च मारुते // 296
text_mt: Bright white radiance, heat, and varied sounds are in fire. / Touch not produced by heat, neither cold nor hot, and varied sound are in wind. // 296

sanskrit_iast:
varṇātmako dhvaniḥ śabdapratibimbānyathāmbare /
yattu na sparśavaddharmaḥ śabda ityādi bhaṇyate // 297
meaning:
वर्णात्मको ध्वनिः शब्दप्रतिबिम्बान्यथाम्बरे /
यत्तु न स्पर्शवद्धर्मः शब्द इत्यादि भण्यते // 297
text_mt: Sound in the form of articulate phonemes, and as echoes of sound, is in space. / As for what is asserted [by opponents] that sound is not a property possessing touch, and so forth, // 297

sanskrit_iast:
kāṇādaistatsvapratītiviruddhaṃ kena gṛhyatām /
paṭahe dhvanirityeva bhātyabādhitameva yat // 298
meaning:
काणादैस्तत्स्वप्रतीतिविरुद्धं केन गृह्यताम् /
पटहे ध्वनिरित्येव भात्यबाधितमेव यत् // 298
text_mt: how could that assertion of the Kāṇādas be accepted, since it contradicts one's own direct experience? / For the awareness 'sound is in the drum' appears entirely uncontradicted. // 298

sanskrit_iast:
na ca hetutvamātreṇa tadādānatvavedanāt /
śrotraṃ cāsmanmate'haṃkṛtkāraṇaṃ tatra tatra tat // 299
meaning:
न च हेतुत्वमात्रेण तदादानत्ववेदनात् /
श्रोत्रं चास्मन्मतेऽहंकृत्कारणं तत्र तत्र तत् // 299
text_mt: Nor is this [awareness] due merely to causality, since it is experienced as its recipient material cause. / And in our doctrine the ear has the ego as its cause, and in each respective place it // 299

sanskrit_iast:
vṛttibhāgīti taddeśaṃ śabdaṃ gṛhṇātyalaṃ tathā /
yastvāha śrotramākāśaṃ karṇasaṃyogabheditam // 300
meaning:
वृत्तिभागीति तद्देशं शब्दं गृह्णात्यलं तथा /
यस्त्वाह श्रोत्रमाकाशं कर्णसंयोगभेदितम् // 300
text_mt: possesses a cognitive function, and thus fully grasps the sound in that place. / As for him who says that the ear is space delimited by its contact with the ear-canal, // 300

sanskrit_iast:
śabdajaḥ śabda āgatya śabdabuddhiṃ prasūyate /
tasya mande'pi murajadhvanāvākarṇake sati // 301
meaning:
शब्दजः शब्द आगत्य शब्दबुद्धिं प्रसूयते /
तस्य मन्देऽपि मुरजध्वनावाकर्णके सति // 301
text_mt: [and that] sound produced by sound arrives and generates the cognition of sound— / even when the drum-sound is faint and has reached the ear, // 301

sanskrit_iast:
amutra śrutireṣeti dūre saṃvedanaṃ katham /
nahi śabdajaśabdasya dūrādūraravoditeḥ // 302
meaning:
अमुत्र श्रुतिरेषेति दूरे संवेदनं कथम् /
नहि शब्दजशब्दस्य दूरादूररवोदितेः // 302
text_mt: how could there be the awareness at a distance: 'this hearing is over there'? / For sound generated by sound, arising from a distant or near sound, // 302

sanskrit_iast:
śrotrākāśagatasyāsti dūrādūrasvabhāvatā /
na cāsau prathamaḥ śabdastāvadvyāpīti yujyate // 303
meaning:
श्रोत्राकाशगतस्यास्ति दूरादूरस्वभावता /
न चासौ प्रथमः शब्दस्तावद्व्यापीति युज्यते // 303
text_mt: and situated in the space of the ear, does not possess the nature of being distant or near. / Nor is it reasonable that this initial sound pervades that far: // 303

sanskrit_iast:
tatrasthaiḥ saha tīvrātmā śrūyamāṇastvanena tu /
kathaṃ śrūyeta mandaḥsannahi dharmāntarāśrayaḥ // 304
meaning:
तत्रस्थैः सह तीव्रात्मा श्रूयमाणस्त्वनेन तु /
कथं श्रूयेत मन्दःसन्नहि धर्मान्तराश्रयः // 304
text_mt: for while heard by those standing near as intense, how could it, / being faint, be heard by this [distant person]? For it cannot be the substratum of opposing properties. // 304

sanskrit_iast:
etaccānyairapākāri bahudheti vṛthā punaḥ /
nāyastaṃ patitāghātadāne ko hi na paṇḍitaḥ // 305
meaning:
एतच्चान्यैरपाकारि बहुधेति वृथा पुनः /
नायस्तं पतिताघातदाने को हि न पण्डितः // 305
text_mt: And this has been refuted in many ways by others, so no further effort / was made [here] in vain; for who is not an expert at striking one who has already fallen? // 305

sanskrit_iast:
amīṣāṃ tu dharādīnāṃ yāvāṃstattvagaṇaḥ purā /
guṇādhikatayā tiṣṭhan vyāptā tāvān prakāśate // 306
meaning:
अमीषां तु धरादीनां यावांस्तत्त्वगणः पुरा /
गुणाधिकतया तिष्ठन् व्याप्ता तावान् प्रकाशते // 306
text_mt: Now, the entire host of tattvas that existed prior to these [gross elements] beginning with earth / is revealed as a pervader, abiding with an increase of qualities. // 306

sanskrit_iast:
vyāpyavyāpakatā yaiṣā tattvānāṃ darśitā kila /
sā guṇādhikyataḥ siddhā na hetutvānna lāghavāt // 307
meaning:
व्याप्यव्यापकता यैषा तत्त्वानां दर्शिता किल /
सा गुणाधिक्यतः सिद्धा न हेतुत्वान्न लाघवात् // 307
text_mt: This relation of pervaded and pervader of the tattvas that has indeed been shown / is established through an increase of qualities, not from causality nor from lightness. // 307

sanskrit_iast:
ahetunāpi rāgo hi vyāpto vidyādinā sphuṭam /
tadvinā na bhavedyattadvyāptamityucyate yataḥ // 308
meaning:
अहेतुनापि रागो हि व्याप्तो विद्यादिना स्फुटम् /
तद्विना न भवेद्यत्तद्व्याप्तमित्युच्यते यतः // 308
text_mt: For attachment is clearly pervaded by vidyā and the rest even without being its cause; / for whatever cannot exist without something is said to be pervaded by it. // 308

sanskrit_iast:
na lāghavaṃ ca nāmāsti kiṃcidatra svadarśane /
guṇādhikyādato jñeyā vyāpyavyāpakatā sphuṭā // 309
meaning:
न लाघवं च नामास्ति किंचिदत्र स्वदर्शने /
गुणाधिक्यादतो ज्ञेया व्याप्यव्यापकता स्फुटा // 309
text_mt: Nor is there any so-called 'lightness' in our own doctrine. / Therefore, the relation of pervaded and pervader must be clearly understood to arise from the increase of qualities. // 309

sanskrit_iast:
yo hi yasmādguṇotkṛṣṭaḥ sa tasmādūrdhva ucyate /
ūrdhvatā vyāptṛtā śrīmanmālinīvijaye sphuṭā // 310
meaning:
यो हि यस्माद्गुणोत्कृष्टः स तस्मादूर्ध्व उच्यते /
ऊर्ध्वता व्याप्तृता श्रीमन्मालिनीविजये स्फुटा // 310
text_mt: For whatever is superior to something in qualities is said to be higher than it; / that being higher is being a pervader is clear in the venerable Mālinīvijaya. // 310

sanskrit_iast:
ataḥ śivatvātprabhṛti prakāśatāsvarūpamādāya nijātmani dhruvam /
samastatattvāvalidharmasaṃcayairvibhāti bhūrvyāptṛtayā sthitairalam // 311
meaning:
अतः शिवत्वात्प्रभृति प्रकाशतास्वरूपमादाय निजात्मनि ध्रुवम् /
समस्ततत्त्वावलिधर्मसंचयैर्विभाति भूर्व्याप्तृतया स्थितैरलम् // 311
text_mt: Therefore, taking the essential nature of luminosity into its own self, constant from the state of Śiva onward, / earth fully appears through the assemblies of properties of all the series of tattvas, abiding as their pervader. // 311

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ jalāderapi śaktitattvaparyantadhāmno vapurasti tādṛk /
kiṃ tūttaraṃ śaktitayaiva tattvaṃ pūrva tu taddharmatayeti bhedaḥ // 312
meaning:
एवं जलादेरपि शक्तितत्त्वपर्यन्तधाम्नो वपुरस्ति तादृक् /
किं तूत्तरं शक्तितयैव तत्त्वं पूर्व तु तद्धर्मतयेति भेदः // 312
text_mt: In this way, water and the others too, up to the realm of the tattva of śakti, have such a nature; / the distinction, however, is that a higher tattva exists as śakti, while a lower exists as its property. // 312

sanskrit_iast:
anuttaraprakriyāyāṃ vaitatyena pradarśitam /
etat tasmāt tataḥ paśyedvistarārthī vivecakaḥ // 313
meaning:
अनुत्तरप्रक्रियायां वैतत्येन प्रदर्शितम् /
एतत् तस्मात् ततः पश्येद्विस्तरार्थी विवेचकः // 313
text_mt: This has been shown in detail in the Anuttaraprakriyā; / therefore, a discriminating person desiring detailed explanation should look there. // 313

sanskrit_iast: iti tattvasyarūpasya kṛtaṃ samyak prakāśanam // 314
meaning: इति तत्त्वस्यरूपस्य कृतं सम्यक् प्रकाशनम् // 314
text_mt: Thus the nature of the tattvas has been correctly revealed. // 314

sanskrit_iast: ucyate trikaśāstrekarahasyaṃ tattvabhedanam // 1
meaning: उच्यते त्रिकशास्त्रेकरहस्यं तत्त्वभेदनम् // 1
text_mt: The differentiation of tattvas, the singular secret of the Trika teachings, is now explained. // 1b
title: Tattvabhedaprakāśana

sanskrit_iast:
teṣāmamīṣāṃ tattvānāṃ svavargeṣvanugāminām /
bhedāntaramapi proktaṃ śāstre'tra śrītrikābhidhe // 2
meaning:
तेषाममीषां तत्त्वानां स्ववर्गेष्वनुगामिनाम् /
भेदान्तरमपि प्रोक्तं शास्त्रेऽत्र श्रीत्रिकाभिधे // 2
text_mt: A further differentiation of these tattvas that follow their respective categories / is also taught in this scripture named the venerable Trika. // 2

sanskrit_iast:
śaktimacchaktibhedena dharādyaṃ mūlapaścimam /
bhidyate pañcadaśadhā svarūpeṇa sahānarāt // 3
meaning:
शक्तिमच्छक्तिभेदेन धराद्यं मूलपश्चिमम् /
भिद्यते पञ्चदशधा स्वरूपेण सहानरात् // 3
text_mt: Through the distinction between possessor of power and power, [each tattva] from earth to the ultimate root / is divided fifteenfold, together with its essential nature, continuously. // 3

sanskrit_iast:
kalāntaṃ bhedayugghīnaṃ rudravatpralayākalaḥ /
tadvanmāyā ca navadhā jñākalāḥ saptadhā punaḥ // 4
meaning:
कलान्तं भेदयुग्घीनं रुद्रवत्प्रलयाकलः /
तद्वन्माया च नवधा ज्ञाकलाः सप्तधा पुनः // 4
text_mt: Up to kalā, it is without a pair of divisions, like Rudra; the pralayākala / is like that, and māyā is ninefold; knowers free of instruments, moreover, are sevenfold. // 4

sanskrit_iast:
mantrāstadīśāḥ pāñcadhye mantreśapatayastridhā /
śivo na bhidyate svaikaprakāśaghanacinmayaḥ // 5
meaning:
मन्त्रास्तदीशाः पाञ्चध्ये मन्त्रेशपतयस्त्रिधा /
शिवो न भिद्यते स्वैकप्रकाशघनचिन्मयः // 5
text_mt: Mantras and their lords are fivefold; the supreme lords of mantras are threefold; / Śiva is not divided, consisting of pure consciousness compacted of his own unique luminosity. // 5

sanskrit_iast:
śivo mantramaheśeśamantrā akalayukkalī /
śaktimantaḥ sapta tathā śaktayastaccaturdaśa // 6
meaning:
शिवो मन्त्रमहेशेशमन्त्रा अकलयुक्कली /
शक्तिमन्तः सप्त तथा शक्तयस्तच्चतुर्दश // 6
text_mt: Śiva, mantramaheśvaras, mantreśvaras, mantras, those endowed with no kalā, those with kalā: / these possessors of power are seven, and likewise their powers are [seven]; that makes fourteen. // 6

sanskrit_iast:
svaṃ svarūpaṃ pañcadaśaṃ tadbhūḥ pañcadaśātmikā /
tathāhi tisro devasya śaktayo varṇitāḥ purā // 7
meaning:
स्वं स्वरूपं पञ्चदशं तद्भूः पञ्चदशात्मिका /
तथाहि तिस्रो देवस्य शक्तयो वर्णिताः पुरा // 7
text_mt: Its own essential nature is the fifteenth; hence earth has fifteen forms. / To explain: three powers of the Lord were described earlier; // 7

sanskrit_iast:
tā eva mātṛmāmeyatrairūpyeṇa vyavasthitāḥ /
parāṃśo mātṛrūpo'tra pramāṇāṃśaḥ parāparaḥ // 8
meaning:
ता एव मातृमामेयत्रैरूप्येण व्यवस्थिताः /
परांशो मातृरूपोऽत्र प्रमाणांशः परापरः // 8
text_mt: they indeed abide in the threefold form of knower, means of knowledge, and object of knowledge. / Here, the supreme aspect has the form of the knower; the intermediate aspect is the means of knowledge; // 8

sanskrit_iast:
meyo'paraḥ śaktimāṃśca śaktiḥ svaṃ rūpamityadaḥ /
tatra svarūpaṃ bhūmeryatpṛthagjaḍamavasthitam // 9
meaning:
मेयोऽपरः शक्तिमांश्च शक्तिः स्वं रूपमित्यदः /
तत्र स्वरूपं भूमेर्यत्पृथग्जडमवस्थितम् // 9
text_mt: the lower aspect is the object of knowledge; and the possessor of power, power, and own nature are this: / in that regard, the essential nature of earth is that which abides distinct as insentient, // 9

sanskrit_iast:
mātṛmānādyupadhibhirasaṃjātoparāgakam /
sakalādiśivāntaistu mātṛbhirvedyatāsya yā // 10
meaning:
मातृमानाद्युपधिभिरसंजातोपरागकम् /
सकलादिशिवान्तैस्तु मातृभिर्वेद्यतास्य या // 10
text_mt: with no tint produced by conditioning factors such as knower and means of knowledge. / But its state of being known by the knowers from sakala up to Śiva— // 10

sanskrit_iast:
śaktimadbhiranudbhūtaśaktibhiḥ sapta tadbhidaḥ /
sakalādiśivāntānāṃ śaktiṣūdrecitātmasu // 11
meaning:
शक्तिमद्भिरनुद्भूतशक्तिभिः सप्त तद्भिदः /
सकलादिशिवान्तानां शक्तिषूद्रेचितात्मसु // 11
text_mt: as possessors of power whose powers are unmanifest—constitutes seven divisions of it; / when the powers of those from sakala up to Śiva have become intensified in their nature, // 11

sanskrit_iast:
vedyatājanitāḥ sapta bhedā iti caturdaśa /
sakalasya pramāṇāṃśo yo'sau vidyākalātmakaḥ // 12
meaning:
वेद्यताजनिताः सप्त भेदा इति चतुर्दश /
सकलस्य प्रमाणांशो योऽसौ विद्याकलात्मकः // 12
text_mt: there are seven divisions produced by being known [by them]: thus there are fourteen. / The aspect of the means of knowledge belonging to a sakala, which consists of vidyā and kalā, // 12

sanskrit_iast:
sāmānyātmā sa śaktitve gaṇito natu tadbhidaḥ /
layākalasya mānāṃśaḥ sa eva paramasphuṭaḥ // 13
meaning:
सामान्यात्मा स शक्तित्वे गणितो नतु तद्भिदः /
लयाकलस्य मानांशः स एव परमस्फुटः // 13
text_mt: is generic in nature and is counted as power, but not as its divisions. / The aspect of the means of knowledge of a layākala is that very same [vidyā and kalā] in an extremely clear state. // 13

sanskrit_iast:
jñānākalasya mānaṃ tu galadvidyākalāvṛti /
aśuddhavidyākalanādhvaṃsasaṃskārasaṃgatā // 14
meaning:
ज्ञानाकलस्य मानं तु गलद्विद्याकलावृति /
अशुद्धविद्याकलनाध्वंससंस्कारसंगता // 14
text_mt: The means of knowledge of a knower free of instruments has the covering of vidyā and kalā dropping away, / joined with the latent impression of the destruction of the grasp of impure knowledge. // 14

sanskrit_iast:
prabubhutsuḥ śuddhavidyā santrāṇāṃ karaṇaṃ bhavet /
prabuddhā śuddhavidyā tu tatsaṃskāreṇa saṃgatā // 15
meaning:
प्रबुभुत्सुः शुद्धविद्या सन्त्राणां करणं भवेत् /
प्रबुद्धा शुद्धविद्या तु तत्संस्कारेण संगता // 15
text_mt: Pure knowledge desiring awakening would be the instrument of mantras; / pure knowledge fully awakened, however, joined with that latent impression, // 15

sanskrit_iast:
mānaṃ mantreśvarāṇāṃ syāttatsaṃskāravivarjitā /
mānaṃ mantramaheśānāṃ karaṇaṃ śaktirucyate // 16
meaning:
मानं मन्त्रेश्वराणां स्यात्तत्संस्कारविवर्जिता /
मानं मन्त्रमहेशानां करणं शक्तिरुच्यते // 16
text_mt: would be the means of knowledge of mantreśvaras; devoid of that latent impression, / it is the means of knowledge of mantramaheśas: this instrument is called śakti. // 16

sanskrit_iast:
svātantryamātrasadbhāvā yā tvicchā śaktiraiśvarī /
śivasya saiva karaṇaṃ tayā vetti karoti ca // 17
meaning:
स्वातन्त्र्यमात्रसद्भावा या त्विच्छा शक्तिरैश्वरी /
शिवस्य सैव करणं तया वेत्ति करोति च // 17
text_mt: The power of will belonging to the Lord, however, which exists purely as absolute autonomy, / is the very instrument of Śiva; by means of it he knows and acts. // 17

sanskrit_iast:
ā śivātsakalāntaṃ ye mātāraḥ sapta te dvidhā /
nyagbhūtodriktaśaktitvāttadbhedo vedyabhedakaḥ // 18
meaning:
आ शिवात्सकलान्तं ये मातारः सप्त ते द्विधा /
न्यग्भूतोद्रिक्तशक्तित्वात्तद्भेदो वेद्यभेदकः // 18
text_mt: The seven knowers from Śiva down to sakala are twofold / because their power is either subordinated or intensified; this division differentiates the object of knowledge. // 18

sanskrit_iast:
tathāhi vedyatā nāma bhāvasyaiva nijaṃ vapuḥ /
caitreṇa vedyaṃ vedmīti kiṃhyatra pratibhāsatām // 19
meaning:
तथाहि वेद्यता नाम भावस्यैव निजं वपुः /
चैत्रेण वेद्यं वेद्मीति किंह्यत्र प्रतिभासताम् // 19
text_mt: To explain: the state of being known is indeed the intrinsic form of an existing thing; / for what else could appear here when one thinks, 'I know the knowable object with Caitra'? // 19

sanskrit_iast:
nanu caitrīyavijñānamātramatra prakāśate /
vedyatākhyastu no dharmo bhāti bhāvasya nīlavat // 20
meaning:
ननु चैत्रीयविज्ञानमात्रमत्र प्रकाशते /
वेद्यताख्यस्तु नो धर्मो भाति भावस्य नीलवत् // 20
text_mt: [Opponent:] 'Surely here only the cognition belonging to Caitra is revealed, / but the property called "being known" does not appear as belonging to the object, as blueness does.' // 20

sanskrit_iast:
vedyatā ca svabhāvena dharmo bhāvasya cettataḥ /
sarvānpratyeva vedyaḥ syāddhaṭanīlādidharmavat // 21
meaning:
वेद्यता च स्वभावेन धर्मो भावस्य चेत्ततः /
सर्वान्प्रत्येव वेद्यः स्याद्धटनीलादिधर्मवत् // 21
text_mt:
And if object-hood is by nature a property of an entity, then
it would be known to all without exception, just like properties such as being a blue pot.

sanskrit_iast:
atha vedakasaṃvittibalādvedyatvadharmabhāk /
bhāvastathāpi doṣo'sau kuvindakṛtavastravat // 22
meaning:
अथ वेदकसंवित्तिबलाद्वेद्यत्वधर्मभाक् /
भावस्तथापि दोषोऽसौ कुविन्दकृतवस्त्रवत् // 22
text_mt:
Now, if through the power of the consciousness of the knower the entity possesses the property of object-hood,
even so, this flaw remains, like cloth made by a weaver.

sanskrit_iast:
vedyatākhyastu yo dharmaḥ so'vedyaścetkhapuṣpavat /
vedyaścedasti tatrāpi vedyetatyanavasthitiḥ // 23
meaning:
वेद्यताख्यस्तु यो धर्मः सोऽवेद्यश्चेत्खपुष्पवत् /
वेद्यश्चेदस्ति तत्रापि वेद्येतत्यनवस्थितिः // 23
text_mt:
Furthermore, if that property called object-hood is unmanifest, it is like a sky-flower;
if it is manifest, then there too [another] object-hood would apply, leading to infinite regress.

sanskrit_iast:
tato na kiṃcidvedyaṃ syānmūrchitaṃ tu jagadbhavet /
nanu vijñātrupādhyaṃ śo paskṛtaṃ vapurucyatām // 24
meaning:
ततो न किंचिद्वेद्यं स्यान्मूर्छितं तु जगद्भवेत् /
ननु विज्ञात्रुपाध्यं शो पस्कृतं वपुरुच्यताम् // 24
text_mt:
Therefore nothing would be an object of knowledge, and the world would be plunged into stupor.
[Opponent:] But surely it should be stated that the entity has a form qualified by a part consisting of the knower,

sanskrit_iast:
bhāvasyārthaprakāśātma yathā jñānamidaṃ tvasat /
ekavijñātṛvedyatve na jñātrantaravedyatā // 25
meaning:
भावस्यार्थप्रकाशात्म यथा ज्ञानमिदं त्वसत् /
एकविज्ञातृवेद्यत्वे न ज्ञात्रन्तरवेद्यता // 25
text_mt:
which consists of the manifestation of the object, just like knowledge—[Reply:] but this is incorrect.
If it were knowable by one knower, it would not be knowable by another knower;

sanskrit_iast:
samastajñātṛvedyatve naikavijñātṛvedyatā /
tasmānna vedyatā nāma bhāvadharmo'sti kaścana // 26
meaning:
समस्तज्ञातृवेद्यत्वे नैकविज्ञातृवेद्यता /
तस्मान्न वेद्यता नाम भावधर्मोऽस्ति कश्चन // 26
text_mt:
if it were knowable by all knowers, it could not be knowable by a single knower.
Therefore there is no property of an entity at all called object-hood.

sanskrit_iast:
bhāvasya vedyatā saiva saṃvido yaḥ samudbhavaḥ /
arthagrahaṇarūpaṃ hi yatra vijñānamātmani // 27
meaning:
भावस्य वेद्यता सैव संविदो यः समुद्भवः /
अर्थग्रहणरूपं हि यत्र विज्ञानमात्मनि // 27
text_mt:
[Opponent:] The object-hood of an entity is merely the arising of consciousness;
for when knowledge having the nature of apprehending an object inheres in the self,

sanskrit_iast:
samavaiti prakāśyo'rthastaṃ pratyeṣaiva vedyatā /
atra brūmaḥ padārthānāṃ na dharmo yadi vedyatā // 28
meaning:
समवैति प्रकाश्योऽर्थस्तं प्रत्येषैव वेद्यता /
अत्र ब्रूमः पदार्थानां न धर्मो यदि वेद्यता // 28
text_mt:
in relation to that object to be illuminated, this alone is its object-hood.
To this we reply: if object-hood is not a property of things,

sanskrit_iast:
avedyā eva te saṃsyurjñāne satyapi varṇite /
yathāhi pṛthubudhnādirūpe kumbhasya satyapi // 29
meaning:
अवेद्या एव ते संस्युर्ज्ञाने सत्यपि वर्णिते /
यथाहि पृथुबुध्नादिरूपे कुम्भस्य सत्यपि // 29
text_mt:
they would be entirely unknowable, even when knowledge as described exists.
For just as, although the form of a pot possessing a broad base and the like exists,

sanskrit_iast:
atadātmā paṭo naiti pṛthubudhnādirūpatām /
tathā satyapi vijñāne vijñātṛsamavāyini // 30
meaning:
अतदात्मा पटो नैति पृथुबुध्नादिरूपताम् /
तथा सत्यपि विज्ञाने विज्ञातृसमवायिनि // 30
text_mt:
a cloth, not having that nature, does not attain the form of having a broad base and the like;
even so, although knowledge inheres in the knower,

sanskrit_iast:
avedyadharmakā bhāvāḥ kathaṃ vedyatvamāpnuyuḥ /
anarthaḥ sumahāṃścaiṣa dṛśyatāṃ vastu yatsvayam // 31
meaning:
अवेद्यधर्मका भावाः कथं वेद्यत्वमाप्नुयुः /
अनर्थः सुमहांश्चैष दृश्यतां वस्तु यत्स्वयम् // 31
text_mt:
how could entities, which lack the property of knowability, attain object-hood?
Moreover, observe this very great absurdity: that an entity, which of itself

sanskrit_iast:
prakāśātma na tatsaṃviccāprakāśā tadāśrayaḥ /
aprakāśo manodīpacakṣurādi tathaiva tat // 32
meaning:
प्रकाशात्म न तत्संविच्चाप्रकाशा तदाश्रयः /
अप्रकाशो मनोदीपचक्षुरादि तथैव तत् // 32
text_mt:
does not consist of luminosity, consciousness [itself] is unilluminated, its locus
is unilluminated, and mind, lamp, eye, and the like are likewise so.

sanskrit_iast:
kiṃ tatprakāśatāṃ nāma supte jagati sarvataḥ /
jñānasyārthaprakāśatvaṃ nanu rūpaṃ pradīpavat // 33
meaning:
किं तत्प्रकाशतां नाम सुप्ते जगति सर्वतः /
ज्ञानस्यार्थप्रकाशत्वं ननु रूपं प्रदीपवत् // 33
text_mt:
With the whole world utterly asleep, what indeed could be illuminated?
[Opponent:] Surely the very nature of knowledge is to illuminate objects, like a lamp!

sanskrit_iast:
apūrvamatra viditaṃ narīnṛtyāmahe tataḥ /
arthaprakāśo jñānasya yadrūpaṃ tannirūpyatām // 34
meaning:
अपूर्वमत्र विदितं नरीनृत्यामहे ततः /
अर्थप्रकाशो ज्ञानस्य यद्रूपं तन्निरूप्यताम् // 34
text_mt:
[Reply:] A unprecedented novelty has been revealed here, so we dance with joy!
Let this nature of knowledge, which is the illumination of an object, be examined:

sanskrit_iast:
arthaḥ prakāśaścedrūpamartho vā jñānameva vā /
athārthasya prakāśo yastadrūpamiti bhaṇyate // 35
meaning:
अर्थः प्रकाशश्चेद्रूपमर्थो वा ज्ञानमेव वा /
अथार्थस्य प्रकाशो यस्तद्रूपमिति भण्यते // 35
text_mt:
if the object is luminosity, is its nature the object or knowledge itself?
Or is it said that its nature is the illumination of an object?

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaṣṭhī kartari cedukto doṣa eva duruddharaḥ /
atha karmaṇi ṣaṣṭhyeṣā ṇyarthastatra hṛdi sthitaḥ // 36
meaning:
षष्ठी कर्तरि चेदुक्तो दोष एव दुरुद्धरः /
अथ कर्मणि षष्ठ्येषा ण्यर्थस्तत्र हृदि स्थितः // 36
text_mt:
If the genitive has an agentive sense, the very flaw stated earlier is irremediable;
if this genitive has an objective sense, then the causative meaning lies at heart.

sanskrit_iast:
tathā cedaṃ darśayāmaḥ kiṃ prakāśaḥ prakāśate /
aprakāśo'pi naivāsau tathāpi ca na kiṃcana // 37
meaning:
तथा चेदं दर्शयामः किं प्रकाशः प्रकाशते /
अप्रकाशोऽपि नैवासौ तथापि च न किंचन // 37
text_mt:
In that case, we show this: does luminosity shine forth?
Even if it is unilluminated, it does not exist, and even so, nothing at all [is illuminated].

sanskrit_iast:
tarhi loke kathaṃ ṇyarthaḥ ucyate cetanasthitau /
mukhyo ṇyarthasya viṣayo jaḍeṣu tvaupacārikaḥ // 38
meaning:
तर्हि लोके कथं ण्यर्थः उच्यते चेतनस्थितौ /
मुख्यो ण्यर्थस्य विषयो जडेषु त्वौपचारिकः // 38
text_mt:
How then is the causative sense used in worldly usage? It is explained: in the domain of the conscious,
the causative sense has its primary application, but with regard to insentient things it is metaphorical.

sanskrit_iast:
tathāhi gantuṃ śakto'pi caitro'nyāyattatāṃ gateḥ /
manvāna eva vaktyasmi gamitaḥ svāmineti hi // 39
meaning:
तथाहि गन्तुं शक्तोऽपि चैत्रोऽन्यायत्ततां गतेः /
मन्वान एव वक्त्यस्मि गमितः स्वामिनेति हि // 39
text_mt:
For instance, Caitra, although capable of walking, thinking that his walking is dependent on another,
says: 'Indeed, I was made to walk by my master.'

sanskrit_iast:
svāmyapyasya gatau śaktiṃ buddhvā svādhīnatāṃ sphuṭam /
paśyannivṛttimāśaṃkya gamayāmīti bhāṣate // 40
meaning:
स्वाम्यप्यस्य गतौ शक्तिं बुद्ध्वा स्वाधीनतां स्फुटम् /
पश्यन्निवृत्तिमाशंक्य गमयामीति भाषते // 40
text_mt:
The master, too, knowing his capacity to walk and clearly seeing his obedience,
suspecting that he might stop, says: 'I make him walk.'

sanskrit_iast:
preryaprerakayorevaṃ maulikī ṇyarthasaṃgatiḥ /
tadabhiprāyato'nyo'pi loke vyavaharettathā // 41
meaning:
प्रेर्यप्रेरकयोरेवं मौलिकी ण्यर्थसंगतिः /
तदभिप्रायतोऽन्योऽपि लोके व्यवहरेत्तथा // 41
text_mt:
Thus the primary connection of the causative sense occurs between the impeller and the impelled;
based on that intention, another person also speaks similarly in worldly usage.

sanskrit_iast:
śaraṃ gamayatītyatra punarvegākhyasaṃskriyām /
vidadhatprerakammanya upacāreṇa jāyate // 42
meaning:
शरं गमयतीत्यत्र पुनर्वेगाख्यसंस्क्रियाम् /
विदधत्प्रेरकम्मन्य उपचारेण जायते // 42
text_mt:
When one says, 'He makes the arrow go,'
producing an impulse called velocity, he considers himself an impeller only metaphorically.

sanskrit_iast:
vāyuradriṃ pātayatītyatra dvāvapi tau jaḍau /
draṣṭṛbhiḥ prerakapreryavapuṣā parikalpitau // 43
meaning:
वायुरद्रिं पातयतीत्यत्र द्वावपि तौ जडौ /
द्रष्टृभिः प्रेरकप्रेर्यवपुषा परिकल्पितौ // 43
text_mt:
In 'The wind brings down the mountain,' both are insentient,
[yet] they are conceptualized by observers in the guise of impeller and impelled.

sanskrit_iast:
itthaṃ jaḍena saṃbandhe na mukhyā ṇyarthasaṃgatiḥ /
āstāmanyatra vitatametadvistarato mayā // 44
meaning:
इत्थं जडेन संबन्धे न मुख्या ण्यर्थसंगतिः /
आस्तामन्यत्र विततमेतद्विस्तरतो मया // 44
text_mt:
Thus, in relation to the insentient, the causative connection is not primary.
Let this rest; I have discussed this extensively elsewhere.

sanskrit_iast:
arthe prakāśanā seyamupacārastato bhavet /
astu cedbhāsate tarhi sa eva patadadrivat // 45
meaning:
अर्थे प्रकाशना सेयमुपचारस्ततो भवेत् /
अस्तु चेद्भासते तर्हि स एव पतदद्रिवत् // 45
text_mt:
Therefore, this illumination in the object would be metaphorical;
if that be accepted, then that [object] alone appears, like the falling mountain.

sanskrit_iast:
upacāre nimittena kenāpi kila bhūyate /
vāyuḥ pātayatītyatra nimittaṃ tatkṛtā kriyā // 46
meaning:
उपचारे निमित्तेन केनापि किल भूयते /
वायुः पातयतीत्यत्र निमित्तं तत्कृता क्रिया // 46
text_mt:
For a metaphor requires some basis or other;
in 'The wind brings down [the mountain],' the basis is the action performed by it,

sanskrit_iast:
girau yenaiṣa saṃyoganāśādbhraṃśaṃ prapadyate /
iha tu jñānamarthasya na kiṃcitkarameva tat // 47
meaning:
गिरौ येनैष संयोगनाशाद्भ्रंशं प्रपद्यते /
इह तु ज्ञानमर्थस्य न किंचित्करमेव तत् // 47
text_mt:
whereby the mountain, through the destruction of its conjunction, undergoes a fall;
but here, knowledge does nothing whatsoever to the object.

sanskrit_iast:
upacāraḥ kathaṃ nāma bhavetso'pi hyavastusan /
aprakāśita evārthaḥ prakāśatvopacārataḥ // 48
meaning:
उपचारः कथं नाम भवेत्सोऽपि ह्यवस्तुसन् /
अप्रकाशित एवार्थः प्रकाशत्वोपचारतः // 48
text_mt:
