How could a metaphor occur if it is entirely unreal?
An object is completely unilluminated through a metaphorical attribution of luminosity.

sanskrit_iast:
tādṛgeva śiśuḥ kiṃ hi dahatyagnyupacārataḥ /
śiśau vahnyupacāre yadbījaṃ taikṣṇyādi tacca sat // 49
meaning:
तादृगेव शिशुः किं हि दहत्यग्न्युपचारतः /
शिशौ वह्न्युपचारे यद्बीजं तैक्ष्ण्यादि तच्च सत् // 49
text_mt:
Does a child burn just because he is metaphorically called fire?
In metaphorically calling a child fire, the basis—sharpness and the like—is real.

sanskrit_iast:
prakāśatvopacāre tu kiṃ bījaṃ yatra satyatā /
siddhe hi cetane yukta upacāraḥ sa hi sphuṭam // 50
meaning:
प्रकाशत्वोपचारे तु किं बीजं यत्र सत्यता /
सिद्धे हि चेतने युक्त उपचारः स हि स्फुटम् // 50
text_mt:
But what is the basis in the metaphorical attribution of luminosity, where truth lies?
For only when a conscious being is established is metaphor appropriate, clearly so;

sanskrit_iast:
adhyāropātmakaḥ so'pi pratisaṃdhānajīvitaḥ /
na cādyāpi kimapyasti cetanaṃ jñānamapyadaḥ // 51
meaning:
अध्यारोपात्मकः सोऽपि प्रतिसंधानजीवितः /
न चाद्यापि किमप्यस्ति चेतनं ज्ञानमप्यदः // 51
text_mt:
even that consists of superimposition, enlivened by synthesis.
And here, not even a single conscious being exists, nor is this knowledge [conscious];

sanskrit_iast:
aprakāśaṃ tadanyena tatprakāśe'pyayaṃ vidhiḥ /
nanu pradīpo rūpasya prakāśaḥ kathamīdṛśam // 52
meaning:
अप्रकाशं तदन्येन तत्प्रकाशेऽप्ययं विधिः /
ननु प्रदीपो रूपस्य प्रकाशः कथमीदृशम् // 52
text_mt:
it is unilluminated; even if it is illuminated by another, this same rule applies.
[Opponent:] Surely a lamp is the illumination of visible form; how can this be so?

sanskrit_iast:
atrāpi na vahantyetāḥ kiṃ nu yuktivikalpanāḥ /
yādṛśā svena rūpeṇa dīpo rūpaṃ prakāśayet // 53
meaning:
अत्रापि न वहन्त्येताः किं नु युक्तिविकल्पनाः /
यादृशा स्वेन रूपेण दीपो रूपं प्रकाशयेत् // 53
text_mt:
Do these dialectical arguments not hold sway here as well?
In the manner in which a lamp illuminates visible form through its own form,

sanskrit_iast:
tādṛśā svayamapyeṣa bhāti jñānaṃ tu no tathā /
pradīpaścaiṣa bhāvānāṃ prakāśatvaṃ dadā[dhā]tyalam // 54
meaning:
तादृशा स्वयमप्येष भाति ज्ञानं तु नो तथा /
प्रदीपश्चैष भावानां प्रकाशत्वं ददा[धा]त्यलम् // 54
text_mt:
in that same manner it shines by itself; but knowledge does not do so.
And this lamp sufficiently bestows luminosity upon things;

sanskrit_iast:
anyathā na prakāśerannabhede cedṛśo vidhiḥ /
tasmātprakāśa evāyaṃ pūrvoktaḥ paramaḥ śivaḥ // 55
meaning:
अन्यथा न प्रकाशेरन्नभेदे चेदृशो विधिः /
तस्मात्प्रकाश एवायं पूर्वोक्तः परमः शिवः // 55
text_mt:
otherwise, they would not be illuminated; in non-difference, such is the rule.
Therefore, it is this very luminosity, previously described as supreme Śiva,

sanskrit_iast:
yathā yathā prakāśeta tattadbhāvavapuḥ sphuṭam /
evaṃ ca nīlatā nāma yathā kācitprakāśate // 56
meaning:
यथा यथा प्रकाशेत तत्तद्भाववपुः स्फुटम् /
एवं च नीलता नाम यथा काचित्प्रकाशते // 56
text_mt:
which shines forth clearly in the form of each respective entity.
And just as a particular blueness shines forth,

sanskrit_iast:
tadvaccakāsti vedyatvaṃ tacca bhāvāṃśapṛṣṭhagam /
phalaṃ prakaṭatārthasya saṃvidveti dvayaṃ tataḥ // 57
meaning:
तद्वच्चकास्ति वेद्यत्वं तच्च भावांशपृष्ठगम् /
फलं प्रकटतार्थस्य संविद्वेति द्वयं ततः // 57
text_mt:
so also shines forth object-hood, and that follows upon a part of the entity.
Therefore, whether the result is the manifestation of the object or consciousness—this pair

sanskrit_iast:
vipakṣato rakṣitaṃ ca saṃdhānaṃ cāpi tanmithaḥ /
tathāhi nibhṛtaścauraścaitravedyamiti sphuṭam // 58
meaning:
विपक्षतो रक्षितं च संधानं चापि तन्मिथः /
तथाहि निभृतश्चौरश्चैत्रवेद्यमिति स्फुटम् // 58
text_mt:
is protected from the opposing view, and their mutual connection is maintained.
To explain: a hidden thief, clearly understanding

sanskrit_iast:
buddhvā nādatta evāśu parīpsāvivaśo'pi san /
seyaṃ paśyati māṃ netratribhāgeneti sādaram // 59
meaning:
बुद्ध्वा नादत्त एवाशु परीप्साविवशोऽपि सन् /
सेयं पश्यति मां नेत्रत्रिभागेनेति सादरम् // 59
text_mt:
that a thing is an object known to Caitra, does not seize it at once, even though overcome by craving;
[and thinking] with delight: 'She looks at me with a sidelong glance,'

sanskrit_iast:
svaṃ dehamamṛteneva siktaṃ paśyati kāmukaḥ /
na caitajjñānasaṃvittimātraṃ bhāvāṃśapṛṣṭhagam // 60
meaning:
स्वं देहममृतेनेव सिक्तं पश्यति कामुकः /
न चैतज्ज्ञानसंवित्तिमात्रं भावांशपृष्ठगम् // 60
text_mt:
a lover sees his body as if sprinkled with nectar;
and this is not mere consciousness of knowledge, but follows upon a part of the entity;

sanskrit_iast:
arthakriyākaraṃ taccenna dharmaḥ konvasau bhavet /
yaccoktaṃ vedyatādharmā bhāvaḥ sarvānapi prati // 61
meaning:
अर्थक्रियाकरं तच्चेन्न धर्मः कोन्वसौ भवेत् /
यच्चोक्तं वेद्यताधर्मा भावः सर्वानपि प्रति // 61
text_mt:
if it produces causal efficacy, what property would it be if not [object-hood]?
And as for the statement that an entity possessing the property of object-hood would be so towards all,

sanskrit_iast:
syādityetatsvapakṣaghnaṃ duṣprayogāstravattava /
asmākaṃ tu svaprakāśaśivatāmātravādinām // 62
meaning:
स्यादित्येतत्स्वपक्षघ्नं दुष्प्रयोगास्त्रवत्तव /
अस्माकं तु स्वप्रकाशशिवतामात्रवादिनाम् // 62
text_mt:
this destroys your own position, like a badly aimed missile.
For us, however, who maintain only the self-luminous nature of Śiva,

sanskrit_iast:
anyaṃ prati cakāstīti vaca eva na vidyate /
sarvānprati ca tannīlaṃ sa ghaṭaśceti yadvacaḥ // 63
meaning:
अन्यं प्रति चकास्तीति वच एव न विद्यते /
सर्वान्प्रति च तन्नीलं स घटश्चेति यद्वचः // 63
text_mt:
the statement 'it shines forth in relation to another' does not even exist.
And as for the claim that 'it is blue to all' and 'it is a pot [to all],'

sanskrit_iast:
tadapyaviditaprāyaṃ gṛhītaṃ mugdhabuddhibhiḥ /
nahi kālāgnirudrīyakāyāvagatanīlimā // 64
meaning:
तदप्यविदितप्रायं गृहीतं मुग्धबुद्धिभिः /
नहि कालाग्निरुद्रीयकायावगतनीलिमा // 64
text_mt:
even that has been accepted largely without understanding by simple-minded people.
For the blueness perceived in the body of Kālāgnirudra

sanskrit_iast:
tava nīlaḥ kiṃ nu pīto maivaṃ bhūnnatu nīlakaḥ /
na kaṃcitprati nīlo'sau nīlo vā yaṃ prati sthitaḥ // 65
meaning:
तव नीलः किं नु पीतो मैवं भून्नतु नीलकः /
न कंचित्प्रति नीलोऽसौ नीलो वा यं प्रति स्थितः // 65
text_mt:
is not blue to you; could it be yellow? Let it not be so, yet it is not blue [to you].
It is not blue to anyone, or rather, to whomsoever it is present as blue,

sanskrit_iast:
taṃ pratyeva sa vedyaḥ syātsaṃkalpadvārako'ntataḥ /
yathā cārthaprakāśātma jñānaṃ saṃgīryate tvayā // 66
meaning:
तं प्रत्येव स वेद्यः स्यात्संकल्पद्वारकोऽन्ततः /
यथा चार्थप्रकाशात्म ज्ञानं संगीर्यते त्वया // 66
text_mt:
in relation to that one alone it would be an object of knowledge, mediated ultimately by conceptual thought.
And just as knowledge consisting of the manifestation of the object is admitted by you,

sanskrit_iast:
tathā tajjñātṛvedyatvaṃ bhāvīyaṃ rūpamucyatām /
na ca jñātātra niyataḥ kaścijjñāne yathā tava // 67
meaning:
तथा तज्ज्ञातृवेद्यत्वं भावीयं रूपमुच्यताम् /
न च ज्ञातात्र नियतः कश्चिज्ज्ञाने यथा तव // 67
text_mt:
So too, let its knowability by a [particular] knower be declared the nature belonging to the thing.
And no [single] knower is fixed here, just as in the case of your cognition. // 67

sanskrit_iast:
arthe jñātā yadā yo yastadvedyaṃ vapurucyatām /
tattadvijñātṛvedyatvaṃ sarvānpratyeva bhāsatām // 68
meaning:
अर्थे ज्ञाता यदा यो यस्तद्वेद्यं वपुरुच्यताम् /
तत्तद्विज्ञातृवेद्यत्वं सर्वान्प्रत्येव भासताम् // 68
text_mt:
When whichever knower relates to an object, let that knowable form be spoken of.
Let that knowability by respective knowers shine forth to all indeed. // 68

sanskrit_iast:
ityevaṃ codayanmanye vrajedbadhiradhuryatām /
nahyanyaṃ prati vai kaṃcidbhāti sā vedyatā tathā // 69
meaning:
इत्येवं चोदयन्मन्ये व्रजेद्बधिरधुर्यताम् /
नह्यन्यं प्रति वै कंचिद्भाति सा वेद्यता तथा // 69
text_mt:
One who objects thus, I consider, would attain the foremost rank among the deaf;
for that knowability does not shine forth to anyone else in that way! // 69

sanskrit_iast:
bhāvasya rūpamityukte keyamasthānavaidhurī /
anena nītimārgeṇa nirmūlamapasāritā // 70
meaning:
भावस्य रूपमित्युक्ते केयमस्थानवैधुरी /
अनेन नीतिमार्गेण निर्मूलमपसारिता // 70
text_mt:
When it is said to be the 'nature of an entity', what is this groundless agitation?
By this line of reasoning, it is completely removed at its root. // 70

sanskrit_iast:
anavasthā tathā hyanyairnīlādyaiḥ sadṛśī na sā /
vedyatā kiṃtu dharmo'sau yadyogātsarvadharmavān // 71
meaning:
अनवस्था तथा ह्यन्यैर्नीलाद्यैः सदृशी न सा /
वेद्यता किंतु धर्मोऽसौ यद्योगात्सर्वधर्मवान् // 71
text_mt:
For such an infinite regress does not exist; that knowability is not like other [properties] such as blue,
but it is a property through connection with which a possessor of properties possessing all properties // 71

sanskrit_iast:
dharmī vedyatvamabhyeti sa sattāsamavāyavat /
brūṣe yathā hi kurute sattā satyasataḥ sataḥ // 72
meaning:
धर्मी वेद्यत्वमभ्येति स सत्तासमवायवत् /
ब्रूषे यथा हि कुरुते सत्ता सत्यसतः सतः // 72
text_mt:
—a subject—attains knowability, just like the inherence of beingness.
For as you say, beingness makes non-existent things existent in an entity; // 72

sanskrit_iast:
samavāyo'pi saṃśliṣṭaḥ śliṣṭānaśliṣṭatājuṣaḥ /
antyo viśeṣo vyāvṛttirūpo vyāvṛttivarjitān // 73
meaning:
समवायोऽपि संश्लिष्टः श्लिष्टानश्लिष्टताजुषः /
अन्त्यो विशेषो व्यावृत्तिरूपो व्यावृत्तिवर्जितान् // 73
text_mt:
inherence also, conjoined, makes those sharing connection or non-connection connected;
the ultimate differentiator, whose nature is distinction, makes those devoid of distinction // 73

sanskrit_iast:
vyāvṛttān śvetimā śuklamaśuklaṃ gamanaṃ tathā /
tadvannīlādidharmāṃśayukto dharmī svayaṃ sthitaḥ // 74
meaning:
व्यावृत्तान् श्वेतिमा शुक्लमशुक्लं गमनं तथा /
तद्वन्नीलादिधर्मांशयुक्तो धर्मी स्वयं स्थितः // 74
text_mt:
distinct; whiteness makes the non-white white, and motion likewise [moves the stationary].
In the same way, the subject, standing by itself, endowed with portions of properties such as blue, // 74

sanskrit_iast:
avedyo vedyatārūpāddharmādvedyatvamāgataḥ /
vedyatā bhāsamānā ca svayaṃ nīlādidharmavat // 75
meaning:
अवेद्यो वेद्यतारूपाद्धर्माद्वेद्यत्वमागतः /
वेद्यता भासमाना च स्वयं नीलादिधर्मवत् // 75
text_mt:
unknowable [in itself], attains knowability from the property consisting of knowability;
and knowability, shining forth by itself like properties such as blue, // 75

sanskrit_iast:
aprakāśā svaprakāśāddharmādeti prakāśatām /
prakāśe khalu viśrāntiṃ viśvaṃ śrayati cettataḥ // 76
meaning:
अप्रकाशा स्वप्रकाशाद्धर्मादेति प्रकाशताम् /
प्रकाशे खलु विश्रान्तिं विश्वं श्रयति चेत्ततः // 76
text_mt:
unilluminated [in itself], comes to luminosity from a self-luminous property.
If, indeed, the universe takes rest in luminosity, then // 76

sanskrit_iast:
nānyā kācidapekṣāsya kṛtakṛtyasya sarvataḥ /
yathā ca śivanāthena svātantryādbhāsyate bhidā // 77
meaning:
नान्या काचिदपेक्षास्य कृतकृत्यस्य सर्वतः /
यथा च शिवनाथेन स्वातन्त्र्याद्भास्यते भिदा // 77
text_mt:
it has accomplished all its ends and has no other expectation whatsoever.
And just as difference is illuminated by the Lord Śiva out of absolute autonomy, // 77

sanskrit_iast:
nīlādivattathaivāyaṃ vedyatā dharma ucyate /
evaṃ siddhaṃ hi vedyatvaṃ bhāvadharmo'stu kā ghṛṇā // 78
meaning:
नीलादिवत्तथैवायं वेद्यता धर्म उच्यते /
एवं सिद्धं हि वेद्यत्वं भावधर्मोऽस्तु का घृणा // 78
text_mt:
just like blue and the rest, so too this property called knowability is explained.
Thus knowability is established; let it be a property of an entity, what shame is there? // 78

sanskrit_iast:
idaṃ tu cintyaṃ sakalaparyantoktapramātṛbhiḥ /
vedyatvamekarūpaṃ syāccāturdaśyamataḥ kutaḥ // 79
meaning:
इदं तु चिन्त्यं सकलपर्यन्तोक्तप्रमातृभिः /
वेद्यत्वमेकरूपं स्याच्चातुर्दश्यमतः कुतः // 79
text_mt:
This, however, must be considered: with the knowers mentioned up to the sakala,
knowability would be uniform; whence, then, is there a fourteenfold division? // 79

sanskrit_iast:
ucyate paripūrṇaṃ cedbhāvīyaṃ rūpamucyate /
tadvibhurbhairavo devo bhagavāneva bhaṇyate // 80
meaning:
उच्यते परिपूर्णं चेद्भावीयं रूपमुच्यते /
तद्विभुर्भैरवो देवो भगवानेव भण्यते // 80
text_mt:
The reply is: if the nature belonging to an entity is said to be completely full,
then the all-pervading divine Lord Bhairava alone is spoken of. // 80

sanskrit_iast:
atha tannijamāhātmyakalpito'ṃśāṃśikākramaḥ /
sahyate kiṃ kṛtaṃ tarhi proktakalpanayānayā // 81
meaning:
अथ तन्निजमाहात्म्यकल्पितोऽंशांशिकाक्रमः /
सह्यते किं कृतं तर्हि प्रोक्तकल्पनयानया // 81
text_mt:
If, on the other hand, the succession of parts and sub-parts fashioned by his own majesty
is accepted, what then is accomplished by this aforementioned assumption? // 81

sanskrit_iast:
ata eva yadā yena vapuṣā bhāti yadyathā /
tadā tathā tattadrūpamityeṣopaniṣatparā // 82
meaning:
अत एव यदा येन वपुषा भाति यद्यथा /
तदा तथा तत्तद्रूपमित्येषोपनिषत्परा // 82
text_mt:
Therefore, when, through whichever form, something shines forth in whatever manner,
then in that way that is its nature: this is the supreme secret doctrine. // 82

sanskrit_iast:
caitreṇa vedyaṃ jānāmi dvābhyāṃ bahubhirapyatha /
mantreṇa tanmaheśena śivenodriktaśaktinā // 83
meaning:
चैत्रेण वेद्यं जानामि द्वाभ्यां बहुभिरप्यथ /
मन्त्रेण तन्महेशेन शिवेनोद्रिक्तशक्तिना // 83
text_mt:
‘I know what is to be known by Caitra, or by two, or by many,
or by a mantra, or by that great lord Śiva whose power has surged forth, // 83

sanskrit_iast:
anyādṛśena vetyevaṃ bhāvo bhāti yathā tathā /
arthakriyādivaicitryamabhyetyaparisaṃkhyayā // 84
meaning:
अन्यादृशेन वेत्येवं भावो भाति यथा तथा /
अर्थक्रियादिवैचित्र्यमभ्येत्यपरिसंख्यया // 84
text_mt:
or by someone of another kind’—in this way, however the entity shines forth,
it attains a manifold variety of causal efficacy and the like beyond counting. // 84

sanskrit_iast:
tathā hyekāgrasakalasāmājikajanaḥ khalu /
nṛttaṃ gītaṃ sudhāsārasāgaratvena manyate // 85
meaning:
तथा ह्येकाग्रसकलसामाजिकजनः खलु /
नृत्तं गीतं सुधासारसागरत्वेन मन्यते // 85
text_mt:
For thus, indeed, the entire audience, when single-minded,
regards the dance and song as an ocean of the essence of nectar. // 85

sanskrit_iast:
tata evocyate mallanaṭaprekṣopadeśane /
sarvapramātṛtādātmyaṃ pūrṇarūpānubhāvakam // 86
meaning:
तत एवोच्यते मल्लनटप्रेक्षोपदेशने /
सर्वप्रमातृतादात्म्यं पूर्णरूपानुभावकम् // 86
text_mt:
For that very reason, it is said in the instruction on witnessing wrestlers and actors:
identity with all knowers brings about the experience of the full form. // 86

sanskrit_iast:
tāvanmātrārthasaṃvittituṣṭāḥ pratyekaśo yadi /
kaḥ saṃbhūya guṇasteṣāṃ pramātraikyaṃ bhavecca kim // 87
meaning:
तावन्मात्रार्थसंवित्तितुष्टाः प्रत्येकशो यदि /
कः संभूय गुणस्तेषां प्रमात्रैक्यं भवेच्च किम् // 87
text_mt:
If each individually were satisfied merely with the consciousness of the object to that extent,
what collective excellence would they have, and what unity of knower would arise? // 87

sanskrit_iast:
yadā tu tattadvedyatvadharmasaṃdarbhagarbhitam /
tadvastu śuṣkātprāgrūpādanyadyuktamidaṃ tadā // 88
meaning:
यदा तु तत्तद्वेद्यत्वधर्मसंदर्भगर्भितम् /
तद्वस्तु शुष्कात्प्राग्रूपादन्यद्युक्तमिदं तदा // 88
text_mt:
When, however, that entity is pregnant with the fabric of various properties of knowability,
then it is fittingly different from its dry earlier form. // 88

sanskrit_iast:
śāstre'pi tattadvedyatvaṃ viśiṣṭārthakriyākaram /
bhūyasaiva tathāca śrīmālinīvijayottare // 89
meaning:
शास्त्रेऽपि तत्तद्वेद्यत्वं विशिष्टार्थक्रियाकरम् /
भूयसैव तथाच श्रीमालिनीविजयोत्तरे // 89
text_mt:
In the scripture too, these various states of knowability produce differentiated causal efficacy
in abundant measure; and so it is in the venerable Mālinīvijayottara: // 89

sanskrit_iast:
tathā ṣaḍvidhamadhvānamanenādhiṣṭhitaṃ smaret /
adhiṣṭhānaṃ hi devena yadviśvasya pravedanam // 90
meaning:
तथा षड्विधमध्वानमनेनाधिष्ठितं स्मरेत् /
अधिष्ठानं हि देवेन यद्विश्वस्य प्रवेदनम् // 90
text_mt:
‘Likewise, one should remember that the sixfold path is presided over by this [mantra].’
For the divine being’s presidership is the knowing of the universe; // 90

sanskrit_iast:
tadīśavedyatvenetthaṃ jñātaṃ prakṛtakāryakṛt /
evaṃ siddhaṃ vedyatākhyo dharmo bhāvasya bhāsate // 91
meaning:
तदीशवेद्यत्वेनेत्थं ज्ञातं प्रकृतकार्यकृत् /
एवं सिद्धं वेद्यताख्यो धर्मो भावस्य भासते // 91
text_mt:
known in this way as knowable by the Lord, it accomplishes the relevant function.
Thus it is established that the property called knowability shines forth as belonging to an entity. // 91

sanskrit_iast:
tadanābhāsayoge tu svarūpamiti bhaṇyate /
upādhiyogitāśaṅkāmapahastayato'sphuṭam // 92
meaning:
तदनाभासयोगे तु स्वरूपमिति भण्यते /
उपाधियोगिताशङ्कामपहस्तयतोऽस्फुटम् // 92
text_mt:
When it does not shine forth, however, it is spoken of as its own essential nature,
clearing away any indistinct apprehension of connection with an adjunct. // 92

sanskrit_iast:
svātmano yena vapuṣā bhātyarthastatsvakaṃ vapuḥ /
jānāmi ghaṭamityatra vedyatānuparāgavān // 93
meaning:
स्वात्मनो येन वपुषा भात्यर्थस्तत्स्वकं वपुः /
जानामि घटमित्यत्र वेद्यतानुपरागवान् // 93
text_mt:
Through whichever form belonging to itself an object shines forth, that is its own form.
In the experience ‘I know the pot’, the pot, untouched by knowability, // 93

sanskrit_iast:
ghaṭa eva svarūpeṇa bhāta ityapadiśyate /
nanu tatra svayaṃvedyabhāvo mantrādyapekṣayā // 94
meaning:
घट एव स्वरूपेण भात इत्यपदिश्यते /
ननु तत्र स्वयंवेद्यभावो मन्त्राद्यपेक्षया // 94
text_mt:
is designated as having shone forth in its own essential nature.
[Objection:] Now, in that case, does not the state of being known by oneself exist, in view of mantras and the like? // 94

sanskrit_iast:
api cāstyeva nanvastu natu sanpratibhāsate /
avedyameva kālāgnivapurmeroḥ parā diśaḥ // 95
meaning:
अपि चास्त्येव नन्वस्तु नतु सन्प्रतिभासते /
अवेद्यमेव कालाग्निवपुर्मेरोः परा दिशः // 95
text_mt:
[Reply:] It may indeed exist, but it does not shine forth as existing.
The body of the Fire of Time and the farther regions of Mount Meru are completely unknowable; // 95

sanskrit_iast:
mameti saṃvidi paraṃ śuddhaṃ vastu prakāśate /
bhātatvādvedyamapi tanna vedyatvena bhāsanāt // 96
meaning:
ममेति संविदि परं शुद्धं वस्तु प्रकाशते /
भातत्वाद्वेद्यमपि तन्न वेद्यत्वेन भासनात् // 96
text_mt:
only the pure object shines forth in consciousness as ‘mine’.
Though knowable because it has shone forth, it is not [experienced] through its shining as knowable. // 96

sanskrit_iast:
avedyameva bhānaṃ hi tathā kamanuyuñjmahe /
evaṃ pañcadaśātmeyaṃ dharā tadvajjalādayaḥ // 97
meaning:
अवेद्यमेव भानं हि तथा कमनुयुञ्ज्महे /
एवं पञ्चदशात्मेयं धरा तद्वज्जलादयः // 97
text_mt:
Its manifestation is indeed unknowable; how could we challenge that?
Thus this earth possesses fifteen forms, and similarly water and the rest, // 97

sanskrit_iast:
avyaktāntā yato'styeṣāṃ sakalaṃ prati vedyatā /
yattūcyate kalādyena dharāntena samanvitāḥ // 98
meaning:
अव्यक्तान्ता यतोऽस्त्येषां सकलं प्रति वेद्यता /
यत्तूच्यते कलाद्येन धरान्तेन समन्विताः // 98
text_mt:
extending up to the unmanifest, since they possess knowability with respect to a sakala.
As for what is said: ‘Those endowed [with tattvas] from kalā to earth // 98

sanskrit_iast:
sakalā iti tatkośaṣaṭkodrekopalakṣaṇam /
udbhūtāśuddhacidrāgakalādirasakañcukāḥ // 99
meaning:
सकला इति तत्कोशषट्कोद्रेकोपलक्षणम् /
उद्भूताशुद्धचिद्रागकलादिरसकञ्चुकाः // 99
text_mt:
are sakalas,’ that is an indicative mark of the predominance of the six sheaths.
They have the cuirasses of the flavor of kalā and so forth, in which impure consciousness and attachment have arisen. // 99

sanskrit_iast:
sakalālayasaṃjñāstu nyagbhūtākhilakañcukāḥ /
jñānākalāstu dhvastaitatkañcukā iti nirṇayaḥ // 100
meaning:
सकलालयसंज्ञास्तु न्यग्भूताखिलकञ्चुकाः /
ज्ञानाकलास्तु ध्वस्तैतत्कञ्चुका इति निर्णयः // 100
text_mt:
Those called sakalālayas, however, have all cuirasses submerged;
and the jñānākalas have these cuirasses destroyed: such is the determination. // 100

sanskrit_iast:
tena pradhāne vedye'pi pumānudbhūtakañcukaḥ /
pramātāstyeva sakalaḥ pāñcadaśyamataḥ sthitam // 101
meaning:
तेन प्रधाने वेद्येऽपि पुमानुद्भूतकञ्चुकः /
प्रमातास्त्येव सकलः पाञ्चदश्यमतः स्थितम् // 101
text_mt:
Therefore, even when the unmanifest is knowable, the soul with arisen cuirasses
exists as a sakala knower; hence the fifteenfold nature is established. // 101

sanskrit_iast:
pāñcadaśyaṃ dharādhantarniviṣṭe sakale'pi ca /
sakalāntaramastyeva prameye'trāpi mātṛ hi // 102
meaning:
पाञ्चदश्यं धराधन्तर्निविष्टे सकलेऽपि च /
सकलान्तरमस्त्येव प्रमेयेऽत्रापि मातृ हि // 102
text_mt:
There is a fifteenfold nature even in a sakala situated within the earth-path,
for another sakala exists as knower even regarding this knowable object. // 102

sanskrit_iast:
sthūlāvṛtādisaṃkocatadanyavyāptṛtājuṣaḥ /
pītādyāḥ sthirakampratvāccaturdaśa dharādiṣu // 103
meaning:
स्थूलावृतादिसंकोचतदन्यव्याप्तृताजुषः /
पीताद्याः स्थिरकम्प्रत्वाच्चतुर्दश धरादिषु // 103
text_mt:
Endowed with the contraction of being gross, covered, and the like, and with the pervasion of other [degrees],
yellow and so forth, because of stability and trembling, are fourteenfold in earth and the rest; // 103

sanskrit_iast:
svarūpībhūtajaḍatāḥ prāṇadehapathe tataḥ /
pramātṛtājuṣaḥ proktā dhāraṇā vijayottare // 104
meaning:
स्वरूपीभूतजडताः प्राणदेहपथे ततः /
प्रमातृताजुषः प्रोक्ता धारणा विजयोत्तरे // 104
text_mt:
having insentience as their own nature, in the path of breath and body,
they are taught in the Vijayottara as dharāṇās possessing knower-hood. // 104

sanskrit_iast:
yadā tu meyatā puṃsaḥ kalāntasya prakalpyate /
tadudbhūtaḥ kañcukāṃśo meyo nāsya pramātṛtā // 105
meaning:
यदा तु मेयता पुंसः कलान्तस्य प्रकल्प्यते /
तदुद्भूतः कञ्चुकांशो मेयो नास्य प्रमातृता // 105
text_mt:
When, however, the knowability of a soul ending with kalā is posited,
the arisen portion of the cuirass is knowable; he has no knower-hood. // 105

sanskrit_iast:
ataḥ sakalasaṃjñasya pramātṛtvaṃ na vidyate /
trayodaśatvaṃ tacchaktiśaktimaddvayavarjanāt // 106
meaning:
अतः सकलसंज्ञस्य प्रमातृत्वं न विद्यते /
त्रयोदशत्वं तच्छक्तिशक्तिमद्द्वयवर्जनात् // 106
text_mt:
Hence, there is no knower-hood for the one called sakala;
there is a thirteenfold nature, owing to the exclusion of the pair of power and power-holder. // 106

sanskrit_iast:
nyagbhūtakañcuko mātā yukta[yata]statra layākalaḥ /
māyāniviṣṭo vijñānākalādyāḥ prāgvadeva tu // 107
meaning:
न्यग्भूतकञ्चुको माता युक्त[यत]स्तत्र लयाकलः /
मायानिविष्टो विज्ञानाकलाद्याः प्राग्वदेव तु // 107
text_mt:
The knower whose cuirass is submerged is the layākala who is properly situated there;
resting in māyā, the vijñānākalas and the rest are just as before. // 107

sanskrit_iast:
māyātattve jñeyarūpe kañcukanyagbhavo'pi yaḥ /
so'pi meyaḥ kañcukaikyaṃ yato māyā susūkṣmikā // 108
meaning:
मायातत्त्वे ज्ञेयरूपे कञ्चुकन्यग्भवोऽपि यः /
सोऽपि मेयः कञ्चुकैक्यं यतो माया सुसूक्ष्मिका // 108
text_mt:
When the māyā-principle is in the form of the knowable, even the submersion of the cuirass
is also knowable, because the identity of the cuirasses is the exceedingly subtle māyā. // 108

sanskrit_iast:
vijñānākala evātra tato mātāpakañcukaḥ /
māyāniviṣṭe'pyakale tathetyekādaśātmatā // 109
meaning:
विज्ञानाकल एवात्र ततो मातापकञ्चुकः /
मायानिविष्टेऽप्यकले तथेत्येकादशात्मता // 109
text_mt:
Therefore, only the vijñānākala, whose cuirass has departed, is the knower here;
and when the akala situated in māyā is likewise [a knower], there is an elevenfold nature. // 109

sanskrit_iast:
vijñānakevale vedye kañcukadhvaṃsasusthite /
udbubhūṣuprabodhānāṃ mantrāṇāmeva mātṛtā // 110
meaning:
विज्ञानकेवले वेद्ये कञ्चुकध्वंससुस्थिते /
उद्बुभूषुप्रबोधानां मन्त्राणामेव मातृता // 110
text_mt:
When the vijñānakevala is the knowable, firmly abiding in the destruction of the cuirasses,
knower-hood belongs only to the mantras whose awakening desires to arise. // 110

sanskrit_iast:
te'pi mantrā yadā meyāstadā mātā tadīśvaraḥ /
sa hyudbhavātpūrṇabodhastasminprāpte tu meyatām // 111
meaning:
तेऽपि मन्त्रा यदा मेयास्तदा माता तदीश्वरः /
स ह्युद्भवात्पूर्णबोधस्तस्मिन्प्राप्ते तु मेयताम् // 111
text_mt:
When those mantras too are knowables, then their lord is the knower,
for he has full awakening from emergence; but when he has attained knowability, // 111

sanskrit_iast:
udbhūtapūrṇarūpo'sau mātā mantramaheśvaraḥ /
tasminvijñeyatāṃ prāpte svaprakāśaḥ paraḥ śivaḥ // 112
meaning:
उद्भूतपूर्णरूपोऽसौ माता मन्त्रमहेश्वरः /
तस्मिन्विज्ञेयतां प्राप्ते स्वप्रकाशः परः शिवः // 112
text_mt:
the Mantramaheśvara, whose full form has arisen, is the knower.
When he has attained the state of being known, the self-luminous supreme Śiva // 112

sanskrit_iast:
pramātā svakatādātmyabhāsitākhilavedyakaḥ /
śivaḥ pramātā no meyo hyanyādhīnaprakāśatā // 113
meaning:
प्रमाता स्वकतादात्म्यभासिताखिलवेद्यकः /
शिवः प्रमाता नो मेयो ह्यन्याधीनप्रकाशता // 113
text_mt:
is the knower, illuminating all knowables through identity with himself.
Śiva is the knower and not the knowable, for knowability is dependent on another. // 113

sanskrit_iast:
meyatā sā na tatrāsti svaprakāśo hyasau prabhuḥ /
svaprakāśe'tra kasmiṃścidanabhyupagate sati // 114
meaning:
मेयता सा न तत्रास्ति स्वप्रकाशो ह्यसौ प्रभुः /
स्वप्रकाशेऽत्र कस्मिंश्चिदनभ्युपगते सति // 114
text_mt: That state of being an object of cognition does not exist there, for that Lord is self-luminous. / If someone self-luminous were not accepted here,

sanskrit_iast:
aprakāśātprakāśatve hyanavasthā duruttarā /
tataśca suptaṃ viśvaṃ syānna caivaṃ bhāsate hi tat // 115
meaning:
अप्रकाशात्प्रकाशत्वे ह्यनवस्था दुरुत्तरा /
ततश्च सुप्तं विश्वं स्यान्न चैवं भासते हि तत् // 115
text_mt: there would indeed be an insurmountable infinite regress in explaining luminosity through what is unilluminated, / and consequently the universe would be asleep; yet it is not so, for it shines forth.

sanskrit_iast:
anyādhīnaprakāśaṃ hi tadbhātyanyastvasau śivaḥ /
ityasya svaprakāśatve kimanyairyuktiḍambaraiḥ // 116
meaning:
अन्याधीनप्रकाशं हि तद्भात्यन्यस्त्वसौ शिवः /
इत्यस्य स्वप्रकाशत्वे किमन्यैर्युक्तिडम्बरैः // 116
text_mt: For it shines forth having its luminosity dependent upon another, while this other is Śiva. / Thus, regarding his self-luminosity, what need is there for other ostentatious arguments?

sanskrit_iast:
mānānāṃ hi paro jīvaḥ sa evetyuktamāditaḥ /
nanvasti svaprakāśe'pi śive vedyatvamīdṛśaḥ // 117
meaning:
मानानां हि परो जीवः स एवेत्युक्तमादितः /
नन्वस्ति स्वप्रकाशेऽपि शिवे वेद्यत्वमीदृशः // 117
text_mt: For it has been stated from the beginning that he alone is the supreme life of means of knowledge. / [Objection:] Now, even though Śiva is self-luminous, can there not be cognisability in him? Otherwise,

sanskrit_iast:
upadeśo[śyo]padeṣṭṛtvavyavahāro'nyathā katham /
satyaṃ sa tu tathā sṛṣṭaḥ parameśena vedyatām // 118
meaning:
उपदेशो[श्यो]पदेष्टृत्वव्यवहारोऽन्यथा कथम् /
सत्यं स तु तथा सृष्टः परमेशेन वेद्यताम् // 118
text_mt: how could the ordinary practice of instruction between teacher and pupil take place? / [Answer:] True, but when he is created thus by the Supreme Lord and brought to cognisability,

sanskrit_iast:
nīto mantramaheśādikakṣyāṃ samadhiśāyyate /
tathābhūtaśca vedyo'sau nānavacchinnasaṃvidaḥ // 119
meaning:
नीतो मन्त्रमहेशादिकक्ष्यां समधिशाय्यते /
तथाभूतश्च वेद्योऽसौ नानवच्छिन्नसंविदः // 119
text_mt: he is made to rest at the level of Mantramaheśvara and the like. / And an entity that has become an object of cognition in such a manner cannot belong to uncircumscribed consciousness.

sanskrit_iast:
pūrṇasya vedyatā yuktā parasparavirodhataḥ /
tathā vedyasvabhāve'pi vastuto na śivātmatām // 120
meaning:
पूर्णस्य वेद्यता युक्ता परस्परविरोधतः /
तथा वेद्यस्वभावेऽपि वस्तुतो न शिवात्मताम् // 120
text_mt: Cognisability of that which is full is inappropriate, because of mutual contradiction. / In that way, even if its nature is an object of cognition, in reality it does not abandon the nature of Śiva.

sanskrit_iast:
ko'pi bhāvaḥ projjhatīti satyaṃ tadbhāvanā phalet /
śrīpūrvaśāstre tenoktaṃ śivaḥ sākṣānna bhidyate // 121
meaning:
कोऽपि भावः प्रोज्झतीति सत्यं तद्भावना फलेत् /
श्रीपूर्वशास्त्रे तेनोक्तं शिवः साक्षान्न भिद्यते // 121
text_mt: No entity whatsoever abandons [that nature]; thus contemplation on that indeed bears fruit. / Therefore it was said in the venerated Pūrvaśāstra: 'Śiva is directly not differentiated.'

sanskrit_iast:
sākṣātpadenāyamarthaḥ samastaḥ prasphuṭīkṛtaḥ /
nanvekarūpatāyuktaḥ śivastadvaśato bhavet // 122
meaning:
साक्षात्पदेनायमर्थः समस्तः प्रस्फुटीकृतः /
नन्वेकरूपतायुक्तः शिवस्तद्वशतो भवेत् // 122
text_mt: By the word 'directly', this entire meaning has been made evident. / [Objection:] Surely, if Śiva is endowed with uniformity, then on that account,

sanskrit_iast:
trivedatāmantramahānāthe kātra vivāditā /
maheśvareśamantrāṇāṃ tathā kevalinordvayoḥ // 123
meaning:
त्रिवेदतामन्त्रमहानाथे कात्र विवादिता /
महेश्वरेशमन्त्राणां तथा केवलिनोर्द्वयोः // 123
text_mt: how can there be dispute regarding the threefold nature of Mantramahānātha? / Likewise, for the Maheśvaras, Īśas, Mantras, and the two classes of solitary souls,

sanskrit_iast:
anantabhedataikaikaṃ sthitā sakalavatkila /
tato layākale meye pramātāsti layākalaḥ // 124
meaning:
अनन्तभेदतैकैकं स्थिता सकलवत्किल /
ततो लयाकले मेये प्रमातास्ति लयाकलः // 124
text_mt: each remains distinct through endless divisions, just like the Sakala. / Therefore, when the layākala is an object of cognition, there is a layākala subject;

sanskrit_iast:
atastrayodaśatvaṃ syāditthaṃ naikādaśātmatā /
vijñānākalavedyatve'pyanyo jñānākalo bhavet // 125
meaning:
अतस्त्रयोदशत्वं स्यादित्थं नैकादशात्मता /
विज्ञानाकलवेद्यत्वेऽप्यन्यो ज्ञानाकलो भवेत् // 125
text_mt: hence there would be thirteen [classes], and in this way not an elevenfold nature. / When the vijñānākala is an object of cognition, there would also be another vijñānākala

sanskrit_iast:
mātā tadekādaśatā syānnaiva tu navātmatā /
evaṃ mantratadīśānāṃ mantreśāntarasaṃbhave // 126
meaning:
माता तदेकादशता स्यान्नैव तु नवात्मता /
एवं मन्त्रतदीशानां मन्त्रेशान्तरसंभवे // 126
text_mt: as subject, and thus it would be elevenfold, and not ninefold at all. / Similarly, in the case of the Mantras and their lords, if another Mantreśa were to exist

sanskrit_iast:
vedyatvānnava sapta syuḥ sapta pañca tu te katham /
ucyate satyamastyeṣā kalanā kiṃtu susphuṭaḥ // 127
meaning:
वेद्यत्वान्नव सप्त स्युः सप्त पञ्च तु ते कथम् /
उच्यते सत्यमस्त्येषा कलना किंतु सुस्फुटः // 127
text_mt: due to cognisability, nine would become seven, and seven would become five—how so? / It is said in reply: True, this enumeration exists, but just as differentiation

sanskrit_iast:
yathātra sakale bhedo na tathā tvakalādike /
anantāvāntaredṛkṣayonibhedavataḥ sphuṭam // 128
meaning:
यथात्र सकले भेदो न तथा त्वकलादिके /
अनन्तावान्तरेदृक्षयोनिभेदवतः स्फुटम् // 128
text_mt: is clearly evident here in the Sakala, it is not so in the Akala and the rest, / which possess clearly endless subdivisions belonging to such wombs [of rebirth].

sanskrit_iast:
caturdaśavidhasyāsya sakalasyāsti bheditā /
layākale tu saṃskāramātrātsatyapyasau bhidā // 129
meaning:
चतुर्दशविधस्यास्य सकलस्यास्ति भेदिता /
लयाकले तु संस्कारमात्रात्सत्यप्यसौ भिदा // 129
text_mt: This fourteenfold Sakala has distinct varieties. / In the layākala, however, although such distinction exists due merely to residual traces,

sanskrit_iast:
akalena viśeṣāya sakalasyaiva yujyate /
vijñānakevalādīnāṃ tāvatyapi na vai bhidā // 130
meaning:
अकलेन विशेषाय सकलस्यैव युज्यते /
विज्ञानकेवलादीनां तावत्यपि न वै भिदा // 130
text_mt: it serves as a distinctive mark only for the Sakala through the Akala. / Among the vijñānakevalas and the rest, not even so much distinction exists;

sanskrit_iast:
śivasvācchandyamātraṃ tu bhedāyaiṣāṃ vijṛmbhate /
ityāśayena saṃpaśyanviśeṣaṃ sakalādiha // 131
meaning:
शिवस्वाच्छन्द्यमात्रं तु भेदायैषां विजृम्भते /
इत्याशयेन संपश्यन्विशेषं सकलादिह // 131
text_mt: only Śiva's sovereign freedom unfolds to produce their distinction. / Seeing the distinction in this world beginning with the Sakala with this intention in mind,

sanskrit_iast:
layākalādau novāca trāyodaśyādikaṃ vibhuḥ /
nanvastu vedyatā bhāvadharmaḥ kiṃtu layākalau // 132
meaning:
लयाकलादौ नोवाच त्रायोदश्यादिकं विभुः /
नन्वस्तु वेद्यता भावधर्मः किंतु लयाकलौ // 132
text_mt: the all-pervading Lord did not teach a thirteenfold division or the like beginning with the layākala. / [Objection:] Granted that cognisability is a property of entities; but the two layākalas

sanskrit_iast:
manvāte neha vai kiṃcittadapekṣā tvasau katham /
śrūyatāṃ saṃvidaikātmyatattve'sminsaṃvyavasthite // 133
meaning:
मन्वाते नेह वै किंचित्तदपेक्षा त्वसौ कथम् /
श्रूयतां संविदैकात्म्यतत्त्वेऽस्मिन्संव्यवस्थिते // 133
text_mt: do not think of anything here at all, so how can there be a relation of dependency for them? / Hear this: when the truth of the oneness of consciousness is firmly established,

sanskrit_iast:
jaḍe'pi citirastyeva bhotsyamāne tu kā kathā /
svabodhāvasare tāvadbhotsyate layakevalī // 134
meaning:
जडेऽपि चितिरस्त्येव भोत्स्यमाने तु का कथा /
स्वबोधावसरे तावद्भोत्स्यते लयकेवली // 134
text_mt: consciousness exists even in the insentient, so what need be said of one who will awaken? / At the time of his own awakening, the layakevalin will indeed awaken.

sanskrit_iast:
dvividhaśca prabodho'sya mantratvāya bhavāya ca /
bhāvanādibalādanyavaiṣṇavādinayoditāt // 135
meaning:
द्विविधश्च प्रबोधोऽस्य मन्त्रत्वाय भवाय च /
भावनादिबलादन्यवैष्णवादिनयोदितात् // 135
text_mt: And his awakening is twofold: toward becoming a Mantra and toward mundane existence. / By the power of contemplation and the like taught in other traditions such as the Vaiṣṇava,

sanskrit_iast:
yathāsvamādharauttaryavicitrātsaṃskṛtastathā /
līnaḥ prabuddho mantratvaṃ tadīśatvamathaiti vā // 136
meaning:
यथास्वमाधरौत्तर्यविचित्रात्संस्कृतस्तथा /
लीनः प्रबुद्धो मन्त्रत्वं तदीशत्वमथैति वा // 136
text_mt: he is appropriately refined through diverse lower and higher [states]. / Having been dissolved, once awakened, he attains the state of a Mantra or its lord.

sanskrit_iast:
svātantryavarjitā ye tu balānmohavaśīkṛtāḥ /
layākalātsvasaṃskārātprabuddhyante bhavāya te // 137
meaning:
स्वातन्त्र्यवर्जिता ये तु बलान्मोहवशीकृताः /
लयाकलात्स्वसंस्कारात्प्रबुद्ध्यन्ते भवाय ते // 137
text_mt: Those, however, who are devoid of freedom and forcibly dominated by delusion, / awaken from the layākala toward mundane existence due to their own residual traces.

sanskrit_iast:
jñānākalo'pi mantreśamaheśatvāya budhyate /
mantrāditvāya vā jātu jātu saṃsṛtaye'pi vā // 138
meaning:
ज्ञानाकलोऽपि मन्त्रेशमहेशत्वाय बुध्यते /
मन्त्रादित्वाय वा जातु जातु संसृतयेऽपि वा // 138
text_mt: The jñānākala also awakens to the state of Mantreśa and Maheśa, / or sometimes to the state of Mantra and the rest, or even to transmigration.

sanskrit_iast:
avatāro hi vijñāniyogibhāve'sya bhidyate /
uktaṃ ca bodhayāmāsa sa sisṛkṣurjagatprabhuḥ // 139
meaning:
अवतारो हि विज्ञानियोगिभावेऽस्य भिद्यते /
उक्तं च बोधयामास स सिसृक्षुर्जगत्प्रभुः // 139
text_mt: For his descent into the state of a knowing yogin differs. / And it is stated in the venerated Pūrvaśāsana: 'The Lord of the universe, desiring to emanate,

sanskrit_iast:
vijñānakevalānaṣṭāviti śrīpūrvaśāsane /
ataḥ prabhotsyamānatve yānayorbodhayogyatā // 140
meaning:
विज्ञानकेवलानष्टाविति श्रीपूर्वशासने /
अतः प्रभोत्स्यमानत्वे यानयोर्बोधयोग्यता // 140
text_mt: awakened the eight vijñānakevalas.' / Therefore, since they are about to awaken, the suitability for awakening belonging to these two

sanskrit_iast:
tadbalādvedyatāyogyabhāvenaivātra vedyatā /
tathāhi gāḍhanidre'pi priye'nāśaṅkitāgatām // 141
meaning:
तद्बलाद्वेद्यतायोग्यभावेनैवात्र वेद्यता /
तथाहि गाढनिद्रेऽपि प्रियेऽनाशङ्कितागताम् // 141
text_mt: is, by virtue of that, cognisability here precisely through being an entity suitable for cognisability. / To explain: even when her beloved is in deep sleep, a woman going to meet him

sanskrit_iast:
māṃ drakṣyatīti nāṅgeṣu sveṣu mātyabhisārikā /
evaṃ śivo'pi manute etasyaitatpravedyatām // 142
meaning:
मां द्रक्ष्यतीति नाङ्गेषु स्वेषु मात्यभिसारिका /
एवं शिवोऽपि मनुते एतस्यैतत्प्रवेद्यताम् // 142
text_mt: overflows with joy in her own limbs, thinking, 'He will see me who have arrived unexpectedly.' / In this way, Śiva too considers, 'He will cognise this;

sanskrit_iast:
yāsyatīti sṛjāmīti tadānīṃ yogyataiva sā /
vedyatā tasya bhāvasya bhoktṛtā tāvatī ca sā // 143
meaning:
यास्यतीति सृजामीति तदानीं योग्यतैव सा /
वेद्यता तस्य भावस्य भोक्तृता तावती च सा // 143
text_mt: I emanate it'—at that time, that very suitability / is the cognisability of that entity, and it is to that extent its enjoyership.

sanskrit_iast:
layākalasya citro hi bhogaḥ kena vikalpyate /
yathā yathā hi samvittiḥ sa hi bhogaḥ sphuṭo'sphuṭaḥ // 144
meaning:
लयाकलस्य चित्रो हि भोगः केन विकल्प्यते /
यथा यथा हि सम्वित्तिः स हि भोगः स्फुटोऽस्फुटः // 144
text_mt: For by whom could the diverse experience of the layākala be mentally conceived? / According as consciousness is, so is that experience, clear or unclear.

sanskrit_iast:
smṛtiyogyo'pyanyathā vā bhogyabhāvaṃ na tūjjhati /
gāḍhanidrāvimūḍho'pi kāntāliṅgitavigrahaḥ // 145
meaning:
स्मृतियोग्योऽप्यन्यथा वा भोग्यभावं न तूज्झति /
गाढनिद्राविमूढोऽपि कान्तालिङ्गितविग्रहः // 145
text_mt: Even if suitable for memory or otherwise, it does not abandon the state of being an object of experience. / Even when bewildered in deep sleep, one whose body is embraced by his beloved

sanskrit_iast:
bhoktaiva bhaṇyate so'pi manute bhoktṛtāṃ purā /
utprekṣāmātrahīno'pi kāṃcitkulavadhūṃ puraḥ // 146
meaning:
भोक्तैव भण्यते सोऽपि मनुते भोक्तृतां पुरा /
उत्प्रेक्षामात्रहीनोऽपि कांचित्कुलवधूं पुरः // 146
text_mt: is said to be an enjoyer indeed; he too earlier thinks of his own state of being an enjoyer. / Even without any mental projection beforehand, seeing a noble wife in front of him

sanskrit_iast:
saṃbhokṣyamāṇāṃ dṛṣṭvaiva rabhasādyāti saṃmadam /
tāmeva dṛṣṭvā ca tadā samānāśayabhāgapi // 147
meaning:
संभोक्ष्यमाणां दृष्ट्वैव रभसाद्याति संमदम् /
तामेव दृष्ट्वा च तदा समानाशयभागपि // 147
text_mt: about to be enjoyed, he experiences exhilaration out of impetuous passion; / whereas upon seeing that very same woman, another person, even if possessing a similar disposition,

sanskrit_iast:
anyastathā na saṃvitte kamatropalabhāmahe /
loke rūḍhamidaṃ dṛṣṭirasminkāraṇamantarā // 148
meaning:
अन्यस्तथा न संवित्ते कमत्रोपलभामहे /
लोके रूढमिदं दृष्टिरस्मिन्कारणमन्तरा // 148
text_mt: does not experience it in that way: whom can we perceive as a cause here? / This is well established in the world when one says, 'Without any external cause, the gaze in this matter

sanskrit_iast:
prasīdatīva magneva nirvātīvetivādini /
itthaṃ vistaratastattvabhedo'yaṃ samudāhṛtaḥ // 149
meaning:
प्रसीदतीव मग्नेव निर्वातीवेतिवादिनि /
इत्थं विस्तरतस्तत्त्वभेदोऽयं समुदाहृतः // 149
text_mt: becomes serene, as if immersed, as if tranquil.' / In this manner, this division of principles has been explained in detail.

sanskrit_iast:
śaktiśaktimatāṃ bhedādanyonyaṃ tatkṛteṣvapi /
bhedeṣvanyonyato bhedāttathā tattvāntaraiḥ saha // 150
meaning:
शक्तिशक्तिमतां भेदादन्योन्यं तत्कृतेष्वपि /
भेदेष्वन्योन्यतो भेदात्तथा तत्त्वान्तरैः सह // 150
text_mt: Due to the mutual differentiation between powers and power-holders, even within the distinctions created by them, / due to mutual differentiation, and likewise with other principles,

sanskrit_iast:
bhedopabhedagaṇanāṃ karvato nāvadhiḥ kvacit /
tata eva vicitro'yaṃ bhuvanādividhiḥ sthitaḥ // 151
meaning:
भेदोपभेदगणनां कर्वतो नावधिः क्वचित् /
तत एव विचित्रोऽयं भुवनादिविधिः स्थितः // 151
text_mt: there is no limit anywhere for one calculating the divisions and subdivisions. / For that very reason, this manifold arrangement of worlds and so forth is established.

sanskrit_iast:
pārthivatve'pi no sāmyaṃ rudravaiṣṇavalokayoḥ /
kā kathānyatra tu bhavedbhoge vāpi svarūpake // 152
meaning:
पार्थिवत्वेऽपि नो साम्यं रुद्रवैष्णवलोकयोः /
का कथान्यत्र तु भवेद्भोगे वापि स्वरूपके // 152
text_mt: Even though both are earthly, there is no equality between the realms of Rudra and Viṣṇu; / what need be said elsewhere, whether in enjoyment or in essential nature?

sanskrit_iast:
sa ca no vistaraḥ sākṣācchakyo yadyapi bhāṣitum /
tathāpi mārgamātreṇa kathyamāno vivicyatām // 153
meaning:
स च नो विस्तरः साक्षाच्छक्यो यद्यपि भाषितुम् /
तथापि मार्गमात्रेण कथ्यमानो विविच्यताम् // 153
text_mt: And although that full extent cannot directly be spoken of, / nevertheless, let it be examined as it is being described merely by way of outline.

sanskrit_iast:
saptānāṃ mātṛśaktīnāmanyonyaṃ bhedane sati /
rūpamekānnapañcāśatsvarūpaṃ cādhikaṃ tataḥ // 154
meaning:
सप्तानां मातृशक्तीनामन्योन्यं भेदने सति /
रूपमेकान्नपञ्चाशत्स्वरूपं चाधिकं ततः // 154
text_mt: When the seven mother powers are mutually distinguished, / their form is forty-nine, and beyond that their own essential natures are even more.

sanskrit_iast:
sarvaṃ sarvātmakaṃ yasmāttasmātsakalamātari /
layākalādiśaktīnāṃ saṃbhavo'styeva tattvataḥ // 155
meaning:
सर्वं सर्वात्मकं यस्मात्तस्मात्सकलमातरि /
लयाकलादिशक्तीनां संभवोऽस्त्येव तत्त्वतः // 155
text_mt: Because everything consists of everything, therefore in the Sakala subject, / the powers of the layākala and the others certainly exist in reality.

sanskrit_iast:
sa tvasphuṭo'stu bhedāṃśaṃ dātuṃ tāvatprabhurbhavet /
teṣāmapi ca bhedānāmanyonyaṃ bahubhedatā // 156
meaning:
स त्वस्फुटोऽस्तु भेदांशं दातुं तावत्प्रभुर्भवेत् /
तेषामपि च भेदानामन्योन्यं बहुभेदता // 156
text_mt: Though it may be unmanifest, it would indeed have the power to impart a share of distinction. / And among those divisions also, there is mutual manifold distinction.

sanskrit_iast:
mukhyānāṃ bhedabhedānāṃ jalādyairbhedane sati /
mukhyabhedaprakāreṇa vidherānantyamucyate // 157
meaning:
मुख्यानां भेदभेदानां जलाद्यैर्भेदने सति /
मुख्यभेदप्रकारेण विधेरानन्त्यमुच्यते // 157
text_mt: When the primary divisions and subdivisions are diversified by water and the other elements, / infinity of the arrangement is declared in terms of the primary distinctions.

sanskrit_iast:
sakalasya samudbhūtāścakṣurādisvaśaktayaḥ /
nyagbhūtāśca pratanvanti bhedāntaramapi sphuṭam // 158
meaning:
सकलस्य समुद्भूताश्चक्षुरादिस्वशक्तयः /
न्यग्भूताश्च प्रतन्वन्ति भेदान्तरमपि स्फुटम् // 158
text_mt: In the Sakala, the innate faculties of sight and the other senses, whether fully emerged / or submerged, clearly unfold yet another division.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ layākalādīnāṃ tatsaṃskārapadoditāt /
pāṭavātprakṣayādvāpi bhedāntaramudīyate // 159
meaning:
एवं लयाकलादीनां तत्संस्कारपदोदितात् /
पाटवात्प्रक्षयाद्वापि भेदान्तरमुदीयते // 159
text_mt: In the same way, for the layākala and the rest, another distinction is stated / arising from the efficacy or the exhaustion originating from their state of residual traces.

sanskrit_iast:
nyakkṛtāṃ śaktimāsthāyāpyudāsīnatayā sthitim /
anāviśyeva yadvetti tatrānyā vedyatā khalu // 160
meaning:
न्यक्कृतां शक्तिमास्थायाप्युदासीनतया स्थितिम् /
अनाविश्येव यद्वेत्ति तत्रान्या वेद्यता खलु // 160
text_mt: When, though having suppressed [its sensory] power, it knows by resting in indifference without as it were entering into [the object], then the state of being an object of cognition is indeed of another kind.

sanskrit_iast:
āviśyeva nimajjyeva vikāsyeva vighūrṇya ca /
vidato vedyatānyaiva bhedo'trārthakriyocitaḥ // 161
meaning:
आविश्येव निमज्ज्येव विकास्येव विघूर्ण्य च /
विदतो वेद्यतान्यैव भेदोऽत्रार्थक्रियोचितः // 161
text_mt: When one knows by as it were entering, as it were plunging in, as it were expanding, and reeling, the state of being an object of cognition is quite different; here, the distinction is fit for purposeful action.

sanskrit_iast:
anyaśaktitirobhāve kasyāścitsusphuṭodaye /
bhedāntaramapi jñeyaṃ vīṇāvādakadṛṣṭivat // 162
meaning:
अन्यशक्तितिरोभावे कस्याश्चित्सुस्फुटोदये /
भेदान्तरमपि ज्ञेयं वीणावादकदृष्टिवत् // 162
text_mt: When another power is submerged and a particular one arises very clearly, another distinction should be recognized, as in the case of a vīṇā player.

sanskrit_iast:
tirobhāvodbhavau śakteḥ svaśaktyantarato'nyataḥ /
cetyamānādacetyādvā tanvāte bahubhedatām // 163
meaning:
तिरोभावोद्भवौ शक्तेः स्वशक्त्यन्तरतोऽन्यतः /
चेत्यमानादचेत्याद्वा तन्वाते बहुभेदताम् // 163
text_mt: The disappearance and emergence of a power, whether from another power of its own or from something else, whether from what is being cognized or what is not being cognized, bring about manifold diversity.

sanskrit_iast:
evametaddharādīnāṃ tattvānāṃ yāvatī daśā /
kācidasti ghaṭākhyāpi tatra saṃdarśitā bhidaḥ // 164
meaning:
एवमेतद्धरादीनां तत्त्वानां यावती दशा /
काचिदस्ति घटाख्यापि तत्र संदर्शिता भिदः // 164
text_mt: In this way, whatever state pertains to the principles beginning with earth, even that called a 'pot', the distinctions within it have been demonstrated.

sanskrit_iast:
atrāpi vedyatā nāma tādātmyaṃ vedakaiḥ saha /
tataḥ sakalavedyo'sau ghaṭaḥ sakala eva hi // 165
meaning:
अत्रापि वेद्यता नाम तादात्म्यं वेदकैः सह /
ततः सकलवेद्योऽसौ घटः सकल एव हि // 165
text_mt: Here too, the state of being an object of cognition is identity with the cognizers; therefore, that pot, which is knowable by a sakala, is indeed a sakala itself.

sanskrit_iast:
yāvacchivaikavedyo'sau śiva evāvabhāsate /
tāvadekaśarīro hi bodho bhātyeva yāvatā // 166
meaning:
यावच्छिवैकवेद्योऽसौ शिव एवावभासते /
तावदेकशरीरो हि बोधो भात्येव यावता // 166
text_mt: Until it shines forth as Śiva himself, knowable solely by Śiva, consciousness shines only as having a single body to that extent.

sanskrit_iast:
adhunātra samastasya dharātattvasya darśyate /
sāmastya evābhihitaṃ pāñcadaśyaṃ puroditam // 167
meaning:
अधुनात्र समस्तस्य धरातत्त्वस्य दर्श्यते /
सामस्त्य एवाभिहितं पाञ्चदश्यं पुरोदितम् // 167
text_mt: Now, in regard to the earth-principle in its entirety, the fifteenfold nature previously declared is demonstrated as a whole.

sanskrit_iast:
dharātattvāvibhedena yaḥ prakāśaḥ prakāśate /
sa eva śivanātho'tra pṛthivī brahma tanmatam // 168
meaning:
धरातत्त्वाविभेदेन यः प्रकाशः प्रकाशते /
स एव शिवनाथोऽत्र पृथिवी ब्रह्म तन्मतम् // 168
text_mt: That light which shines undifferentiated from the earth-principle is here the Lord Śiva himself; the earth is considered to be Brahman.

sanskrit_iast:
dharātattvagatāḥ siddhīrvitarītuṃ samudyatān /
prerayanti śivecchāto ye te mantramaheśvarāḥ // 169
meaning:
धरातत्त्वगताः सिद्धीर्वितरीतुं समुद्यतान् /
प्रेरयन्ति शिवेच्छातो ये ते मन्त्रमहेश्वराः // 169
text_mt: Those who, by Śiva's will, impel those intent upon bestowing the supernatural powers belonging to the earth-principle, are the Mantramaheśvaras.

sanskrit_iast:
preryamāṇāstu mantreśā mantrāstadvācakāḥ sphuṭam /
dharātattvagataṃ yogamabhyasya śivavidyayā // 170
meaning:
प्रेर्यमाणास्तु मन्त्रेशा मन्त्रास्तद्वाचकाः स्फुटम् /
धरातत्त्वगतं योगमभ्यस्य शिवविद्यया // 170
text_mt: The Mantreśas, however, are those being impelled; the Mantras clearly express them, having practiced the yoga belonging to the earth-principle by means of Śiva's wisdom;

sanskrit_iast:
na tu pāśavasāṃkhyīyavaiṣṇavādidvitādṛśā /
aprāptadhruvadhāmāno vijñānākalatājuṣaḥ // 171
meaning:
न तु पाशवसांख्यीयवैष्णवादिद्वितादृशा /
अप्राप्तध्रुवधामानो विज्ञानाकलताजुषः // 171
text_mt: not, however, those bound souls of the Sāṃkhyas, Vaiṣṇavas, and others, who, not having attained the immutable abode, participate in the state of vijñānākalas.

sanskrit_iast:
tāvattattvopabhogena ye kalpānte layaṃ gatāḥ /
sauṣuptāvasthayopetāste'tra pralayakevalāḥ // 172
meaning:
तावत्तत्त्वोपभोगेन ये कल्पान्ते लयं गताः /
सौषुप्तावस्थयोपेतास्तेऽत्र प्रलयकेवलाः // 172
text_mt: Those who, through experiencing that principle up to that point, have dissolved at the end of a cosmic age and are endowed with the state of deep sleep, are here the pralayakevalas.

sanskrit_iast:
sauṣupte tattvalīnatvaṃ sphuṭameva hi lakṣyate /
anyathā niyatasvapnasaṃdṛṣṭirjāyate kutaḥ // 173
meaning:
सौषुप्ते तत्त्वलीनत्वं स्फुटमेव हि लक्ष्यते /
अन्यथा नियतस्वप्नसंदृष्टिर्जायते कुतः // 173
text_mt: Indeed, dissolution into the principles is clearly observed in deep sleep; otherwise, how could a determinate dream-vision arise?

sanskrit_iast:
sauṣuptamapi citraṃ ca svacchāsvacchādi bhāsate /
asvāpsaṃ sukhamityādismṛtivaicitryadarśanāt // 174
meaning:
सौषुप्तमपि चित्रं च स्वच्छास्वच्छादि भासते /
अस्वाप्सं सुखमित्यादिस्मृतिवैचित्र्यदर्शनात् // 174
text_mt: Deep sleep also shines variegated as clear, unclear, and so forth, because one observes a variety of memories such as 'I slept pleasantly.'

sanskrit_iast:
yadaiva sa kṣaṇaṃ sūkṣmaṃ nidrāyaiva prabuddhyate /
tadaiva smṛtireṣeti nārthajajñānajā smṛtiḥ // 175
meaning:
यदैव स क्षणं सूक्ष्मं निद्रायैव प्रबुद्ध्यते /
तदैव स्मृतिरेषेति नार्थजज्ञानजा स्मृतिः // 175
text_mt: Precisely when one awakens after having slept for even a subtle moment, this memory arises at that very time; it is not a memory born of cognition arising from an external object.

sanskrit_iast:
tena mūḍhairyaducyeta prabuddhasyāntarāntarā /
tūlikādisukhasparśasmṛtireṣeti tatkutaḥ // 176
meaning:
तेन मूढैर्यदुच्येत प्रबुद्धस्यान्तरान्तरा /
तूलिकादिसुखस्पर्शस्मृतिरेषेति तत्कुतः // 176
text_mt: Therefore, when fools claim that this is the awakened person's memory of the pleasant contact with a mattress and the like at various intervals, how could that be so?

sanskrit_iast:
māhākarmasamullāsasaṃmiśritamalābilāḥ /
dharādhirohiṇo jñeyāḥ sakalā iha pudgalāḥ // 177
meaning:
माहाकर्मसमुल्लाससंमिश्रितमलाबिलाः /
धराधिरोहिणो ज्ञेयाः सकला इह पुद्गलाः // 177
text_mt: Those who are soiled by impurity intermingled with the surging of great karma, ascending the earth-[principle], are to be known here as the sakala embodied souls.

sanskrit_iast:
asyaiva saptakasya svasvavyāpāraprakalpane /
prakṣobho yastadevoktaṃ śaktīnāṃ saptakaṃ sphuṭam // 178
meaning:
अस्यैव सप्तकस्य स्वस्वव्यापारप्रकल्पने /
प्रक्षोभो यस्तदेवोक्तं शक्तीनां सप्तकं स्फुटम् // 178
text_mt: When this very heptad is deployed in its respective operations, the agitation that occurs is clearly declared to be the heptad of powers.

sanskrit_iast:
śivo hyacyutacidrūpastisrastacchaktayastu yāḥ /
tāḥ svātantryavaśopāttagrahītrākāratāvaśāt // 179
meaning:
शिवो ह्यच्युतचिद्रूपस्तिस्रस्तच्छक्तयस्तु याः /
ताः स्वातन्त्र्यवशोपात्तग्रहीत्राकारतावशात् // 179
text_mt: For Śiva's nature is imperishable consciousness; but his three powers, by virtue of assuming the form of the cognizer through his absolute autonomy,

sanskrit_iast:
tridhā mantrāvasānāḥ syurudāsīnā iva sthitāḥ /
grāhyākāroparāgāttu grahītrākāratāvaśāt // 180
meaning:
त्रिधा मन्त्रावसानाः स्युरुदासीना इव स्थिताः /
ग्राह्याकारोपरागात्तु ग्रहीत्राकारतावशात् // 180
text_mt: would be threefold down to the Mantras, resting as if indifferent. But from the coloring by the form of the knowable, by virtue of the form of the cognizer,

sanskrit_iast:
sakalāntāstu tāstisra icchājñānakriyā matāḥ /
saptadhetthaṃ pramātṛtvaṃ tatkṣobho mānatā tathā // 181
meaning:
सकलान्तास्तु तास्तिस्र इच्छाज्ञानक्रिया मताः /
सप्तधेत्थं प्रमातृत्वं तत्क्षोभो मानता तथा // 181
text_mt: those three down to the sakalas are considered to be will, knowledge, and action. Thus cognizership is sevenfold, and its agitation is the means of knowledge;

sanskrit_iast:
yattu grahītṛtārūpasaṃvitsaṃsparśavarjitam /
śuddhaṃ jaḍaṃ tatsvarūpamitthaṃ viśvaṃ trikātmakam // 182
meaning:
यत्तु ग्रहीतृतारूपसंवित्संस्पर्शवर्जितम् /
शुद्धं जडं तत्स्वरूपमित्थं विश्वं त्रिकात्मकम् // 182
text_mt: whereas that which is devoid of the touch of consciousness in the form of a cognizer is pure, insentient objectivity. In this way the universe consists of the Trika.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ jalādyapi vadedbhedairbhinnaṃ mahāmatiḥ /
anayā tu diśā prāyaḥ sarvabhedeṣu vidyate // 183
meaning:
एवं जलाद्यपि वदेद्भेदैर्भिन्नं महामतिः /
अनया तु दिशा प्रायः सर्वभेदेषु विद्यते // 183
text_mt: In this manner, a person of great intellect should speak of water and the other principles as divided by distinctions. Along this direction, virtually in all distinctions,

sanskrit_iast:
bhedo mantramaheśānteṣveṣa pañcadaśātmakaḥ /
tathāpi sphuṭatābhāvātsannapyeṣa na carcitaḥ // 184
meaning:
भेदो मन्त्रमहेशान्तेष्वेष पञ्चदशात्मकः /
तथापि स्फुटताभावात्सन्नप्येष न चर्चितः // 184
text_mt: this fifteenfold division exists ending with the Mantramaheśas; nevertheless, because of its lack of obviousness, even though existing, it has not been discussed [at length].

sanskrit_iast:
etacca sūtritaṃ dhātrā śrīpūrve yadbravīti hi /
savyāpārādhipatvenetyādinā jāgradāditām // 185
meaning:
एतच्च सूत्रितं धात्रा श्रीपूर्वे यद्ब्रवीति हि /
सव्यापाराधिपत्वेनेत्यादिना जाग्रदादिताम् // 185
text_mt: And this has been aphorized by the creator in the venerable Pūrva-śāstra, which indeed teaches the waking state and the others with the words: 'By possessing agency with its operations', etc.

sanskrit_iast:
abhinne'pi śive'ntaḥsthasūkṣmabodhānusārataḥ /
adhunā prāṇaśaktisthe tattvajāle vivicyate // 186
meaning:
अभिन्नेऽपि शिवेऽन्तःस्थसूक्ष्मबोधानुसारतः /
अधुना प्राणशक्तिस्थे तत्त्वजाले विविच्यते // 186
text_mt: Even though Śiva is undivided, the web of principles resting in the vital power is now distinguished according to the subtle inner awareness,

sanskrit_iast:
bhedo'yaṃ pāñcadaśyādiryathā śrīśaṃbhurādiśat /
samaste'rthe'tra nirgrāhye tuṭayaḥ ṣoḍaśa kṣaṇāḥ // 187
meaning:
भेदोऽयं पाञ्चदश्यादिर्यथा श्रीशंभुरादिशत् /
समस्तेऽर्थेऽत्र निर्ग्राह्ये तुटयः षोडश क्षणाः // 187
text_mt: just as the venerable Śambhu taught this fifteenfold and other division: in every object to be grasped here, there are sixteen moments called tuṭis,

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaṭtriṃśadaṅgule cāre sāṃśadvyaṅgulakalpitāḥ /
tatrādyaḥ paramādvaito nirvibhāgarasātmakaḥ // 188
meaning:
षट्त्रिंशदङ्गुले चारे सांशद्व्यङ्गुलकल्पिताः /
तत्राद्यः परमाद्वैतो निर्विभागरसात्मकः // 188
text_mt: reckoned as parts of two digits in a movement of thirty-six digits. Among them, the first is supreme non-duality, whose essence is undivided relish;

sanskrit_iast:
dvitīyo grāhakollāsarūpaḥ prativibhāvyate /
antyastu grāhyatādātmyātsvarūpībhāvamāgataḥ // 189
meaning:
द्वितीयो ग्राहकोल्लासरूपः प्रतिविभाव्यते /
अन्त्यस्तु ग्राह्यतादात्म्यात्स्वरूपीभावमागतः // 189
text_mt: the second is discerned as having the nature of the surging forth of the grasper. But the last, through identity with the object to be grasped, has attained its own form;

sanskrit_iast:
pravibhāvyo na hi pṛthagupāntyo grāhakaḥ kṣaṇaḥ /
tṛtīyaṃ kṣaṇamārabhya kṣaṇaṣaṭkaṃ tu yatsthitam // 190
meaning:
प्रविभाव्यो न हि पृथगुपान्त्यो ग्राहकः क्षणः /
तृतीयं क्षणमारभ्य क्षणषट्कं तु यत्स्थितम् // 190
text_mt: the penultimate moment is the grasper, not to be discerned separately. The six moments, however, which exist beginning with the third moment,

sanskrit_iast:
tannirvikalpaṃ prodgacchadvikalpācchādanātmakam /
tadeva śivarūpaṃ hi paraśaktyātmakaṃ viduḥ // 191
meaning:
तन्निर्विकल्पं प्रोद्गच्छद्विकल्पाच्छादनात्मकम् /
तदेव शिवरूपं हि परशक्त्यात्मकं विदुः // 191
text_mt: are non-conceptual, having the nature of veiling the emerging conceptual constructs; they know that to be the nature of Śiva, consisting of the supreme power.

sanskrit_iast:
dvitīyaṃ madhyamaṃ ṣaṭkaṃ parāparapadātmakam /
vikalparūḍhirapyeṣā kramātprasphuṭatāṃ gatā // 192
meaning:
द्वितीयं मध्यमं षट्कं परापरपदात्मकम् /
विकल्परूढिरप्येषा क्रमात्प्रस्फुटतां गता // 192
text_mt: The second, middle hexad has the nature of the intermediate level; this firm establishment of conceptual constructs also gradually attains clear manifestation.

sanskrit_iast:
ṣaṭke'tra prathame devyastisraḥ pronmeṣavṛttitām /
nimeṣavṛttitāṃ cāśu spṛśantyaḥ ṣaṭkatāṃ gatāḥ // 193
meaning:
षट्केऽत्र प्रथमे देव्यस्तिस्रः प्रोन्मेषवृत्तिताम् /
निमेषवृत्तितां चाशु स्पृशन्त्यः षट्कतां गताः // 193
text_mt: In this first hexad, the three goddesses become a hexad by swiftly touching the activity of opening and the activity of closing.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ dvitīyaṣaṭke'pi kiṃ tvatra grāhyavartmanā /
uparāgapadaṃ prāpya parāparatayā sthitāḥ // 194
meaning:
एवं द्वितीयषट्केऽपि किं त्वत्र ग्राह्यवर्त्मना /
उपरागपदं प्राप्य परापरतया स्थिताः // 194
text_mt: The same is true in the second hexad; but here, by following the path of the knowable and attaining the status of coloring, they stand as intermediate.

sanskrit_iast:
ādye'tra ṣaṭke tā devyaḥ svātantryollāsamātrataḥ /
jighṛkṣite'pyupādhau syuḥ pararūpādavicyutāḥ // 195
meaning:
आद्येऽत्र षट्के ता देव्यः स्वातन्त्र्योल्लासमात्रतः /
जिघृक्षितेऽप्युपाधौ स्युः पररूपादविच्युताः // 195
text_mt: In this first hexad, those goddesses, through the mere surging of absolute autonomy, even when an adjunct is sought to be grasped, remain undeviated from the supreme form.

sanskrit_iast:
asti cātiśayaḥ kaścittāsāmapyuttarottaram /
yo vivekadhanairdhīraiḥ sphuṭīkṛtyāpi darśyate // 196
meaning:
अस्ति चातिशयः कश्चित्तासामप्युत्तरोत्तरम् /
यो विवेकधनैर्धीरैः स्फुटीकृत्यापि दर्श्यते // 196
text_mt: And there is a certain progressive excellence among them as well, which is revealed and demonstrated by the wise whose wealth is discernment.

sanskrit_iast:
kecittvekāṃ tuṭiṃ grāhye caikāmapi grahītari /
tādātmyena vinikṣipya saptakaṃ saptakaṃ viduḥ // 197
meaning:
केचित्त्वेकां तुटिं ग्राह्ये चैकामपि ग्रहीतरि /
तादात्म्येन विनिक्षिप्य सप्तकं सप्तकं विदुः // 197
text_mt: Some, however, by consigning one tuṭi to the knowable and one to the knower through identity, recognize a heptad and a heptad.

sanskrit_iast:
tadasyāṃ sūkṣmasaṃvittau kalanāya samudyatāḥ /
saṃvedayante yadrūpaṃ tatra kiṃ vāgvikatthanaiḥ // 198
meaning:
तदस्यां सूक्ष्मसंवित्तौ कलनाय समुद्यताः /
संवेदयन्ते यद्रूपं तत्र किं वाग्विकत्थनैः // 198
text_mt: Therefore, what is the use of verbal boasting concerning the form which those who are intent on measuring experience in this subtle consciousness?

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ dharādimūlāntaṃ prakriyā prāṇagāminī /
guruparvakramātproktā bhede pañcadaśātmake // 199
meaning:
एवं धरादिमूलान्तं प्रक्रिया प्राणगामिनी /
गुरुपर्वक्रमात्प्रोक्ता भेदे पञ्चदशात्मके // 199
text_mt: In this manner, the process extending to vital breath from the earth up to the root principle has been taught according to the lineage of gurus in its fifteenfold distinction.

sanskrit_iast:
kramāttu bhedanyūnatve nyūnatā syāttuṭiṣvapi /
tasyāṃ hrāso vikalpasya sphuṭatā cāvikalpinaḥ // 200
meaning:
क्रमात्तु भेदन्यूनत्वे न्यूनता स्यात्तुटिष्वपि /
तस्यां ह्रासो विकल्पस्य स्फुटता चाविकल्पिनः // 200
text_mt: When the distinction decreases gradually, there is a decrease in the tuṭis as well; in that [decrease], there is the waning of conceptual constructs and the clarity of the non-conceptual.

sanskrit_iast:
yathā hi ciraduḥkhārtaḥ paścādāttasukhasthitiḥ /
vismaratyeva tadduḥkhaṃ sukhaviśrāntivartmanā // 201
meaning:
यथा हि चिरदुःखार्तः पश्चादात्तसुखस्थितिः /
विस्मरत्येव तद्दुःखं सुखविश्रान्तिवर्त्मना // 201
text_mt: Just as someone long afflicted by sorrow, having subsequently attained a state of pleasure, completely forgets that sorrow by way of resting in pleasure,

sanskrit_iast:
tathā gatavikalpe'pi rūḍhāḥ saṃvedane janāḥ /
vikalpaviśrāntibalāttāṃ sattāṃ nābhimanvate // 202
meaning:
तथा गतविकल्पेऽपि रूढाः संवेदने जनाः /
विकल्पविश्रान्तिबलात्तां सत्तां नाभिमन्वते // 202
text_mt: even so people who have become firmly established in consciousness wherein conceptual constructs have ceased, do not conceive of that [objective] existence by the force of the resting of conceptual constructs.

sanskrit_iast:
vikalpanirhrāsavaśena yāti vikalpavandhyā paramārthasatyā /
saṃvitsvarūpaprakaṭatvamitthaṃ tatrāvadhāne yatatāṃ subuddhiḥ // 203
meaning:
विकल्पनिर्ह्रासवशेन याति विकल्पवन्ध्या परमार्थसत्या /
संवित्स्वरूपप्रकटत्वमित्थं तत्रावधाने यततां सुबुद्धिः // 203
text_mt: By virtue of the waning of conceptual constructs, consciousness, devoid of conceptual constructs and true in the highest sense, comes to reveal its essential nature; thus let one of good intellect strive with attentiveness towards it.

sanskrit_iast:
grāhyagrāhakasaṃvittau saṃbandhe sāvadhānatā /
iyaṃ sā tatra tatroktā sarvakāmadughā yataḥ // 204
meaning:
ग्राह्यग्राहकसंवित्तौ संबन्धे सावधानता /
इयं सा तत्र तत्रोक्ता सर्वकामदुघा यतः // 204
text_mt: Attentiveness to the relationship in the consciousness of knower and known is that which is taught in various contexts, because it grants all desires.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ dvayaṃ dvayaṃ yāvannyūnībhavati bhedagam /
tāvattuṭidvayaṃ yāti nyūnatāṃ kramaśaḥ sphuṭam // 205
meaning:
एवं द्वयं द्वयं यावन्न्यूनीभवति भेदगम् /
तावत्तुटिद्वयं याति न्यूनतां क्रमशः स्फुटम् // 205
text_mt: In this way, as long as each pair belonging to the distinction diminishes, so long clearly does the pair of tuṭis diminish by degrees.

sanskrit_iast:
ata eva śivāveśe dvituṭiḥ parigīyate /
ekā tu sā tuṭistatra pūrṇā śuddhaiva kevalam // 206
meaning:
अत एव शिवावेशे द्वितुटिः परिगीयते /
एका तु सा तुटिस्तत्र पूर्णा शुद्धैव केवलम् // 206
text_mt:
For this very reason, in absorption into Śiva, a two-tuṭi [state] is proclaimed;
and among these, one tuṭi is completely full and purely alone. // 206

sanskrit_iast:
dvitīyā śiva(śakti)rūpaiva sarvajñānakriyātmikā /
tasyāmavahito yogī kiṃ na vetti karoti vā // 207
meaning:
द्वितीया शिव(शक्ति)रूपैव सर्वज्ञानक्रियात्मिका /
तस्यामवहितो योगी किं न वेत्ति करोति वा // 207
text_mt:
The second is of the nature of Śiva's power itself, consisting of all-knowledge and all-action;
attentive to this, what does the yogin not know or do? // 207

sanskrit_iast:
tathā coktaṃ kallaṭena śrīmatā tuṭipātagaḥ /
lābhaḥ sarvajñakartṛtve tuṭeḥ pāto'parā tuṭiḥ // 208
meaning:
तथा चोक्तं कल्लटेन श्रीमता तुटिपातगः /
लाभः सर्वज्ञकर्तृत्वे तुटेः पातोऽपरा तुटिः // 208
text_mt:
And thus it was declared by the illustrious Kallaṭa: "The acquisition consisting in all-knowing and all-doing [arises] when one is situated at the fall of a tuṭi;
the fall of a tuṭi is the other tuṭi." // 208

sanskrit_iast:
ādyāyāṃ tu tuṭau sarvaṃ sarvataḥ pūrṇamekatām /
gataṃ kiṃ tatra vedyaṃ vā kāryaṃ vā vyapadeśabhāk // 209
meaning:
आद्यायां तु तुटौ सर्वं सर्वतः पूर्णमेकताम् /
गतं किं तत्र वेद्यं वा कार्यं वा व्यपदेशभाक् // 209
text_mt:
In the first tuṭi, however, everything, completely full in every way, has merged into unity;
what could be an object of cognition there, or what effect could receive a designation? // 209

sanskrit_iast:
ato bhedasamullāsakalāṃ prāthamikīṃ budhāḥ /
cinvanti pratibhāṃ devīṃ sarvajñatvādisiddhaye // 210
meaning:
अतो भेदसमुल्लासकलां प्राथमिकीं बुधाः /
चिन्वन्ति प्रतिभां देवीं सर्वज्ञत्वादिसिद्धये // 210
text_mt:
Therefore, the wise cultivate the goddess of intuitive flash, the initial fraction of the manifestation of difference,
for the attainment of omniscience and the rest. // 210

sanskrit_iast:
saiva śaktiḥ śivasyoktā tṛtīyādituṭiṣvatha /
mantrādi(dhi)nāthatacchaktimantreśādyāḥ kramoditāḥ // 211
meaning:
सैव शक्तिः शिवस्योक्ता तृतीयादितुटिष्वथ /
मन्त्रादि(धि)नाथतच्छक्तिमन्त्रेशाद्याः क्रमोदिताः // 211
text_mt:
That very [intuition] is declared to be the power of Śiva. Then, in the third and subsequent tuṭis,
the lords of mantras and their powers, the Mantreśvaras, and the like, are taught in succession. // 211

sanskrit_iast:
tāsu saṃdadhataścittamavadhānaikadharmakam /
tattatsiddhisamāveśaḥ svayamevopajāyate // 212
meaning:
तासु संदधतश्चित्तमवधानैकधर्मकम् /
तत्तत्सिद्धिसमावेशः स्वयमेवोपजायते // 212
text_mt:
For one who fixes the mind, whose sole characteristic is attentiveness, on them,
absorption into those respective spiritual accomplishments arises spontaneously. // 212

sanskrit_iast:
ata eva yathā bhedabahutvaṃ dūratā tathā /
saṃvittau tuṭibāhulyādakṣārthāsaṃnikarṣavat // 213
meaning:
अत एव यथा भेदबहुत्वं दूरता तथा /
संवित्तौ तुटिबाहुल्यादक्षार्थासंनिकर्षवत् // 213
text_mt:
For this very reason, just as there is a multiplicity of difference, so there is distance
in consciousness due to the abundance of tuṭis, like the lack of contact between a sense organ and its object. // 213

sanskrit_iast:
yathā yathā hi nyūnatvaṃ tuṭīnāṃ hrāsato bhidaḥ /
tathā tathātinaikaṭyaṃ saṃvidaḥ syācchivāvadhi // 214
meaning:
यथा यथा हि न्यूनत्वं तुटीनां ह्रासतो भिदः /
तथा तथातिनैकट्यं संविदः स्याच्छिवावधि // 214
text_mt:
For to the extent that there is a diminution of the tuṭis due to the decrease of difference,
to that extent there is an extreme proximity of consciousness, up to Śiva. // 214

sanskrit_iast:
śivatattvamataḥ proktamantikaṃ sarvato'mutaḥ /
ata eva prayatno'yaṃ tatpraveśe na vidyate // 215
meaning:
शिवतत्त्वमतः प्रोक्तमन्तिकं सर्वतोऽमुतः /
अत एव प्रयत्नोऽयं तत्प्रवेशे न विद्यते // 215
text_mt:
Hence, the Śiva principle is declared to be closer than everything [else];
for this reason, no effort exists for entry into it. // 215

sanskrit_iast:
yathā yathā hi dūratvaṃ yatnayogastathā tathā /
bhāvanākaraṇādīnāṃ śive niravakāśatām // 216
meaning:
यथा यथा हि दूरत्वं यत्नयोगस्तथा तथा /
भावनाकरणादीनां शिवे निरवकाशताम् // 216
text_mt:
For to the extent that there is distance, to that extent there is the application of effort;
people rich in oral tradition consider meditation, ritual instruments, and the like // 216

sanskrit_iast:
ata eva hi manyante saṃpradāyadhanā janāḥ /
tathā hi dṛśyatāṃ loko ghaṭādervedane yathā // 217
meaning:
अत एव हि मन्यन्ते संप्रदायधना जनाः /
तथा हि दृश्यतां लोको घटादेर्वेदने यथा // 217
text_mt:
to have no scope in Śiva for this very reason.
For let ordinary experience be observed: just as in knowing a pot or the like // 217

sanskrit_iast:
prayatnavānivābhāti tathā kiṃ sukhavedane /
āntaratvamidaṃ prāhuḥ saṃvinnaikaṭyaśālitām // 218
meaning:
प्रयत्नवानिवाभाति तथा किं सुखवेदने /
आन्तरत्वमिदं प्राहुः संविन्नैकट्यशालिताम् // 218
text_mt:
one appears as if making an effort, does one do so in the cognition of pleasure?
They call this internality, possessing proximity to consciousness, // 218

sanskrit_iast:
tāṃ ca cidrūpatonmeṣaṃ bāhyatvaṃ tannimeṣatām /
bhavināṃ tvantiko'pyevaṃ na bhātītyatidūratā // 219
meaning:
तां च चिद्रूपतोन्मेषं बाह्यत्वं तन्निमेषताम् /
भविनां त्वन्तिकोऽप्येवं न भातीत्यतिदूरता // 219
text_mt:
and that [internality is] the opening of the nature of consciousness, while externality is its closing.
Yet even though it is so close, it does not appear to worldly beings; hence it is extremely distant. // 219

sanskrit_iast:
dūre'pi hyantikībhūte bhānaṃ syāttvatra tatkatham /
na ca bījāṅkuralatādalapuṣpaphalādivat // 220
meaning:
दूरेऽपि ह्यन्तिकीभूते भानं स्यात्त्वत्र तत्कथम् /
न च बीजाङ्कुरलतादलपुष्पफलादिवत् // 220
text_mt:
For even what is distant appears when it becomes near, but how could that be so here?
Nor does this consciousness become sequential // 220

sanskrit_iast:
kramikeyaṃ bhavetsaṃvitsūtastatra kilāṅkuraḥ /
bījāllatā tvaṅkurānno bījādiha sarvataḥ // 221
meaning:
क्रमिकेयं भवेत्संवित्सूतस्तत्र किलाङ्कुरः /
बीजाल्लता त्वङ्कुरान्नो बीजादिह सर्वतः // 221
text_mt:
like seed, sprout, creeper, leaf, flower, fruit, and so on.
There, indeed, the sprout is produced from the seed, and the creeper from the sprout, but not here from the seed in all respects. // 221

sanskrit_iast:
saṃvittattvaṃ bhāsamānaṃ paripūrṇaṃ hi sarvataḥ /
sarvasya kāraṇaṃ proktaṃ sarvatraivoditaṃ yataḥ // 222
meaning:
संवित्तत्त्वं भासमानं परिपूर्णं हि सर्वतः /
सर्वस्य कारणं प्रोक्तं सर्वत्रैवोदितं यतः // 222
text_mt:
For the principle of consciousness, shining forth completely full on all sides,
is declared to be the cause of everything, because it arises everywhere. // 222

sanskrit_iast:
tata eva ghaṭe'pyeṣā prāṇavṛttiryadi sphuret /
viśrāmyeccāśu tatraiva śivabīje layaṃ vrajet // 223
meaning:
तत एव घटेऽप्येषा प्राणवृत्तिर्यदि स्फुरेत् /
विश्राम्येच्चाशु तत्रैव शिवबीजे लयं व्रजेत् // 223
text_mt:
Therefore, even in the case of a pot, if this movement of the vital breath pulses forth,
it should quickly come to rest right there, and dissolve into the seed of Śiva. // 223

sanskrit_iast:
na tu kramikatā kācicchivātmatve kadācana /
anyanmantrādi(dhi)nāthādi kāraṇaṃ tattu saṃnidheḥ // 224
meaning:
न तु क्रमिकता काचिच्छिवात्मत्वे कदाचन /
अन्यन्मन्त्रादि(धि)नाथादि कारणं तत्तु संनिधेः // 224
text_mt:
Never, however, is there any sequentiality in being the essence of Śiva;
what is other—the lords of mantras and the rest—is a cause because of proximity // 224

sanskrit_iast:
śivābhedācca kiṃ cātha dvaite naikaṭyavedanāt /
anayā ca diśā sarva sarvadā pravivecayan // 225
meaning:
शिवाभेदाच्च किं चाथ द्वैते नैकट्यवेदनात् /
अनया च दिशा सर्व सर्वदा प्रविवेचयन् // 225
text_mt:
and non-difference from Śiva, or further, in duality, because of the cognition of nearness.
And by examining everything at all times in this manner, // 225

sanskrit_iast:
bhairavāyata eva drāk ciccakreśvaratāṃ gataḥ /
sa itthaṃ prāṇago bhedaḥ khecarīcakragopitaḥ // 226
meaning:
भैरवायत एव द्राक् चिच्चक्रेश्वरतां गतः /
स इत्थं प्राणगो भेदः खेचरीचक्रगोपितः // 226
text_mt:
one swiftly acts like Bhairava, having attained the sovereignty of the wheel of consciousness.
Thus this division residing in the vital breath, concealed by the wheel of khecarīs, // 226

sanskrit_iast:
mayā prakaṭitaḥ śrīmacchāmbhavājñānuvartinā /
atraivādhvani vedyatvaṃ prāpte yā saṃvidudbhavet // 227
meaning:
मया प्रकटितः श्रीमच्छाम्भवाज्ञानुवर्तिना /
अत्रैवाध्वनि वेद्यत्वं प्राप्ते या संविदुद्भवेत् // 227
text_mt:
has been revealed by me, following the command of the illustrious Śaṃbhu.
When this very path attains the status of an object of cognition, the consciousness that arises // 227

sanskrit_iast:
tasyāḥ svakaṃ yadvaicitryaṃ tadavasthāpadābhidham /
jāgratsvapnaḥ suṣuptaṃ ca turyaṃ ca tadatītakam // 228
meaning:
तस्याः स्वकं यद्वैचित्र्यं तदवस्थापदाभिधम् /
जाग्रत्स्वप्नः सुषुप्तं च तुर्यं च तदतीतकम् // 228
text_mt:
has a diversity of its own that is named the states or planes:
waking, dreaming, deep sleep, the fourth, and that which transcends it. // 228

sanskrit_iast:
iti pañca padānyāhurekasminvedake sati /
tatra yaiṣā dharātattvācchivāntā tattvapaddhatiḥ // 229
meaning:
इति पञ्च पदान्याहुरेकस्मिन्वेदके सति /
तत्र यैषा धरातत्त्वाच्छिवान्ता तत्त्वपद्धतिः // 229
text_mt:
Thus they speak of five planes, while the knower remains one.
There, that series of principles extending from the earth principle to Śiva, // 229

sanskrit_iast:
tasyāmekaḥ pramātā cedavaśyaṃ jāgradādikam /
taddarśyate śaṃbhunāthaprasādādviditaṃ mayā // 230
meaning:
तस्यामेकः प्रमाता चेदवश्यं जाग्रदादिकम् /
तद्दर्श्यते शंभुनाथप्रसादाद्विदितं मया // 230
text_mt:
if there is a single knower in it, inevitably [exhibits] waking and the rest;
that is now demonstrated by me, known through the grace of Śaṃbhunātha. // 230

sanskrit_iast:
yadadhiṣṭheyameveha nādhiṣṭhātṛ kadācana /
saṃvedanagataṃ vedyaṃ tajjāgratsamudāhṛtam // 231
meaning:
यदधिष्ठेयमेवेह नाधिष्ठातृ कदाचन /
संवेदनगतं वेद्यं तज्जाग्रत्समुदाहृतम् // 231
text_mt:
That which is strictly an object governed, never a governing subject,
being an object of cognition within awareness, is called the waking state. // 231

sanskrit_iast:
caitramaitrādibhūtāni tattvāni ca dharāditaḥ /
abhidhākaraṇībhūtāḥ śabdāḥ kiṃ cābhidhā pramā // 232
meaning:
चैत्रमैत्रादिभूतानि तत्त्वानि च धरादितः /
अभिधाकरणीभूताः शब्दाः किं चाभिधा प्रमा // 232
text_mt:
The entities such as Caitra and Maitra, the principles beginning with earth,
the words serving as instruments of naming, and also naming, cognition, // 232

sanskrit_iast:
pramātṛmeyatanmānapramārūpaṃ catuṣṭayam /
viśvametadadhiṣṭheyaṃ yadā jāgrattadā smṛtam // 233
meaning:
प्रमातृमेयतन्मानप्रमारूपं चतुष्टयम् /
विश्वमेतदधिष्ठेयं यदा जाग्रत्तदा स्मृतम् // 233
text_mt:
the tetrad consisting of the knower, the object of knowledge, its means of cognition, and cognition—
when all this universe is an object governed, then it is remembered as waking. // 233

sanskrit_iast:
tathā hi bhāsate yattannīlamantaḥ pravedane /
saṃkalparūpe bāhyasya tadadhiṣṭhātṛ bodhakam // 234
meaning:
तथा हि भासते यत्तन्नीलमन्तः प्रवेदने /
संकल्परूपे बाह्यस्य तदधिष्ठातृ बोधकम् // 234
text_mt:
To explain: that blue object which appears in internal cognition
of a conceptual nature is the governing, revealing agent of the external [object]. // 234

sanskrit_iast:
yattu bāhyatayā nīlaṃ cakāstyasya na vidyate /
kathaṃcidapyadhiṣṭhātṛbhāvastajjāgraducyate // 235
meaning:
यत्तु बाह्यतया नीलं चकास्त्यस्य न विद्यते /
कथंचिदप्यधिष्ठातृभावस्तज्जाग्रदुच्यते // 235
text_mt:
However, that blue object which shines as external has no
governing nature whatsoever; that is called waking. // 235

sanskrit_iast:
tatra caitre bhāsamāne yo dehāṃśaḥ sa kathyate /
abuddho yastu mānāṃśaḥ sa buddho mitikārakaḥ // 236
meaning:
तत्र चैत्रे भासमाने यो देहांशः स कथ्यते /
अबुद्धो यस्तु मानांशः स बुद्धो मितिकारकः // 236
text_mt:
There, when Caitra appears, the bodily portion is declared to be
the unawakened; the portion consisting of the means of knowledge, producing cognition, is the awakened; // 236

sanskrit_iast:
prabuddhaḥ suprabuddhaśca pramāmātreti ca kramaḥ /
cāturvidhyaṃ hi piṇḍasthanāmni jāgrati kīrtitam // 237
meaning:
प्रबुद्धः सुप्रबुद्धश्च प्रमामात्रेति च क्रमः /
चातुर्विध्यं हि पिण्डस्थनाम्नि जाग्रति कीर्तितम् // 237
text_mt:
the well-awakened, and the fully awakened, and sheer cognition—such is the sequence.
For a fourfold division is proclaimed in the waking state called "residing in the body." // 237

sanskrit_iast:
jāgradādi catuṣkaṃ hi pratyekamiha vidyate /
jāgrajjāgradabuddhaṃ tajjāgratsvapnastu buddhatā // 238
meaning:
जाग्रदादि चतुष्कं हि प्रत्येकमिह विद्यते /
जाग्रज्जाग्रदबुद्धं तज्जाग्रत्स्वप्नस्तु बुद्धता // 238
text_mt:
For the tetrad beginning with waking is found individually here:
waking within waking is the unawakened, while dreaming within waking is the state of being awakened, // 238

sanskrit_iast:
ityādi turyātītaṃ tu sarvagatvātpṛthakkutaḥ /
uktaṃ ca piṇḍagaṃ jāgradabuddhaṃ buddhameva ca // 239
meaning:
इत्यादि तुर्यातीतं तु सर्वगत्वात्पृथक्कुतः /
उक्तं च पिण्डगं जाग्रदबुद्धं बुद्धमेव च // 239
text_mt:
and so on. But the transcendent fourth, because it is omnipresent, how could it be separate?
And it is stated: "Residing in the body is the waking state; unawakened, and awakened, // 239

sanskrit_iast:
prabuddhaṃ suprabuddhaṃ ca caturvidhamidaṃ smṛtam /
meyabhūmiriyaṃ mukhyā jāgradākhyānyadantarā // 240
meaning:
प्रबुद्धं सुप्रबुद्धं च चतुर्विधमिदं स्मृतम् /
मेयभूमिरियं मुख्या जाग्रदाख्यान्यदन्तरा // 240
text_mt:
and well-awakened, and fully awakened—this is remembered as fourfold."
This principal level of the object of knowledge is named waking; between the others, // 240

sanskrit_iast:
bhūtatattvābhidhānānāṃ yo'ṃśo'dhiṣṭheya ucyate /
piṇḍasthamiti taṃ prāhuriti śrīmālinīmate // 241
meaning:
भूततत्त्वाभिधानानां योऽंशोऽधिष्ठेय उच्यते /
पिण्डस्थमिति तं प्राहुरिति श्रीमालिनीमते // 241
text_mt:
that portion of the elements, principles, and names which is said to be the object governed
they call "residing in the body," according to the tradition of the illustrious Mālinī. // 241

sanskrit_iast:
laukikī jāgradityeṣā saṃjñā piṇḍasthamityapi /
yogināṃ yogasiddhyarthaṃ saṃjñeyaṃ paribhāṣyate // 242
meaning:
लौकिकी जाग्रदित्येषा संज्ञा पिण्डस्थमित्यपि /
योगिनां योगसिद्ध्यर्थं संज्ञेयं परिभाष्यते // 242
text_mt:
This designation "waking" is conventional, and "residing in the body"
is defined as a technical term for yogins for the sake of yogic accomplishment. // 242

sanskrit_iast:
adhiṣṭheyasamāpattimadhyāsīnasya yoginaḥ /
tādātmyaṃ kila piṇḍasthaṃ mitaṃ piṇḍaṃ hi piṇḍitam // 243
meaning:
अधिष्ठेयसमापत्तिमध्यासीनस्य योगिनः /
तादात्म्यं किल पिण्डस्थं मितं पिण्डं हि पिण्डितम् // 243
text_mt:
For the yogin who is seated in attunement to what is governed,
identity is indeed "residing in the body," for a body is limited, gathered together. // 243

sanskrit_iast:
prasaṃkhyānaikarūḍhānāṃ jñānināṃ tu taducyate /
sarvatobhadramāpūrṇaṃ sarvato vedyasattayā // 244
meaning:
प्रसंख्यानैकरूढानां ज्ञानिनां तु तदुच्यते /
सर्वतोभद्रमापूर्णं सर्वतो वेद्यसत्तया // 244
text_mt:
For the knowers who are firmly rooted solely in philosophical discernment, however, that is called
"auspicious on all sides," completely filled on all sides by the existence of the knowable. // 244

sanskrit_iast:
sarvasattāsamāpūrṇa viśvaṃ paśyedyato yataḥ /
jñānī tatastataḥ saṃvittatvamasya prakāśate // 245
meaning:
सर्वसत्तासमापूर्ण विश्वं पश्येद्यतो यतः /
ज्ञानी ततस्ततः संवित्तत्वमस्य प्रकाशते // 245
text_mt:
From whatever [aspect] the knower sees the universe completely filled with the reality of everything,
from that very [aspect] the principle of consciousness shines forth to him. // 245

sanskrit_iast:
lokayogaprasaṃkhyānatrairūpyavaśataḥ kila /
nāmāni trīṇi bhaṇyante svapnādiṣvapyayaṃ vidhiḥ // 246
meaning:
लोकयोगप्रसंख्यानत्रैरूप्यवशतः किल /
नामानि त्रीणि भण्यन्ते स्वप्नादिष्वप्ययं विधिः // 246
text_mt:
Indeed, on account of the threefold nature consisting of common worldly usage, yoga, and philosophical discernment,
three names are spoken; this rule applies to dreaming and the rest as well. // 246

sanskrit_iast:
yattvadhiṣṭhānakaraṇabhāvamadhyāsya vartate /
vedyaṃ satpūrvakathitaṃ bhūtatattvābhidhāmayam // 247
meaning:
यत्त्वधिष्ठानकरणभावमध्यास्य वर्तते /
वेद्यं सत्पूर्वकथितं भूततत्त्वाभिधामयम् // 247
text_mt:
However, that which exists having entered the condition of being an instrument of governance,
being an object of cognition previously described as consisting of the elements, principles, and names, // 247

sanskrit_iast:
tatsvapno mukhyato jñeyaṃ tacca vaikalpike pathi /
vaikalpikapathārūḍhavedyasāmyāvabhāsanāt // 248
meaning:
तत्स्वप्नो मुख्यतो ज्ञेयं तच्च वैकल्पिके पथि /
वैकल्पिकपथारूढवेद्यसाम्यावभासनात् // 248
text_mt:
that is primarily to be known as dreaming, and that is on the conceptual path,
because it manifests a resemblance to an object of knowledge situated on the conceptual path. // 248

sanskrit_iast:
lokarūḍho'pyasau svapnaḥ sāmyaṃ cābāhyarūpatā /
utprekṣāsvapnasaṃkalpasmṛtyunmādādidṛṣṭiṣu // 249
meaning:
लोकरूढोऽप्यसौ स्वप्नः साम्यं चाबाह्यरूपता /
उत्प्रेक्षास्वप्नसंकल्पस्मृत्युन्मादादिदृष्टिषु // 249
text_mt:
This dreaming is also well-known in worldly usage, and the resemblance is the non-external nature
in visions of imagination, dreaming, intention, memory, madness, and the like. // 249

sanskrit_iast:
vispaṣṭaṃ yadvedyajātaṃ jāgranmukhyatayaiva tat /
yattu tatrāpyavispaṣṭaṃ spaṣṭādhiṣṭhātṛ bhāsate // 250
meaning:
विस्पष्टं यद्वेद्यजातं जाग्रन्मुख्यतयैव तत् /
यत्तु तत्राप्यविस्पष्टं स्पष्टाधिष्ठातृ भासते // 250
text_mt:
Whatever aggregate of knowables is clear, that is primarily waking;
but that which, even in that case, is unclear, while its governing subject appears clearly, // 250

sanskrit_iast:
vikalpāntaragaṃ vedyaṃ tatsvapnapadamucyate /
tadaiva tasya vettyeva svayameva hyabāhyatām // 251
meaning:
विकल्पान्तरगं वेद्यं तत्स्वप्नपदमुच्यते /
तदैव तस्य वेत्त्येव स्वयमेव ह्यबाह्यताम् // 251
text_mt: An object of knowledge that falls within another conceptual construct is called the sphere of dream; / for at that very moment, the knower himself indeed knows its non-external nature // 251

sanskrit_iast:
pramātrantarasādhārabhāvahānyasthirātmate /
tatrāpi cāturvidhyaṃ tat prāgdiśaiva prakalpayet // 252
meaning:
प्रमात्रन्तरसाधारभावहान्यस्थिरात्मते /
तत्रापि चातुर्विध्यं तत् प्राग्दिशैव प्रकल्पयेत् // 252
text_mt: Because of its lack of commonality with other knowers and its unstable nature. / There too, one should conceiving of that fourfold division just according to the previous manner: // 252

sanskrit_iast:
gatāgataṃ suvikṣiptaṃ saṃgataṃ susamāhitam /
atrāpi pūrvavannāma laukikaṃ svapna ityadaḥ // 253
meaning:
गतागतं सुविक्षिप्तं संगतं सुसमाहितम् /
अत्रापि पूर्ववन्नाम लौकिकं स्वप्न इत्यदः // 253
text_mt: ‘Gone and come back’, ‘well dispersed’, ‘collected’, and ‘well concentrated’. / Here too, as before, this is the conventional worldly designation: ‘dream’. // 253

sanskrit_iast:
bāhyābhimatabhāvānāṃ svāpo hyagrahaṇaṃ matam /
sarvādhvanaḥ padaṃ prāṇaḥ saṃkalpo'vagamātmakaḥ // 254
meaning:
बाह्याभिमतभावानां स्वापो ह्यग्रहणं मतम् /
सर्वाध्वनः पदं प्राणः संकल्पोऽवगमात्मकः // 254
text_mt: For ‘sleep’ is considered the non-grasping of entities regarded as external. / The sphere of the entire path is vital breath; conceptualization consists in comprehension. // 254

sanskrit_iast:
padaṃ ca tatsamāpatti padasthaṃ yogino viduḥ /
