text_mt: One should place the little finger of the right hand over the left, / [and] with the joining of the forefinger and thumb, [place] the fingers of the left hand beneath the right;

sanskrit_iast:
niḥsandhibandhau dvāvitthaṃ vellitā śuktirucyate /
ye tatra pānakāle tu bindavo yānti medinīm // 96
meaning:
निःसन्धिबन्धौ द्वावित्थं वेल्लिता शुक्तिरुच्यते /
ये तत्र पानकाले तु बिन्दवो यान्ति मेदिनीम् // 96
text_mt: the two clasps thus being without gaps is called the ‘rolled pearl-oyster’. / Whatever drops fall to the ground at the time of drinking therein,

sanskrit_iast:
taistuṣyanti hi vetālaguhyakādyā gabhastayaḥ /
dhārayā bhairavastuṣyet karapānaṃ paraṃ tataḥ // 97
meaning:
तैस्तुष्यन्ति हि वेतालगुह्यकाद्या गभस्तयः /
धारया भैरवस्तुष्येत् करपानं परं ततः // 97
text_mt: the rays consisting of Vetālas, Guhyakas, and others are satisfied by them. / Bhairava is satisfied by the stream; therefore drinking from the hand is supreme.

sanskrit_iast:
praveśo'tra na dātavyaḥ pūrvameva hi kasyacit /
pramādāttu praviṣṭasya vicāraṃ naiva carcayet // 98
meaning:
प्रवेशोऽत्र न दातव्यः पूर्वमेव हि कस्यचित् /
प्रमादात्तु प्रविष्टस्य विचारं नैव चर्चयेत् // 98
text_mt: No entrance at all should be granted to anyone beforehand; / but in the case of someone who has entered through inadvertence, one should not raise an inquiry.

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ kṛtvā kramādyāgamante dakṣiṇayā yutam /
samālambhanatāmbūlavastrādyaṃ vitaredbudhaḥ // 99
meaning:
एवं कृत्वा क्रमाद्यागमन्ते दक्षिणया युतम् /
समालम्भनताम्बूलवस्त्राद्यं वितरेद्बुधः // 99
text_mt: Having thus performed the sacrifice in proper order, accompanied by a fee at the end, / the wise one should distribute unguent, betel, cloth, and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
rūpakārdhāt paraṃ hīnāṃ na dadyāddakṣiṇāṃ sudhīḥ /
samayibhyaḥ kramāddvidviguṇā gurvantakaṃ bhavet // 100
meaning:
रूपकार्धात् परं हीनां न दद्याद्दक्षिणां सुधीः /
समयिभ्यः क्रमाद्द्विद्विगुणा गुर्वन्तकं भवेत् // 100
text_mt: The wise one should not give a fee less than half a silver coin; / [beginning] from the initiates into the rule, it should double successively up to the guru.

sanskrit_iast:
eṣa syānmūrtiyāgastu sarvayāgapradhānakaḥ /
kāmye tu saṃvidhau saptakṛtvaḥ kāryastathāvidhaḥ // 101
meaning:
एष स्यान्मूर्तियागस्तु सर्वयागप्रधानकः /
काम्ये तु संविधौ सप्तकृत्वः कार्यस्तथाविधः // 101
text_mt: This bodily sacrifice (mūrtiyāga) is the chief among all sacrifices; / in an optional rite (kāmya), however, it should be performed seven times in this manner. // 101

sanskrit_iast:
jānanti prathamaṃ gehaṃ tatastasya samarthatām /
balābalaṃ tataḥ paścādvismayante'tra mātaraḥ // 102
meaning:
जानन्ति प्रथमं गेहं ततस्तस्य समर्थताम् /
बलाबलं ततः पश्चाद्विस्मयन्तेऽत्र मातरः // 102
text_mt: First they perceive the house, then his competence, / and then his strength and weakness; thereafter, the Mothers are struck with wonder here. // 102

sanskrit_iast:
tato'pi saṃnidhīyante prīyante varadāstataḥ /
devīnāmatha nāthasya parivārayujo'pyalam // 103
meaning:
ततोऽपि संनिधीयन्ते प्रीयन्ते वरदास्ततः /
देवीनामथ नाथस्य परिवारयुजोऽप्यलम् // 103
text_mt: Then they become present, then they are pleased and grant boons, / as do exceedingly the retinues of the Goddesses and of the Lord. // 103

sanskrit_iast:
vallabho mūrtiyāgo'yamataḥ kāryo vipaścitā /
rāktau gupte gṛhe vīrāḥ śaktayo'nyonyamapyalam // 104
meaning:
वल्लभो मूर्तियागोऽयमतः कार्यो विपश्चिता /
राक्तौ गुप्ते गृहे वीराः शक्तयोऽन्योन्यमप्यलम् // 104
text_mt: Hence, this bodily sacrifice is beloved [to them], and should be performed by the wise person. / At night, in a secluded house, the heroes and the powers among themselves [are gathered] abundantly. // 104

sanskrit_iast:
asaṃketayujo yojyā devatāśabdakīrtanāt /
alābhe mūrticakrasya kumārīreva pūjayet // 105
meaning:
असंकेतयुजो योज्या देवताशब्दकीर्तनात् /
अलाभे मूर्तिचक्रस्य कुमारीरेव पूजयेत् // 105
text_mt: Unbound by conventional codes, they should be applied by chanting the names of the deities. / If the circle of bodily deities is unavailable, one should worship young maidens instead. // 105

sanskrit_iast:
kāmyārthe tu na tāṃ vyaṅgāṃ stanapuṣpavatīṃ tathā /
pratipacchrutisaṃjñe ca caturthī cottarātraye // 106
meaning:
काम्यार्थे तु न तां व्यङ्गां स्तनपुष्पवतीं तथा /
प्रतिपच्छ्रुतिसंज्ञे च चतुर्थी चोत्तरात्रये // 106
text_mt: For an optional aim, however, one must not [worship] a deformed maiden, nor one with breasts or menstruation. / Now, the first tithi [paired with] Śravaṇā, the fourth [with] the three Uttarās, // 106

sanskrit_iast:
haste ca pañcamī ṣaṣṭhī pūrvāsvatha punarvasau /
saptamī tatparā pitrye rohiṇyāṃ navamī tathā // 107
meaning:
हस्ते च पञ्चमी षष्ठी पूर्वास्वथ पुनर्वसौ /
सप्तमी तत्परा पित्र्ये रोहिण्यां नवमी तथा // 107
text_mt: and the fifth [paired with] Hasta, the sixth with the Pūrvās, then the seventh with Punarvasu, / the eighth with Maghā (the Pitṛs' asterism), and the ninth with Rohiṇī, // 107

sanskrit_iast:
mūle tu dvādaśī brāhme bhūtāśvinyāṃ ca pūrṇimā /
dhaniṣṭhāyāmamāvasyā so'yamekādaśātmakaḥ // 108
meaning:
मूले तु द्वादशी ब्राह्मे भूताश्विन्यां च पूर्णिमा /
धनिष्ठायाममावस्या सोऽयमेकादशात्मकः // 108
text_mt: the twelfth with Mūla, the fourteenth with Rohiṇī (the asterism of Brahmā), the full moon with Aśvinī, / and the new moon with Dhaniṣṭhā—this set of eleven, // 108

sanskrit_iast:
arkāditrayaśukrānyatamayukto'pyahargaṇaḥ /
yogaparveti vikhyāto rātrau vā dina eva vā // 109
meaning:
अर्कादित्रयशुक्रान्यतमयुक्तोऽप्यहर्गणः /
योगपर्वेति विख्यातो रात्रौ वा दिन एव वा // 109
text_mt: joined with Sunday, Monday, Tuesday, or Friday (the three beginning with the Sun, or Venus), / is known as a conjunction-junction (yogaparvan), occurring either by night or by day. // 109

sanskrit_iast:
yogaparvaṇi kartavyo mūrtiyāgastu sarvathā /
yaḥ sarvānyogaparvākhyān vāsarān pūjayetsudhīḥ // 110
meaning:
योगपर्वणि कर्तव्यो मूर्तियागस्तु सर्वथा /
यः सर्वान्योगपर्वाख्यान् वासरान् पूजयेत्सुधीः // 110
text_mt: On a conjunction-junction, the bodily sacrifice must by all means be performed. / The wise one who worships on all days called conjunction-junctions // 110

sanskrit_iast:
mūrtiyāgena so'pi syāt samayī maṇḍalaṃ vinā /
ityeṣa mūrtiyāgaḥ śrīsiddhayogīśvarīmate // 111
meaning:
मूर्तियागेन सोऽपि स्यात् समयी मण्डलं विना /
इत्येष मूर्तियागः श्रीसिद्धयोगीश्वरीमते // 111
text_mt: by means of the bodily sacrifice becomes an initiate into the rule (samayī) even without a maṇḍala. / Such is the bodily sacrifice according to the doctrine of the venerable Siddhayogīśvarī. // 111

sanskrit_iast:
athocyate śivenoktaḥ pavitrakavidhiḥ sphuṭaḥ /
śrīratnamālātriśiraḥśāstrayoḥ sūcitaḥ punaḥ // 112
meaning:
अथोच्यते शिवेनोक्तः पवित्रकविधिः स्फुटः /
श्रीरत्नमालात्रिशिरःशास्त्रयोः सूचितः पुनः // 112
text_mt: Now the clear rite of the sacred thread (pavitraka) spoken by Śiva is explained, / which was further indicated in the venerable Ratnamālā and Triśirobhairava scriptures, // 112

sanskrit_iast:
śrīsiddhāṭanasadbhāvamālinīsāraśāsane /
tatra prādhānyataḥ śrīmanmālokto vidhirucyate // 113
meaning:
श्रीसिद्धाटनसद्भावमालिनीसारशासने /
तत्र प्राधान्यतः श्रीमन्मालोक्तो विधिरुच्यते // 113
text_mt: and in the scriptures Siddhadharmāṭana, Sadbhāva, and Mālinīsāra. / Among these, the rite taught in the venerable Ratnamālā is related primarily: // 113

sanskrit_iast:
kṣīrābdhimathanodbhūtaviṣanidrāvimūrcchitaḥ /
nāgarājaḥ svabhuvane meghakāle sma nāvasat // 114
meaning:
क्षीराब्धिमथनोद्भूतविषनिद्राविमूर्च्छितः /
नागराजः स्वभुवने मेघकाले स्म नावसत् // 114
text_mt: Fainting in the slumber caused by the poison arising from the churning of the milk-ocean, / the serpent king could not dwell in his own realm during the rainy season. // 114

sanskrit_iast:
kevalaṃ tu pavitro'yaṃ vāyubhakṣaḥ samāḥ śatam /
divyaṃ daśaguṇaṃ nāthaṃ bhairavaṃ paryapūjayat // 115
meaning:
केवलं तु पवित्रोऽयं वायुभक्षः समाः शतम् /
दिव्यं दशगुणं नाथं भैरवं पर्यपूजयत् // 115
text_mt: Being wholly pure (pavitra) and feeding only on wind, he worshipped the Lord Bhairava / for a divine century multiplied ten-fold. // 115

sanskrit_iast:
vyajijñapacca taṃ tuṣṭaṃ nāthaṃ varṣāsvahaṃ nije /
pātāle nāsituṃ śaktaḥ so'pyenaṃ parameśvaraḥ // 116
meaning:
व्यजिज्ञपच्च तं तुष्टं नाथं वर्षास्वहं निजे /
पाताले नासितुं शक्तः सोऽप्येनं परमेश्वरः // 116
text_mt: And he petitioned the pleased Lord: "During the rains I am unable to remain / in my own subterranean realm (Pātāla)." And the Supreme Lord // 116

sanskrit_iast:
nāgaṃ nijajaṭājūṭapīṭhagaṃ paryakalpayat /
tataḥ samastadevaughairdhārito'sau svamūrdhani // 117
meaning:
नागं निजजटाजूटपीठगं पर्यकल्पयत् /
ततः समस्तदेवौघैर्धारितोऽसौ स्वमूर्धनि // 117
text_mt: placed the serpent upon the throne of his own matted hair. / Then he was held upon their heads by the entire assembly of gods. // 117

sanskrit_iast:
mahatāṃ mahitānāṃ hi nādbhuta viśvapūjyatā /
tasmānmaheśiturmūrdhni devatānāṃ ca sarvaśaḥ // 118
meaning:
महतां महितानां हि नाद्भुत विश्वपूज्यता /
तस्मान्महेशितुर्मूर्ध्नि देवतानां च सर्वशः // 118
text_mt: For it is not surprising that the great who are honoured [by Śiva] are revered by all the universe. / Therefore, upon the head of the Great Lord, of the deities in every respect, // 118

sanskrit_iast:
ātmanaśca pavitraṃ taṃ kuryādyāgapuraḥsaram /
daśa koṭyo na pūjānāṃ pavitrārohaṇe samāḥ // 119
meaning:
आत्मनश्च पवित्रं तं कुर्याद्यागपुरःसरम् /
दश कोट्यो न पूजानां पवित्रारोहणे समाः // 119
text_mt: and of oneself, one should place that sacred thread preceded by sacrifice. / A hundred million acts of worship are not equal to the investiture of the sacred thread. // 119

sanskrit_iast:
vṛthā dīkṣā vṛthā jñānaṃ gurvārādhanameva ca /
vinā pavitrādyenaitaddharennāgaḥ śivājñayā // 120
meaning:
वृथा दीक्षा वृथा ज्ञानं गुर्वाराधनमेव च /
विना पवित्राद्येनैतद्धरेन्नागः शिवाज्ञया // 120
text_mt: Vain is initiation, vain is knowledge, and [vain is] worship of the guru; / without the sacred thread and similar rites, the serpent seizes this by Śiva's command. // 120

sanskrit_iast:
tasmātsarvaprayatnena sa kāryaḥ kulavedibhiḥ /
āṣāḍhaśuklānmithunakarkaṭasthe ravau vidhiḥ // 121
meaning:
तस्मात्सर्वप्रयत्नेन स कार्यः कुलवेदिभिः /
आषाढशुक्लान्मिथुनकर्कटस्थे रवौ विधिः // 121
text_mt: Therefore, it must be performed with every effort by the knowers of the Kula. / Beginning from the bright fortnight of Āṣāḍha, while the sun is in Gemini or Cancer, // 121

sanskrit_iast:
kartavyaḥ so'nirodhena yāvatsā tulapūrṇimā /
tulopalakṣitasyāntyaṃ kārtikasya dinaṃ matam // 122
meaning:
कर्तव्यः सोऽनिरोधेन यावत्सा तुलपूर्णिमा /
तुलोपलक्षितस्यान्त्यं कार्तिकस्य दिनं मतम् // 122
text_mt: this rite should be carried out unobstructed up to the full moon of Libra. / The final day of the [solar period] marked by Libra is held to be [that of] Kārttika. // 122

sanskrit_iast:
kulaśabdaṃ paṭhanto'nye vyākhyābhedaṃ prakurvate /
nityātantravidaḥ kṛṣṇaṃ kārtikāccaramaṃ dinam // 123
meaning:
कुलशब्दं पठन्तोऽन्ये व्याख्याभेदं प्रकुर्वते /
नित्यातन्त्रविदः कृष्णं कार्तिकाच्चरमं दिनम् // 123
text_mt: Others reciting the word *kula* offer a different interpretation: / the knowers of the Nityātantra hold the last dark day after Kārttika // 123

sanskrit_iast:
kulasya nityācakrasya pūrṇatvaṃ yatra tanmatam /
māghaśuklāntyadivasaḥ kulaparveti tanmatam // 124
meaning:
कुलस्य नित्याचक्रस्य पूर्णत्वं यत्र तन्मतम् /
माघशुक्लान्त्यदिवसः कुलपर्वेति तन्मतम् // 124
text_mt: to be that on which the fullness of the Kula, the circle of the Nityās, occurs. / In their view, the last day of the bright fortnight of Māgha is the festival of the Kula (kulaparvan). // 124

sanskrit_iast:
pūrṇatvaṃ tatra candrasya sā tithiḥ kulapūrṇimā /
dakṣiṇottaragaḥ kālaḥ kulākulatayoditaḥ // 125
meaning:
पूर्णत्वं तत्र चन्द्रस्य सा तिथिः कुलपूर्णिमा /
दक्षिणोत्तरगः कालः कुलाकुलतयोदितः // 125
text_mt: There the moon attains fullness; that tithi is the full moon of the Kula. / Time proceeding south and north is taught as having the nature of Kula and Akula. // 125

sanskrit_iast:
kulasya tasya carame dine pūrṇatvamucyate /
dakṣiṇāyanaṣaṇmāsakartavyatvamato vidhau // 126
meaning:
कुलस्य तस्य चरमे दिने पूर्णत्वमुच्यते /
दक्षिणायनषण्मासकर्तव्यत्वमतो विधौ // 126
text_mt: Fullness is stated on the final day of that Kula; / hence, for the rite of the sacred thread, there is an obligation [extending over] the six months of the southern course, // 126

sanskrit_iast:
pavitrake prakāśatvasiddhyai kṛṣṇasya vartmanaḥ /
tadetadbahuśāstroktaṃ rūpaṃ devo nyarūpayat // 127
meaning:
पवित्रके प्रकाशत्वसिद्ध्यै कृष्णस्य वर्त्मनः /
तदेतद्बहुशास्त्रोक्तं रूपं देवो न्यरूपयत् // 127
text_mt: in order to achieve luminosity for the dark path. / The Lord explained this form, taught in many scriptures, // 127

sanskrit_iast:
ekenaiva padena śrīratnamālākulāgame /
tadatra samaye sarvavidhisaṃpūraṇātmakaḥ // 128
meaning:
एकेनैव पदेन श्रीरत्नमालाकुलागमे /
तदत्र समये सर्वविधिसंपूरणात्मकः // 128
text_mt: by a single word in the venerable scripture of the Ratnamālā Kula. / Therefore, at this time, consisting of the fulfillment of all rites, // 128

sanskrit_iast:
pavitrakavidhiḥ kāryaḥ śuklapakṣe tu sarvathā /
pūraṇaṃ śaktiyogena śaktyātma ca sitaṃ dalam // 129
meaning:
पवित्रकविधिः कार्यः शुक्लपक्षे तु सर्वथा /
पूरणं शक्तियोगेन शक्त्यात्म च सितं दलम् // 129
text_mt: the rite of the sacred thread must by all means be performed in the bright fortnight. / Fulfillment is through union with the power, and the bright fortnight is the nature of the power. // 129

sanskrit_iast:
dakṣiṇāyanasājātyāt tena tadvidhirucyate /
ekadvitricatuḥpañcaṣaḍlataikatamaṃ mahat // 130
meaning:
दक्षिणायनसाजात्यात् तेन तद्विधिरुच्यते /
एकद्वित्रिचतुःपञ्चषड्लतैकतमं महत् // 130
text_mt: Because of its common nature with the southern course, that rite is explained accordingly: / One of one, two, three, four, five, or six strands, large, // 130

sanskrit_iast:
hemaratnāṅkitagranthi kuryānmuktāpavitrakam /
sauvarṇasūtraṃ triguṇaṃ saikagranthiśataṃ gurau // 131
meaning:
हेमरत्नाङ्कितग्रन्थि कुर्यान्मुक्तापवित्रकम् /
सौवर्णसूत्रं त्रिगुणं सैकग्रन्थिशतं गुरौ // 131
text_mt: having knots marked with gold and gems, a pearl sacred thread should be made. / A golden thread, threefold, with one hundred and one knots, is for the guru; // 131

sanskrit_iast:
pare gurau tu tryadhikamadhyabdhi parameṣṭhini /
prāksiddhācāryayogeśa viṣaye tu rasādhikam // 132
meaning:
परे गुरौ तु त्र्यधिकमध्यब्धि परमेष्ठिनि /
प्राक्सिद्धाचार्ययोगेश विषये तु रसाधिकम् // 132
text_mt: for the supreme guru, however, having three more [i.e. 104]; for the Parameṣṭhin, [having four more, i.e.] 108; / in the case of the previously accomplished masters and lords of yoga, having six more [i.e. 106]; // 132

sanskrit_iast:
aṣṭādhikaṃ śivasyoktaṃ citraratnaprapūritam /
vidyāpīṭhākṣasūtrādau guruvacchivavat punaḥ // 133
meaning:
अष्टाधिकं शिवस्योक्तं चित्ररत्नप्रपूरितम् /
विद्यापीठाक्षसूत्रादौ गुरुवच्छिववत् पुनः // 133
text_mt: having eight more [i.e. 108] is taught for Śiva, filled with varied gems. / For the throne of knowledge, the rosary, and so forth, it is as for the guru; again, as for Śiva // 133

sanskrit_iast:
vaṭuke kanakābhāve raupyaṃ tu parikalpayet /
pāṭṭasūtramatha kṣaumaṃ kārpāsaṃ tritritānitam // 134
meaning:
वटुके कनकाभावे रौप्यं तु परिकल्पयेत् /
पाट्टसूत्रमथ क्षौमं कार्पासं त्रित्रितानितम् // 134
text_mt: for Vaṭuka. In the absence of gold, one should substitute silver. / Or a silk thread, or linen, or cotton, threefold-threefold spun; // 134

sanskrit_iast:
tasmānnavaguṇāt sūtrāttriguṇādikramāt kuru /
caṇḍāṃśuguṇaparyantaṃ tato'pi triguṇaṃ ca vā // 135
meaning:
तस्मान्नवगुणात् सूत्रात्त्रिगुणादिक्रमात् कुरु /
चण्डांशुगुणपर्यन्तं ततोऽपि त्रिगुणं च वा // 135
text_mt: from that ninefold thread, make [it] in the sequence beginning with three-fold / up to twelve-fold (the multiplier of the fierce-rayed Sun), or even threefold that. // 135

sanskrit_iast:
tenāṣṭādaśatantūtthamadhamaṃ madhyamaṃ punaḥ /
aṣṭottaraśataṃ tasmāt triguṇaṃ tūttamaṃ matam // 136
meaning:
तेनाष्टादशतन्तूत्थमधमं मध्यमं पुनः /
अष्टोत्तरशतं तस्मात् त्रिगुणं तूत्तमं मतम् // 136
text_mt: Therefore, that made of eighteen strands is the lowest; the middling is / of one hundred and eight; while that threefold from it is considered the best. // 136

sanskrit_iast:
granthayastattvasaṃkhyātāḥ ṣaḍadhvakalanāvaśāt /
yadvā vyāsasamāsābhyāṃ citrāḥ sadgandhapūritāḥ // 137
meaning:
ग्रन्थयस्तत्त्वसंख्याताः षडध्वकलनावशात् /
यद्वा व्याससमासाभ्यां चित्राः सद्गन्धपूरिताः // 137
text_mt: The knots are numbered according to the principles (tattva), by virtue of the enumeration of the six paths, / or else, in detailed or abbreviated forms, variegated and infused with fragrant scents. // 137

sanskrit_iast:
viśeṣavidhinā pūrvaṃ pūjayitvārpayettataḥ /
pavitrakaṃ samastādhvaparipūrṇatvabhāvanāt // 138
meaning:
विशेषविधिना पूर्वं पूजयित्वार्पयेत्ततः /
पवित्रकं समस्ताध्वपरिपूर्णत्वभावनात् // 138
text_mt: Having first worshipped it according to the special injunction, one should then offer / the sacred thread, through the contemplation of the complete fullness of all the paths, // 138

sanskrit_iast:
gurvātmanorjānunābhikaṇṭhamūrdhāntagaṃ ca vā /
tato mahotsavaḥ kāryo gurupūjāpuraḥsaraḥ // 139
meaning:
गुर्वात्मनोर्जानुनाभिकण्ठमूर्धान्तगं च वा /
ततो महोत्सवः कार्यो गुरुपूजापुरःसरः // 139
text_mt: reaching down to the knees, navel, throat, or head of the guru and oneself. / Then a great festival must be celebrated, preceded by worship of the guru. // 139

sanskrit_iast:
tarpyāḥ śāsanagāḥ sarve dakṣiṇāvastrabhojanaiḥ /
mahotsavaḥ prakartavyo gītanṛttātmako mahān // 140
meaning:
तर्प्याः शासनगाः सर्वे दक्षिणावस्त्रभोजनैः /
महोत्सवः प्रकर्तव्यो गीतनृत्तात्मको महान् // 140
text_mt: All followers of the teaching should be gratified with fees, garments, and food; / a great festival consisting of song and dance should be performed, // 140

sanskrit_iast:
cāturmāsyaṃ saptadinaṃ tridinaṃ vāpyalābhataḥ /
tadante kṣamayeddevaṃ maṇḍalādi visarjayet // 141
meaning:
चातुर्मास्यं सप्तदिनं त्रिदिनं वाप्यलाभतः /
तदन्ते क्षमयेद्देवं मण्डलादि विसर्जयेत् // 141
text_mt: lasting four months, seven days, or three days if [resources are] lacking. / At its end, one should ask the Lord's forgiveness, and dismiss the maṇḍala and other items, // 141

sanskrit_iast:
vahniṃ ca paścātkartavyaścakrayāgaḥ puroditaḥ /
māse māse caturmāse varṣe vāpi pavitrakam // 142
meaning:
वह्निं च पश्चात्कर्तव्यश्चक्रयागः पुरोदितः /
मासे मासे चतुर्मासे वर्षे वापि पवित्रकम् // 142
text_mt: and the fire; and afterwards the previously explained sacrifice of the circle (cakrayāga) is to be performed. / Every month, every four months, or once a year, the sacred thread [rite] // 142

sanskrit_iast:
sarvathaiva prakartavyaṃ yathāvibhavavistaram /
vittābhāve punaḥ kāryaṃ kāśairapi kuśombhitaiḥ // 143
meaning:
सर्वथैव प्रकर्तव्यं यथाविभवविस्तरम् /
वित्ताभावे पुनः कार्यं काशैरपि कुशोम्भितैः // 143
text_mt: is by all means to be performed according to the extent of one's wealth. / But in the absence of wealth, it should still be performed, even with kāśa or kuśa grasses woven together. // 143

sanskrit_iast:
sati vitte punaḥ śāṭhyaṃ vyādhaye narakāya ca /
nityapūjāsu pūrṇatvaṃ parvapūjāprapūraṇāt // 144
meaning:
सति वित्ते पुनः शाठ्यं व्याधये नरकाय च /
नित्यपूजासु पूर्णत्वं पर्वपूजाप्रपूरणात् // 144
text_mt: If wealth exists, however, deceitfulness leads to disease and hell. / Fullness in the regular daily rites is due to the completion through the junction worship; // 144

sanskrit_iast:
tatrāpi paripūrṇatvaṃ pavitrakasamarcanāt /
pavitrakavilope tu prāyaścittaṃ japetsudhīḥ // 145
meaning:
तत्रापि परिपूर्णत्वं पवित्रकसमर्चनात् /
पवित्रकविलोपे तु प्रायश्चित्तं जपेत्सुधीः // 145
text_mt: and complete fullness even in that is through the worship of the sacred thread. / If the sacred thread rite is omitted, the wise one should recite an expiation, // 145

sanskrit_iast:
suśuddhaḥ sanpunaḥ kuryādityājñā parameśituḥ /
atha triśirasi prokto likhyate tadvidhiḥ sphuṭaḥ // 146
meaning:
सुशुद्धः सन्पुनः कुर्यादित्याज्ञा परमेशितुः /
अथ त्रिशिरसि प्रोक्तो लिख्यते तद्विधिः स्फुटः // 146
text_mt: and becoming thoroughly purified, perform it again: such is the command of the Supreme Lord. / Now that clear rite taught in the Triśirobhairava is written. // 146

sanskrit_iast:
triprameyasya śaivasya pañcapañcātmakasya vā /
daśāṣṭādaśabhedasya ṣaṭsrotasa ihocyate // 147
meaning:
त्रिप्रमेयस्य शैवस्य पञ्चपञ्चात्मकस्य वा /
दशाष्टादशभेदस्य षट्स्रोतस इहोच्यते // 147
text_mt: For the Śaiva doctrine consisting of three objects of knowledge, or comprising five times five [categories], / divided into ten and eighteen, having six streams, [the ritual] is stated here. // 147

sanskrit_iast:
ye narāḥ samayabhraṣṭā guruśāstrādidūṣakāḥ /
nityanaimittikādyanyaparvasandhivivarjitāḥ // 148
meaning:
ये नराः समयभ्रष्टा गुरुशास्त्रादिदूषकाः /
नित्यनैमित्तिकाद्यन्यपर्वसन्धिविवर्जिताः // 148
text_mt: Those men who have fallen from the rule, who revile the guru, the scriptures, and the like, / who are devoid of the daily, occasional, and other rites at festive junctures, // 148

sanskrit_iast:
akāmāt kāmato vāpi sūkṣmapāpapravartinaḥ /
teṣāṃ praśamanārthāya pavitraṃ kriyate śive // 149
meaning:
अकामात् कामतो वापि सूक्ष्मपापप्रवर्तिनः /
तेषां प्रशमनार्थाय पवित्रं क्रियते शिवे // 149
text_mt: or who commit subtle sins involuntarily or voluntarily— / for their pacification, the pavitraka rite is performed unto Śiva. // 149

sanskrit_iast:
śrāvaṇādau kārtikānte śuklapakṣe śubhaprade /
natu duḥkhaprade kṛṣṇe kartṛrāṣṭranṛpādiṣu // 150
meaning:
श्रावणादौ कार्तिकान्ते शुक्लपक्षे शुभप्रदे /
नतु दुःखप्रदे कृष्णे कर्तृराष्ट्रनृपादिषु // 150
text_mt: In the bright fortnight, which bestows auspiciousness, beginning in Śrāvaṇa and ending in Kārtika, / and not in the dark fortnight, which brings distress upon the patron, the realm, the king, and others. // 150

sanskrit_iast:
pāṭṭasūtraṃ tu kauśeyaṃ kārpāsaṃ kṣaumameva ca /
cāturāśramikāṇāṃ tu subhruvā kartitokṣitam // 151
meaning:
पाट्टसूत्रं तु कौशेयं कार्पासं क्षौममेव च /
चातुराश्रमिकाणां तु सुभ्रुवा कर्तितोक्षितम् // 151
text_mt: Silk thread, tussar silk, cotton, and flax— / spun and sprinkled by fair-browed women belonging to the four stages of life. // 151

sanskrit_iast:
tridhā tu triguṇīkṛtya mānasaṃkhyāṃ tu kārayet /
aṣṭottaraṃ tantuśataṃ tadardhaṃ vā tadardhakam // 152
meaning:
त्रिधा तु त्रिगुणीकृत्य मानसंख्यां तु कारयेत् /
अष्टोत्तरं तन्तुशतं तदर्धं वा तदर्धकम् // 152
text_mt: Folding it threefold and making it three-ply, one should establish the measure and count: / one hundred and eight threads, or half that, or half of that. // 152

sanskrit_iast:
hrāsastu pūrvasaṃkhyāyā daśabhirdaśabhiḥ kramāt /
navabhiḥ pañcabhiḥ saptaviṃśatyā vā śivāditaḥ // 153
meaning:
ह्रासस्तु पूर्वसंख्याया दशभिर्दशभिः क्रमात् /
नवभिः पञ्चभिः सप्तविंशत्या वा शिवादितः // 153
text_mt: The reduction from the initial number is by tens in succession, / or by nine, by five, or by twenty-seven, beginning from Śiva. // 153

sanskrit_iast:
yādṛśastantuvinyāso granthīnkuryāttu tāvataḥ /
catuḥsamaviliptāṃstānathavā kuṅkumena tu // 154
meaning:
यादृशस्तन्तुविन्यासो ग्रन्थीन्कुर्यात्तु तावतः /
चतुःसमविलिप्तांस्तानथवा कुङ्कुमेन तु // 154
text_mt: However many the arrangement of threads may be, one should tie that many knots, / anointed with catuḥsama unguent or with saffron. // 154

sanskrit_iast:
vyakte jānutaṭāntaṃ syālliṅge pīṭhāvasānakam /
arcāsu śobhanaṃ mūrghni tritattvaparikalpanāt // 155
meaning:
व्यक्ते जानुतटान्तं स्याल्लिङ्गे पीठावसानकम् /
अर्चासु शोभनं मूर्घ्नि त्रितत्त्वपरिकल्पनात् // 155
text_mt: On an anthropomorphic image it should reach the knees; on a liṅga, ending at the pedestal; / on images it looks splendid at the head, owing to the configuration of the three principles. // 155

sanskrit_iast:
dvādaśagranthiśaktīnāṃ brahmavaktrārciṣāmapi /
vidyāpīṭhe cale liṅge sthaṇḍile ca gurorgaṇe // 156
meaning:
द्वादशग्रन्थिशक्तीनां ब्रह्मवक्त्रार्चिषामपि /
विद्यापीठे चले लिङ्गे स्थण्डिले च गुरोर्गणे // 156
text_mt: There are twelve knots for the powers, and also for the flames of the faces of the Brahmans; / on the Vidyāpīṭha, on the movable liṅga, on the bare ground, and on the assembly of the guru, // 156

sanskrit_iast:
ghaṇṭāyāṃ sruksruve śiṣyaliṅgiṣu dvāratoraṇe /
svadehe vahnipīṭhe ca yathāśobhaṃ tadiṣyate // 157
meaning:
घण्टायां स्रुक्स्रुवे शिष्यलिङ्गिषु द्वारतोरणे /
स्वदेहे वह्निपीठे च यथाशोभं तदिष्यते // 157
text_mt: on the bell, on the ladle and spoon, on disciples and ascetics, on the door and archway, / on one's own body, and on the fire altar, it is desired according to propriety. // 157

sanskrit_iast:
prāsāde yāgagehe ca kārayennavaraṅgikam /
vidyāpīṭhe tu khaśarāḥ pratimāliṅgapīṭhagam // 158
meaning:
प्रासादे यागगेहे च कारयेन्नवरङ्गिकम् /
विद्यापीठे तु खशराः प्रतिमालिङ्गपीठगम् // 158
text_mt: On the temple and on the sacrificial pavilion, one should make it with nine colors; / on the Vidyāpīṭha, fifty; on the image, the liṅga, and the pedestal, // 158

sanskrit_iast:
vasuvedaṃ ca ghaṇṭāyāṃ śarākṣyaṣṭādaśa sruve /
vedākṣi sruci ṣaṭtriṃśat prāsāde maṇḍape raviḥ // 159
meaning:
वसुवेदं च घण्टायां शराक्ष्यष्टादश स्रुवे /
वेदाक्षि स्रुचि षट्त्रिंशत् प्रासादे मण्डपे रविः // 159
text_mt: forty-eight; on the bell, twenty-five; eighteen on the ladle; / twenty-four on the spoon; thirty-six on the temple; twelve on the pavilion; // 159

sanskrit_iast:
rasendu snānagehe'bdhinetre dhyānagṛhe gurau /
sapta sādhakagāḥ pañca putrake sapta sāmaye // 160
meaning:
रसेन्दु स्नानगेहेऽब्धिनेत्रे ध्यानगृहे गुरौ /
सप्त साधकगाः पञ्च पुत्रके सप्त सामये // 160
text_mt: sixteen in the bath-house; twenty-four in the chamber of meditation; on the guru / seven; five assigned to the adept; seven on the spiritual son; on the initiate into the rule // 160

sanskrit_iast:
catvāro'thānyaśāstrasthe śiṣye pañcakamucyate /
liṅgināṃ kevalo granthistoraṇe daśa kalpayet // 161
meaning:
चत्वारोऽथान्यशास्त्रस्थे शिष्ये पञ्चकमुच्यते /
लिङ्गिनां केवलो ग्रन्थिस्तोरणे दश कल्पयेत् // 161
text_mt: four; on a disciple adhering to another scripture, a group of five is prescribed; / for ascetics, a single knot; on an archway, one should fashion ten; // 161

sanskrit_iast:
dvāreṣvaṣṭau granthayaḥ syuḥ kṛtvetthaṃ tu pavitrakam /
pūjayitvā mantrajālaṃ tatsthatvātmasthate tataḥ // 162
meaning:
द्वारेष्वष्टौ ग्रन्थयः स्युः कृत्वेत्थं तु पवित्रकम् /
पूजयित्वा मन्त्रजालं तत्स्थत्वात्मस्थते ततः // 162
text_mt: at the doors there should be eight knots. Having made the pavitraka in this manner, / and having worshipped the collection of mantras, then [realizing] their presence in that [thread] and in oneself, // 162

sanskrit_iast:
pavitrakāṇāṃ saṃpādya kuryātsaṃpātasaṃskriyām /
tataḥ saṃvatsaraṃ dhyāyedbhairavaṃ chidrasākṣiṇam // 163
meaning:
पवित्रकाणां संपाद्य कुर्यात्संपातसंस्क्रियाम् /
ततः संवत्सरं ध्यायेद्भैरवं छिद्रसाक्षिणम् // 163
text_mt: and having prepared the pavitrakas, one should perform the consecration by dropping [clarified butter]. / Then, one should meditate upon the Year, Bhairava, the witness to omissions. // 163

sanskrit_iast:
dattvā pūrṇāhutiṃ devi praṇamenmantrabhairavam /
oṃ samastakriyādoṣapūraṇeśa vrataṃ prati // 164
meaning:
दत्त्वा पूर्णाहुतिं देवि प्रणमेन्मन्त्रभैरवम् /
ओं समस्तक्रियादोषपूरणेश व्रतं प्रति // 164
text_mt: Having offered the full oblation, O goddess, one should bow to Mantra-Bhairava: / 'Om, Lord who makes whole the defects of all rites! In regard to my vow, // 164

sanskrit_iast:
yatkiṃcidakṛtaṃ duṣṭaṃ kṛtaṃ vā mātṛnandana /
tatsarvaṃ mama deveśa tvatprasādātpraṇaśyatu // 165
meaning:
यत्किंचिदकृतं दुष्टं कृतं वा मातृनन्दन /
तत्सर्वं मम देवेश त्वत्प्रसादात्प्रणश्यतु // 165
text_mt: whatever has been left undone, or done improperly, O delight of the Mother, / may all that perish through your grace, O Lord of gods! // 165

sanskrit_iast:
sarvathā raśmicakreśa namastubhyaṃ prasīda me /
anena dadyāddevāya nimantraṇapavitrakam // 166
meaning:
सर्वथा रश्मिचक्रेश नमस्तुभ्यं प्रसीद मे /
अनेन दद्याद्देवाय निमन्त्रणपवित्रकम् // 166
text_mt: In every way, O Lord of the wheel of rays, obeisance to you! Be pleased with me!' / With this [prayer], one should offer the invitation pavitraka to the deity. // 166

sanskrit_iast:
yoginīkṣetramātṝṇāṃ baliṃ dadyāttato guruḥ /
pañcagavyaṃ caruṃ dantakāṣṭhaṃ śiṣyaiḥ samantataḥ // 167
meaning:
योगिनीक्षेत्रमातॄणां बलिं दद्यात्ततो गुरुः /
पञ्चगव्यं चरुं दन्तकाष्ठं शिष्यैः समन्ततः // 167
text_mt: Then the guru should offer oblations to the yoginīs, the fields, and the Mothers, / along with the five products of the cow, cooked oblation rice, and tooth-sticks through the disciples all around. // 167

sanskrit_iast:
ācārya nidrāṃ kurvīta prātarutthāya cāhnikam /
tato vidhiṃ pūjayitvā pavitrāṇi samāharet // 168
meaning:
आचार्य निद्रां कुर्वीत प्रातरुत्थाय चाह्निकम् /
ततो विधिं पूजयित्वा पवित्राणि समाहरेत् // 168
text_mt: Having eaten, the master should sleep; and having risen at dawn, [perform] the daily rite; / then, having worshipped according to rule, he should bring the pavitrakas. // 168

sanskrit_iast:
dantakāṣṭhaṃ mṛcca dhātrī samṛddhātrī sahāmbunā /
catuḥsamaṃ ca taiḥ sārdhaṃ bhasma pañcasu yojayet // 169
meaning:
दन्तकाष्ठं मृच्च धात्री समृद्धात्री सहाम्बुना /
चतुःसमं च तैः सार्धं भस्म पञ्चसु योजयेत् // 169
text_mt: Tooth-stick, clay, myrobalan, and wealthy emblic myrobalan together with water / and catuḥsama perfume—along with these, one should apply ash to the five. // 169

sanskrit_iast:
prāgdakṣapaścimordhvasthavāmavaktreṣu vai kramāt /
pañcaitāni pavitrāṇi sthāpayecceśagocare // 170
meaning:
प्राग्दक्षपश्चिमोर्ध्वस्थवामवक्त्रेषु वै क्रमात् /
पञ्चैतानि पवित्राणि स्थापयेच्चेशगोचरे // 170
text_mt: In succession on the east, south, west, upper, and north faces, / one should place these five pavitrakas in the domain of the Lord. // 170

sanskrit_iast:
kuśedhma pañcagavyaṃ ca śarvāgre viniyojayet /
vāmāmṛtādisaṃyuktaṃ naivedyaṃ trividhaṃ tataḥ // 171
meaning:
कुशेध्म पञ्चगव्यं च शर्वाग्रे विनियोजयेत् /
वामामृतादिसंयुक्तं नैवेद्यं त्रिविधं ततः // 171
text_mt: One should offer kuśa grass, firewood, and the five products of the cow before Śarva; / then the threefold food offering, joined with nectar of the left, and so forth. // 171

sanskrit_iast:
dadyādasṛk tathā madyaṃ pānāni vividhāni ca /
tato homo mahākṣmājamāṃsaistilayutairatho // 172
meaning:
दद्यादसृक् तथा मद्यं पानानि विविधानि च /
ततो होमो महाक्ष्माजमांसैस्तिलयुतैरथो // 172
text_mt: One should offer blood, liquor, and various drinks; / then the fire sacrifice with the flesh of the great tree combined with sesame seeds; or // 172

sanskrit_iast:
tilairghṛtayutairyadvā taṇḍulairatha dhānyakaiḥ /
śarkarākhaṇḍasaṃyuktapañcāmṛtapariplutaiḥ // 173
meaning:
तिलैर्घृतयुतैर्यद्वा तण्डुलैरथ धान्यकैः /
शर्कराखण्डसंयुक्तपञ्चामृतपरिप्लुतैः // 173
text_mt: with sesame seeds mixed with ghee, or with husked grains or other seeds, / mixed with pieces of sugar and drenched in the five nectars. // 173

sanskrit_iast:
mūlaṃ sahasraṃ sāṣṭoktaṃ triśaktau brahmavaktrakam /
arciṣāṃ tu śataṃ sāṣṭaṃ tataḥ pūrṇāhutiṃ kṣipet // 174
meaning:
मूलं सहस्रं साष्टोक्तं त्रिशक्तौ ब्रह्मवक्त्रकम् /
अर्चिषां तु शतं साष्टं ततः पूर्णाहुतिं क्षिपेत् // 174
text_mt: The basic mantra is stated [to be recited] one thousand and eight times; for the three powers and the Brahman faces, / and for the flames, one hundred and eight; then one should cast the full oblation. // 174

sanskrit_iast:
tato'ñjalau pavitraṃ tu gṛhītvā prapaṭhedidam /
akāmādathavā kāmādyanmayā na kṛtaṃ vibho // 175
meaning:
ततोऽञ्जलौ पवित्रं तु गृहीत्वा प्रपठेदिदम् /
अकामादथवा कामाद्यन्मया न कृतं विभो // 175
text_mt: Then, taking the pavitraka in folded hands, one should recite this: / 'Whatever was not performed by me, O omnipresent Lord, involuntarily or voluntarily, // 175

sanskrit_iast:
tadacchidraṃ mamāstvīśa pavitreṇa tavājñayā /
mūlamantraḥ pūrayeti kriyāniyamamityatha // 176
meaning:
तदच्छिद्रं ममास्त्वीश पवित्रेण तवाज्ञया /
मूलमन्त्रः पूरयेति क्रियानियममित्यथ // 176
text_mt: may that become flawless for me, O Lord, through the pavitraka, by your command!' / Then the basic mantra, saying 'make whole the rule of action', // 176

sanskrit_iast:
vauṣaḍantaṃ pavitraṃ ca dadyādbindvavasānakam /
nādāntaṃ samanāntaṃ cāpyunmanāntaṃ kramāttrayam // 177
meaning:
वौषडन्तं पवित्रं च दद्याद्बिन्द्ववसानकम् /
नादान्तं समनान्तं चाप्युन्मनान्तं क्रमात्त्रयम् // 177
text_mt: ending with 'vauṣaṭ', and one should offer the pavitraka terminating at the point (bindu), / terminating at the resonance (nāda), terminating at samanā, and terminating at unmanā—three successively. // 177

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ catuṣṭayaṃ dadyādanulomena bhautikaḥ /
naiṣṭhikastu vilomena pavitrakacatuṣṭayam // 178
meaning:
एवं चतुष्टयं दद्यादनुलोमेन भौतिकः /
नैष्ठिकस्तु विलोमेन पवित्रकचतुष्टयम् // 178
text_mt: Thus the householder should offer the four in the forward order; / but the perpetual celibate should offer the four pavitrakas in the reverse order. // 178

sanskrit_iast:
yatkiñcidvividhaṃ vastracchatrālaṅkaraṇādikam /
tannivedyaṃ dīpamālāḥ suvarṇatilabhājanam // 179
meaning:
यत्किञ्चिद्विविधं वस्त्रच्छत्रालङ्करणादिकम् /
तन्निवेद्यं दीपमालाः सुवर्णतिलभाजनम् // 179
text_mt: Whatever various garments, parasols, ornaments, and the like, / that food offering, rows of lamps, and a vessel of sesame with gold, // 179

sanskrit_iast:
vastrayugmayutaṃ sarvasampūraṇanimittataḥ /
bhojanīyāḥ pūjanīyāḥ śivabhaktāstu śaktitaḥ // 180
meaning:
वस्त्रयुग्मयुतं सर्वसम्पूरणनिमित्ततः /
भोजनीयाः पूजनीयाः शिवभक्तास्तु शक्तितः // 180
text_mt: along with a pair of cloths, for the purpose of completing everything— / the devotees of Śiva should be fed and honoured according to one's capacity. // 180

sanskrit_iast:
catustridvyekamāsādidinaikāntaṃ mahotsavam /
kuryāttato na vrajeyuranyasthānaṃ kadācana // 181
meaning:
चतुस्त्रिद्व्येकमासादिदिनैकान्तं महोत्सवम् /
कुर्यात्ततो न व्रजेयुरन्यस्थानं कदाचन // 181
text_mt: One should hold a great festival lasting four, three, two, or one month, down to a single day; / during that time, they should never depart for another place. // 181

sanskrit_iast:
tatastu daiśikaḥ pūjyo gāmasmai kṣīriṇīṃ navām /
dadyātsuvarṇaratnādirupyavastravibhūṣitām // 182
meaning:
ततस्तु दैशिकः पूज्यो गामस्मै क्षीरिणीं नवाम् /
दद्यात्सुवर्णरत्नादिरुप्यवस्त्रविभूषिताम् // 182
text_mt: Then the spiritual guide is to be worshipped; one should give him a fresh milch cow / adorned with gold, gems, silver, and cloth. // 182

sanskrit_iast:
vadedguruśca saṃpūrṇo vidhistava bhavatviti /
vaktavyaṃ devadevasya punarāgamanāya ca // 183
meaning:
वदेद्गुरुश्च संपूर्णो विधिस्तव भवत्विति /
वक्तव्यं देवदेवस्य पुनरागमनाय च // 183
text_mt: And the guru should say: 'May your rite be complete!' / And words must be spoken for the return of the God of gods. // 183

sanskrit_iast:
tato visarjanaṃ kāryaṃ guptamābharaṇādikam /
naivedyaṃ gururādāya yāgārthe tanniyojayet // 184
meaning:
ततो विसर्जनं कार्यं गुप्तमाभरणादिकम् /
नैवेद्यं गुरुरादाय यागार्थे तन्नियोजयेत् // 184
text_mt: Then the dismissal is to be performed; taking the concealed ornaments and the like / and the food offering, the guru should employ it for the sacrifice. // 184

sanskrit_iast:
caturṇāmapi sāmānyaṃ pavitrakamiti smṛtam /
nāsmādvrataṃ paraṃ kiñcit kā vāsya stutirucyate // 185
meaning:
चतुर्णामपि सामान्यं पवित्रकमिति स्मृतम् /
नास्माद्व्रतं परं किञ्चित् का वास्य स्तुतिरुच्यते // 185
text_mt: This pavitraka rite is held to be common to all four [castes]; / there is no observance higher than this—what praise can be spoken of it? // 185

sanskrit_iast:
śeṣaṃ tvagādhe vāryoghe kṣipenna sthāpayetsthiram /
atha naimittikavidhiryaḥ purāsūtrito mayā // 186
meaning:
शेषं त्वगाधे वार्योघे क्षिपेन्न स्थापयेत्स्थिरम् /
अथ नैमित्तिकविधिर्यः पुरासूत्रितो मया // 186
text_mt: The remains one should throw into a deep current of water, and not let them remain in place. / Now the occasional rite that was previously outlined by me // 186

sanskrit_iast:
sa bhaṇyate tatra kāryā devasyārcā viśeṣataḥ /
cakrayāgaśca kartavyaḥ pūrvoktavidhinā budhaiḥ // 187
meaning:
स भण्यते तत्र कार्या देवस्यार्चा विशेषतः /
चक्रयागश्च कर्तव्यः पूर्वोक्तविधिना बुधैः // 187
text_mt: is explained: in that rite, special worship of the deity is to be performed, / and the sacrifice of the wheel is to be performed by the wise according to the previously stated rule. // 187

sanskrit_iast:
tatra yadyannijābhīṣṭabhogamokṣopakārakam /
pāramparyeṇa sākṣādvā bhaveccidacidātmakam // 188
meaning:
तत्र यद्यन्निजाभीष्टभोगमोक्षोपकारकम् /
पारम्पर्येण साक्षाद्वा भवेच्चिदचिदात्मकम् // 188
text_mt: Therein, whatever aids one's desired enjoyment and liberation, / whether indirectly or directly, whether having the nature of consciousness or insentience, // 188

sanskrit_iast:
tatpūjyaṃ tadupāyāśca pūjyāstanmayatāptaye /
tadupāyo'pi saṃpūjyo mūrtikālakriyādikaḥ // 189
meaning:
तत्पूज्यं तदुपायाश्च पूज्यास्तन्मयताप्तये /
तदुपायोऽपि संपूज्यो मूर्तिकालक्रियादिकः // 189
text_mt: that is to be worshipped, and its means are to be worshipped in order to attain identity with it; / the means to that, too, such as the physical form, time, and action, should be thoroughly worshipped. // 189

sanskrit_iast:
upeyasūtisāmarthyamupāyatvaṃ tadarcanāt /
tadrūpatanmayībhāvādupeyaṃ śīghramāpnuyāt // 190
meaning:
उपेयसूतिसामर्थ्यमुपायत्वं तदर्चनात् /
तद्रूपतन्मयीभावादुपेयं शीघ्रमाप्नुयात् // 190
text_mt: The nature of a means is the capacity to produce the end; through worshipping that, / by absorption into and identification with its nature, one quickly attains the end. // 190

sanskrit_iast:
yathā yathā ca naikaṭyamupāyeṣu tathā tathā /
avaśyaṃbhāvi kāryatvaṃ viśeṣāccārcanādike // 191
meaning:
यथा यथा च नैकट्यमुपायेषु तथा तथा /
अवश्यंभावि कार्यत्वं विशेषाच्चार्चनादिके // 191
text_mt:
And in proportion as there is closeness to the means,
just so is its indispensability, especially in worship and the like.

sanskrit_iast:
jñānasya kasyacitprāptirbhogamokṣopakāriṇaḥ /
yadā tanmukhyamevoktaṃ naimittikadinaṃ budhaiḥ // 192
meaning:
ज्ञानस्य कस्यचित्प्राप्तिर्भोगमोक्षोपकारिणः /
यदा तन्मुख्यमेवोक्तं नैमित्तिकदिनं बुधैः // 192
text_mt:
When any attainment of knowledge occurs that is conducive to enjoyment and liberation,
that very day has been declared by the wise to be the primary occasion for occasional rites.

sanskrit_iast:
tadupāyaḥ śāstramatra vaktāpyaupayiko guruḥ /
tadvidyo'pi gurubhrātā saṃvādājjñānadāyakaḥ // 193
meaning:
तदुपायः शास्त्रमत्र वक्ताप्यौपयिको गुरुः /
तद्विद्योऽपि गुरुभ्राता संवादाज्ज्ञानदायकः // 193
text_mt:
The means to it is scripture here, and the speaker, the guru, is also the instrumental means;
and the guru's brother who knows that [teaching] is also a giver of knowledge through dialogue.

sanskrit_iast:
guroḥ patnī tathā bhrātā putra ityādiko gaṇaḥ /
na yonisaṃbandhavaśādvidyāsaṃbandhajastu saḥ // 194
meaning:
गुरोः पत्नी तथा भ्राता पुत्र इत्यादिको गणः /
न योनिसंबन्धवशाद्विद्यासंबन्धजस्तु सः // 194
text_mt:
The guru's wife, brother, son, and the rest of the group
arise not by virtue of physical connection, but by connection through spiritual knowledge.

sanskrit_iast:
vīryāruṇaparīṇāmadehāhantāpratiṣṭhitāḥ /
dehopakārasantānā jñāteye pariniṣṭhitāḥ // 195
meaning:
वीर्यारुणपरीणामदेहाहन्ताप्रतिष्ठिताः /
देहोपकारसन्ताना ज्ञातेये परिनिष्ठिताः // 195
text_mt:
Those who are anchored in an ego-sense identified with the body, which is a transformation of semen and ovum,
maintain lineages of bodily benefit and are firmly established in kinship relations.

sanskrit_iast:
tathāca smṛtiśāstreṣu santaterdāyahāritā /
yuktaiva tāvānsa hyukto bhedāddūrāntikatvataḥ // 196
meaning:
तथाच स्मृतिशास्त्रेषु सन्ततेर्दायहारिता /
युक्तैव तावान्स ह्युक्तो भेदाद्दूरान्तिकत्वतः // 196
text_mt:
And so in the legal treatises the inheritance of an estate is given to the lineage;
that is entirely fitting, for that [relation] has been stated according to divisions of distance and proximity.

sanskrit_iast:
ye tu tyaktaśarīrāsthā bodhāhambhāvabhāginaḥ /
bodhopakārasantānadvayātte bandhutājuṣaḥ // 197
meaning:
ये तु त्यक्तशरीरास्था बोधाहम्भावभागिनः /
बोधोपकारसन्तानद्वयात्ते बन्धुताजुषः // 197
text_mt:
Those, however, who have abandoned clinging to the body and partake of the I-consciousness of awareness
enjoy kinship because of the two continuities of benefit to awareness.

sanskrit_iast:
tatretthaṃ prāgyadā paśyecchaktyunmīlitadṛkkriyaḥ /
dehastāvadayaṃ pūrvapūrvopādānanirmitaḥ // 198
meaning:
तत्रेत्थं प्राग्यदा पश्येच्छक्त्युन्मीलितदृक्क्रियः /
देहस्तावदयं पूर्वपूर्वोपादाननिर्मितः // 198
text_mt:
In this regard, when earlier one sees with the power of vision and action awakened:
this body is produced from preceding material causes;

sanskrit_iast:
ātmā vikārarahitaḥ śāśvatatvādahetukaḥ /
svātantryāt punarātmīyādayaṃ channa iva sthitaḥ // 199
meaning:
आत्मा विकाररहितः शाश्वतत्वादहेतुकः /
स्वातन्त्र्यात् पुनरात्मीयादयं छन्न इव स्थितः // 199
text_mt:
the Self is free of modification, and, being eternal, has no cause;
yet, through its own absolute autonomy, it remains as if concealed,

sanskrit_iast:
punaśca prakaṭībhūya bhairavībhāvabhājanam /
tatrāsya prakaṭībhāve bhuktimuktyātmake bhṛśam // 200
meaning:
पुनश्च प्रकटीभूय भैरवीभावभाजनम् /
तत्रास्य प्रकटीभावे भुक्तिमुक्त्यात्मके भृशम् // 200
text_mt:
and having become manifest once again, it is the vessel of the state of Bhairava.
In that manifestation of it, whose nature is enjoyment and liberation,
whatever appropriate means exists is exceedingly this continuity of knowledge.

sanskrit_iast:
ya upāyaḥ samucito jñānasantāna eṣa saḥ /
kramasphuṭībhavattādṛksadṛśajñānadhārayā // 201
meaning:
य उपायः समुचितो ज्ञानसन्तान एष सः /
क्रमस्फुटीभवत्तादृक्सदृशज्ञानधारया // 201
text_mt:
By a stream of similar knowledge of such a kind becoming gradually manifest,
what is to be attained is quickly gained, because of the melting away of alien elements.

sanskrit_iast:
galadvijātīyatayā prāpyaṃ śīghraṃ hi labhyate /
evaṃ cānādisaṃsārocitavijñānasantateḥ // 202
meaning:
गलद्विजातीयतया प्राप्यं शीघ्रं हि लभ्यते /
एवं चानादिसंसारोचितविज्ञानसन्ततेः // 202
text_mt:
And so, upon the destruction of the continuity of consciousness suited to beginningless transmigration,
transmundane knowledge assumes a different continuity.

sanskrit_iast:
dhvaṃse lokottaraṃ jñānaṃ santānāntaratāṃ śrayet /
asaṃsārocitodāratathāvijñānasantateḥ // 203
meaning:
ध्वंसे लोकोत्तरं ज्ञानं सन्तानान्तरतां श्रयेत् /
असंसारोचितोदारतथाविज्ञानसन्ततेः // 203
text_mt:
The primary, first cause of such an exalted continuity of consciousness suited to non-transmigration
is that consciousness of the guru residing in oneself, clearly because of the complete transfer of his specific qualities into it.

sanskrit_iast:
kāraṇaṃ mukhyamādyaṃ tadguruvijñānamātmagam /
atyantaṃ svaviśeṣāṇāṃ tatrārpaṇavaśāt sphuṭam // 204
meaning:
कारणं मुख्यमाद्यं तद्गुरुविज्ञानमात्मगम् /
अत्यन्तं स्वविशेषाणां तत्रार्पणवशात् स्फुटम् // 204

sanskrit_iast:
upādānaṃ hi tadyuktaṃ dehabhede hi satyapi /
dehasantatigau bhedābhedau vijñānasantateḥ // 205
meaning:
उपादानं हि तद्युक्तं देहभेदे हि सत्यपि /
देहसन्ततिगौ भेदाभेदौ विज्ञानसन्ततेः // 205
text_mt:
When a yogin imparts life to another's body and the like
without abandoning his own body, is he not the material cause of manifold consciousness?

sanskrit_iast:
na tathātvāya yogīcchāviṣṭaśāvaśarīravat /
yoginaḥ paradehādijīvattāpādane nijam // 206
meaning:
न तथात्वाय योगीच्छाविष्टशावशरीरवत् /
योगिनः परदेहादिजीवत्तापादने निजम् // 206
text_mt:
Therefore, because of the pre-eminence of the continuity of consciousness over physical lineage,
the lineage of the guru consists of each other, established in the knowledge of Śiva.

sanskrit_iast:
dehamatyajato nānājñānopādānatā na kim /
tena vijñānasantānaprādhānyādyaunasantateḥ // 207
meaning:
देहमत्यजतो नानाज्ञानोपादानता न किम् /
तेन विज्ञानसन्तानप्राधान्याद्यौनसन्ततेः // 207
text_mt:
This being established, the guru's group consists of three primary factors:
the cause, the auxiliary, and the effect of the single cause.

sanskrit_iast:
anyonyaṃ gurusantāno yaḥ śivajñānaniṣṭhitaḥ /
itthaṃ sthite trayaṃ mukhyaṃ kāraṇaṃ sahakāri ca // 208
meaning:
अन्योन्यं गुरुसन्तानो यः शिवज्ञाननिष्ठितः /
इत्थं स्थिते त्रयं मुख्यं कारणं सहकारि च // 208
text_mt:
The guru is said to be the cause here, and his wife is the auxiliary,
because without a consort he has no qualification for the sacrifice.

sanskrit_iast:
ekakāraṇakāryaṃ ca vastvityeṣa gurorgaṇaḥ /
guruḥ kāraṇamatroktaṃ tatpatnī sahakāriṇī // 209
meaning:
एककारणकार्यं च वस्त्वित्येष गुरोर्गणः /
गुरुः कारणमत्रोक्तं तत्पत्नी सहकारिणी // 209
text_mt:
Even without an external consort, one has the power of the exalted inner consciousness;
just as a yogin has capacity even without an auxiliary.

sanskrit_iast:
yato niḥśaktikasyāsya na yāge'dhikṛtirbhavet /
antaḥsthodārasaṃvittiśakterbāhyāṃ vināpi tām // 210
meaning:
यतो निःशक्तिकस्यास्य न यागेऽधिकृतिर्भवेत् /
अन्तःस्थोदारसंवित्तिशक्तेर्बाह्यां विनापि ताम् // 210
text_mt:
Brothers would be those born of the same [cause], and whoever is similar to that [is likewise one].
Furthermore, through the connection of succession, the lineage of gurus is also described.

sanskrit_iast:
sāmarthyaṃ yogino yadvadvināpi sahakāriṇam /
ekajanyā bhrātaraḥ syustatsadṛgyastu ko'pi saḥ // 211
meaning:
सामर्थ्यं योगिनो यद्वद्विनापि सहकारिणम् /
एकजन्या भ्रातरः स्युस्तत्सदृग्यस्तु कोऽपि सः // 211
text_mt:
This primary lineage is to be worshipped and honoured at all times.
And on the birth, initiation, and death of the guru and the others,

sanskrit_iast:
punaḥ paramparāyogādguruvargo'pi bhaṇyate /
mukhya eṣa tu santānaḥ pūjyo mānyaśca sarvadā // 212
meaning:
पुनः परम्परायोगाद्गुरुवर्गोऽपि भण्यते /
मुख्य एष तु सन्तानः पूज्यो मान्यश्च सर्वदा // 212
text_mt:
that day is indeed the cause of the body and other [instruments], which are the means to consciousness.
Thus one's own birthday is called a means to consciousness,

sanskrit_iast:
gurvādīnāṃ ca sambhūtau dīkṣāyāṃ prāyaṇe'pi ca /
yadahastaddhi vijñānopāyadehādikāraṇam // 213
meaning:
गुर्वादीनां च सम्भूतौ दीक्षायां प्रायणेऽपि च /
यदहस्तद्धि विज्ञानोपायदेहादिकारणम् // 213
text_mt:
the cause of the body, which is the cause of such enjoyment, liberation, and so forth.
And the day on which a consecration such as initiation occurs for oneself,

sanskrit_iast:
evaṃ svajanmadivaso vijñānopāya ucyate /
tādṛgbhogāpavargādihetordehasya kāraṇam // 214
meaning:
एवं स्वजन्मदिवसो विज्ञानोपाय उच्यते /
तादृग्भोगापवर्गादिहेतोर्देहस्य कारणम् // 214
text_mt:
that would be the primary birthday, because of the birth of the continuity of knowledge.
One's own day of death, however, will be an occasional rite for others,

sanskrit_iast:
dīkṣādikaśca saṃskāraḥ svātmano yatra cāhni tat /
bhavejjanmadinaṃ mukhyaṃ jñānasantānajanmataḥ // 215
meaning:
दीक्षादिकश्च संस्कारः स्वात्मनो यत्र चाह्नि तत् /
भवेज्जन्मदिनं मुख्यं ज्ञानसन्तानजन्मतः // 215
text_mt:
since the dead one at that time becomes non-different from Śiva.
In that context, by way of digression, we explain clearly the true nature of death.

sanskrit_iast:
svakaṃ mṛtidinaṃ yattu tadanyeṣāṃ bhaviṣyati /
naimittikaṃ mṛto yasmācchivābhinnastadā bhavet // 216
meaning:
स्वकं मृतिदिनं यत्तु तदन्येषां भविष्यति /
नैमित्तिकं मृतो यस्माच्छिवाभिन्नस्तदा भवेत् // 216
text_mt:
Though all-pervasive, Śiva, through the sealing of contraction fashioned by His own will,
partakes of various bodies under the sway of a torrent of actions with diverse fruits.

sanskrit_iast:
tatra prasaṅgānmaraṇasvarūpaṃ brūmahe sphuṭam /
vyāpako'pi śivaḥ svecchākḷptasaṅkocamudraṇāt // 217
meaning:
तत्र प्रसङ्गान्मरणस्वरूपं ब्रूमहे स्फुटम् /
व्यापकोऽपि शिवः स्वेच्छाकॢप्तसङ्कोचमुद्रणात् // 217
text_mt:
And partaking of a body consists merely in this: residing in the body within the womb,
there occurs the first rise of vital breathing from consciousness settled in the void.

sanskrit_iast:
vicitraphalakarmaughavaśāttattaccharīrabhāk /
śarīrabhāktvaṃ caitāvadyattadgarbhasthadehagaḥ // 218
meaning:
विचित्रफलकर्मौघवशात्तत्तच्छरीरभाक् /
शरीरभाक्त्वं चैतावद्यत्तद्गर्भस्थदेहगः // 218
text_mt:
Moreover, in the formation of the body within the womb, He alone is the Lord;
being uncontracted, He is the creator of the body and the rest, and therefore He is called the Lord.

sanskrit_iast:
saṃvitteḥ śūnyarūḍhāyāḥ prathamaḥ prāṇanodayaḥ /
garbhasthadehanirmāṇe tasyaiveśvaratā punaḥ // 219
meaning:
संवित्तेः शून्यरूढायाः प्रथमः प्राणनोदयः /
गर्भस्थदेहनिर्माणे तस्यैवेश्वरता पुनः // 219
text_mt:
That vital breath, having the nature of air, when the bodily machine has become firm,
moves about, impelled by the conscious Self, like air in a blacksmith's bellows.

sanskrit_iast:
asaṅkocasya tanvādikartā teneśa ucyate /
sa vāyvātmā dṛḍhe tasmindehayantre cidātmanā // 220
meaning:
असङ्कोचस्य तन्वादिकर्ता तेनेश उच्यते /
स वाय्वात्मा दृढे तस्मिन्देहयन्त्रे चिदात्मना // 220
text_mt:
Hence, like one awakened from deep sleep, it wakes up beforehand;
and gradually, along with the body, the vital functioning becomes stronger.

sanskrit_iast:
preryamāṇo vicarati bhastrāyantragavāyuvat /
ataḥ prāggāḍhasaṃsuptotthitavatsa prabuddhyate // 221
meaning:
प्रेर्यमाणो विचरति भस्त्रायन्त्रगवायुवत् /
अतः प्राग्गाढसंसुप्तोत्थितवत्स प्रबुद्ध्यते // 221
text_mt:
Even there, by the force of the destiny of karma, that vital functioning acquires senses,
because of an excess of touch-consciousness in the empty apertures.

sanskrit_iast:
kramāddehena sākaṃ ca prāṇanā syādbalīyasī /
tatrāpi karmaniyatibalātsā prāṇanākṣatām // 222
meaning:
क्रमाद्देहेन साकं च प्राणना स्याद्बलीयसी /
तत्रापि कर्मनियतिबलात्सा प्राणनाक्षताम् // 222
text_mt:
Thus, in this sequence, having his bodily and vital strength greatly nurtured,
residing in a body born of a womb or not born of a womb, he enjoys the karmically generated enjoyments.

sanskrit_iast:
gṛhṇāti śūnyasuṣirasaṃvitsparśādhikatvataḥ /
evaṃ krameṇa saṃpuṣṭadehaprāṇabalo bhṛśam // 223
meaning:
गृह्णाति शून्यसुषिरसंवित्स्पर्शाधिकत्वतः /
एवं क्रमेण संपुष्टदेहप्राणबलो भृशम् // 223
text_mt:
And it has been stated in the scripture named Gahvara by the Moon-crested Lord:
'Just as a householder, having built a house, occupies it,

sanskrit_iast:
bhogānkarmakṛtānbhuṅkte yonyayonijadehagaḥ /
uktaṃ ca gahvarābhikhye śāstre śītāṃśumaulinā // 224
meaning:
भोगान्कर्मकृतान्भुङ्क्ते योन्ययोनिजदेहगः /
उक्तं च गह्वराभिख्ये शास्त्रे शीतांशुमौलिना // 224
text_mt:
so the embodied soul, having made a body, devoid of the attributes of action and the rest,
possessing at first merely a slight pulsing, is also called without parts (niṣkala);

sanskrit_iast:
yathā gṛhaṃ viniṣpādya gṛhī samadhitiṣṭhati /
tathā dehī tanuṃ kṛtvā kriyādiguṇavarjitaḥ // 225
meaning:
यथा गृहं विनिष्पाद्य गृही समधितिष्ठति /
तथा देही तनुं कृत्वा क्रियादिगुणवर्जितः // 225
text_mt:
but when the reality of the senses and the rest has become manifest, it is declared to be with parts (sakala).'
This and more has been said in the venerable Gahvara; one should read much from that very work.

sanskrit_iast:
kiñcitsphuraṇamātraḥ prāgniṣkalaḥ so'pi śabdyate /
sphuṭendriyāditattvastu sakalātmeti bhaṇyate // 226
meaning:
किञ्चित्स्फुरणमात्रः प्राग्निष्कलः सोऽपि शब्द्यते /
स्फुटेन्द्रियादितत्त्वस्तु सकलात्मेति भण्यते // 226
text_mt:
When those karmas are exhausted, however, and the bodily machine undergoes deterioration,
the machine of the vital breath breaks down, and the body then becomes like a wall.

sanskrit_iast:
ityādi śrīgahvaroktaṃ tata eva paṭhedbahu /
kṣaye tu karmaṇāṃ teṣāṃ dehayantre'nyathāgate // 227
meaning:
इत्यादि श्रीगह्वरोक्तं तत एव पठेद्बहु /
क्षये तु कर्मणां तेषां देहयन्त्रेऽन्यथागते // 227
text_mt:
There are contraction and expansion in the channels in a reverse manner,
breaking, drying, or moisture, through the decrease or increase of wind, phlegm, and fire.

sanskrit_iast:
prāṇayantraṃ vighaṭate dehaḥ syātkuḍyavattataḥ /
nāḍīcakreṣu saṅkocavikāsau viparītataḥ // 228
meaning:
प्राणयन्त्रं विघटते देहः स्यात्कुड्यवत्ततः /
नाडीचक्रेषु सङ्कोचविकासौ विपरीततः // 228
text_mt:
Whatever destroys the previous constitution in such ways
is declared by the wise to be the breakdown of the bodily machine.

sanskrit_iast:
bhaṅgaḥ śoṣaḥ klidirvātaśleṣmāgnyapacayoccayaiḥ /
ityevamādi yatkiñcit prāksaṃsthānopamardakam // 229
meaning:
भङ्गः शोषः क्लिदिर्वातश्लेष्माग्न्यपचयोच्चयैः /
इत्येवमादि यत्किञ्चित् प्राक्संस्थानोपमर्दकम् // 229
text_mt:
When that machine has broken down, that consciousness assumes the nature of vital breathing
in another body, born of a womb or otherwise, variegated by karma.

sanskrit_iast:
dehayantre vighaṭanaṃ tadevoktaṃ manīṣibhiḥ /
tasminvighaṭite yantre sā saṃvitprāṇanātmatām // 230
meaning:
देहयन्त्रे विघटनं तदेवोक्तं मनीषिभिः /
तस्मिन्विघटिते यन्त्रे सा संवित्प्राणनात्मताम् // 230
text_mt:
That body then awakens like one risen from sleep.
For it too, enjoyment, its loss, and death occur just as before;

sanskrit_iast:
gṛhṇāti yonije'nyatra vā dehe karmacitrite /
sa dehaḥ pratibudhyeta prasuptotthitavattadā // 231
meaning:
गृह्णाति योनिजेऽन्यत्र वा देहे कर्मचित्रिते /
स देहः प्रतिबुध्येत प्रसुप्तोत्थितवत्तदा // 231
text_mt:
for these emissions, maintenances, and dissolutions are due to the power of karma,
and therefore they conform to the diversity of destiny, time, and so forth.

sanskrit_iast:
tasyāpi bhogataddhānimṛtayaḥ prāgvadeva hi /
visṛṣṭisthitisaṃhārā ete karmabalādyataḥ // 232
meaning:
तस्यापि भोगतद्धानिमृतयः प्राग्वदेव हि /
विसृष्टिस्थितिसंहारा एते कर्मबलाद्यतः // 232
text_mt:
Grace, however, which consists in cognition within one's own expanding essence,
how could it look to karma, destiny, and the like?

sanskrit_iast:
ato niyatikālādivaicitryānuvidhāyinaḥ /
anugrahastu yaḥ so'yaṃ svasvarūpe vikasvare // 233
meaning:
अतो नियतिकालादिवैचित्र्यानुविधायिनः /
अनुग्रहस्तु यः सोऽयं स्वस्वरूपे विकस्वरे // 233
text_mt:
Since karma, time, destiny, and the like have contraction as their very life,
how could they be the cause of this grace, whose nature is the destruction of contraction?

sanskrit_iast:
jñaptyātmeti kathaṃ karmaniyatyādi pratīkṣate /
karmakālaniyatyādi yataḥ saṅkocajīvitam // 234
meaning:
ज्ञप्त्यात्मेति कथं कर्मनियत्यादि प्रतीक्षते /
कर्मकालनियत्यादि यतः सङ्कोचजीवितम् // 234
text_mt:
And grace is differentiated as gradual or intense;
and this was previously explained at length, so what is the use of repetitions?

sanskrit_iast:
saṅkocahānirūpe'sminkathaṃ heturanugrahe /
anugrahaśca kramikastīvraśceti vibhidyate // 235
meaning:
सङ्कोचहानिरूपेऽस्मिन्कथं हेतुरनुग्रहे /
अनुग्रहश्च क्रमिकस्तीव्रश्चेति विभिद्यते // 235
text_mt:
Therefore, one whose bond of contraction has been burnt by initiation and the knowledge of Śiva
is Śiva alone at the end of the body, and has no remaining in another body.

sanskrit_iast:
prāk caiṣa vistarātprokta iti kiṃ punaruktibhiḥ /
tena dīkṣāśivajñānadagdhasaṅkocabandhanaḥ // 236
meaning:
प्राक् चैष विस्तरात्प्रोक्त इति किं पुनरुक्तिभिः /
तेन दीक्षाशिवज्ञानदग्धसङ्कोचबन्धनः // 236
text_mt: Even of those who have descended into the realities, following the command of Śaṅkara,

sanskrit_iast:
dehānte śiva eveti nāsya dehāntarasthitiḥ /
ye'pi tattvāvatīrṇānāṃ śaṃkarājñānuvartinām // 237
meaning:
देहान्ते शिव एवेति नास्य देहान्तरस्थितिः /
येऽपि तत्त्वावतीर्णानां शंकराज्ञानुवर्तिनाम् // 237

sanskrit_iast:
svayambhūmunidevarṣimanujādibhuvāṃ gṛhe /
mṛtāste tatpuraṃ prāpya pureśairdīkṣitāḥ kramāt // 238
meaning:
स्वयम्भूमुनिदेवर्षिमनुजादिभुवां गृहे /
मृतास्ते तत्पुरं प्राप्य पुरेशैर्दीक्षिताः क्रमात् // 238
text_mt: Those who die in the abode of the self-born, sages, divine seers, men, and others, / reaching that realm, are initiated successively by the lords of the realm; // 238

sanskrit_iast:
martye'vatīrya vā no vā śivaṃ yāntyapunarbhavāḥ /
tatra svayambhuvo dvedhā ke'pyanugrahatatparāḥ // 239
meaning:
मर्त्येऽवतीर्य वा नो वा शिवं यान्त्यपुनर्भवाः /
तत्र स्वयम्भुवो द्वेधा केऽप्यनुग्रहतत्पराः // 239
text_mt: whether descending into the mortal world or not, free from rebirth, they go to Śiva. / Among them, the self-born are twofold: some intent upon bestowing grace, // 239

sanskrit_iast:
ke'pi svakṛtyāyātāṃśasthānamātropasevinaḥ /
ye'nugrahārthamājñaptāsteṣu yo mriyate naraḥ // 240
meaning:
केऽपि स्वकृत्यायातांशस्थानमात्रोपसेविनः /
येऽनुग्रहार्थमाज्ञप्तास्तेषु यो म्रियते नरः // 240
text_mt: And some [self-manifested abodes] are occupied merely as dwelling places for parts [of the divine] that have arrived on account of their own specific task. / A person who dies in the presence of those [manifestations] that are commanded to bestow grace // 240

sanskrit_iast:
so'nugrahaṃ sphuṭaṃ yāti vinā martyāvatārataḥ /
yastu svakāryaṃ kurvāṇastatsthānaṃ nāṃśatastyajet // 241
meaning:
सोऽनुग्रहं स्फुटं याति विना मर्त्यावतारतः /
यस्तु स्वकार्यं कुर्वाणस्तत्स्थानं नांशतस्त्यजेत् // 241
text_mt: clearly attains grace without having to descend into mortal [birth]. / But [as for a divinity] who, performing his own task, does not abandon that place with part [of himself], // 241

sanskrit_iast:
yathā gaurī tapasyantī kaśmīreṣu guhāgatā /
tatraiva vā yathā dhyānoḍḍāre naraharirvibhuḥ // 242
meaning:
यथा गौरी तपस्यन्ती कश्मीरेषु गुहागता /
तत्रैव वा यथा ध्यानोड्डारे नरहरिर्विभुः // 242
text_mt: just as Gaurī practicing tapas inside a cave in Kashmir, / or just as the omnipresent Narahari at Dhyānoḍḍāra in that very [country], // 242

sanskrit_iast:
vitastāṃ nayato daityāṃstrāsayandṛpta utthitaḥ /
sāligrāme yathā viṣṇuḥ śivo vā svopabhoginaḥ // 243
meaning:
वितस्तां नयतो दैत्यांस्त्रासयन्दृप्त उत्थितः /
सालिग्रामे यथा विष्णुः शिवो वा स्वोपभोगिनः // 243
text_mt: who, risen in majesty, terrified the Daityas as he brought the Vitastā; / or like Viṣṇu at Śāligrāma, or Śiva [in places] where they experience their own enjoyments; // 243

sanskrit_iast:
tapasyantau badaryāṃ ca naranārāyaṇau tathā /
ityevamādayo devāḥ svakṛtyāṃśasthitāstathā // 244
meaning:
तपस्यन्तौ बदर्यां च नरनारायणौ तथा /
इत्येवमादयो देवाः स्वकृत्यांशस्थितास्तथा // 244
text_mt: and likewise Nara and Nārāyaṇa practicing tapas at Badarī— / deities such as these who thus abide as a part [of themselves] for their own specific task, // 244

sanskrit_iast:
ārādhitāḥ svocitaṃ tacchīghraṃ vidadhate phalam /
svakṛtyāṃśasthitānāṃ ca dhāmni ye'ntaṃ vrajanti te // 245
meaning:
आराधिताः स्वोचितं तच्छीघ्रं विदधते फलम् /
स्वकृत्यांशस्थितानां च धाम्नि येऽन्तं व्रजन्ति ते // 245
text_mt: when worshiped, swiftly bestow the fruit appropriate to themselves. / And those who meet their end in the abode of those who abide as a part [of themselves] for their own specific task, // 245

sanskrit_iast:
tatra bhogāṃstathā bhuktvā martyeṣvavatarantyapi /
martyāvatīrṇāste tattadaṃśakāstanmayāḥ punaḥ // 246
meaning:
तत्र भोगांस्तथा भुक्त्वा मर्त्येष्ववतरन्त्यपि /
मर्त्यावतीर्णास्ते तत्तदंशकास्तन्मयाः पुनः // 246
text_mt: having enjoyed [various] enjoyments there, also descend among mortals. / Having descended as mortals, those portions of those [beings], composed of them, // 246

sanskrit_iast:
taddīkṣājñānacaryādikramādyānti śivātmatām /
sthāvarādyāstiryagantāḥ paśavo'smindvaye mṛtāḥ // 247
meaning:
तद्दीक्षाज्ञानचर्यादिक्रमाद्यान्ति शिवात्मताम् /
स्थावराद्यास्तिर्यगन्ताः पशवोऽस्मिन्द्वये मृताः // 247
text_mt: subsequently attain the state of Śiva by stages through initiation, knowledge, conduct, and the like in relation to that [deity]. / Immobile beings and the rest, ending with animals, who die in either of these two [types of places], // 247

sanskrit_iast:
svakarmasaṃskriyāvedhāttalloke citratājuṣaḥ /
puṃsāṃ ca paśumātrāṇāṃ sālokyamavivekataḥ // 248
meaning:
स्वकर्मसंस्क्रियावेधात्तल्लोके चित्रताजुषः /
पुंसां च पशुमात्राणां सालोक्यमविवेकतः // 248
text_mt: enjoy varied states in that world because of being penetrated by the latent impressions of their own karman. / And for mere bound souls among men, there is co-residence [with the deity] due to non-discrimination; // 248

sanskrit_iast:
avivekastadviśeṣānunmeṣānmauḍhyatastathā /
sthāvarādyāstathābhāvamuttarottaratāṃ ca vā // 249
meaning:
अविवेकस्तद्विशेषानुन्मेषान्मौढ्यतस्तथा /
स्थावराद्यास्तथाभावमुत्तरोत्तरतां च वा // 249
text_mt: non-discrimination [results] from the non-manifestation of its specific distinctions, as well as from delusion. / Immobile beings and the rest [obtain] that state or successively higher states; // 249

sanskrit_iast:
prapadyante na te sākṣādrudratāṃ tāṃ kramātpunaḥ /
haṃsakāraṇḍavākīrṇe nānātarukulākule // 250
meaning:
प्रपद्यन्ते न ते साक्षाद्रुद्रतां तां क्रमात्पुनः /
हंसकारण्डवाकीर्णे नानातरुकुलाकुले // 250
text_mt: they do not attain that Rudrahood directly, but rather gradually in course of time. / In a [sanctuary] filled with swans and kāraṇḍava ducks, crowded with various kinds of trees, // 250

sanskrit_iast:
ityetadāgameṣūktaṃ tata eva pure pure /
kṣetramānaṃ bruve śrīmatsarvajñānādiṣūditam // 251
meaning:
इत्येतदागमेषूक्तं तत एव पुरे पुरे /
क्षेत्रमानं ब्रुवे श्रीमत्सर्वज्ञानादिषूदितम् // 251
text_mt: so it is declared in the Āgamas; therefore, for each city, / I state the measure of the sacred field as taught in the venerable Sarvajñāna and other [texts]: // 251

sanskrit_iast:
liṅgāddhastaśataṃ kṣetramācāryasthāpite sati /
svayambhūte sahasraṃ tu tadardhamṛṣiyojite // 252
meaning:
लिङ्गाद्धस्तशतं क्षेत्रमाचार्यस्थापिते सति /
स्वयम्भूते सहस्रं तु तदर्धमृषियोजिते // 252
text_mt: The sacred field extends one hundred cubits from a liṅga installed by an ācārya; / but when it is self-manifested, a thousand; and half of that when established by a ṛṣi. // 252

sanskrit_iast:
tattvavitsthāpite liṅge svayambhūsadṛśaṃ phalam /
atattvavidyadācāryo liṅgaṃ sthāpayate tadā // 253
meaning:
तत्त्ववित्स्थापिते लिङ्गे स्वयम्भूसदृशं फलम् /
अतत्त्वविद्यदाचार्यो लिङ्गं स्थापयते तदा // 253
text_mt: At a liṅga installed by a knower of reality, the fruit is equal to a self-manifested one. / When an ācārya who does not know reality installs a liṅga, then // 253

sanskrit_iast:
punarvidhirbhaveddoṣo hyanyathobhayadūṣakaḥ /
ahamanyaḥ parātmānyaḥ śivo'nya iti cenmatiḥ // 254
meaning:
पुनर्विधिर्भवेद्दोषो ह्यन्यथोभयदूषकः /
अहमन्यः परात्मान्यः शिवोऽन्य इति चेन्मतिः // 254
text_mt: the rite must be performed again, for otherwise there would be a flaw defiling both. / If one has the notion: 'I am one, the supreme Self is another, Śiva is another,' // 254

sanskrit_iast:
na mocayenna muktaśca sarvamātmamayaṃ yataḥ /
tasmāttattvavidā yadyatsthāpitaṃ liṅgamuttamam // 255
meaning:
न मोचयेन्न मुक्तश्च सर्वमात्ममयं यतः /
तस्मात्तत्त्वविदा यद्यत्स्थापितं लिङ्गमुत्तमम् // 255
text_mt: he cannot liberate [others] nor is he himself liberated, since everything consists of the Self. / Therefore, whatever excellent liṅga is installed by a knower of reality, // 255

sanskrit_iast:
tadevāyatanatvena saṃśrayedbhuktimuktaye /
uktaṃ śrīratnamālāyāṃ jñātvā kālamupasthitam // 256
meaning:
तदेवायतनत्वेन संश्रयेद्भुक्तिमुक्तये /
उक्तं श्रीरत्नमालायां ज्ञात्वा कालमुपस्थितम् // 256
text_mt: that alone should be resorted to as a sanctuary for enjoyment and liberation. / It is stated in the venerable Ratnamālā: having recognized that one's time has arrived, // 256

sanskrit_iast:
mokṣārthī na bhayaṃ gacchettyajeddehamaśaṅkitaḥ /
tīrthāyatanapuṇyeṣu kālaṃ vā vañcayetpriye // 257
meaning:
मोक्षार्थी न भयं गच्छेत्त्यजेद्देहमशङ्कितः /
तीर्थायतनपुण्येषु कालं वा वञ्चयेत्प्रिये // 257
text_mt: the seeker of liberation should not succumb to fear, but cast off the body free from doubt; / or, O dear one, one may cheat death in holy places, sanctuaries, and sacred spots. // 257

sanskrit_iast:
ayogināmayaṃ panthā yogī yogena vañcayet /
vañcane tvasamarthaḥ san kṣetramāyatanaṃ vrajet // 258
meaning:
अयोगिनामयं पन्था योगी योगेन वञ्चयेत् /
वञ्चने त्वसमर्थः सन् क्षेत्रमायतनं व्रजेत् // 258
text_mt: This is the way for non-yogins; a yogin should cheat [death] through yoga. / But being unable to cheat it, one should go to a sacred field or a sanctuary; // 258

sanskrit_iast:
tīrthe samāśrayāttasya vañcanaṃ tu vijāyate /
anena ca dharādyeṣu tattveṣvabhyāsayogataḥ // 259
meaning:
तीर्थे समाश्रयात्तस्य वञ्चनं तु विजायते /
अनेन च धराद्येषु तत्त्वेष्वभ्यासयोगतः // 259
text_mt: by taking refuge in a holy place, however, the cheating of [death] does take place for him. / And by this means, through the application of practice on the tattvas beginning with earth, // 259

sanskrit_iast:
tāvatsiddhijuṣo'pyuktā muktyai kṣetropayogitā /
samyagjñānini vṛttāntaḥ purastāttūpadekṣyate // 260
meaning:
तावत्सिद्धिजुषोऽप्युक्ता मुक्त्यै क्षेत्रोपयोगिता /
सम्यग्ज्ञानिनि वृत्तान्तः पुरस्तात्तूपदेक्ष्यते // 260
text_mt: the usefulness of the sacred field for liberation is taught even for those who enjoy [merely] mundane spiritual accomplishments. / But the account regarding one possessed of complete knowledge will be taught later. // 260

sanskrit_iast:
paśūnāmeṣa vṛttānto ye tu tattattvadīkṣitāḥ /
te tadīśasamīpatvaṃ yānti svaucityayogataḥ // 261
meaning:
पशूनामेष वृत्तान्तो ये तु तत्तत्त्वदीक्षिताः /
ते तदीशसमीपत्वं यान्ति स्वौचित्ययोगतः // 261
text_mt: This is the account concerning bound souls. As for those who have received initiation into the various tattvas, / they attain proximity to the Lord of that [tattva] according to their own suitability. // 261

sanskrit_iast:
yogyatāvaśasaṃjātā yasya yatraiva vāsanā /
sa tatraiva niyoktavyaḥ pureśāccordhvaśuddhibhāk // 262
meaning:
योग्यतावशसंजाता यस्य यत्रैव वासना /
स तत्रैव नियोक्तव्यः पुरेशाच्चोर्ध्वशुद्धिभाक् // 262
text_mt: In whatever [tattva] one has a latent impression born under the sway of one's fitness, / he should be assigned right there, and subsequently receives purification above it from the lord of that city. // 262

sanskrit_iast:
iti śrīpūrvakathitaṃ śrīmatsvāyambhuve'pica /
yo yatrābhilaṣedbhogānsa tatraiva niyojitaḥ // 263
meaning:
इति श्रीपूर्वकथितं श्रीमत्स्वायम्भुवेऽपिच /
यो यत्राभिलषेद्भोगान्स तत्रैव नियोजितः // 263
text_mt: So it is declared in the venerable Pūrva [Mālinīvijayottara], and also in the venerable Svāyambhuva: / 'Whatever enjoyments one may desire in whatever place, he is assigned right there; // 263

sanskrit_iast:
siddhibhāṅmantrasāmarthyādityādyanyatra varṇitam /
ye tu tattattvavijñānamantracaryādivartinaḥ // 264
meaning:
सिद्धिभाङ्मन्त्रसामर्थ्यादित्याद्यन्यत्र वर्णितम् /
ये तु तत्तत्त्वविज्ञानमन्त्रचर्यादिवर्तिनः // 264
text_mt: he participates in accomplishment through the efficacy of the mantra,' etc., as described elsewhere. / But those wise ones who abide in the knowledge, mantra, conduct, and other practices of the various tattvas, // 264

sanskrit_iast:
mṛtāste tatra tadrudrasayuktvaṃ yānti kovidāḥ /
teṣāṃ sayuktvaṃ yātānāmapi saṃskārato nijāt // 265
meaning:
मृतास्ते तत्र तद्रुद्रसयुक्त्वं यान्ति कोविदाः /
तेषां सयुक्त्वं यातानामपि संस्कारतो निजात् // 265
text_mt: when they die, they attain unity with the Rudra of that [tattva]. / Even for those who have attained unity, on account of their own latent impressions, // 265

sanskrit_iast:
tathā tathā vicitraḥ syādavatārastadaṃśataḥ /
siddhāntādau purāṇeṣu tathāca śrūyate bahu // 266
meaning:
तथा तथा विचित्रः स्यादवतारस्तदंशतः /
सिद्धान्तादौ पुराणेषु तथाच श्रूयते बहु // 266
text_mt: there may be a descent as a portion of him in various ways. / And so it is frequently heard in the Siddhānta and other [texts], and in the Purāṇas, // 266

sanskrit_iast:
tulye rudrāvatāratve citratvaṃ karmabhogayoḥ /
anekaśaktikhacitaṃ yato bhāvasya yadvapuḥ // 267
meaning:
तुल्ये रुद्रावतारत्वे चित्रत्वं कर्मभोगयोः /
अनेकशक्तिखचितं यतो भावस्य यद्वपुः // 267
text_mt: that although the descent as Rudra is equal, there is diversity in action and enjoyment. / Because the nature of an entity is inlaid with manifold powers, // 267

sanskrit_iast:
śaktibhyo'rthāntaraṃ naiṣa tatsamūhādṛte bhavet /
tena śaktisamūhākhyāt tasmādrudrādyadaṃśataḥ // 268
meaning:
शक्तिभ्योऽर्थान्तरं नैष तत्समूहादृते भवेत् /
तेन शक्तिसमूहाख्यात् तस्माद्रुद्राद्यदंशतः // 268
text_mt: it cannot be a distinct reality from those powers, apart from their totality. / Therefore, from that Rudra, which is called an aggregate of powers, whatever portion // 268

sanskrit_iast:
kṛtyaṃ taducitaṃ siddhyet so'ṃśo'vatarati sphuṭam /
ye cādharaprāptadīkṣāstadāsthānujjhitāḥ pare // 269
meaning:
कृत्यं तदुचितं सिद्ध्येत् सोऽंशोऽवतरति स्फुटम् /
ये चाधरप्राप्तदीक्षास्तदास्थानुज्झिताः परे // 269
text_mt: can accomplish the task suitable to it—that portion clearly descends. / And those who have received initiation into a lower [tattva], but have not abandoned their devotion to it, // 269

sanskrit_iast:
tattve mṛtāḥ kāṣṭhavatte'dhare'pyutkarṣabhāginaḥ /
ye tūjjhitatadutkarṣāste taduttarabhāginaḥ // 270
meaning:
तत्त्वे मृताः काष्ठवत्तेऽधरेऽप्युत्कर्षभागिनः /
ये तूज्झिततदुत्कर्षास्ते तदुत्तरभागिनः // 270
text_mt: when they die in a higher tattva, like logs of wood, they attain preeminence in the lower [tattva] too. / But those who have abandoned [attachment to] that lower preeminence share in that higher [state]. // 270

sanskrit_iast:
ye'pyūrdhvatattvadīkṣāste vinā tāvadvivekataḥ /
prāptādharāntā api taddīkṣāphalasubhāginaḥ // 271
meaning:
येऽप्यूर्ध्वतत्त्वदीक्षास्ते विना तावद्विवेकतः /
प्राप्ताधरान्ता अपि तद्दीक्षाफलसुभागिनः // 271
text_mt: Even those initiated into a higher tattva who, lacking discernment, / have reached an inferior end, still partake fully of the fruit of that initiation. // 271

sanskrit_iast:
atyaktāsthā hi te tatra dīkṣāyāmapi śāstritāt /
vinā vivekādāsthāṃ te śritā lokaprasiddhitaḥ // 272
meaning:
अत्यक्तास्था हि ते तत्र दीक्षायामपि शास्त्रितात् /
विना विवेकादास्थां ते श्रिता लोकप्रसिद्धितः // 272
text_mt: For they have not abandoned devotion to that [higher tattva] in their initiation as prescribed by scripture, / [though] without discernment they had adopted devotion [to a lower deity] because of worldly convention. // 272

sanskrit_iast:
paśumātrasya sālokyaṃ sāmīpyaṃ dīkṣitasya tu /
tatparasya tu sāyujyamityuktaṃ parameśinā // 273
meaning:
पशुमात्रस्य सालोक्यं सामीप्यं दीक्षितस्य तु /
तत्परस्य तु सायुज्यमित्युक्तं परमेशिना // 273
text_mt: Co-residence belongs to the mere bound soul, but proximity belongs to the initiate; / union, however, belongs to the one devoted to Him: so it is taught by the Supreme Lord. // 273

sanskrit_iast:
yastūrdhvaśāstragastatra tyaktāsthaḥ saṃśayena saḥ /
vrajannāyatanaṃ naiva phalaṃ kiñcitsamaśnute // 274
meaning:
यस्तूर्ध्वशास्त्रगस्तत्र त्यक्तास्थः संशयेन सः /
व्रजन्नायतनं नैव फलं किञ्चित्समश्नुते // 274
text_mt: However, he who follows a higher scripture but abandons devotion to it out of doubt, / receives no fruit whatsoever when resorting to [that] sanctuary. // 274

sanskrit_iast:
uktaṃ tadviṣayaṃ caitaddevadevena yadvṛthā /
dīkṣā jñānaṃ tathā tīrthaṃ tasyetyādi savistaram // 275
meaning:
उक्तं तद्विषयं चैतद्देवदेवेन यद्वृथा /
दीक्षा ज्ञानं तथा तीर्थं तस्येत्यादि सविस्तरम् // 275
text_mt: And on this subject, it has been stated at length by the God of gods: 'Useless / are initiation, knowledge, and likewise the holy place for him,' and so forth. // 275

sanskrit_iast:
yastu tāvadayogyo'pi tathāste sa śivālaye /
paścādāsthānibandhena tāvadeva phalaṃ bhajet // 276
meaning:
यस्तु तावदयोग्योऽपि तथास्ते स शिवालये /
पश्चादास्थानिबन्धेन तावदेव फलं भजेत् // 276
text_mt: Yet one who, even though unfit, resides in an abode of Śiva, / will subsequently, on account of devotion, obtain that very fruit. // 276

sanskrit_iast:
nadīnagahradaprāyaṃ yacca puṇyaṃ na tanmṛtau /
utkṛṣṭaṃ tanmṛtānāṃ tu svargabhogopabhogitā // 277
meaning:
नदीनगह्रदप्रायं यच्च पुण्यं न तन्मृतौ /
उत्कृष्टं तन्मृतानां तु स्वर्गभोगोपभोगिता // 277
text_mt: Whatever sacred place consists mainly of rivers, mountains, and lakes does not lead to the highest [fruit] upon death; / for those who die there, there is merely the experience of heavenly enjoyments. // 277

sanskrit_iast:
ye punaḥ prāptavijñānavivekā maraṇāntike /
adharāyataneṣvāsthāṃ śritāste'tra tirohitāḥ // 278
meaning:
ये पुनः प्राप्तविज्ञानविवेका मरणान्तिके /
अधरायतनेष्वास्थां श्रितास्तेऽत्र तिरोहिताः // 278
text_mt: Those, however, who have attained discernment and knowledge, but at the approach of death / adhere to lower sanctuaries, become obscured in this matter. // 278

sanskrit_iast:
tajjñānadūṣaṇoktaṃ yatteṣāṃ syātkila pātakam /
tattatpureśadīkṣādikramānnaśyediti sthitiḥ // 279
meaning:
तज्ज्ञानदूषणोक्तं यत्तेषां स्यात्किल पातकम् /
तत्तत्पुरेशदीक्षादिक्रमान्नश्येदिति स्थितिः // 279
text_mt: Whatever sin they incur that is described as a fault against that knowledge / will perish by stages through the initiation and other rites of the lords of those cities: such is the established rule. // 279

sanskrit_iast:
dīkṣāyatanavijñānadūṣiṇo ye tu cetasā /
ācaranti ca tatte'tra sarve nirayagāminaḥ // 280
meaning:
दीक्षायतनविज्ञानदूषिणो ये तु चेतसा /
आचरन्ति च तत्तेऽत्र सर्वे निरयगामिनः // 280
text_mt: Those, however, who mentally disparage initiation, sanctuaries, and knowledge / and act accordingly, all go to hell in this world. // 280

sanskrit_iast:
jñānāyatanadīkṣādāvāsthābandhaparicyutiḥ /
vyāpāravyāhṛtairjñeyā tānyapi dvividhāni ca // 281
meaning:
ज्ञानायतनदीक्षादावास्थाबन्धपरिच्युतिः /
व्यापारव्याहृतैर्ज्ञेया तान्यपि द्विविधानि च // 281
text_mt: A lapse in the bond of devotion toward knowledge, sanctuaries, initiation, and the like / is to be recognized by actions and words; and these are also of two kinds: // 281

sanskrit_iast:
yāni jātucidapyeva svāsthye nodamiṣanpunaḥ /
asvāsthye dhātudoṣotthānyeva tadbhogamātrakam // 282
meaning:
यानि जातुचिदप्येव स्वास्थ्ये नोदमिषन्पुनः /
अस्वास्थ्ये धातुदोषोत्थान्येव तद्भोगमात्रकम् // 282
text_mt: those that never manifested while in good health, / but arose in illness solely from a disorder of the bodily humors—they are merely an experience of that [illness]. // 282

sanskrit_iast:
dhātudoṣācca saṃsārasaṃskārāste prabodhitāḥ /
chidragā api bhūyiṣṭhajñānadagdhā na rohiṇaḥ // 283
meaning:
धातुदोषाच्च संसारसंस्कारास्ते प्रबोधिताः /
छिद्रगा अपि भूयिष्ठज्ञानदग्धा न रोहिणः // 283
text_mt: And from the disorder of bodily humors, those latent impressions of saṃsāra are awakened; / though finding an opening, being mostly burned by knowledge, they do not sprout. // 283

sanskrit_iast:
ye tu kaivalyabhāgīyāḥ svāsthye'nunmiṣitāḥ sadā /
asvāsthye conmiṣantyete saṃskārāḥ śaktipātataḥ // 284
meaning:
ये तु कैवल्यभागीयाः स्वास्थ्येऽनुन्मिषिताः सदा /
अस्वास्थ्ये चोन्मिषन्त्येते संस्काराः शक्तिपाततः // 284
text_mt: Those [impressions], however, that pertain to liberation never manifest during health, / but through the descent of power, these latent impressions do manifest during illness, // 284

sanskrit_iast:
yataḥ sāṃsārikāḥ pūrvagāḍhābhyāsopasaṃskṛtāḥ /
ityūce bhujagādhīśastacchidreṣviti sūtrataḥ // 285
meaning:
यतः सांसारिकाः पूर्वगाढाभ्यासोपसंस्कृताः /
इत्यूचे भुजगाधीशस्तच्छिद्रेष्विति सूत्रतः // 285
text_mt: because worldly [impressions] are reinforced by deep previous practice. / Thus the Lord of Serpents [Patañjali] taught in the sūtra: 'In the intervals thereof...' // 285

sanskrit_iast:
ye tu kaivalyabhāgīyāḥ pratyayāste na jātucit /
abhyastāḥ saṃsṛterbhāvāttenaite śaktipātataḥ // 286
meaning:
ये तु कैवल्यभागीयाः प्रत्ययास्ते न जातुचित् /
अभ्यस्ताः संसृतेर्भावात्तेनैते शक्तिपाततः // 286
text_mt: Those cognitions, however, that pertain to liberation have never been / cultivated because of the nature of transmigratory existence; therefore, they occur through the descent of power. // 286

sanskrit_iast:
vyāpāravyāhṛtaistena dhātudoṣaprakopitaiḥ /
aprāptaniścayāmarśaiḥ suptamattopamānakaiḥ // 287
meaning:
व्यापारव्याहृतैस्तेन धातुदोषप्रकोपितैः /
अप्राप्तनिश्चयामर्शैः सुप्तमत्तोपमानकैः // 287
text_mt: Therefore, through [states] brought about by activities, agitated by disturbances of bodily humours, / devoid of determinate reflective awareness, resembling sleep or intoxication, // 287

sanskrit_iast:
viparītairapi jñānadīkṣāgurvādidūṣakaiḥ /
tirobhāvo na vijñeyo hṛdaye rūḍhyabhāvataḥ // 288
meaning:
विपरीतैरपि ज्ञानदीक्षागुर्वादिदूषकैः /
तिरोभावो न विज्ञेयो हृदये रूढ्यभावतः // 288
text_mt: and even through contrary [states] reviling knowledge, initiation, the guru, and the like, / one should not understand that concealment occurs, because [these] have no root in the heart. // 288

sanskrit_iast:
ata eva prabuddho'pi karmotthānbhogarūpiṇaḥ /
yamakiṅkarasarpādipratyayāndehago bhajet // 289
meaning:
अत एव प्रबुद्धोऽपि कर्मोत्थान्भोगरूपिणः /
यमकिङ्करसर्पादिप्रत्ययान्देहगो भजेत् // 289
text_mt: For this very reason, even an awakened one, dwelling in the body, may experience / cognitions arising from karma that take the form of experiences—such as the messengers of Yama, serpents, and so on. // 289

sanskrit_iast:
naitāvatā na mukto'sau mṛtirbhogo hi janmavat /
sthitivacca tato duḥkhasukhābhyāṃ maraṇaṃ dvidhā // 290
meaning:
नैतावता न मुक्तोऽसौ मृतिर्भोगो हि जन्मवत् /
स्थितिवच्च ततो दुःखसुखाभ्यां मरणं द्विधा // 290
text_mt: Not by this much is he unliberated, for dying is an experience just like birth / and just like life; therefore death is twofold through pain and pleasure. // 290

sanskrit_iast:
ato yathā prabuddhasya sukhaduḥkhavicitratāḥ /
sthitau na ghnanti muktatvaṃ maraṇe'pi tathaiva tāḥ // 291
meaning:
अतो यथा प्रबुद्धस्य सुखदुःखविचित्रताः /
स्थितौ न घ्नन्ति मुक्तत्वं मरणेऽपि तथैव ताः // 291
text_mt: Therefore, just as the varied experiences of pleasure and pain of an awakened one / during life do not destroy his state of liberation, so too do they not destroy it at death. // 291

sanskrit_iast:
ye punaryoginaste'pi yasmiṃstattve subhāvitāḥ /
cittaṃ niveśayantyeva tattattvaṃ yāntyaśaṅkitāḥ // 292
meaning:
ये पुनर्योगिनस्तेऽपि यस्मिंस्तत्त्वे सुभाविताः /
चित्तं निवेशयन्त्येव तत्तत्त्वं यान्त्यशङ्किताः // 292
text_mt: Moreover, yogins too, steeped in whatever reality, / enter it without doubt just by directing their consciousness into it. // 292

sanskrit_iast:
śrīsvacchande tataḥ proktaṃ gandhadhāraṇayā mṛtāḥ /
ityādi mālinīśāstre dhāraṇānāṃ tathā phalam // 293
meaning:
श्रीस्वच्छन्दे ततः प्रोक्तं गन्धधारणया मृताः /
इत्यादि मालिनीशास्त्रे धारणानां तथा फलम् // 293
text_mt: Therefore it was stated in the venerable Svacchanda: 'those who die through concentration on smell...', / and likewise in the Mālinī treatise regarding the fruit of concentrations. // 293

sanskrit_iast:
eteṣāṃ maraṇābhikhyo bhogo nāsti tu ye tanum /
dhāraṇābhistyajantyāśu paradehapraveśavat // 294
meaning:
एतेषां मरणाभिख्यो भोगो नास्ति तु ये तनुम् /
धारणाभिस्त्यजन्त्याशु परदेहप्रवेशवत् // 294
text_mt: For those, however, who quickly abandon the body by means of concentrations, / as in entering another's body, the experience called dying does not exist. // 294

sanskrit_iast:
etāvānmṛtibhogo hi marmacchinmūḍhatākṣagā /
dhvāntābilatvaṃ manasi taccaiteṣu na vidyate // 295
meaning:
एतावान्मृतिभोगो हि मर्मच्छिन्मूढताक्षगा /
ध्वान्ताबिलत्वं मनसि तच्चैतेषु न विद्यते // 295
text_mt: For such an experience of dying is the cutting of vital spots, delusion occurring in the senses, / and turbid darkness in the mind; and that is not present in these [yogins]. // 295

sanskrit_iast:
tathāhi mānasaṃ yatnaṃ tāvatsamadhitiṣṭhati /
ahaṃrūḍhyā pare dehe yāvatsyādbuddhisaṃcaraḥ // 296
meaning:
तथाहि मानसं यत्नं तावत्समधितिष्ठति /
अहंरूढ्या परे देहे यावत्स्याद्बुद्धिसंचरः // 296
text_mt: To explain: mental effort persists to that extent, / by establishing the sense of 'I' in the other body, as long as the transition of the intellect occurs. // 296

sanskrit_iast:
prāṇacakraṃ tadāyattamapi saṃcarate pathā /
tenaivātaḥ prabuddhyeta paradehe'kṣacakrakam // 297
meaning:
प्राणचक्रं तदायत्तमपि संचरते पथा /
तेनैवातः प्रबुद्ध्येत परदेहेऽक्षचक्रकम् // 297
text_mt: The circle of vital breaths, dependent on it, also moves along that very same / path; therefore, the circle of senses awakens in the other body. // 297

sanskrit_iast:
makṣikā makṣikārājaṃ yathotthitamanūtthitāḥ /
sthitaṃ cānuviśantyevaṃ cittaṃ sarvākṣavṛttayaḥ // 298
meaning:
मक्षिका मक्षिकाराजं यथोत्थितमनूत्थिताः /
स्थितं चानुविशन्त्येवं चित्तं सर्वाक्षवृत्तयः // 298
text_mt: Just as flies rise up after the queen bee rises / and settle after it settles, so do all sense operations [follow] the mind. // 298

sanskrit_iast:
ato'sya paradehādisaṃcāre nāsti melanam /
akṣāṇāṃ madhyagaṃ sūkṣmaṃ syādetaddehavatpunaḥ // 299
meaning:
अतोऽस्य परदेहादिसंचारे नास्ति मेलनम् /
अक्षाणां मध्यगं सूक्ष्मं स्यादेतद्देहवत्पुनः // 299
